papers.title: A Multidimensional Arithmetical Ontology for High-Parameter Cytometry: Gaussian Primes and Cryptographic Hashing for Cell Population Standardization
papers.abstract: Background. The rapid expansion of high-dimensional single-cell technologies has outpaced the development of standardized metadata infrastructure. Current text-based ontology for cell populations and gating strategies lacks computational rigor, hindering process automation and cross-study reproducibility. Our previous frameworks, the Prime Population System (PPS) and the Unique Gating Identifier (UGI), proposed arithmetical solutions but were limited by biological fragility (no inherent link between a protein and its structural isoforms) and by computational bottlenecks caused by exponential integer growth. Objective. To develop a scalable, multidimensional arithmetical ontology that unambiguously identifies cell populations and hierarchical gating strategies. Methods. We transition the marker dictionary from the one-dimensional real axis (R) to the complex plane of Gaussian integers (a+bi). The reviewed human proteome of the UniProt Knowledgebase is paired with Gaussian primes satisfying a > b > 0. Each protein receives a contiguous reserved block of 64 primes: slot 0 addresses the protein with isoform unresolved, and slot k addresses UniProt isoform k, the slot index being read directly off the accession. Carbohydrate epitopes, which have no UniProt entry, are paired through the CD nomenclature instead: in a CD region beyond the 80,000 blocks reserved for the proteome, each CD number receives a block of 1,024 primes, with the slot read off the suffix of the designation. A bipartite encoding represents positive (a+bi) and negative (b+ai) expression states through Conjugate Pair Symmetry. To avoid the integer explosion of Godel exponentiation, hierarchical gating sequences are held as vectorized arrays of complex numbers and compressed by SHA-256 deterministic hashing. Results. Pairing against the human proteome assigns 53,296 identifiers, 20,431 protein-level and 32,865 isoform-level. Every isoform description resolves under a single rule, including the 329 descriptions whose accession prefix differs from the entry that cites them. The 19 carbohydrate designations of the CD list, CD57 among them, receive identifiers in the CD region. Localized vectorization with SHA-256 hashing yields immutable 64-character hexadecimal fingerprints for entire gating strategies, resolving the integer explosion problem. Conclusion. By combining Gaussian primes with hashing, Gaussian Prime Cytometry provides a scalable, computationally lightweight and biologically accurate identifier system. The system eliminates nomenclature ambiguity and facilitates machine learning applications and centralized global cytometry databases.
affiliations: Luxembourg Institute of Health, Esch-sur-Alzette, Luxembourg (corresponding author)

papers.title: Red-light-catalyzed photolipid switching enables leaflet-selective control of membrane mechanics
papers.abstract: Azobenzene photolipids are versatile actuators of membrane mechanics and protein function, yet long-wavelength control and leaflet-selective perturbations remain difficult to impose. Here, we address both limitations. First, we confirm that red-light excitation of a lipidated Nile Blue derivative (NB-lipid) catalyzes rapid cis[->]trans photoisomerization of co-localized azobenzene photolipids in planar bilayers without requiring covalent conjugation. Second, we demonstrate that photocatalysis is predominantly intraleaflet, enabling leaflet-selective actuation by incorporating the membrane-targeted chromophore into only one bilayer leaflet. This enables on-demand and rapid writing of transbilayer mechanical asymmetry, which we track via lock-in capacitance signatures. Critically, symmetric and asymmetric leaflet mechanical perturbations can be evoked within the same membrane by illuminating with blue or red light, respectively. For electron-rich azobenzenes, the anticipated singlet-state photoredox pathway is expected to limit triplet-associated photodamage. Repeated, reversible modulation of gramicidin A, a mechanosensitive peptide ion channel susceptible to reactive oxygen species, supports the compatibility of photocatalysis with membrane protein function. Our results establish a novel tool for dissecting the role of dynamic leaflet-specific mechanical changes in membrane remodeling and protein function.
affiliations: Johannes Kepler University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Mapping the journey of a neuro-invasive virus in zebrafish larvae: contrasted viral spread and type I interferon responses in periphery and central nervous system
papers.abstract: Organ-to-organ dissemination of viruses is a critical feature of host-virus interactions. Neuroinvasive viruses can enter the central nervous systems (CNS), which often results in death or permanent neurological impairment. The complex mechanisms underpinning this spread are poorly understood, as they depend on a variety of parameters, including initial site of entry, route of access to the CNS, and immune responses. To better understand these phenomena, we analyzed the spatial dynamics of Sindbis virus (SINV) dissemination in the transparent zebrafish larva. Using fluorescent reporter viruses, we observed that SINV readily invaded the CNS after inoculation at various peripheral sites. Both sensory and motor neurons were gateways to the CNS, with 2 to 3 occurrences of CNS entry par larva. While peripheral infection was transient, CNS infection was persistent and more variable. Within the CNS, viral dissemination resulted both from long-distance axonal transport and short distance shedding. Type I interferon (IFN) response was systemic in the periphery, and local in the CNS; nevertheless, it played a key role in controlling the infection in both compartments, as shown by IFN receptor knockdown or with IFN triple mutants. We built a mathematical model of the infection based on our quantitative imaging, providing additional insight. The rate of new virion production was estimated around 1 to 2 infective virions per productively infected cell per hour. The model also found that IFN did not only prevent new infections but accelerated the death of infected cells, and had a stronger effect in periphery than CNS. This study paves the way for a deeper understanding of the mechanisms at play in pathogen- and host response- mediated neurological damage during viral encephalitis.
affiliations: Institut Pasteur (corresponding author)

papers.title: A chromosome-level, haplotype-resolved genome assembly of the impressed tortoise, Manouria impressa
papers.abstract: Background. The impressed tortoise, Manouria impressa (Gunther, 1882), is an Endangered, largely fungivorous tortoise of the montane forests of Southeast Asia and one of the two living species of the basal testudinid genus Manouria. It is one of the least-studied tortoises, and no chromosome-level genome was available for the genus. Findings. From 68.5 Gb of PacBio HiFi reads (28x), 9.8 Gb of Hi-C read pairs and RNA-seq of heart and lung from a single female, we assembled a 2.42 Gb primary assembly with a contig N50 of 86.9 Mb and a scaffold N50 of 138.6 Mb. Hi-C scaffolding followed by quantitative curation -- every scaffold join scored against the within-contig contact-decay expectation -- placed 94.5 % of the sequence in 26 chromosomes, matching the testudinid karyotype (2n = 52); the remaining 335 scaffolds are unplaced. Consensus accuracy is QV 67.9 (Merqury), k-mer completeness 95.1 %, and 99.3 % of vertebrate BUSCO genes are complete. Two phased haplotype assemblies (scaffold N50 87.8 and 91.6 Mb; QV 69.1 and 68.5; 99.2 % combined k-mer completeness) and the 18.1-kb mitochondrial genome were assembled from the same data. Repeats mask 48.6 % of the genome (LINEs 11.5 %, LTR retrotransposons 10.0 %, DNA transposons 7.6 %, SINEs 2.6 %, unclassified families 15.4 %); 24,875 protein-coding genes were predicted from RNA-seq and OrthoDB protein evidence (97.6 % complete vertebrate BUSCOs), 89.0 % of them functionally annotated. Conclusions. This haplotype-resolved reference, with its curation evidence and scripts, provides the first chromosome-level genomic resource for Manouria and a foundation for conservation genomics and for studies of the dietary specialisation of this fungivorous tortoise.
affiliations: Shanghai ImmunoBiotech Co.,Ltd. (corresponding author)

papers.title: DNA-MGC+: A versatile codec for reliable and resource-efficient data storage on synthetic DNA
papers.abstract: The biochemical processes underlying DNA data storage, including synthesis, amplification, and sequencing, are inherently noisy, leading to insertion, deletion, and substitution errors as well as sequence dropouts that challenge reliable data retrieval. Here we introduce DNA-MGC+, a DNA storage codec designed for reliable and resource-efficient retrieval under diverse operating conditions. We evaluate DNA-MGC+ across various in silico and in vitro settings. In comparison with selected representative codecs, the results show that DNA-MGC+ consistently improves key performance metrics under explicit reliability constraints, including required sequencing depth, read cost, decoding time, storage density, and error-correction capability. In silico experiments show that DNA-MGC+ supports reliable decoding at error rates up to 24% for a 15-KB file, while separate scalability experiments demonstrate reliable decoding of files up to 200 MB at a 5% error rate. In vitro experiments involving a 24-KB file and electrochemical synthesis show that different DNA-MGC+ configurations achieve minimum sequencing depths below 3x and read costs below 3.5 nts/bit under both Illumina and Nanopore sequencing.
affiliations: CNRS (corresponding author)

papers.title: CCIDeconv: Hierarchical model for deconvolution of subcellular cell-cell interactions in single-cell data
papers.abstract: Cell-cell interaction (CCI) underlies several fundamental biological processes, including development, homeostasis and disease progression. Subcellular spatial transcriptomics (sST) provides an opportunity to examine whether CCI-associated signals show compartment-specific patterns within cells. Assessing CCI at subcellular level can help us gain insights into the distinct pathway activation and signalling patterns. We developed a novel approach that deconvolutes CCI into subcellular CCI (sCCI) information from non-spatial single-cell transcriptomics (scRNA- seq) based CCI using a modified CellChat-derived communication score. By estimating communication scores separately for cytoplasmic and nuclear compartments, we identified compartment-associated sCCI. We then deconvolved whole-cell communication scores into subcellular compartments using a hierarchical classification and regression framework, which we call CCIDeconv. To ensure biological fidelity, we integrated protein localization data from the Human Protein Atlas in our deconvolution model. Across nine publicly available human sST datasets, leave-one- dataset-out validation achieved a median composite score of 0.75, with mean R2 values of 0.87 and 0.80 for cytoplasmic- and nuclear-associated scores, respectively. Performance without spatial features approached that of spatial models as the number of training datasets increased, supporting application to non-spatial scRNA-seq data. This highlighted the potential for prediction of sCCI from scRNA-seq, given a sufficiently large number of training datasets. Overall, our method can attribute whole-cell CCI to its subcellular compartments, allowing researchers to dissect sCCI patterns and gain insights into the underlying biology of healthy and disease tissues. Keywords Cell-Cell Communication, Single Cell RNA-seq, Predictive Modeling, Bioinformatics, Transcriptomics, Machine Learning
affiliations: The University of Sydney (corresponding author)

papers.title: Skiver: Reference-free quality control of metagenomic sequencing datasets using (k,v)-mer sketches
papers.abstract: Quality control is essential in numerous Bioinformatics pipelines, yet existing approaches often depend on inefficient mapping to reference genomes or potentially uncalibrated quality scores. We present skiver, a reference-free, alignment-free quality control tool that uses (k, v)-mer sketches. By deriving consensus from sketched (k, v)-mers, skiver estimates survival and hazard rates that capture the positional distribution of errors. Across simulated and real datasets from multiple sequencing platforms, skiver accurately estimates overall error rates, error-type proportions, and quality-score calibration. An iterative outlier-filtering strategy enables robust performance on complex datasets with multiple strains, alleles, and repetitive regions.
affiliations: Genome Institute of Singapore (corresponding author)

papers.title: RICO enables integrated analysis of ribosomal DNA copy number and methylation from nanopore long-read sequencing
papers.abstract: Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) provides the structural and catalytic core of ribosomes and is encoded by ribosomal RNA genes (rDNA) arranged in tandem repeat arrays. rDNA copy number (CN) is highly dynamic, representing a clinically relevant form of structural variation, but its accurate quantification has been challenging due to its highly repetitive and GC-rich nature. Here, we present RICO (RIbosomal dna Integrated COpy number and methylation analysis), a novel computational pipeline for integrated estimation of rDNA CN and methylation using Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing. RICO leverages long sequencing reads that span entire rDNA repeats, mapped to an rDNA-augmented reference genome, and normalizes coverage using a single-copy gene panel. We demonstrate that RICO provides accurate rDNA CN estimates in simulated datasets and reproducible measurements across human samples, with strong agreement to short-read sequencing and PCR-based methods. Furthermore, RICO reproduces a ~40% reduction in rDNA CN in Atrx-knockout mouse embryonic stem cells, consistent with established effects of ATRX loss on rDNA CN. RICO also captures an increased total and active rDNA CN in malignant cells from a MYC-driven B-cell lymphoma mouse model, in agreement with prior studies. Applying RICO to independent human cohorts, we uncover that individuals with higher total rDNA CN consistently exhibit higher fractions of highly methylated rDNA copies, suggesting a dosage compensation mechanism that potentially maintains a similar number of active rDNA copies across individuals. Together, RICO enables integrated analysis of rDNA CN and methylation state, providing a scalable framework for investigating rDNA regulation across population and disease studies. RICO is available at https://github.com/comprna/RICO.
affiliations: Australian National University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Sequestration-based Protein Neural Networks Tolerate the Effects of Shared Translational Resources
papers.abstract: Biochemical neural networks offer a promising framework for implementing advanced computation in living cells, yet how competition for shared cellular resources shapes their behavior remains poorly characterized. In this work, we develop a resource-aware mathematical framework to analyze how competition for ribosomes affects protein neural networks implemented via molecular sequestration in bacterial systems. Focusing on classification tasks, we show that when all mRNA species share identical ribosome-binding affinities, competition induces a uniform rescaling of the network's effective weights, reducing the output magnitude while preserving the geometry of the decision boundary. When these affinities differ, competition introduces curvature in the decision boundary, transforming a linear classifier into a nonlinear one through resource coupling. This curvature is constrained to a well-defined region of the input space whose extent is determined by the degree of variability in the binding affinities, making the effect both predictable and, potentially, exploitable for design. Next, we numerically extend our analysis from a single perceptron to multi-layer architectures with two hidden-layer nodes and show that, for both closed and non-convex decision boundaries, resource competition preserves the boundary geometry in the homogeneous-affinity case, while in the heterogeneous case, curvature distortions from hidden-layer nodes propagate and compose at the output within a bounded uncertainty region. Finally, we incorporate growth-mediated feedback into the framework and show that the structural form of the activation function and decision boundary is preserved. Overall, our results provide a quantitative basis for understanding how translational resource competition shapes the behavior of protein-level molecular classifiers.
affiliations: Carnegie Mellon University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Damaged motile cilia undergo phagolysosomal clearance during regeneration
papers.abstract: The remodelling and regeneration of motile cilia are widespread yet poorly understood cellular responses to stress. Whether components from damaged cilia are reutilised during regeneration remains unclear. Here, we apply acute, non-lethal stress to the multiciliated eukaryote Tetrahymena thermophila to investigate the fate of damaged motile cilia during regeneration. We find that damaged axonemes accumulate intracellularly as coiled structures, termed c-rings, which are sequestered within phagosome-associated membrane compartments and subsequently associate with acidic compartments for clearance. Imaging, quantitative proteomics and genetic perturbations reveal a phagolysosomal route for processing damaged axonemes, accompanied by recruitment of autophagy-associated machinery. Remarkably, ciliary regeneration proceeds without detectable c-ring accumulation, even when new protein synthesis is inhibited, indicating that reutilisation of internalised axonemal material is not essential for ciliogenesis. Our findings uncover an unexpected mechanism for clearing damaged motile cilia and reveal how ciliary degradation and regeneration can operate as distinct cellular processes.
affiliations: Sir William Dunn School of Pathology, University of Oxford (corresponding author)

papers.title: Talking Brains: Neonatal Aperiodic Activity in Resting State EEG Relates to Later Communicative Abilities
papers.abstract: Communicative abilities acquired over the first year of life are foundational for language development. Understanding the neural mechanisms underlying these abilities can explain individual differences and improve predictions of later language outcomes. While prior research on neural markers of language development has focused predominantly on oscillatory neural activity, the underlying aperiodic component of the neural signal may provide further insights into cortical maturation by indirectly reflecting variation in neural excitation/inhibition (E/I) balance. In neurodevelopmental conditions, both reduced and elevated aperiodic activity are linked to atypical development, and initial evidence from at-risk cohorts also relates aperiodic activity to language outcome. Moving beyond clinical populations, the present study examined whether aperiodic activity during neonatal resting-state EEG relates to 12-month communicative abilities in typically developing infants. Aperiodic offset and exponent were extracted from resting-state EEG recorded two weeks after birth in n = 50 neonates using the FOOOF algorithm. At 12 months, communicative abilities were assessed with the parent-report CSBS-DP Infant-Toddler Checklist. Quadratic regression analyses showed an inverted U-shaped relationship between the neonatal aperiodic exponent and communicative abilities: both lower and higher exponent values were associated with poorer outcomes, with intermediate values linked to better abilities. No robust association was found for the offset. These findings suggest that aperiodic activity captures variability in early communicative development, with an optimum at intermediate levels, consistent with a balanced E/I state. The scope of aperiodic brain activity as a developmental marker may thus extend beyond clinical populations to predicting communicative development in healthy infants.
affiliations: University of Salzburg (corresponding author)

papers.title: YAP1-2α-TAZ heterodimerization promotes BRD4-associated LLPS-like assembly at candidate super-enhancers and cancer cell malignancy
papers.abstract: YAP1 is a transcriptional coactivator expressed as multiple splice isoforms, but how individual isoforms specify malignant cell states remains unclear. Here, we identify YAP1-2 as an isoform that drives a distinct transcriptional state in cancer cells. The YAP1-2-TAZ heterodimer, together with TEAD, forms BRD4-associated nuclear assemblies with LLPS-like properties. These assemblies are enriched at candidate super-enhancer-associated regions and promote transcription. Disrupting YAP1-2-TAZ heterodimerization, TEAD binding, or BRD4 interaction impairs assembly formation and associated phenotypes. Exon-6 exclusion promotes YAP1-2-associated nuclear puncta, invasion, and therapeutic resistance in high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC), and enhances intraperitoneal tumor progression in gastric cancer xenografts. Gastric cancer cells selected through peritoneal dissemination exhibit increased YAP1-2, nuclear YAP1 puncta, and therapeutic resistance. In HGSOC specimens, YAP1-2 abundance, YAP1-BRD4 proximity, and nuclear YAP1 puncta are associated with advanced stages. Thus, YAP1-2 drives a BRD4-associated condensate-like transcriptional state linked to malignant progression across multiple cancer contexts.
affiliations: Institute of Microbial Chemistry (corresponding author)

papers.title: Peptide Sequence Determines the Efficacy of Single-Dose AAV-Vectorized GLP-1R Agonists in Diet-Induced Obese Mice
papers.abstract: Background: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonists such as semaglutide produce substantial weight loss and glycemic improvement, but their long-term efficacy depends on sustained adherence to chronic dosing. Adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene therapy could, in principle, provide durable GLP-1R agonist (GLP-1RA) exposure from a single administration, but the degree of peptide engineering required for a vectorized GLP-1RA transgene to be efficacious in vivo is unknown. Methods: We generated four self-complementary AAV (scAAV) constructs encoding: native human GLP-1(7-36) (GLP-1), a DPP-IV-resistant Gly8-GLP-1(7-36) variant (Gly8), Exendin-4 (Ex4), or an Exendin-4 human IgG4 Fc fusion protein (Ex4-Fc). All four constructs were validated to secrete functional GLP-1R agonists in vitro using a conditioned-media potency assay. Subsequently, these constructs were packaged into PHP.eB capsids and administered as a single intravenous dose (5x1012 vg/kg) to diet-induced obese (DIO) mice alongside a vehicle control. Body weight, body composition, food intake, fasting plasma insulin, and oral glucose tolerance were assessed over a 3-week period. At the end of the study, tissues were harvested for assessments of plasma/liver lipids, tissue transgene transcript and peptide levels. Results: HEK293 cells transfected with the four AAV constructs all secreted active peptides/proteins as assessed by a cell-based GLP-1R activation assay, although the effective concentration of the GLP-1 constructs in the media spanned nearly four orders of magnitude 72 hours after transfection. In diet-induced obese (DIO) mice, Ex4 and Ex4-Fc vectors, but not GLP-1 or Gly8 vectors, produced significant reductions in body weight of up to 22.6% of starting body weight out to 21 days after a single dose. In addition, reductions in food intake, fat mass, and fasting insulin relative to vehicle were also observed for Ex4 and Ex4-Fc. Furthermore, Ex4-Fc improved oral glucose tolerance while reducing plasma cholesterol and liver triglycerides relative to vehicle. Although transcript levels did not differ appreciably among the four constructs in either brain or liver, measurable peptide product in plasma and brain lysate tracked the rank order of the in vitro supernatant screen, with GLP-1 and Gly8 groups indistinguishable from endogenous background. Conclusions: PHP.eB scAAV Ex4 and Ex4-Fc showed robust efficacy on multiple metabolic endpoints including weight loss and glucose tolerance. In contrast, vectorized GLP-1 and Gly8 showed no in vivo efficacy despite comparable levels of viral transcript in the brain and the liver. Vectorized GLP-1 and Gly8 also performed poorly compared to exendin-4-based constructs in vitro, suggesting that conditioned-media potency screening is a valid early filter for construct selection in vectorized-peptide AAV development. Engineering peptides to improve translation and secretion efficiency, in addition to circulating plasma stability, could further optimize vectorized GLP-1RA therapeutics.
affiliations: Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc. (corresponding author)

papers.title: Use of Antibody Structural Information in Disease Prediction Models Reveals Antigen Specific B Cell Receptor Sequences in Bulk Repertoire Data
papers.abstract: Convergent antibodies are highly similar antibodies elicited in multiple individuals in response to the same antigen. Convergent antibodies provide insight into shared immunological responses and show great promise as diagnostic biomarkers. They have typically been identified using methods that consider the amino acid sequence of the third complementarity-determining region (CDR3) of immunoglobulin heavy chain (IgH). In this study, we extend this definition of convergent antibodies to use structural information about the three IgH CDR regions (CDR1-3) and antibody isotype. We measure the performance of both definitions of convergence by their ability to predict disease status from bulk IgH sequencing data for two different disease cohorts: HIV infection and food allergen sensitization. We show that using predicted structural information outperforms prior approaches for the prediction of food sensitization status and performs on par for HIV infection status. Additionally, the use of structural information and antibody isotype enables better model interpretation and more immunological insights. The structurally convergent antibody groups driving HIV prediction accuracy are from known HIV-binding antibodies expressing the appropriate isotype. Thus, the incorporation of structural information can enable the identification of antigen specific antibody groups from bulk IgH sequencing data.
affiliations: Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA (corresponding author)

papers.title: Genome-wide interrogation of genetic requirements for root colonization by CRISPRi-seq in Bacillus subtilis
papers.abstract: Bacillus subtilis is a known plant growth promoting rhizobacterium. Yet, the genetic basis for effective B. subtilis root colonization remains unclear. Here, we applied genome-wide CRISPR interference sequencing (CRISPRi-seq) to systematically identify bacterial genes required for early Arabidopsis thaliana root colonization by the undomesticated B. subtilis strain NCIB3610. Complementary bacterial RNA-seq experiments in the same conditions further revealed a distinct transcriptional state of root-associated cells. Together, we identified 249 B. subtilis genes impacting root colonization. We reveal a critical, biofilm-independent, role of cell envelope remodeling during early root association, specifically wall teichoic acid synthesis and D-alanylation. Moreover, we observed a metabolic shift toward TCA-cycle-driven aerobic growth and utilization of fructose, induction of secondary metabolite biosynthesis, as well as active repression of sporulation, competence and prophage programs. Our work establishes CRISPRi-seq as a powerful tool for dissecting bacterial-plant interactions relevant to sustainable agriculture.
affiliations: University of Lausanne (corresponding author)

papers.title: Effect of Lactobacillus postbiotic supplementation on intestinal permeability, nutrient digestibility, and gut microbial and metabolic profiles in aging cats
papers.abstract: Aging in cats is associated with declining nutrient digestibility and increased intestinal permeability, but evidence supporting microbiome-targeted interventions in older cats remains limited. We investigated whether daily supplementation with the Lactobacillus-derived postbiotic LB fermentate HF (LBHF) affected intestinal permeability, apparent total tract digestibility, gut microbiome composition, and fecal and plasma metabolomic profiles in older cats. Twenty cats aged 7.7-13.8 years were enrolled in a blinded, placebo-controlled crossover trial comprising two 29-day treatment periods separated by a 28-day washout; 18 cats completed both periods. Intestinal permeability was the primary endpoint, while nutrient digestibility, microbiome composition, and metabolomic profiles were secondary endpoints. LBHF did not affect intestinal permeability or absorptive capacity relative to placebo, although intestinal permeability was positively associated with age. Overall nutrient digestibility was higher during LBHF treatment, with the clearest endpoint-specific evidence observed for protein digestibility. LBHF was associated with a non-significant overall increase in Shannon diversity and a reduction in the relative abundance of Streptococcus lutetiensis. The increase in Shannon diversity was significant only in cats receiving placebo followed by LBHF, indicating a treatment-sequence-dependent response. Thirty-three plasma and 29 fecal metabolites showed significantly different changes during LBHF treatment compared with placebo. Plasma metabolites generally showed more positive changes during LBHF treatment, whereas most associated fecal metabolites showed more negative changes. Sequence-stratified microbiome and metabolome responses differed substantially, suggesting possible period, treatment-order, or carryover effects. Overall, LBHF did not improve intestinal permeability but was well tolerated and improved nutrient digestibility, particularly protein digestibility, while producing modest and sequence-dependent microbiome and metabolome responses. These findings suggest that the effects of LBHF in healthy older cats may relate more strongly to digestive efficiency and host metabolic responses than to intestinal permeability.
affiliations: dsm-firmenich Houdan SAS, Houdan, France (corresponding author)

papers.title: The staphylococcal type VII secretion system delays inflammatory cell death during macrophage infection
papers.abstract: The human pathogen Staphylococcus aureus is a facultatively intracellular bacterium that can replicate and survive within macrophages. While macrophage-mediated immune modulation is pivotal in S. aureus pathogenesis, bacterial manipulation of macrophage pathways remains poorly understood. The specialised type VII secretion system (T7SSb) is an important virulence-associated factor during staphylococcal infection, although, unlike its mycobacterial counterparts, its role in controlling staphylococcal-macrophage interactions remains unclear. Employing high-resolution time-lapse imaging, we demonstrated an induction of pore-induced cellular traps (PITs) during S. aureus infection of macrophages in vitro, with a higher number of PITs forming in macrophages infected with S. aureus lacking EssC ({Delta}essC), a central T7SS transporter. Interestingly, {Delta}essC-infected macrophages displayed increased bacterial escape compared to wild type (WT)-infected cells, implicating a role for T7SS in delaying macrophage cell death. Changes in cell death were accompanied by a reduction in efferocytosis of {Delta}essC-infected cells in vitro. Investigation of cell death signalling markers in WT and {Delta}essC-infected macrophages demonstrated that the T7SS delayed induction of key cell death pathways, necroptosis and pyroptosis, and a dual RNAseq analysis of WT- and {Delta}essC-infected macrophages indicated a T7SS-dependent modulation of bacterial oxidative stress and selected host chemokines. We also demonstrated that T7SS effectors, EsxA and EsxC individually delayed macrophage cell death. Interestingly, {Delta}esxC mutants demonstrated accelerated calcium fluxes, indicating that the T7SS-mediated suppression of cellular calcium signalling may cause the delay in cell death. Furthermore, in a murine skin infection model, we showed that effector and transporter mutants have distinct S. aureus infection outcomes. Our findings suggest for the first time a key role for T7SSb proteins in controlling macrophage cell death, which impacts staphylococcal survival within the host during infection.

papers.title: Promoter-responsiveness to distal regulatory elements is mediated by the promoter-proximal region
papers.abstract: Gene promoters induce transcription in response to distal enhancers located in large gene regulatory domains. How this long-range regulation specifically activates the target promoter while bypassing other promoters located in the same regulatory domain remains unclear. Here, we find that the promoter-proximal region is critical for cell-type specific promoter responsiveness. Using high-throughput genome-engineering in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESC), we systematically replace the endogenous Sox9 promoter with different libraries of core and extended (i.e. full) promoters and assess their response to long-range regulatory elements in mESCs and neural progenitor cells. We find that only a subset of full promoters is activated by distal neuronal enhancers and that the promoter-proximal region is necessary for this promoter responsiveness. Core promoters alone are insufficient to respond to distal enhancers but modulate the transcriptional output of responsive promoters. Our results suggest that within multipartite regulatory domains, the promoter-proximal region fulfills a facilitator-like function that filters and transmits signal from distal enhancers, ultimately conferring promoter responsiveness to long-range regulatory elements.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses identify novel biomarkers of bladder outlet obstruction
papers.abstract: Bladder outlet obstruction leads to pathological remodeling and emergence of lower urinary tract symptoms. Although relief of obstruction is associated with symptomatic improvement, it is not universally successful, reflecting persistent alterations in the bladder. Reliable surrogate biomarkers of obstruction are lacking, particularly early in the disease course before irreversible damage to the bladder may have occurred. In this study, re-analysis of publicly available transcriptomic datasets from diverse rodent models of obstruction identified tissue transcripts including Cthrc1, Grem1, Ltbp2, Acta1 and Msn that were induced in response to injury. Candidate markers were validated experimentally in an independent model of neurogenic obstruction demonstrating time-dependent changes, and a subset (GREM1, LTBP2, ACTA1, MSN) was increased in bladder tissue from pediatric patients with neurogenic bladder. Several candidates including CTHRC1, ACTA1 and MSN were also differentially abundant in independent proteomic datasets from a rat model of partial bladder outlet obstruction. Candidate markers were also attenuated in datasets from rats with either surgical removal of obstruction or treatment with anticholinergic medication or inosine. Integrated analysis of tissue transcriptomics data and tissue and urine proteomics data from a model of neurogenic obstruction revealed modest but statistically significant concordance between markers observed in tissue and urine. These findings identify tissue and urine biomarkers of both non-neurogenic and neurogenic obstruction that may reflect early changes in obstructive uropathy that could be monitored in a non-invasive manner.

A national baseline for methane sink habitats and methanotroph diversity
papers.abstract: Methane emissions account for nearly a third of the Earth’s effective radiative forcing, with methanotrophs playing a critical role in mitigating emissions by oxidising methane in diverse environments. Despite their ecological importance, methanotrophic diversity and environmental distribution remain incompletely characterised due to cultivation challenges, incomplete or low-quality metagenome-assembled genomes, and limited taxonomic resolution in marker gene surveys. Here, we present a national study of the biogeography of novel and known methanotrophs across Denmark’s major natural, urban and agricultural habitats, using genome-resolved classification of 10,683 metagenomes and 102 new methanotrophic species. By linking metabolic potential to habitat-specific distributions, we reveal uncharacterised methanotrophs as dominant in natural ecosystems. These findings provide a comprehensive baseline of methanotroph diversity, reveal clear contrasts between natural and disturbed habitats, and highlight candidate species and habitats for future methane-mitigation strategies. In this study, the authors use metagenomics to map the diverse and previously unknown bacteria responsible for taking up methane across Denmark’s varied environments and highlight the natural habitats and methanotroph species with the potential for methane mitigation.

papers.title: Global environmental genomics reveals vast uncultivated protist diversity and taxonomic blind spots
papers.abstract: Protists, defined as eukaryotes distinct from plants, animals and fungi, comprise much of eukaryotic phylogenetic diversity and perform key ecological functions, yet most lineages remain uncultivated and poorly represented in reference databases. Amplicon-based 18S rRNA gene surveys have transformed protist ecology, but primer bias, PCR bias and marker length can limit recovery of divergent lineages. Here, we conduct a cultivation-independent, rDNA operon-centered survey of over 30,000 assembled metagenomes, protist single-cell genomes and 21 long-amplicon datasets spanning marine, freshwater and soil-associated environments. We recover 157,956 long 18S rRNA gene sequences (≥800 bp), which together with reference sequences cluster into 103,338 OTUs at 97% identity and 24,438 OTUs at 85% identity. After excluding non-protist groups and singletons, 81% of the remaining 9543 protist 85%-OTUs consist exclusively of environmental sequences with no described representative. A concatenated 18S-28S rRNA framework reveals strong underrepresentation of Amoebozoa, Discoba, and Rhizaria in current references and identifies 13 candidate deeply divergent lineages with little or no database representation, some of which we link to partial genomes recovered by single-cell genomics. We further characterize their ecosystem distributions and predict associations with bacteria and other eukaryotes. This study provides a global, cultivation-independent resource for targeted sampling and downstream genomic, ecological and experimental characterization. In this study, the authors analyze over 30,000 assembled metagenomes across ecosystems to uncover hidden protist diversity, including major novel uncultivated lineages, and reveal their habitats and connections to other microbes.

papers.title: The representational geometry of cognitive maps under cognitive control
papers.abstract: Recent work has shown that the brain abstracts non-spatial relationships between entities or task states into representations called cognitive maps. Here, we investigate how cognitive control enables flexible top-down selection of goal-relevant information from multidimensional cognitive maps retrieved from memory. We examine the relationship between cognitive control and representational geometry by conducting parallel analyses of functional magnetic resonance imaging data and recurrent neural network models trained to perform the same task. We find both stable map-like representations in a medial temporal lobe and orbitofrontal cortical network that reflect both task-relevant and irrelevant dimensions and context-dependent, orthogonal representations of only task-relevant dimensions in a frontoparietal network. These representational motifs also emerge with distinct temporal profiles over the course of training in the recurrent neural network, with map-like representations appearing first. We further show that increasing control demands due to incongruence (conflicting responses) between current task-relevant and irrelevant dimensions impact the geometry of subjective representations, and the degree of this effect further accounts for individual differences in cognitive control. Taken together, our findings show how complementary representational geometries balance stability and behavioral flexibility, and reveal an intricate relationship between cognitive control and cognitive map geometry. The brain organizes relationships between entities into cognitive maps. Here, the authors show that complementary stable and context-dependent representational geometries balance stability and behavioral flexibility, with their geometry shaped by cognitive control.

papers.title: Conserved molecular properties of dissolved organic matter during Weddell Sea Deep Water formation
papers.abstract: Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW) is decreasing in volume due to climate change with potential consequences for abyssal carbon storage, where carbon is locked away from the atmosphere for centuries. Understanding the formation and export of dissolved organic matter (DOM) on the Antarctic shelf is therefore essential to determine how organic carbon enters this deep-sea reservoir. Here, we investigate solid-phase extractable DOM (SPE-DOM) transformations in the Weddell Sea, where half of AABW forms. Molecular and structural properties of SPE-DOM remain unchanged during dense-water formation. Shelf processes minimally affect exported organics into the deep-sea, likely due to remineralization to inorganic carbon enhanced by long residence times on the shelf. Consequently, the dominant SPE-DOM signature in Weddell Sea Deep Water (WSDW) is established before dense shelf waters mix with warmer off-shelf waters. We estimate that 0.155 ± 0.03 PgC are transferred annually from the Weddell Sea to AABW, and that its molecular composition is expected to remain conserved despite ongoing climate-driven weakening of AABW. The study reveals that molecular properties of dissolved organic matter are conserved during dense-water formation in the Weddell Sea, showing that Antarctic shelf processes minimally affect the dissolved organics exported into the deep ocean.

papers.title: Prospective and genetic analyses implicate lower immunosurveillance in the aetiology of prostate cancer
papers.abstract: Tumour-promoting inflammation and immune evasion are key features of cancer, but prospective evidence linking specific immune pathways to prostate cancer risk remains limited. Here we show that circulating proteins involved in immune regulation may influence prostate cancer development. We analyse 368 immune- and inflammation-related proteins measured in blood samples from men in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC), including 1434 cases and matched controls, and combine these results with data from UK Biobank. While no proteins are associated with risk in EPIC alone after multiple testing correction, meta-analysis identifies several proteins linked to prostate cancer risk, including IL15 and FLT3LG, in particular, in blood taken long before diagnosis. Higher levels of immune surveillance-related proteins, particularly those involved in natural killer and T cell activity, are associated with lower prostate cancer risk, whereas genetic evidence implicates PARP1, SPINT2 and NME3 in increased risk. These findings suggest that immune pathways play a role in prostate cancer development and highlight potential targets for prevention. Role of specific immune and inflammation-related pathways and protein markers in the development of prostate cancer remains to be elucidated. Here the authors show evidence for potential protective role of dendritic cell mediated immunosurveillance, with protective associations with immune and inflammation related proteins measured more than seven years before diagnosis.

papers.title: Temporal dynamics of premenstrual dysphoric disorder revealed through predictive symptom networks
papers.abstract: Temporal dynamics of psychiatric symptoms challenge researchers and clinicians due to their inherent unpredictability. The cyclical on–off nature of symptoms linked to physiological rhythms, such as the menstrual cycle, provides a unique window to apply temporal and dynamic modeling of psychiatric symptoms. This can be studied in premenstrual dysphoric disorder, a female hormone-triggered condition characterized by cyclical symptoms. Yet intra-individual temporal patterns and dynamics of these symptoms remain unknown. Here we show that individuals with premenstrual dysphoric disorder differ widely in symptom timing, severity, and persistence, clustering into distinct temporal symptom profiles. Dynamic modelling uncovers temporal order among core psychiatric symptoms, with anxiety emerging as a central symptom in the unfolding of affective dysregulation. Depression shows the strongest predictive associations with subsequent severity of the other core symptoms, while irritability predicts the severity of depression at the longest time-interval. These temporal symptom dynamics reveal mechanistic psychoneuroendocrine pathways and inform precision, time-sensitive interventions for the mental health of individuals with premenstrual dysphoric disorder. Premenstrual dysphoric disorder causes cyclical mental symptoms, but how these symptoms unfold over time is not yet understood. This study reveals temporal patterns and identifies anxiety as a promising treatment target.

papers.title: A lactate-fatty acid loop drives prostate cancer bone colonization by mediating metabolic interplay between tumor cells and osteoblasts
papers.abstract: Bone metastasis is the major cause of morbidity and mortality in advanced prostate cancer, yet current therapies provide only limited clinical benefit. Here, we show that prostate cancer cells metabolically adapt to the bone microenvironment by utilizing bone-cell-derived lactate as an alternative nutrient source. Beyond fueling oxidative phosphorylation, lactate serves as carbon source for fatty acid synthesis. Among the resulting lipid products, oleic acid is secreted to reward osteoblast, establishing a reciprocal metabolic interplay that supports both tumor progression and pathological bone formation. Mechanistically, we identify MCT1 as the essential transporter mediating lactate uptake in bone-colonizing tumor cells. MCT1 expression is coordinately regulated by NFAT signaling and extracellular glucose availability at both transcriptional and post-translational levels. Genetic deletion and pharmacological inhibition of MCT1 markedly suppresses prostate tumor growth in bone. Together, these findings uncover a lactate-driven metabolic crosstalk, identifying MCT1 as a promising therapeutic target for prostate cancer bone metastasis. Bone metastases in advanced prostate cancer remain difficult to treat and are associated with poor outcomes. Here, the authors show that bone-colonizing prostate tumor cells exploit lactate uptake via MCT1 to fuel tumor growth and promote osteogenesis, identifying MCT1 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Toward personalized deep brain stimulation via white matter stimulation and microstructure in depression
papers.abstract: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) affects a substantial proportion of individuals with major depressive disorder, posing a significant clinical and societal burden. Among emerging interventions, tractography-guided Subcallosal Cingulate Deep Brain Stimulation (SCC-DBS) shows promise as a treatment for TRD. However, despite the use of connectome-based targeting methods, clinical outcomes remain variable across individuals. Here, we examined individual white matter (WM) properties underlying the variability of SCC-DBS response for depression by analyzing a patient-specific diffusion MRI dataset of SCC-DBS patients (n = 51), incorporating individualized stimulation modeling and weekly clinical assessments over the first 24 weeks of DBS. We evaluated two distinct WM measures: the volumetric proportion of stimulated WM tracts (STP: stimulated-tract proportion) and the microstructural integrity of these tracts estimated by fractional anisotropy (FA). The STP in the bilateral mid-cingulum bundles and forceps minor reaching the left ventral frontal pole was positively associated with clinical improvement. Although FA alone did not show association with clinical improvement, it moderated the relationship between STP and clinical improvement, suggesting differential contributions of the two pathways in mediating antidepressant effects of SCC-DBS. These findings underscore that future refinements in stimulation delivery may be guided by greater attention to patient-specific WM metrics within the targeted network. A study of 51 patients receiving deep brain stimulation for treatment-resistant depression shows that individual white matter stimulation and integrity jointly influence antidepressant response, supporting more personalized neuromodulation strategies.

Blood-based RNA biomarker for the early detection of ovarian cancer
papers.abstract: Flower-Win/Lose signaling underlies a tumor–host fitness conflict in ovarian cancer, in which tumor-derived exosomal Tu-stroma reduces the fitness of surrounding host cells, favoring tumor expansion within host tissues. High-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC), the most prevalent histotype of epithelial ovarian cancer and leading cause of ovarian-cancer-related mortality, arises from serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC), a noninvasive precursor typically identifiable only by histopathologic examination of excised fallopian tube tissue. Here we evaluated Tu-stroma, a tumor-associated long noncoding RNA enriched in serum extracellular vesicles (EVs), as a circulating biomarker in STIC and early-stage HGSC, representing the earliest histopathologically defined phases of disease. Tu-stroma was quantified in serum EVs from 506 individuals with histologically normal adnexa, benign-adnexal lesions, isolated STIC and HGSC across International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stages I–IV. Normalized EV Tu-stroma ΔCT values were elevated in STIC (n = 43) and HGSC (n = 232) versus controls (n = 143) and benign-adnexal lesions (n = 88), including premenopausal women (controls = 57, benign = 34, STIC = 32, HGSC = 88). In paired receiver operating characteristic analyses, Tu-stroma showed higher discrimination than cancer antigen 125 (CA125) for STIC versus controls (area under the curve (AUC) = 0.99 versus 0.59, P < 0.001) and benign-adnexal masses (0.99 versus 0.31, P < 0.001), and for HGSC versus controls (AUC = 0.99 versus 0.96, P = 0.001) and benign-adnexal masses (0.98 versus 0.84, P < 0.001). Tu-stroma showed no systematic elevation across inflammatory or physiologic comparators (n = 116) or nonovarian malignancies (n = 160), each assessed against healthy controls (n = 100), supporting disease-context specificity. Modeled risk-enriched contexts yielded predictive values compatible with intended-use populations. These findings identify Tu-stroma as a candidate EV-RNA marker associated with pre-invasive and early HGSC biology. Prospective evaluation in consecutively enrolled real-world cohorts is required to validate diagnostic performance, predictive value and clinical utility. Tested in a cohort of 506 individuals, the RNA-based biomarker of microenvironment fitness Tu-stroma shows high performance in discriminating early-stage ovarian cancer from benign lesions, outperforming CA125.

papers.title: A novel candidate biomarker for detecting premalignant and early ovarian cancer
In situ profiling of plasma cell clonality with image-based single-cell transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Image-based single-cell transcriptomics can identify diverse cell types in intact tissues. However, in adaptive immunity, V(D)J recombination generates unique immune receptors in cells of the same type, leading to important functional variation that is not yet defined by these methods. Here we introduce B cell receptor multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (BCR-MERFISH), which measures plasma cell clonality based on V gene usage in combination with transcriptome profiling. We demonstrate that BCR-MERFISH accurately identifies V gene usage in cell culture and in mice with restricted or native plasma cell diversity. We then use BCR-MERFISH to elucidate the microbiota-dependent changes in plasma cell abundance, clonal diversity, and public clonotype usage in the mouse gut and the non-uniform distribution of plasma cell clones along the mouse ileum. Given that tissue context is an essential modulator of plasma cell dynamics, we anticipate that BCR-MERFISH may offer new insights into a wide range of immunological questions. BCR-MERFISH enables tracking of plasma cell clones by combining V gene-specific detection with spatial transcriptomics.

papers.title: Efficient count-based models improve power and robustness for large-scale single-cell eQTL mapping
papers.abstract: Population-scale single-cell RNA sequencing enables mapping genetic effects on gene regulation at the cellular level (for example, single-cell expression quantitative trait loci (sc-eQTLs)). However, existing sc-eQTL mapping approaches are either not designed for analyzing sparse counts in single-cell RNA sequencing data or become computationally intractable at scale. Here we developed jaxQTL—an efficient pseudobulk sc-eQTL mapping framework using highly efficient count-based models. In simulations, we demonstrated that jaxQTL with a negative binomial model provides calibrated inference while outperforming linear models. In OneK1K data, jaxQTL identified 16% more eGenes than linear models, while running substantially faster than single-cell Poisson mixed effect models. We found that fine-mapped sc-eQTLs are more distal from transcription starting site than those identified in all cells (bulk-eQTLs; P = 1 × 10−4) and more enriched in cell-type-specific enhancers (P = 3 × 10−10), revealing distal regulatory effects that are missed in bulk tissues. Although sc-eQTLs are largely shared across cell types, cell-type-specificity increases with distance to transcription starting site. Finally, sc-eQTLs explain a greater proportion of single nucleotide polymorphism-heritability than bulk-eQTLs across 16 blood and immune-related traits (9.90 ± 0.88% versus 6.10 ± 0.76%) and prioritize disease-associated genes missed by the bulk approach (such as IL6ST), improving, but not closing, the missing link between genome-wide association studies and eQTLs. This study presents jaxQTL, an efficient count-based pseudobulk single-cell eQTL mapping framework. When applied to OneK1K data, jaxQTL discovers more eGenes than existing methods while running faster.

papers.title: Theoretical considerations regarding an acidic nanolayer surrounding lysosomes
A conserved urate oxidase helix-tiling assembly promotes metabolic robustness in peroxisomes
papers.abstract: Cells organize metabolism within a crowded intracellular milieu, yet the structural logic and functional consequences of supramolecular enzyme assemblies in vivo remain poorly defined. Here, using in situ cryo-electron tomography, we identify a previously uncharacterized high-order architecture of urate oxidase in mouse liver. Urate oxidase homotetramers assemble into helical fibers that tile laterally to form a stable, porous lamellar scaffold. This organization preserves extensive accessible surface area while permitting efficient substrate and product exchange. Structure-guided perturbation abolishes the assembly in vivo without measurably altering intrinsic catalytic activity, indicating a primary role in spatial organization rather than allosteric regulation. Consistent with this, the assembled state enhances resistance to thermal, proteolytic and oxidative stress, supporting sustained activity in the peroxide-rich peroxisomal matrix. Conserved across mammals, this architecture reveals a strategy for metabolic compartmentalization that couples efficient catalysis to increased molecular robustness without the trade-off between supramolecular assembly and enzyme accessibility. Enzyme organization inside cells remains poorly understood. Here, the authors use cryo-electron tomography to show that urate oxidase forms conserved helix-tiling assemblies in liver peroxisomes, stabilizing the enzyme while preserving efficient catalysis.

papers.title: Natural killer cell inflammatory circuits in antitumor immunity
papers.abstract: Emerging evidence positions natural killer (NK) cells as key initiators of the inflammatory programs required for effective tumor immunity. Beyond direct tumor killing, NK cells trigger early immune responses by recruiting and activating dendritic cells (DCs), thereby enabling downstream T cell activation. However, in established tumors, NK cell–DC communication is often disrupted by metabolic stress and immunosuppressive pathways, leading to immune evasion. Here, we review advances in NK cell–DC cross-talk, cytokine-driven amplification loops and metabolic control of NK cell fitness. We propose that restoring these integrated immune ‘circuits’ may be key in converting immune-excluded tumors into immunotherapy-responsive states. Huntington et al. provide an overview of the biology and role of natural killer (NK) cells in cancer, highlighting the importance of NK cell–dendritic cell cross-talk and NK cell metabolic fitness in regulating the antitumor immune response.

papers.title: Programming golden triple helices
Host specific sphingomyelin is critical for replication of diverse RNA viruses
Activated TILs are restricted by iron availability in pancreatic cancer
The nucleocytoplasmic actin circuit in genome maintenance
Interconnected reservoirs of multidrug-resistant bacteria and plasmids within hospital plumbing infrastructure
papers.abstract: Hospital sinks and wastewater streams are hotspots for contamination and colonization with multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria (MDR-GNB). While hospital water systems may facilitate MDR-GNB transmission during outbreaks, longitudinal population dynamics of environmental MDR-GNB and their long-term relationship with patient isolates remain unclear. Here we aimed to characterize the diversity and abundance of MDR-GNB within the hospital built environment and evaluate their relationship with clinical isolates. We performed nanopore sequencing on MDR-GNB cultured from sink drains (n=523) and wastewater (n=146) at a New York City hospital between March-August 2023. We assessed spatial and longitudinal genomic strain and plasmid dynamics and quantified relatedness to historical clinical isolates from the same hospital (n=602). Sink drains (54-73%) and wastewater (100%) demonstrated widespread, longitudinal colonization with MDR-GNB, driven primarily by carbapenem-resistant GNB including opportunistic organisms and Enterobacterales encoding blaKPC. While bacterial colonization differed across environmental niches, we identified both MDR-GNB strains and resistance plasmids that were shared between clinical and environmental sources, as well a distinct interplay between clinical and wastewater versus sink drain samples. This study supports the role of hospital plumbing as an important reservoir for clinically relevant MDR-GNB, but highlights differences across environmental sources, which may impact surveillance approaches.

papers.title: Molecular Modulation of the SAM-I Riboswitch Drives Global Dynamical Shifts
papers.abstract: A surge in antimicrobial resistance in recent years has made protein-targeting antibiotics less effective against key pathogens. It is possible to expand the range of therapeutic targets by using RNA-based therapies, but it remains necessary to improve the molecular-level understanding of interactions between RNA and known and potential binders. The SAM-I riboswitch, which controls the transcriptional termination of gene expression involved in sulfur metabolism in most bacteria, is an excellent ligand target. Thus, understanding its behavior with and without ligand complexes would be helpful for drug design. Here, we studied the interactions between the SAM-I riboswitch and its natural ligand, SAM, which controls riboswitch function, and compared those to its interactions with the similar small molecule SAH, which does not control riboswitch function, and to its interactions with a potential binder JS4, identified via virtual screening. From our simulations, we deepen understanding of small molecule interactions with the SAM-I riboswitch on both a local and a distal level. The results reveal how differently ligands (SAM, SAH and JS4) can bind to and potentially induce conformational changes in the riboswitch. Our findings offer valuable insight into the molecular mechanisms underlying riboswitch RNA-ligand interactions for the design of more effective RNA-targeting therapeutics.

papers.title: Implicit Hierarchical Tensor Decomposition of Single-Cell Four-Omics Data Reveals Cell-Type-Linked Candidate Enhancer--Promoter-Associated Programs
papers.abstract: Single-cell multi-omics provides complementary views of gene regulation, but integrating modalities with natural features comprising enhancers, genes, and three-dimensional (3D) genomic loci remains challenging. This study developed an implicit hierarchical tensor decomposition framework and applied it to the CHARM single-cell four-omics mouse brain data (GSE303006) by jointly analyzing ATAC, H3K27ac, RNA, and reconstructed 3D enhancer--promoter (E--P) distances. After quality control, 730,969 E--P pairs, 42,669 enhancers, 16,239 genes, 391,435 20-kb bin pairs, and 4,258 cells were retained. Each modality was independently reduced to 20 components and mapped to an implicit 730,969x4{,}258x20x4 tensor, which was decomposed without materializing the full array. In a joint model, cell type explained more variance than biological replicate for all 12 distinct cell components represented among the 100 largest Tucker core elements. A representative core linked the Inh_Ndnf/Lamp5--Ex_L3/4_IT cell axis to contrasting presynaptic-transmission and developmental/morphogenetic candidate E--P-associated programs. Its E--P and cell factors were recovered when the whole analysis was repeated independently on each pair of replicates, and the E--P pairs it prioritized agreed in direction with the cell-type-resolved enhancer--gene links of the original CHARM study. No single modality reproduced the program, which required the combination of accessibility, chromatin contact, and expression. Backprojection showed reproducible ATAC, H3K27ac, and 3D effects across three biological replicates; RNA differed clearly for the developmental module but not for the presynaptic module. The framework thus identifies regulatory structure that is shared across molecular modalities and is not recoverable from any single modality.

papers.title: Simple models outperform single-cell foundation models on downstream benchmarks
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data exhibit strong and reproducible statistical structure. This has motivated the development of large-scale foundation models, such as TranscriptFormer, that use transformer-based architectures to learn a generative model for gene expression by embedding genes into a latent vector space. These embeddings have been used to obtain state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on downstream tasks such as cell-type classification, disease-state prediction, and cross-species learning. Here, we ask whether similar performance can be achieved without utilizing computationally intensive deep learning-based representations. Using simple, interpretable pipelines that rely on careful normalization and linear methods, we obtain SOTA or near SOTA performance across multiple benchmarks commonly used to evaluate single-cell foundation models, including outperforming foundation models on out-of-distribution tasks involving novel cell types and organisms absent from the training data. Our findings highlight the need for rigorous benchmarking and suggest that the biology of cell identity can be captured by simple linear representations of single cell gene expression data.
affiliations: Boston University (corresponding author)

papers.title: A Proteome-Wide Gain-of-Function Atlas Mapping the Landscape of Chemotherapy Response
papers.abstract: Background: Conventional chemotherapies remain the core therapeutic backbone of cancer treatment, yet the rapid emergence of chemoresistance often compromises their clinical efficacy. Although large-scale functional genomics has transformed precision oncology, existing reference maps rely predominantly on loss-of-function paradigms and lack systematic data on gain-of-function (GOF) events that commonly drive clinical resistance. Methods: To address this gap, we engineered a site-specific Bxb1 integrase landing-pad system in HeLa cells, enabling single-copy integration of a human proteome-wide library [18,388 open reading frames (ORFs)] at the AAVS1 locus under a uniform EF1 promoter. We systematically profiled cellular fitness across 16 chemotherapeutics. We integrated this GOF perturbation screen with bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, FACS-based lysosomal functional screening, clinical cohort survival analyses, and preclinical xenograft modeling. Results: Stratified modeling of over 230,000 gene-drug interactions defined distinct functional categories that are strongly enriched for clinical cancer biomarkers and prognostic relevance. Global network analysis and organelle-specific lysosomal functional screening uncovered that chemotherapeutic agents, most prominently the nucleoside analog TAS-102 (Lonsurf), converge upon a shared survival hub centered on the BCL-2 family-associated autophagy-endolysosomal network. Mechanistically, TAS-102 triggered lysosomal activation as an adaptive survival response. Co-treatment with the BCL-2 family inhibitor ABT-263 (Navitoclax) attenuated this TAS-102-induced lysosomal response and synergistically reversed TAS-102 resistance across colorectal and pancreatic cancer models in vitro and in colorectal cell line- and patient-derived xenograft (CDX, PDX) models in vivo. Conclusions: Our study establishes an open-access, proteome-wide GOF reference atlas that systematically maps chemotherapeutic responses, recapitulates canonical resistance biology, and nominates rational drug combinations. This systems-genomics resource bridges massive-scale perturbation mapping with actionable target discovery, providing a translational framework to overcome therapeutic resistance and reprogram cancer drug responses.

papers.title: BenchRep-T: A Systematic Evaluation of T-Cell Repertoire-Based Disease Diagnostics
papers.abstract: Adaptive immune receptor repertoire sequencing data has emerged as a promising potential modality for disease diagnosis, relying on computational methods to analyze T-cell receptor (TCR) sequences from an individual's blood sample. Published methods rely on different cohorts, data preprocessing pipelines, and evaluation metrics, making direct comparison across methods challenging. We present BenchRep-T, a unified benchmark that standardizes multiple publicly available TCR repertoire datasets and evaluates nine computational approaches, spanning statistical enrichment of shared sequences, feature-engineered ensembles, deep learning, and sequence clustering. BenchRep-T evaluates methods on four tasks: disease classification across conditions, performance scaling under restricted sequence-sampling depth, recovery of known antigen-specific driver sequences, and evaluation of sensitivity to demographic confounding. Under controlled evaluation, simple baselines prove competitive, with tree-based models trained on V- and J-gene usage and short sequence motifs approaching the classification performance of more complex methods. Our findings underscore the complexity of modeling TCR repertoire data, and show that no single method dominates across all tasks. BenchRep-T provides a framework for rigorous and reproducible evaluation of TCR repertoire classification methods to accelerate the development of immune repertoire-based diagnostics.
affiliations: Stanford University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Systemic TLR7 agonism moderates disease severity in acute DSS-induced colitis in mice
papers.abstract: Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7) is an endosomal sensor of single-stranded RNA, studied for its antiviral and pro-inflammatory functions. Its role in intestinal inflammation is undefined, and no approved or clinical-stage therapy for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) engages this pathway. Here we report that systemic administration of the reference TLR7 agonist GS-9620 (vesatolimod) moderates disease severity in acute dextran sodium sulfate (DSS)-induced colitis in mice. GS-9620-treated mice lost less weight, had lower Disease Activity Index scores, and were protected from DSS-induced colon shortening. Immunophenotyping of the spleen showed reduced Th17 and Tr17 populations and an increased proportion of regulatory T cells. These findings indicate that pharmacological TLR7 agonism is not merely tolerated in the inflamed intestine but is associated with a shift of the systemic immune compartment toward a regulatory phenotype. The results identify TLR7 as a candidate disease-moderating target in IBD and motivate direct tests of causality, route and chronic-disease relevance.
affiliations: Mass General Brigham (corresponding author)

papers.title: Metagenomic Insights into the Fecal Microbiome, Resistome, and Mobilome of Beef Cattle in Cow-Calf Operations in Florida, United States
papers.abstract: Food-producing animals are a focus of One Health approaches to antimicrobial resistance (AMR) as reservoirs of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria (ARB) and antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). We hypothesized that microbial composition, ARGs profiles, and mobile genetic element (MGE) profiles would differ by operation size and animal age group. Fecal samples from 162 cows and calves were combined into 54 composite samples, each comprising three animals of the same age group. Across operation sizes, Bacillota (51.4-64.9%), Bacteroidota (12.0-17.3%), Pseudomonadota (10.3-16.5%), and Actinomycetota (3.3-10.9%) were predominant phyla. Alpha diversity did not differ among operation sizes; however, cows exhibited greater observed richness, Shannon diversity, and Simpson diversity than calves (all P < 0.001). Microbial composition did not differ significantly among operation sizes (PERMANOVA, R{superscript 2} = 0.065, P = 0.609) but differed significantly between cows and calves (R{superscript 2} = 0.200, P < 0.001). Seventy-five ARGs representing 14 resistance classes were identified. Normalized ARG hit rates were higher in small operations (0.444) than in medium (0.278) and large operations (0.222; P = 0.088), whereas calves exhibited a higher estimated marginal mean normalized ARG hit rate than cows (0.383 vs. 0.247 hits/million reads; P < 0.001). Of 1,054 curated ARG hits, 23.9% occurred on predicted plasmid contigs, 0.9% on predicted viral contigs, and 7.1% on contigs containing insertion sequences. Overall findings demonstrate differences in fecal microbiome diversity and ARG abundance between cows and calves and indicate that predicted plasmids are associated with a notable proportion of ARG hits in Florida beef cow-calf operations.
affiliations: University of Florida (corresponding author)

papers.title: Structural basis of virion assembly in the Mycobacterium tuberculosis-infecting mycobacteriophage SWU1
papers.abstract: The rising threat of drug-resistant tuberculosis has renewed interest in bacteriophage therapy as an urgently needed alternative. Rational engineering of these viruses, however, requires an atomic-level understanding of virion architecture. Mycobacteriophage SWU1 belongs to subcluster A2, one of the few mycobacteriophage lineages known to infect Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M. tuberculosis). Using single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM), we resolved essentially the entire SWU1 virion architecture by localized reconstruction of four modules, the capsid, portal vertex, tail and baseplate, at resolutions of 3.62 [A], 3.51 [A], 3.70 [A] and 3.22 [A], respectively. The T=7 capsid comprises 415 copies of an HK97-fold major capsid protein and lacks any decoration protein in density. The 12-fold portal reconciles its C5-C12 mismatch with the capsid vertex through defined, non-equivalent subunit contacts. The baseplate carries a 13-fold tail-fiber ring on a 6-fold hub, a geometry without precedent among characterized phages, established here by symmetry-free reconstruction. These findings provide the critical insights into the assembly and infection of SWU1, laying a structural foundation for the future optimization of phage-based anti-TB therapeutics.
