papers.title: Residual barcode-like sequences and barcode-associated artifacts after Dorado and Barbell preprocessing of metagenomic reads
papers.abstract: Background Residual barcode-like sequences after preprocessing are a quality-control concern in multiplexed Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) sequencing data, particularly in low-biomass, host-dominated samples such as blood. Using blood datasets spiked with a microbial mock community and prepared with the Native Barcoding Kit 96 V14 (SQK-NBD114.96), we compared Dorado 1.1.1, Dorado 2.0.0, and Barbell 0.3.2. Results Dorado demultiplexing reduced barcode-positive reads to approximately 2% of reads, with internal barcode-like matches in 0.17-0.19% of reads. Barbell 0.3.2 applied to untrimmed Dorado basecalls yielded an approximately 50-fold lower detector-defined internal-match rate (0.0035-0.0037%) while retaining 91.2-91.8% of input reads. In the NCBI core_nt release of 12 September 2026, the focused screen identified complete, ungapped 24 nt identity for 64 of the 96 barcodes (66.7%), comprising 505 distinct barcode-accession pairs across 482 accessions and 195 exported TaxID groups of mixed taxonomic ranks. Records annotated as rRNA genes, chromosomes/genomes, and plasmids accounted for 35.6%, 23.2%, and 22.4% of the pairs, respectively. The barcode was located within its native ligation flanks in 224 pairs (44.4%), including 170 (33.7%) with the complete Dorado barcode search window and 3 (0.6%) with the full adapter construct. Conclusion Barbell combined 91-92% read retention with lower detected internal barcode signals. After demultiplexing, barcode-like sequences remained in sample data. Moreover, kit barcode sequences, often within their native ligation flanks, were detected in reference records. Both findings call for careful preprocessing, reference inspection, and downstream validation. Further research should determine whether barcode-associated artifacts in reads and reference records affect taxonomic classification in clinical metagenomic workflows.

papers.title: siRNA/mRNA payload of lipid nanoparticles quantified using fluorescence microscopy and correlation spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have emerged as the most promising vectors to deliver nucleic acids to mammalian cells. Advanced delivery strategies involving multiple nucleic acid species require a reliable determination of RNA payload and LNP size. Here, we use total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy and fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS) to determine mRNA payload and siRNA/mRNA codelivered payload. Particularly, FCS proves to be a reliable method for payload determination, independently of fluorophore properties that can be altered during encapsulation. By varying the PEG-lipid fraction relative to the reference ONPATTRO formulation, we find that mRNA payload of enhanced green fluorescent protein (eGFP) coding mRNA increases from [~]10 with LNP size according to a power law with an exponent 1.3. Cryogenic electron microscopy (Cryo-EM) reveals that in this case blebs occur more frequently in small LNPs. For siRNA/mRNA coencapsulation the siRNA fraction within LNPs exceeds that in the initial RNA mixture, suggesting that coencapsulation is competitive and constrained by nucleic acid diffusion. Together, our findings highlight the importance of particle size and encapsulation kinetics in controlling the loading and composition of RNA payloads in LNPs.

papers.title: Maximum Likelihood Localization Maps
papers.abstract: Single-molecule localization microscopy commonly reconstructs images from estimated emitter coordinates. We calculate maximum-likelihood localization maps (MLLM), a non-iterative approach that evaluates positional likelihood from measured data and a supplied point-spread function. The MLLM of each detected single molecule image is added into a final upsampled image representing the overall molecular probability map, preserving the positional likelihood structure and obviating separate coordinate-based rendering. MLLM calculation is noniterative, fast, supports any calibrated point-spread function, accounts for local background variation, supports two- and three-dimensional reconstruction, and can be calculated in parallel.

papers.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals Tumorigenic Lineages and Interactions Persisting and Evolving From Premalignancy to Cancer in the Stomach
papers.abstract: Background & Aims Gastric cancer is often diagnosed at advanced stages, making the premalignant window critical for early detection. However, the epithelial changes that characterize this stage remain poorly defined. We used CTLA4-knockdown (CTLA4KD) mice, which model human CTLA4 insufficiency-associated gastric cancer, that develops autoimmune gastritis, metaplasia, and adenocarcinoma, to define molecular changes across disease progression. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing and 40-color spectral flow cytometry were performed on gastric tissue across premalignant and cancer stages. We evaluated epithelial lineage relationships, cell-cell communication pathways, and candidate markers at the transcript and protein levels in murine and human gastric adenocarcinoma. Results We identified a metaplastic/tumorigenic population in CTLA4KD mice that emerged in premalignancy with a chief cell transcriptomic origin. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed a progressive increase in fibronectin (FN1) signaling from premalignancy through cancer, transitioning from stromal to autocrine signaling in the metaplastic/tumorigenic population. Expression of Embigin (EMB), a fibronectin receptor, increased at both transcript and protein levels in premalignancy and remained elevated in cancer. EMB epithelial cells co-expressed CD133, a cancer stem cell marker, consistent with a stem-like phenotype. EMB expression was also higher in human gastric adenocarcinoma than in matched normal tissue. Conclusions Using a model that captures the full histopathological cascade of gastric tumorigenesis, we delineate single-cell transcriptional programs that persist and evolve from premalignancy to adenocarcinoma. In-depth computational analyses identified novel markers involved in cell-cell communication during tumorigenesis, including EMB, an epithelial marker that persists from premalignancy through cancer in the murine model and validated in human gastric adenocarcinoma, suggesting EMB as a marker of premalignant progression.

papers.title: Mutant Isocitrate Dehydrogenase 1 Alters Extracellular Vesicle Secretion and Cargo Composition in Cellular Models
papers.abstract: Somatic mutations in isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1) define major subtypes of adult diffuse gliomas and occur across a broad spectrum of cancers. These mutations ablate the conventional turnover of isocitrate to alpha-ketoglutarate and confer the neomorphic production of D-2-hydroxyglutarate (D2HG), which drives epigenetic remodeling. Growing evidence suggests this neomorphic activity may also affect how tumor cells communicate; small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) are elevated in gliomas, though how mutant IDH1 shapes sEV production and cargo remains poorly understood. Using glioblastoma and chondrosarcoma cell models, we show expression of mutant IDH1 correlates with a trend of increased sEV secretion, and that D2HG is packaged into sEVs that are taken up by cells. Cell-permeable D2HG treatment dose-dependently increased sEV release from IDH1 wild type cells. Untargeted proteomics showed that mutant IDH1 expression remodeled sEV cargo in a cell type-specific fashion, with mutant chondrosarcoma sEVs enriched in one-carbon metabolism enzymes, and mutant glioma sEVs in lysosomal luminal proteins and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) chaperones. Mutant IDH1 glioma cell transcriptomics suggested expanded ER folding capacity and reduced ribosomal pathways, and sEVs from these cells decreased nascent protein synthesis in IDH1 wild type recipient cells. Together, this suggests sEVs can serve as carriers of mutant IDH1 phenotypes.
affiliations: Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry, San Diego State University, San Diego, California, USA (corresponding author)

papers.title: Targeting REV1 Exposes Context-Dependent Therapeutic Responses in Colorectal Cancer
papers.abstract: Translesion synthesis (TLS) promotes DNA damage tolerance and contributes to chemotherapy resistance by enabling replication across damaged DNA templates. REV1, a central TLS regulator, is a potential therapeutic target to enhance the efficacy of genotoxic chemotherapy. Here, we investigated the therapeutic consequences of pharmacologic and genetic REV1 targeting in colorectal cancer (CRC) and evaluated the sensitivity of patient-derived CRC organoids to the REV1 inhibitor JH-RE-06. JH-RE-06 enhanced oxaliplatin sensitivity in HCT116 cells and 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) sensitivity in HT-29 cells, whereas reciprocal combinations produced limited sensitization, indicating treatment- and cellular context-dependent responses. siRNA-mediated REV1 depletion similarly enhanced chemotherapy sensitivity, supporting REV1 involvement in these responses. MNNG sensitivity assays and MLH1 expression analyses did not reveal consistent treatment-associated changes in mismatch repair function, while targeted HPRT1 sequencing identified no detectable sequence alterations in the region examined. Chemosensitization was not accompanied by consistent increases in caspase-3/7 activation under the conditions tested. REV1 inhibition also caused LC3-II accumulation and, after prolonged inhibitor exposure, reduced beta-tubulin abundance, indicating additional autophagy-associated and cytoskeletal responses. In two patient-derived CRC organoid models, JH-RE-06 exhibited single-agent growth-inhibitory activity, with mean IC50 values of 2.01 micromolar and 1.4 micromolar, respectively. Together, these findings demonstrate context-dependent chemosensitization and organoid growth inhibition following REV1 targeting, suggesting that its therapeutic consequences may extend beyond canonical TLS-mediated DNA damage tolerance.
affiliations: University of Vermont (corresponding author)

papers.title: TGF-b/TIF1g signaling restrains CD8+ T cell expansion while preserving cytotoxic competence
papers.abstract: Transforming growth factor b exerts complex and often opposing effects on CD8+ T cell biology, yet the molecular mechanisms that distinguish these functions remain poorly understood. Here, we identify TIF1g (TRIM33) as a critical signal threshold regulator that couples TGF b signaling to CD8+ T cell activation and cytotoxic function. In the presence of TGF b, TIF1g deficient CD8+ T cells bypass canonical suppressive signals and acquire a transcriptional program characterized by enhanced activation and proliferation. Despite this hyperactivated state, TIF1g deficient cells fail to acquire full effector function, exhibiting markedly reduced Granzyme B and Perforin expression under TGF b signaling. We confirmed this functional uncoupling in vivo using a secondary Listeria monocytogenes challenge model, in which TIF1g deficient CD8+ T cells underwent robust expansion yet failed to efficiently control bacterial infection because of impaired cytotoxic activity. In a lymphopenic homeostatic proliferation model, TIF1g deficiency disrupted cellular quiescence, leading to excessive proliferation and spontaneous effector differentiation. Consistent with these findings, loss of TIF1g accelerated B16 melanoma growth and was associated with reduced Perforin expression in tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells. Together, these findings identify TIF1g as a key regulator of TGF b mediated CD8+ T cell responses, uncoupling activation from cytotoxic differentiation and revealing a mechanism by which TGF b independently regulates proliferative and effector programs.
affiliations: Instituto de Fisiologia Celular, Universidad Nacional Autonoma de Mexico (corresponding author)

papers.title: Genomic features and instability of linezolid resistance in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecalis ST525
papers.abstract: This study investigated the mechanisms of oxazolidinone resistance and genomic background in clinical ST525 Enterococcus faecalis isolates, a poorly characterized lineage reported in Brazilian hospitals as either vancomycin-resistant (VRE) or linezolid- and vancomycin-resistant (LVRE). Five LVREfs from intensive care unit patients (linezolid MICs, 8-32 mg/L; vancomycin MICs, >256 mg/L) carried only G2576T and G2505A (in three of four rrl copies) as known linezolid resistance determinants, despite variable linezolid MICs. During serial in vitro passages without antibiotic pressure, isolates with initial MICs of 8-16 mg/L exhibited progressive MIC reductions accompanied by reversion of mutant to wild-type rrl copies, whereas the isolate with an initial MIC of 32 mg/L maintained high-level resistance without reversion. Additional domain V substitutions emerged during MIC decline, while growth kinetics remained broadly similar. Whole-genome sequencing of a representative isolate (LVREfs L7) revealed a ~2.8-Mb chromosome enriched in mobile genetic elements (~8.6%), lacking a functional CRISPR-Cas system. A plasmid-borne prototype Tn1546 carrying vanA, devoid of internal insertion sequences, was found inserted into a Tn3-family transposase gene, a platform not typically associated with vanA mobilization. Together, these findings indicate that ST525 LVREfs, whose genomic features are consistent with long-term persistence in hospitals, may pose a challenge to routine susceptibility testing. A single mutational mechanism can yield variable linezolid MICs, and the ratio of mutated vs wild-type rrl copies can become heterogeneous in the absence of antibiotic pressure, without correlating directly with these values, contrary to the well-documented copy number-MIC correlation.

papers.title: Transition Fibers Play a Central Role in Import of a Glucose Transporter into the Flagellar Membrane
papers.abstract: Leishmania parasite promastigotes have a motile flagellum that encompasses a variety of integral membrane proteins, but how such proteins traffic selectively to the flagellum is largely unknown. The flagellar-specific glucose transporter, GT1, binds to the KHARON protein via the transporter hydrophilic amino terminal domain, and KHARON is essential for trafficking of GT1 from the flagellar pocket membrane at the base of the flagellum into the flagellar membrane. A major objective of this study was to determine the mechanism whereby KHARON transports GT1 into the flagellar membrane. We have determined that KHARON is a novel component of the transition fibers that project from the basal body at the base of the flagellum toward the flagellar membrane. We propose that KHARON binds GT1 at the transition fibers and then transfers it to intraflagellar transport (IFT) trains as they enter the flagellum at this site. The IFT trains, associated with the membrane tethering protein TULP, then move GT1 through the transition zone filter into the body of the flagellum. These results provide evidence for a role for transition fibers in transport of membrane proteins into flagella.
affiliations: Oregon Health Sciences University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Breaking the bottleneck: semi-automated quantification of actin filament dynamics
papers.abstract: Actin reconstitution assays visualized by total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy have been crucial for defining mechanisms of filament assembly, disassembly, and higher-order organization. Yet quantitative analysis remains slow, labor-intensive, and subject to investigator bias. We developed SMAUG (Single filament Measurement and Analysis Using a GUI), a semi-automated image analysis interface that extends TSOAX filament segmentation and tracking with user-verified trace analysis of time-lapse TIRF images. SMAUG generates kymographs and quantifies filament nucleation, elongation, pausing, junctions, and filament-associated fluorescence while retaining measurements at the individual filament level. We tested the approach across actin reconstitution assays producing concentration-dependent polymerization, formin-stimulated elongation, capping-induced arrest, Arp2/3 branching, and fascin-mediated bundling. SMAUG reproduced manual measurement while reducing analysis time and revealed where dense networks and bundled filaments require user validation. Together, TSOAX and SMAUG provide a semi-automated approach for quantitative analysis of actin filament dynamics.

papers.title: Agentic AI enables cell segmentation-free cell-type inference and cell-type-guided cell segmentation in spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Cell-type identification in spatial transcriptomics often relies on cell segmentation, which can introduce inaccuracies in cell boundaries and transcript assignment. Segmentation-free or cell-free methods have been developed to completely avoid cell segmentation, but inaccurate cell typing hinder accurate downstream analysis. Here, we introduce SSAF-T, a segmentation-free agentic framework that identifies cell types directly from spatial gene expression without predefined reference datasets. For the reference-free cell typing, SSAF-T incorporates CeLLMan, which employs expert-level agents for each organ to annotate cell types using a literature-grounded knowledge graph. We benchmark SSAF-T on both array-based and imaging-based spatial transcriptomics datasets in terms of accuracy, reproducibility, and scalability. We further show that SSAF-T provides an accurate cell segmentation based on the segmentation-free mapping, which ensure compatibility to existing downstream analysis ecosystem, and eventually enable quantitative analysis at single-cell level.
affiliations: Pusan National University (corresponding author)

papers.title: TailEnrich enables discovery of dysregulated genes through disease sample enrichment testing
papers.abstract: Identifying differentially expressed genes is fundamental to elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying complex diseases. However, in complex disorders such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), the genes exhibiting dysregulated expression may vary among patient subsets, reflecting the heterogeneity of the underlying pathological processes. Consequently, pathogenic genes are profoundly dysregulated in only a subset of patients. Conventional differential expression tools, such as DESeq2 and edgeR, are primarily designed to detect population-level expression shifts and may have limited power to identify subgroup-specific dysregulation. To overcome this limitation, we developed TailEnrich, a novel computational method that discovers dysregulated genes within patient subsets. TailEnrich independently tests the extreme left (downregulated) or right (upregulated) tails of a gene's expression distribution for disease sample enrichment. We quantify this enrichment using a new metric, i.e. the PE (Percentage of Enriched disease samples) score. On simulated datasets, TailEnrich demonstrates markedly improved accuracy over DESeq2 and edgeR in identifying dysregulated genes specific to patient subsets. Applied to AD gene expression data, TailEnrich uncovers a distinct, biologically relevant set of genes within key pathological pathways that are missed by mean shift-based approaches. TailEnrich provides a novel method for identifying dysregulated genes, and readily extends to other omics data including genomic variants and proteomics to uncover pathogenic genes in complex diseases.

papers.title: Organotchi: an open-source tool for the automated segmentation, morphological characterization, and longitudinal tracking of organoids
papers.abstract: Neural organoids are three-dimensional stem cell-derived models widely used to study brain development and model disease. Brightfield imaging offers a non-invasive readout of their growth and morphology, and recent advances have made automated organoid segmentation from such images increasingly attainable. Yet existing tools largely leave morphological characterization, quality assessment, and comparisons between conditions to manual or ad hoc analysis. Here we present Organotchi, an open-source tool that integrates automated segmentation with longitudinal morphological analysis of neural organoids. Organotchi quantifies ten morphological features, including area, perimeter, and eccentricity, and tracks cystic structures over time, reports variability within and between batches, and flags outlier organoids and segmentation failures, supporting objective organoid characterization and enhancing downstream analysis. As a proof of concept, we apply Organotchi to disease modelling, pharmacological perturbation, and protocol optimization in neural organoids. One use case assesses drug response in breast cancer spheroids, demonstrating its use beyond its development domain.

papers.title: Structural Basis of Second-Generation HIV-1 Maturation Inhibitor Activity by Magic Angle Spinning NMR
papers.abstract: The CA-SP1 junction of HIV-1 Gag forms a six-helix bundle (6HB) within the immature Gag lattice, sequestering the CA-SP1 cleavage site. Maturation inhibitors (MIs), such as Bevirimat (BVM) and its analogs, are an emerging class of HIV-1 antiviral compounds that stabilize Gag maturation intermediates by interfering with CA-SP1 proteolytic processing. Here, we report the binding modes of a potent second-generation BVM analog with an extended scaffold, HRF-4467, in crystalline CACTD-SP1-NC11 assemblies with inositol hexakisphosphate (IP6), as determined by magic-angle-spinning solid-state NMR (MAS NMR) spectroscopy. The atomic-level structure reveals that HRF-4467 binds asymmetrically in the SP1-NC11 six-helix bundle and stabilizes its helical conformation in the immature lattice, in both the wild-type and the BVM-resistant SP1-V7A Gag variant. Additionally, in the presence of HRF-4467, IP6 adopts distinct conformations in the wild-type CACTD-SP1-NC11 and the SP1-V7A variant. Taken together, our results establish a molecular basis for HRF-4467's improved antiviral activity relative to BVM and suggest strategies for designing inhibitors with enhanced performance against MI-resistant HIV-1 variants for potential therapeutic use.
affiliations: Department of Chemistry, University of California, Berkeley, Berkeley, CA, 94720, USA (corresponding author)

papers.title: Opposing Roles of Cholesterol and Cholesterol Sulfate in Proton Transfer and Diffusion at Membrane Interfaces
papers.abstract: Sterols are fundamental components of biological membranes that modulate membrane fluidity and organisation, yet their role in governing interfacial proton dynamics remains underexplored. Here, we elucidate how cholesterol (Ch) and cholesterol sulfate (ChS) regulate excited-state proton transfer (PT) and long-range proton diffusion (PD) using a complementary dual-approach experimental framework combined with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Using a membrane-anchored photoacid in small unilamellar vesicles, we demonstrate that Ch accelerates local PT dynamics in gel-phase phosphatidylcholine membranes by inducing a fluid, liquid-ordered phase. Surprisingly, ChS inhibits local PT despite its negative headgroup. MD simulations reveal this inhibition stems from deeper probe embedding within ChS containing bilayers and the reduced basicity of sulfate relative to phosphate. Conversely, solid-state electrical measurements on supported lipid bilayers show a stark reversal for long range proton conduction (lateral PD): ChS increases lateral proton conductance by 400 fold under controlled relative humidity, whereas Ch decreases conductivity. This divergence arises mainly because ChS supplies titratable sulfate charge carriers, whereas Ch dilutes key phosphate proton mediators that promote a percolating interfacial hydrogen bonding network without providing charge carriers. Our findings demonstrate that sterols exert scale-dependent control over membrane PT/PD, revealing how headgroup chemistry, membrane fluidity, and hydration synergistically govern bioenergetic proton dynamics.
affiliations: The University of Sheffield (corresponding author)

papers.title: Opportunistically Detecting Signs of Hypertension on a Consumer Smartwatch
papers.abstract: Hypertension is a silent killer, with over half of affected adults unaware of their condition1,2. This lack of awareness is a major concern, as early intervention is critical for preventing major adverse cardiovascular events3,4. Here we show that applying artificial intelligence (AI) to multimodal waveforms (photoplethysmography and accelerometry) recorded using a widely available consumer smartwatch (AI-PPG-ACC-HTN), without any cuff calibration, can detect hypertension with accuracy levels comparable to traditional cuffed blood pressure (BP) devices in the existing clinical framework. We validated AI-PPG-ACC-HTN in a prospective, multicenter study of 196 diverse participants free from known cardiovascular disease and antihypertensive medication against gold-standard 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring. Over seven days of real-world monitoring, AI-PPG-ACC-HTN detected hypertension with a sensitivity of 65.8% (95% CI, 54.0%-76.3%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%), and positive predictive value (PPV) of 80.6% (95% CI, 68.6%-89.6%). In comparison, initial office BP screening achieved a sensitivity of 55.3% (95% CI, 43.4%-66.7%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%) and PPV of 77.8% (95% CI, 64.4%-88.0%). These results highlight an opportunity for consumer smartwatches to facilitate population-level opportunistic hypertension screening by prompting at-risk individuals toward clinical assessment and confirmatory diagnosis using established cuff-based methodologies, offering an accessible tool to address this major public health challenge.

papers.title: Hydrogen Derivatives Enable Cost-Effective Carbon Neutrality in China
papers.abstract: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change recommended 1.5°C carbon reduction target, requiring powerful enforcement from major economies. China, the largest CO2 emitter, is facing severe difficulties for both variable renewable accommodation and decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors. Hydrogen, as a critical green energy carrier bridging renewable to end-users, faces significant obstacles in real-world deployment such as costly transportation, storage and fuel-cell adoption. Affordable and coordinated hydrogen deployment plan to accelerate the carbon-neutral transition remains ambiguous. Here, we present cost-effective carbon-neutral transition pathways for entire energy economy of China emphasizing the significant role of hydrogen and derivatives as green energy carriers, considering high-resolution renewable deployments, hourly power system operations in 29 provincial regions, over 46,000 rail/road/marine/pipeline transfer routing of hydrogen derivatives, process-level fuel adoption strategies in all end-use sectors. Results show that incorporating hydrogen and derivatives can reduce the overall transition cost by $ 10.7 trillion compared with renewable and electrification pathways, achieving negative carbon abatement costs ($-6.15/ton), eliminating external oil import expenses, equivalent to over 50% of China trade surplus (2023 level)1, significantly boosting employment and economic growth. Hydrogen derivative based transition pathway offers a vital direction for affordable and secure decarbonization for China and beyond under volatile international energy markets.

papers.title: Daily briefing: Toothbrush zaps bacteria to clear plaque
Entangled-to-packed crossover in nonlinear extensional rheology of entangled polymers
papers.abstract: The tube model, which reduces the interaction of many-chain entanglement to a single-chain picture, has enabled quantitative descriptions of the mechanical behaviors of polymeric materials and underpins applications from polymer processing to life sciences. In strong extensional flows, however, this theory systematically fails. Herein, through molecular dynamics simulations of entangled polymers, we reveal a strain-induced crossover from the entangled state to a packed state in the inter-chain configuration. Following the saturation of primitive chain stretch, convective disentanglement and chain alignment reorganize the system into a packed configuration of aligned segments. This crossover makes an explicit inter-chain contribution necessary for describing tensile stress beyond the intra-chain conformational stress, explaining the breakdown of tube-based descriptions and quantitatively capturing the mechanical response at large extensional strains. These findings clearly show how the inter-chain reorganization governs the nonlinear extensional behaviors. Entanglements among long-chain macromolecules dictate the mechanical performance of polymeric materials and are described with the tube model but the validity of this model has been questioned for nonlinear extension. Here the authors reveal the key mechanism that governs the mechanical response during extension by elucidating the evolution of entanglements using computer simulations and theoretical analysis.

papers.title: Multiscale neural dynamics reveal how striatal subregions shape stress vulnerability and resilience
papers.abstract: Effective stress coping relies on neural and endocrine coordination, with the mesostriatal system serving as a central substrate. However, how striatal subregions contribute to stress vulnerability versus resilience remains unclear. Here, we show dissociable roles of the nucleus accumbens (NAC) and dorsal caudate (dCA) and their associated brain networks in shaping stress responses. We identify neural stability (NS)—capturing stress-induced changes in state-switching frequency over the course of stress responses—as a marker: task-state NS correlates positively with stress-related NAC activity, whereas resting-state NS correlates inversely with stress-related dCA activity. NAC-mediated networks and associated NS further predict faster cortisol recovery. Intriguingly, NAC-related functional connectivity patterns spatially covary with dopamine D2 receptor distributions and gene expression in inhibitory neurons and glia, whereas dCA-related patterns covary with μ-opioid receptor distributions. Together, these findings reveal striatal subregional heterogeneity in stress coping and characterize resilience as a multisystem homeostatic process integrating neural, endocrine, and molecular layers. This study shows that striatal subregions shape individual differences in stress vulnerability and resilience through distinct patterns of multiscale network dynamics during stress coping.

papers.title: Pulsed photoelectrocatalysis enables efficient urea synthesis over Cu(salen)-COF
papers.abstract: Electrocatalytic urea synthesis from carbon dioxide and nitrate under ambient conditions offers a sustainable alternative to the energy-intensive Bosch-Meiser process. However, its efficiency is constrained by the spatiotemporal mismatch of key carbon and nitrogen intermediates at the catalyst-electrolyte interface. Herein, we address this limitation through interfacial microenvironment optimization combining ionic liquid modification of copper-salen covalent organic framework, pulsed electrolysis, and photoelectrocatalytic coupling. The ionic liquid modification enriches carbon dioxide and facilitates interfacial charge transfer, pulsed electrolysis promotes the dynamic matching of carbon and nitrogen intermediates, and photoelectrocatalytic coupling boosts interfacial electron accumulation. The integrated system achieves a urea yield rate of 69.2 mmol gcat−1 h−1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 56.7% in an H-type cell and 82.5% in a flow cell. In this work, we establish a generalizable strategy for efficient urea electrosynthesis via hierarchical interfacial control and highlight the potential of pulsed photoelectrocatalysis. Urea electrosynthesis suffers from C/N mismatched intermediates. This study integrates ionic-liquid modification, pulsed electrolysis, and photo-assistance into a synergistic strategy that cumulatively promotes C–N coupling and boosts urea yield.

papers.title: Resident cardiac macrophage-like cells induced by an ILC2 cytokine cocktail confer cardioprotection through enhanced efferocytosis in a mouse model of myocardial infarction
papers.abstract: Resident cardiac macrophages (RCM) are essential for myocardial repair following acute myocardial infarction (AMI); however, their therapeutic application is hindered by limited availability. Here, we show that RCM transplantation from healthy mice markedly attenuates cardiac injury in mice. Importantly, we identify a pro-reparative CD301b⁺ RCM population profoundly depleted after AMI and show that adoptive transfer of this subset alone mitigates cardiac injury following myocardial infarction. To overcome the scarcity of native RCMs and favour their replenishment, we expand ex vivo a CD301b+ macrophage-like population (RCML) by polarizing bone marrow-derived macrophages with an ILC2-derived cytokine cocktail, and show that RCML transplantation confers robust post-AMI cardioprotection. Mechanistically, CD301b promotes efferocytosis by enhancing TFEB-mediated lysosomal function via a GATM-AMPK-mTOR axis, a pathway conserved in human macrophages. Thus, our findings identify a key pro-reparative macrophage subset and establish a feasible cell-based strategy for cardiac repair. Resident cardiac macrophages (RCM) contribute to cardiac repair after myocardial infarction (MI); however, their number is reduced upon injury. Here, the authors identify a population of efferocytosing CD301b+ macrophages that promote post-ischemic cardiac repair and develop an ex vivo protocol to generate RCM-like cells induced with enhanced efferocytic potential for post-MI cardioprotection.

papers.title: Strong-gain water-window X-ray laser driven by plasma photocathode wakefield acceleration
papers.abstract: X-ray free-electron lasers are large and complex machines, limited by electron beam brightness. Here we show through start-to-end simulations how to realise compact, robust and tunable X-ray lasers in the water window, based on ultra-bright electron beams from plasma wakefield accelerators. First, an ultra-low-emittance electron beam is released by a plasma photocathode in a metre-scale plasma wakefield accelerator. By tuning the beam charge, space-charge forces create a balance between beam fields and wakefields that reduces beam energy spread and improves energy stability – both critical for beam extraction, transport, and focusing into a metre-scale undulator. Here, the resulting ultra-bright beams produce wavelength-tunable, coherent, femtosecond-scale photon pulses at strong gain. This regime enables reliable generation of multi-gigawatt-class X-ray laser pulses across the water window, offering tunability via the witness beam charge and robustness against variations in plasma wakefield strength and plasma photocathode laser jitter. Our findings help democratise access to coherent, high-power, soft X-ray radiation. Plasma wakefield accelerators promise compact X-ray lasers but have so far lacked sufficiently bright, stable electron beams. The authors show that beam loading by plasma photocathode-injected electron beams boosts brightness and self-stabilises acceleration inside wakefields, paving the way to compact, robust water-window X-ray lasers.

papers.title: Electrolyte-dependent physico-chemical interfacial kinetics shape degradation pathways and lifetime in lithium-ion batteries
papers.abstract: Electrolyte-dependent lifetime variability remains a major obstacle to sustainable deployment of lithium-ion batteries, contributing to premature retirement, increased material demand and uncertainty in lifecycle assessment. However, most continuum degradation models represent the electrolyte through bulk transport, without capturing its role in interfacial degradation. Here, we use customised multi-layer pouch cells with varied ethylene carbonate:dimethyl carbonate ratio, lithium hexafluorophosphate concentration and electrolyte amount to examine how electrolyte conditions shape degradation trajectories under accelerated degradation. Within this formulation framework, changing the solvent ratio leads to distinct lifetime trajectories across otherwise comparable cells. Electrochemical diagnostics, gas analysis and post-mortem interfacial characterisation show that this divergence is associated with electrolyte-sensitive interphase growth, parasitic reactions and spatially heterogeneous surface degradation. We incorporate electrolyte-dependent transport and thermodynamic properties into a physics-based degradation model. A transport-only implementation does not reproduce the observed separation in capacity-retention trajectories. Introducing a minimal electrolyte-sensitive refinement through an effective interphase transport parameter improves agreement in the ethylene-carbonate-rich case. These results identify electrolyte-sensitive interfacial degradation as a necessary modelling dimension for reliable lifetime prediction. Electrolytes shape battery ageing, yet continuum models often describe them mainly through transport. Here, the authors combine custom cells, gas/surface analysis and physics-based modelling to identify interfacial degradation as a missing modelling dimension for lifetime prediction.

Pathology-adapted peptide–oligonucleotide nanohybrid mitigates glucocorticoid-induced bone loss
papers.abstract: Glucocorticoid-induced bone loss (GIBL) remains a major clinical challenge, manifested by both systemic osteopenia and osteonecrosis of the femoral head under chronic glucocorticoid exposure, yet current therapies are limited in coordinately addressing bone deterioration and vascular impairment. With advances in precision medicine, oligonucleotide therapeutics offer opportunities for pathophysiology-informed intervention. Here, we report a pathology-adapted peptide-oligonucleotide nanohybrid (PON) developed for targeted miR-26a-5p delivery to glucocorticoid-injured bone. By integrating self-assembly, bone targeting, enzyme responsiveness, cell penetration, and lysosomal escape, PONs were designed to incorporate pathology-responsive delivery features and address key barriers to oligonucleotide delivery. Mechanistically, PON-mediated miR-26a-5p delivery reduced GSK-3β expression and promoted HIF-1α stabilization, thereby preserving osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling and attenuating apoptosis. In a rat model of GIBL, systemic PON administration protects against early skeletal and vascular injury and limits progression after disease establishment. These findings identify the therapeutic relevance of miR-26a-5p in GIBL, and support the potential of PON system for bone-targeted oligonucleotide therapy. Glucocorticoids can cause severe bone loss and osteonecrosis. Here, the authors develop a pathology-adapted peptide–oligonucleotide nanohybrid that delivers miR 26a-5p to mitigate bone loss and support vascular recovery.

papers.title: Engineering filamentous myosins for optical control of contractility
papers.abstract: Understanding the behaviors of contractile actomyosin systems requires precise spatiotemporal control of filamentous myosin activity. Here, we develop a tool for optical control of contractility by extending the MyLOV family of gearshifting motors to create engineered filamentous myosins that change velocity in response to blue light. We characterize these minifilaments using in vitro single-molecule tracking assays, contractility assays in reconstituted actin networks, and imaging of contractile phenotypes in live cells. In vitro, gearshifting minifilaments change speed and/or direction when illuminated, and contraction rates of minifilaments in actin networks can be modulated using blue light. In cells, gearshifting minifilaments enable optical control of protrusion retraction, cortical flow, and cell migration. Finally, we develop an alternative design for minifilaments that only interact processively with actin in blue light. Engineered minifilaments could be used to dissect behaviors such as self-organization and mechanotransduction in contractile systems both in vitro and in cells and tissues. Zemsky and colleagues employ protein engineering to create filamentous myosins controlled by light. These optogenetic motors enable spatiotemporal control of contractility in vitro and in cells, providing a tool for probing contractile actomyosin systems.

papers.title: Strong hydrogels through precisely oriented crystallization regulation
papers.abstract: Achieving high mechanical strength and environmental stability is critical for hydrogels in demanding engineering scenarios. Crystalline hydrogels hold promise because their crystallites act as physical crosslinks and energy dissipators; however, precise control over crystalline architecture remains underexplored. Inspired by industrial thermoplastic processing, we report an ASGS strategy for crystalline hydrogels that integrates alkali-induced chain activation (A), ultra-stretching-driven orientation (S), and glycerol-seawater-mediated densification (GS). Alkali treatment yields moderate initial crystallinity with refined nascent crystallites. Ultra-stretching establishes a highly oriented chain network, and subsequent densification achieves maximum crystallinity and highly oriented crystallites. The resultant hydrogels, in the fully hydrated state, combine a tensile strength of 160.0 MPa, a modulus of 746.0 MPa, and a fracture energy of 26.4 kJ·m⁻². The corresponding plastic reaches 414.2 MPa tensile strength while retaining flexibility. This thermoplastic-inspired crystallization engineering provides a scalable paradigm for fabricating strong and stable crystalline hydrogels, promising for load-bearing and harsh underwater engineering applications. Hydrogels have potential in a range of applications, but achieving the required properties and stability can be challenging. Here, the authors report the development of a combination strategy for crystalline hydrogels with oriented structures.

papers.title: A language model-informed minimalistic design of functional coacervate vesicles
papers.abstract: Hierarchical biopolymer interactions in nature yield intricate architectures, while synthetic biomimetics adopt a reductionist approach to create scalable and tunable systems. Inspired by intracellular liquid-liquid phase separation into membraneless, vesicle-like condensates, synthetic coacervate vesicles (CVs) have emerged for drug delivery, protocell design, and catalysis. However, a general reductionist framework for rationally constructing CVs remains challenging due to insufficient understanding of the minimal motifs required to drive coacervates into stable vesicular topologies. Here, we present a protein language model-informed design of such minimal systems, where arginine-rich oligopeptides and competing anionic oligomers self-assemble into oligo-coacervate vesicles (OCVs) without any chemical modifications or external fuels. Combining experiments and molecular dynamics simulations, we demonstrate an assembly mechanism governed by an electrostatic-hydrophobic balance, which enables vesiculation across a broad range of oligomer pairs. This principle further permits de novo functionalization, exemplified by OCVs engineered to selectively recognize and encapsulate DNA G-quadruplex structures. Together, these findings establish sequence-encoded design rules for the predictable construction of vesicle-like compartments. The study presents a protein language model guided design of minimal coacervate vesicles that are composed entirely of oligomeric biomolecules, with functions programmable through oligopeptide sequences.

papers.title: The modular evolution of chitinases is governed by coevolution of auxiliary and catalytic domains
papers.abstract: The modular architecture of multi-domain enzymes is a key source of functional diversity. GH18 chitinases exemplify this, possessing a variety of auxiliary domains that have been postulated to underpin their role as essential global nutrient cyclers. However, there is no evolutionary framework that accounts for the vast assortment of domain compositions observed across the protein family. Here, we map the sequence space of prokaryotic chitinases, integrating phylogenetics with a quantitative analysis of domain promiscuity to decode their evolutionary history. We reveal that diversification follows distinct trajectories: enzymes necessary for environmental chitin scavenging evolve via high modular plasticity and structural elaboration of the catalytic core, whereas sequences required for specialized, essential developmental roles fix their domain architecture to fulfil lineage-specific physiological roles. By resolving how domain accretion co-evolves with catalytic scaffolds, this work provides a framework for understanding how multi-domain enzymes adapt to complex environments. Changes in the arrangement of protein domains shape the evolution of chitin-degrading enzymes, helping bacteria and archaea specialize for different ecological niches.

papers.title: Personalized adjunctive phage therapy for difficult-to-treat musculoskeletal infections
papers.abstract: Musculoskeletal infections (MSIs), including fracture-related infections (FRIs) and periprosthetic joint infections (PJIs), remain difficult to treat because of biofilm formation and increasing antimicrobial resistance. Bacteriophage therapy (PT) has re-emerged as a promising adjunctive strategy, although prospective clinical evidence remains scarce. Here, we prospectively evaluated adjunctive local PT in 13 patients with refractory MSIs treated within the multidisciplinary PHAGEFORCE framework at University Hospitals Leuven (BE). Following surgery, personalized phage preparations were administered through a closed drain system for 8–10 days alongside systemic antibiotics. Clinical, microbiological, immunological, and genomic data were collected. Four patients with refractory MSIs lacking suitable phages served as a control cohort. Clinical remission was observed in nine of eleven evaluable phage-treated patients (82%), whereas all control patients experienced infection recurrence during follow-up. PT was well tolerated, with no serious adverse reactions or clinically meaningful toxicity. Local phage titers remained detectable throughout therapy despite interpatient variability. Serum-mediated phage neutralization was observed during and after PT, and longitudinal genomic monitoring revealed patient-specific phage dynamics, neither of which was clearly associated with clinical outcome. These findings demonstrate the feasibility and safety of standardized local PT and support further evaluation of this approach in controlled clinical trials. In this prospective study, authors found that personalized adjunctive local phage therapy was feasible and well tolerated in difficult-to-treat musculoskeletal infections, with 9 of 11 evaluable patients achieving remission.

papers.title: Genomic language models decode bidirectional promoter activity and reveal conserved regulatory patterns across plant species
papers.abstract: Bidirectional promoters (BDPs), intergenic regions that coordinate transcription of oppositely oriented genes, pervade eukaryotic genomes, yet sequence signatures remain poorly defined. Existing approaches to BDP identification rely on distance thresholds and cannot infer activity from DNA. Here, we use Evo2, a genomic language model, to predict BDP activity and uncover sequence-encoded regulatory principles across four plant species (Arabidopsis, maize, rice, and wheat). We stratify BDPs by co-expression strength and compare Evo2-derived embeddings against k-mer profiles, transcription factor binding site matrices, and convolutional neural networks trained on sequence. Evo2 embeddings outperform all baselines, demonstrating that genomic language models capture regulatory information underlying BDP activity. Models trained on one or multiple species transfer to held-out species, and in planta validation in Spartina alterniflora confirms predicted high-activity BDPs. Sparse autoencoder analysis links Evo2 embeddings to nucleosome positioning and species-specific transcription factor landscapes, providing insight into sequence determinants underlying BDP activity . This work establishes how genomic language models can extract bidirectional promoter logic from sequence and identify conserved regulatory rules across plants. Bidirectional promoters (BDPs) are intergenic regions that initiate transcription of two oppositely oriented genes. Here, the authors report a framework that employs Evo2 genomic language model embeddings to predict BDP activity directly from raw DNA sequence.

papers.title: Digital readiness for cardiovascular care in high-burden US communities with cardiology workforce constraints
papers.abstract: Digital health may extend cardiovascular care in communities with limited specialist access, but its effectiveness depends on whether communities have the infrastructure, devices, affordability, and capacity needed to use digital services. We linked national data on cardiometabolic disease burden, cardiology workforce, and digital readiness across 82,999 US census tracts. Among high-burden tracts in counties with no cardiologist or declining per-capita cardiologist supply, 4,765 (18.0%) tracts representing 19.9 million residents had higher digital readiness and were thus classified as deployment-priority tracts, whereas 21,752 (82.0%) tracts representing 74.1 million residents had lower readiness and were investment-priority tracts. Investment-priority tracts were spread across the urban-rural continuum and faced different barriers (adoption versus infrastructure). Contrasting classifications frequently occurred among neighboring census tracts within the same metropolitan area, highlighting geographic variation not captured by county-level targeting. Findings were broadly consistent across nine additional analyses with varying measures of readiness, workforce access, and classification thresholds. These findings provide a national framework for distinguishing communities where digital cardiovascular care may be deployed from those where infrastructure and adoption support may first be needed to enable equitable implementation. As presented at 2026 AHA Scientific Sessions: Analysis of U.S. Census and other national health data identifies communities with high cardiovascular care needs and assess health system readiness for digital care deployment.

papers.title: Nondisruptive 3D profiling of combinations of epigenetic marks in single cells
papers.abstract: Advances in single-cell sequencing and spatial omics technologies have enhanced our understanding of diverse cellular identities, compositions, architectures and functions. However, the single-cell three-dimensional (3D) organization of the epigenome is still not well understood, due to an absence of spatial single-cell methods that allow high-resolution, locus-specific detection of combinations of epigenetic marks while maintaining 3D genome organization. Here we develop epigenetic proximity hybridization reaction (Epi-PHR), a nondisruptive image-based single-cell spatial epigenetic profiling technology. Epi-PHR detects combinations of epigenetic marks in situ at hundreds of gene targets within single cells while preserving 3D genome organization. Phased Epi-PHR combined with chromatin tracing reveals unexpected associations between epigenetic mark enrichment and chromatin folding of an imprinted gene cluster at the single-chromatin-copy level for the distinct alleles from different parental origins. We expect Epi-PHR will be broadly applicable in research requiring single-cell spatial epigenetic information, advancing our understanding of the combinatorial epigenetic code and its relationship with chromatin organization. Epi-PHR is an imaging method that maps combinations of epigenetic marks at single genes while preserving 3D genome structure, revealing how chromatin folding and histone modifications are linked among single-chromatin copies.

Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor
papers.abstract: The pseudogap stands out in the phase diagram of the cuprate high-temperature superconductors because its origin and relationship to superconductivity remain elusive. The origin of the pseudogap has been debated, with competing hypotheses attributing it to preformed electron pairs or local order, such as charge density waves. We present unambiguous evidence supporting the pairing scenario, using local shot-noise spectroscopy measurements in Bi 2 Sr 2 CaCu 2 O 8+δ . Our data demonstrate that the pseudogap energy coincides with the onset of electron pairing and is spatially heterogeneous with values reaching up to 70 milli–electron volts. Our results exclude a pure local order origin of the pseudogap, link the pseudogap to Cooper pair formation, and suggest that the limiting factor for higher critical temperature in cuprates is phase coherence.

papers.title: Discovering molecular modulators with nanoswitch screening
papers.abstract: Molecules that modulate protein-protein interactions, including through ternary complex formation, have been established as key therapeutics. Yet they can be challenging to discover, as standard screening approaches often lack throughput or fail to directly assay multibody interactions. We addressed this by combining DNA nanoswitch–based selection of nucleotide-encoded libraries with next-generation sequencing to create FIND (Functional Interaction–based Nanoswitch Discovery), which enables ultrahigh-throughput discovery of compounds that induce or increase protein-protein interactions. We demonstrate FIND by discovering nanobodies that stabilize the interaction between angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 and the receptor-binding domain of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 and by discovering agonists of peroxisome proliferator–activated receptor gamma from a DNA-barcoded small-molecule library. By enabling rapid discovery of molecular modulators, FIND could lead to new therapeutics across many conditions.

papers.title: Echoes of the Anthropocene: Noise pollution as a global threat
papers.abstract: Anthropogenic noise is a rapidly expanding global pollutant, but its effects across biological levels from individuals to ecosystems remain unquantified. We conducted phylogenetically controlled meta-analyses of 214 experimental studies on 177 aquatic and terrestrial species with ranges that span six continents. Noise altered at least one physiological, developmental, or behavioral trait in 80% of species studied, with declines in fitness and abundance and disruptions of predator-prey interactions. Effects occurred in every habitat, although response mechanisms varied for some traits and species, creating winners and losers. Only multispecies analyses can reveal such species- and ecosystem-level impacts of anthropogenic stressors. Our results establish noise as a novel selection pressure reshaping ecosystem dynamics and as a pervasive stressor requiring soundscape protection alongside habitat conservation.

papers.title: Quantum gas microscopy of three-flavor Hubbard systems
papers.abstract: Hubbard systems are paradigmatic realizations of strongly correlated many-body systems. Introducing additional species breaks the SU(2) symmetry of the Hubbard model and leads to a wide variety of new exotic quantum phases. Here, we extended quantum gas microscopy to three-flavor Fermi lattice gases in the Hubbard regime. Relying on site- and flavor-resolved detection, we studied the phase diagram of the three-flavor Hubbard model and found signatures of flavor-selective localization and selective pairing at temperatures down to the tunneling energy scale. Our measurements were then compared with numerical linked-cluster expansion calculations. Further increase of phase space density may enable the observation of a distinct pair Mott phase at half filling and shows a path toward the study of color superfluidity and other aspects of quantum chromodynamics.

papers.title: Tumor metastasis co-opts liver hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated hematopoietic abnormalities contribute to systemic immunosuppression. However, whether tumors can initiate localized extramedullary hematopoiesis to suppress antitumor immunity remains unclear. In this study, we identify a distinct form of hepatic hematopoiesis driven by liver metastasis–associated hematopoietic stem cells (LM-HSCs). Liver metastases establish ectopic periportal hematopoietic niches that recruit bone marrow HSCs through Kupffer cell–dependent C-C motif chemokine receptor 1 (CCR1) signaling. Although LM-HSCs retain self-renewal and multipotency, cAMP response element–binding protein (CREB) activation skews their differentiation toward the myeloid lineage, particularly annexin A1–positive (ANXA1 + ) immature neutrophils. These neutrophils produce glucocorticoids, which activate glucocorticoid receptor signaling in a paracrine manner and induce immune checkpoint receptor expression and functional anergy in CD8 + T and natural killer cells. Collectively, these findings suggest that liver metastases reprograms hepatic hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression.

papers.title: Glacial abrupt transitions in ocean circulation were much slower than ice-core records imply
papers.abstract: Dansgaard-Oeschger (DO) events during the last ice age are thought to reflect rapid shifts in the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC). Greenland ice cores suggest warming transitions within only a few decades—or even just over 10 years. Using precisely dated speleothem oxygen-isotope records from the Asian monsoon region, we have shown that the same DO warmings unfolded over more than a century. Isotope modeling revealed that Greenland records primarily capture a rapid atmospheric reorganization triggered by the initial sea-ice retreat in the northeastern North Atlantic, whereas the parallel AMOC recovery and hemispheric thermal adjustment proceeded much more slowly. These findings reveal that natural AMOC transitions evolved more slowly than the rapid North Greenland oxygen-isotope shifts would imply, thereby refining our understanding of “abruptness” during DO events.

papers.title: Targeting hormone conversion through dietary fiber improves polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome
papers.abstract: Excessive androgens serve as a primary driver for many phenotypic features of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Although dietary fiber has been shown to alleviate PMOS, its effects on androgen concentrations and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In a clinical trial, we demonstrated that a dietary fiber combination consisting of inulin, resistant starch, and β-glucan reduces androgen concentrations in patients’ plasma. Mechanistically, dietary fiber increased the abundance of Bacteroides xylanisolven s, which converts androstenedione into a nonandrogenic secondary hormone metabolite we named coproandrosterone, which is further metabolized by gut microbiota into dihydro-coproandrosterone. This metabolic pathway was validated in a mouse model. These findings highlight the potential of dietary fiber to alleviate PMOS by modulating androgen homeostasis through gut microbiota, offering insights for prebiotic and probiotic therapies.

papers.title: When fat adapts: From physiological remodeling to disease
papers.abstract: Adipose tissue undergoes extensive remodeling to adapt to changing physiological demands. This plasticity encompasses changes in adipocyte metabolism and number, extracellular matrix organization, vascularization, immune composition, and innervation. When coordinated, these processes preserve energy buffering, thermogenesis, endocrine function, and local tissue support. Pathological adipose tissue remodeling drives obesity-related complications and contributes to many diseases involving organ-associated adipose depots throughout the body. In cancer, tumor-associated fat can develop a metabolic and fibroinflammatory niche that promotes tumor growth and invasion, and remodeling of other depots can directly disrupt neighboring tissues. Recent studies have identified mesenchymal, immune, vascular, and adipocyte states that govern adaptive or pathological outcomes. These findings broaden therapeutic goals beyond reducing fat mass toward restoring adipogenesis, substrate turnover, thermogenic capacity, and tissue-niche function.

papers.title: Direct evidence for psychoactive cannabis use 2800 years ago
papers.abstract: Cannabis is the world’s most-used illicit psychoactive plant, yet direct prehistoric evidence for its consumption is rare. In this study, we present the earliest direct evidence of cannabis use: offerings of plant parts and chemical compounds in ancient human hair recovered from a monumental tomb in Siberia. The findings suggest that the plant was used for its psychoactive qualities across Eurasia, where specific wild populations might have had naturally higher active compound levels. We show that the practice of cannabis consumption dates back at least 2800 years, anchoring debates around contemporary usage and informing discussions on cannabis in medicine, public health, law, and industry.

papers.title: Seafloor geodesy delineates fast megathrust relocking after the giant 2011 Tohoku earthquake
papers.abstract: How and when the subduction megathrust recovers its locking state after a great earthquake is important to understanding earthquake-cycle physics and future hazards. Here we report the delineation of the relocking process after the 2011 magnitude 9 Tohoku earthquake with 14 years of postseismic seafloor geodetic observations. These data, combined with onshore geodetic observations, analyses of repeating earthquakes, and numerical modeling, reveal how the recovery of locking is interrupted by afterslip on the megathrust and accompanied by stress relaxation in the viscoelastic upper mantle. The results indicate that the megathrust has already arrived at a locking state today similar to that before the earthquake despite the ongoing stress relaxation. The acquired knowledge aids understanding of megathrust earthquake cycles at other subduction zones.

papers.title: Stacked porous NiTi structure with low cost and ultrahigh fatigue life for elastocaloric cooling
papers.abstract: Elastocaloric cooling (eC) uses shape memory alloys (SMAs) as energy-efficient, eco-friendly refrigerants. However, cost-effectively fabricating SMAs into fatigue-resistant, heat transfer–enhanced structures remains a key obstacle to commercialization of the eC technology. We introduce a “stamping and stacking” (S-S) method for producing porous, fatigue-resistant SMA structures. Honeycomb-like chips are stamped from nitinol (NiTi) thin sheets and then stacked into a layered tubular structure to increase heat exchange surface and at the same time avoid buckling and splitting failures encountered in existing SMA structures. The stacked structure endures >10 8 compression cycles and can deliver high specific cooling power of 3850 watts per kilogram. Our S-S method reduces fabrication costs by one order of magnitude compared with existing approaches, enabling mass production of eC refrigerant structures for commercial deployment.

papers.title: The first 1000 days: Modeling language learning from individual children’s everyday speech
papers.abstract: Children learn to understand and speak from the speech around them, yet how that everyday input shapes learning remains unresolved. Large language models show that language is learnable from data, but their scale and training conditions differ sharply from a child’s natural experience. We trained cognitively feasible, child-specific models on longitudinal home recordings from eight children across their first 1000 days of life. Each model learned incrementally from a single child’s ordered speech input without prior linguistic knowledge, developing phoneme-like and word-form representations that tracked each child’s learning pace. Learning was dependent on dense daily sampling and replay of recent input, indicating that both experience- and memory-related processes are necessary. These findings show that everyday experience contains sufficient structure for language learning and establish child-specific modeling for testing developmental theories.

Obesity management medications: The way forward
papers.abstract: Obesity is now widely recognized as a chronic progressive condition. The altered biological mechanisms that cause obesity frequently require long-term treatment, including pharmacotherapies or bariatric surgery. In recent decades, the pathophysiology of obesity has been understood to an extent that obesity management medication (OMM) discovery could be rationally pursued. Advances in defining the regulation of food intake and energy expenditure by molecular communication from peripheral organs to the brain led to the development of OMMs that appear capable of safely achieving scalable and sustained body weight loss. However, side effects, heterogeneous treatment responses, long-term metabolic adaptations, adherence, and other factors may limit the use of existing OMMs and justify the development of additional medications to improve the health of people living with obesity.

papers.title: Denoising the US Census: Succinct block hierarchical regression
papers.abstract: The 2020 United States Census adopted differential privacy to protect individual confidentiality, adding calibrated noise to summary demographic measurements that are then reconciled into population tables. We developed BlueDown, a postprocessing algorithm that combines techniques from linear regression and constrained optimization while exploiting measurement structure for efficiency. On 2020 Census data, BlueDown reduced the error of groupings by race at the county level by 21 to 36% and of all county-level groupings by 9 to 58%; at the tract level, it reduced error of groupings by housing type by 38 to 61%. These gains came at no cost to confidentiality or computational efficiency and would improve the validity of research relying on this definitive dataset and analyses used to guide the distribution of more than $1.5 trillion in annual federal spending.

Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition
papers.abstract: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer’s disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)–based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

papers.abstract: Ultracold atom platforms enable low temperatures and long free evolution times, which are crucial for fundamental physics tests and atom interferometry. The lowest equivalent temperature reported in such a system is 38 pK with a free expansion time of 2 s, achieved in atom-chip-based magnetic traps in microgravity. Optical dipole trap (ODT) systems offer better optical access and the flexibility to condense both magnetic and non-magnetic atoms, but have not been used to prepare quantum degenerate gases under microgravity conditions. Here we report an ODT-based Bose-Einstein condensate created aboard the China Space Station, containing 2.0 × 10 4 atoms, reaching an equivalent temperature of 9.7 − 2.7 + 3.2 pK with a free expansion time of 7.0 s. This record-low temperature could stimulate a new generation of ODT-based experiments in quantum simulation and precision measurements in space.

papers.title: A peripheral blood mononuclear cell DNA methylation-based risk stratification tool for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
papers.abstract: There is an urgent need for minimally invasive and accurate tools to prioritize individuals for timely endoscopic evaluation of ESCC. papers.title: Trends at 50: a mission that matters
Dynamic allocation of MurJ coordinates bacterial growth and division
papers.abstract: Rod-shaped bacteria grow by inserting peptidoglycan into the lateral cell wall during elongation and into the septal cell wall during division. These two modes of growth are driven by distinct peptidoglycan synthesis machineries that consume the shared precursor Lipid II and must be coordinated so that cell enlargement remains matched to division. However, how cells spatially allocate this shared precursor, and whether Lipid II translocation itself contributes to this coordi-nation, remain unclear. Here we show that the spatial distribution of the essential Lipid II flippase MurJ coordinates this balance in Escherichia coli. Increasing nonseptal MurJ abundance shifted cell-wall synthesis toward elongation and reduced septal synthesis. Single-molecule tracking revealed that MurJ diffuses throughout the membrane but is transiently captured at the division site, rather than stably incorporated into the septal synthesis machinery. This recruitment requires active septal cell-wall synthesis, but not ongoing Lipid II synthesis or flipping, indicating that MurJ recruitment is coupled to the active synthesis machinery rather than to substrate availability or transport. Thus, activation of septal synthesis creates transient MurJ capture at the division site, providing a mechanism to preferentially supply Lipid II for septal growth during cytokinesis. These findings reveal a capture-and-release mechanism that dynamically enriches MurJ at active division sites and thereby coordinates elongation and division in bacterial cells.

papers.title: T cell transcriptomes in simulated microgravity in vivo
papers.abstract: Spaceflight exposes astronauts to a combination of stressors, among which microgravity remains the least well characterized at the level of human immune cell function. We examined the in vivo effect of long-term simulated microgravity (SMG) on T cell transcriptomes in ten healthy male volunteers who completed a three-week dry immersion protocol without countermeasures. Peripheral blood was collected at five time points covering a pre-immersion baseline (day -7), three intra-exposure time points (days 7, 14 and 21) and a recovery time point one week after the end of exposure (day 28). CD3+ T cells were isolated and analysed by RNA-seq, with differential expression assessed per volunteer and KEGG pathway enrichment used to identify the most affected gene networks. SMG was associated with transcript-level changes in genes mapping to key molecular pathways, including those involved in cell proliferation, cell-cycle regulation, maintenance of genome integrity, and oncogenic and tumour-suppressor networks. Hub genes shared across the most significant pathways were differentially expressed in the majority of volunteers. A notable finding was pronounced inter-individual heterogeneity: samples clustered primarily by volunteer identity, yet a coordinated temporal shift during exposure and a partial return toward baseline by day 28 were detectable across donors, and these changes occurred in the absence of detectable systemic inflammation. These results indicate that SMG is associated with altered T cell transcriptional programs in vivo and that the response is sufficiently variable between individuals to favor personalized rather than uniform countermeasure strategies.

papers.title: Genome evolution and glycosyltransferase diversification shape asperosaponin biosynthesis in Dipsacus asperoides
papers.abstract: Deciphering the genomic and enzymatic features associated with high-abundance specialized metabolism is important for understanding and engineering bioactive natural product biosynthesis. Asperosaponin , a hederagenin-based saponin, accumulates at exceptionally high levels in Dipsacus asperoides roots and is by far the predominant triterpenoid saponin. Here, by integrating a chromosome-level genome assembly with comparative genomics, transcriptomics, metabolite profiling, and biochemical characterization, we reconstructed a major biosynthetic route to asperosaponin and identified diversification of triterpenoid-associated gene families. Functional analyses revealed an ordered glycosylation sequence in which DaUGT73GZ2 preferentially accepts C-3-glycosylated substrates retaining a free C-28 carboxyl group, thereby establishing a C-3-before-C-28 glycosylation order during asperosaponin biosynthesis. Phylogenetic and biochemical analyses further uncovered functional differentiation among UGT85CA enzymes involved in C-3 arabinosylation, while genomic and expression analyses revealed lineage-specific patterns of pathway gene duplication and transcriptional regulation. Together, these findings identify genomic, enzymatic, and transcriptional features associated with the distinctive, high-abundance triterpenoid saponin profile of D. asperoides roots and provide a framework for understanding and engineering triterpenoid saponin biosynthesis.

papers.title: Salinity adaptation in date palm (Phoenix dactylifera): evidence for selective sweeps at Salt Overly Sensitive (SOS) genes
papers.abstract: The date palm is a high salinity tolerant fruit tree grown mainly in the region spanning from North Africa to parts of South Asia. Climate change models of this region indicate the possibility of increasing salinity in the future. The Salt Overly Sensitive (SOS) pathway is crucial for salinity tolerance in plants, serving as a primary defense mechanism by facilitating sodium exclusion. To better understand date palms' salt tolerance, we analyzed variation in SOS pathway genes in a set of 197 date palm genomes collected from across the range of cultivation. Here, we show evidence for selective sweeps in multiple SOS pathway genes. A single major pdSOS1 haplotype is at very high frequency in Eastern and Western subpopulations, with a minor, likely ancestral haplotype still present in both geographical locations. Allele-specific gene expression analysis showed differences in salt-treated roots between swept and ancestral haplotypes. Interestingly, sequence-based analysis of the pdSOS1 haplotype suggested a second, much earlier introgression event between P. theophrasti and date palm, though direction is unclear. This event happened before both the selective sweep and the previously reported recent introgression to date palm. We identified a MITE transposable element inserted into a pdSOS1 intron on the swept haplotype, and a similar insertion was found in an intron of the SOS2 paralog pdCIPK8. Both insertions are unique to date palm among Phoenix species. The pdCIPK8 haplotype containing the MITE is also at high frequency in both populations. Further analysis showed evidence for a selective sweep spanning the pdSOS3 region in the western population that shares similarity to an Eastern haplotype spanning the promoter region only. Slower extended haplotype homozygosity decay surrounding the genes in the western population suggests that the swept haplotype originated in the East and spread to the West in all cases. Altogether, our data provide evidence of selective sweeps in the date palm SOS pathway and may go to explaining how this species has developed such high salinity tolerance.

papers.title: TRPP Ion Channels Function in the π-Conformation Rather Than the α-Conformation
papers.abstract: PKD2 (TRPP1) is a TRPP ion channel whose dysfunction causes autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). Understanding its conformational states and gating mechanism is important for elucidating its function and for structure-based drug discovery. Cryo-EM structures of WT-PKD2 contain a local {pi}-helical turn in the S6 pore-lining helix ({pi}-conformation). In contrast, a fully -helical S6 (-conformation) was observed in the gain-of-function mutant F604P-PKD2 and interpreted as the open state, leading to the proposed {pi}-to- activation mechanism. However, whether the -conformation can support function has never been directly established. Here, using molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate the functional properties of the -and {pi}-conformations of PKD2. The -conformation remains dewetted unless the lower gate is widened beyond the conformational range observed in mammalian TRP channels. By contrast, the {pi}-conformation supports pore hydration and ion conduction following a small opening of the L677 gate, with simulated conductance comparable to experimental measurements. The closely related PKD2L1 (TRPP2) channel shows a similar dependence on conformation, with a hydrated {pi}-conformation and a dewetted -conformation. Together, these findings challenge the assignment of the -conformation as the conductive state and support a model in which the {pi}-conformation represents the functionally relevant state of TRPP channels. This model suggests that activation may involve an -to-{pi} transition rather than the previously proposed {pi}-to- transition, providing a new framework for understanding TRPP channel gating. This work sheds light on the molecular basis of polycystin channel dysfunction and could facilitate the development of PKD2-targeted therapeutic strategies for ADPKD.
