papers.title: Longitudinal remodeling of the tumor-immune microenvironment during regorafenib, nivolumab, and chemotherapy in advanced gastric cancer
papers.abstract: Previous studies combining the multikinase inhibitor regorafenib with a PD-1 inhibitor showed promising activity in gastric cancer. We conducted a phase 1b/2 trial (NCT05394740) of first-line regorafenib, nivolumab, and chemotherapy in 30 patients with mismatch repair–proficient gastric cancer and investigated its impact on the tumor microenvironment. The primary end point was met; 22 of 30 patients showed objective tumor response (73%; 80% confidence interval, 60.3 to 83.8). Single-cell RNA and T cell receptor sequencing were performed on biopsy samples at baseline, during treatment, and at disease progression. The combination treatment increased tumor antigen–reactive CD8 + T cells and M1-like proinflammatory macrophages and decreased immunosuppressive and tumor-promoting populations, including activated CCR8 + regulatory T cells, LRRC15 + cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), RGS5 + pericytes, and APLN + tip cells. At progression, LRRC15 + CAFs and APLN + tip cells remained reduced, activated CCR8 + regulatory T cells reexpanded, and additional treatment-resistant subsets emerged, including APOC1 + lipid-associated macrophages. In murine models of acquired resistance, therapeutic targeting of these suppressive immune cell populations with antibodies against CCR8 or TREM2 in combination with PD-1 blockade restored antitumor immunity. These findings demonstrate dynamic remodeling of the tumor microenvironment and suggest potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: A synthetic heparin oligosaccharide decouples anticoagulation from heparin-induced thrombocytopenia risk
papers.abstract: Low–molecular weight heparin (LMWH) remains clinically indispensable for the prevention and treatment of thrombosis in cardiovascular surgery, hemodialysis, and other critical care settings. However, LMWH is constrained by heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) and supply chain vulnerabilities of animal-derived sources. This study used chemoenzymatic synthesis to engineer homogeneous dodecasaccharide 12G-2, decoupling anticoagulant efficacy from HIT risk via dual structural modulation. Substitution with 2- O -sulfated glucuronic acid conferred conformational rigidity, and engineered sulfation attenuated platelet factor 4 (PF4) binding, whereas the antithrombin-binding domain remained intact. 12G-2 exhibited nanomolar anti–Factor Xa (FXa) activity in vitro, enoxaparin-equivalent venous antithrombotic efficacy, and superior arterial antithrombotic activity in murine thrombosis models, and it showed diminished PF4 binding, attenuated pathological β sheet formation, and minimal recognition by HIT-related antibodies in vitro. Both in vitro and in a murine tail-bleeding model, 12G-2 demonstrated high protamine reversibility, exceeding standard LMWH enoxaparin neutralization efficiency. In washed human platelets, 12G-2–PF4 complexes with the HIT-mimicking antibody KKO failed to induce integrin αIIbβ3 activation or P-selectin release and elicited minimal platelet spreading comparable to resting controls. Safety assessments in mice showed no hepatotoxicity at tested doses and low immunogenicity in a murine PF4-heparin immunization model. In PF4-heparin antibody–positive mice, 12G-2 attenuated platelet activation while exerting stronger FXa inhibition than enoxaparin. These findings established 12G-2 as an alternative to LMWH.

papers.title: Cancer-specific T cell receptor discovery using 150,000 clinical genomics samples
papers.abstract: T cell receptors (TCRs) can enable detection and elimination of cancer cells via recognition of cancer-specific peptides presented on human leukocyte antigen (HLA). We speculated that shared cancer antigens could be recognized by recurrent (“public”) TCRs, which might be identifiable using statistical methods. Here, we identified public TCRs against therapeutically relevant targets via computational analysis of large-scale bulk RNA sequencing data obtained from routine clinical genomics testing. Using data from ∼150,000 patient tumor samples, we identified TCR chains that were associated with well-known cancer antigens, including human papillomavirus, mutated KRAS, and CT83. We devised methods for pairing enriched TCR-α and TCR-β chain sequences and validated 44 TCRs across nine peptide-HLA targets for antigen recognition, including potent cytotoxic TCRs. Our results suggest that public anticancer TCRs are common and may represent a new source for the development of cancer therapeutics.

CRISPR mutagenesis of the MYC locus reveals a druggable ultraconserved RNA element
papers.abstract: CRISPR tiling mutagenesis of the 10-kb human MYC locus mapped the fitness landscape of an entire human gene at base-pair resolution. This unbiased interrogation revealed that 67% of functionally essential base pairs are noncoding. An ultraconserved RNA regulatory element was identified that controls MYC localization and can be therapeutically targeted to suppress cancer cell growth in patient-derived tumor organoids.

papers.title: Tumor-to-dendritic cell reprogramming induces immunogenic lymphoid structures across cancers
papers.abstract: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) support effective cancer immunity but remain difficult to induce experimentally. Ascic, Chatelain, et al. establish tumor-to-cDC1 reprogramming as a strategy to generate immunogenic TLSs across multiple cancers, uncovering how localized migratory cDC1 and CD40-dependent T cell interactions coordinate local and systemic cellular and humoral immunity.

papers.title: Exosome secretion is required for Sonic Hedgehog dispersal and signal gradient formation in the embryonic limb bud mesenchyme
papers.abstract: Corcoran et al. report a role for exosome packaging and secretion in regulating Sonic Hedgehog dispersal within the limb bud mesenchyme. They demonstrate that Sonic Hedgehog-associated exosomes are required for signal gradient formation, utilizing two dispersal modes: diffusion in the extracellular space and transport along cytonemes.

papers.title: Programmed bacterial lysis in vivo alters host immune responses and microbial pathogenesis
papers.abstract: To mimic T6SS-mediated killing, Lembke et al. engineer bacterial lysis strains and identify proinflammatory muropeptides that differentially trigger infant mouse intestinal immune signaling. Lysis or co-administration of synthetic muropeptides directly enhanced colonization of bystander non-lysing V. cholerae ΔT6SS cells and disease severity, revealing how bacterial debris shape V. cholerae pathogenesis.

papers.title: A single-cell atlas of pediatric undifferentiated recurrent fever reveals candidate immune regulators
papers.abstract: Jung et al. present a single-cell immune atlas of 29 children with syndrome of undifferentiated recurrent fever (SURF). The resource reveals a persistent inflammatory signature even in the absence of fever and identified a monocyte NAMPT-TLR4 feedback loop as a candidate signaling axis implicated in the condition.

papers.title: Intermittent fasting enhances muscle regeneration via an EDA2R-NIK-myomixer axis
papers.abstract: Skeletal muscle injury triggers regeneration. Arabaci et al. demonstrate that intermittent fasting accelerates this process in mice by expanding the satellite cell population and stimulating myogenic gene expression in progenitors. These effects depend on EDA2R-NIK signaling, which drives myogenic fusion via Myomixer, highlighting a potential therapeutic strategy for muscle repair.

papers.title: eHLAstic reveals an extended canonical and non-canonical HLA-E immunopeptidome in human cancers
papers.abstract: Liao et al. develop eHLAstic, an HLA-E ligand predictor, enabling the discovery and experimental validation of an expanded HLA-E peptide repertoire. Canonical and non-canonical ligands recur across individuals and cancers, with non-canonical ligands predominantly associated with cancer. This expanded repertoire offers new opportunities for HLA-E-directed immune recognition and therapeutic targeting.

papers.title: Clearing perivascular light chain-derived amyloid to counteract aging-associated decline in liver regeneration
papers.abstract: Zhang et al. show that aging drives perivascular light chain-derived amyloid deposition, which activates the endothelial immunoproteasome, leading to degradation of pro-angiogenic TAZ and subsequent impairment of liver regeneration. Removal of these amyloid deposits suppresses this aberrant activation and restores regenerative capacity in aged mice.

papers.title: 5-Azacytidine incorporation into mRNAs disrupts translation and induces ribosome collisions
papers.abstract: Roberson et al. show that the nucleoside analog chemotherapeutic, 5-Azacytidine, incorporates into mRNAs and disrupts translation. This translational perturbation is caused by 5-Azacytidine-induced ribosome collisions, which activate disome-mediated signaling. Further, loss of the ribosome-associated quality control factor, ZNF598, increases sensitivity to 5-Azacytidine, collectively supporting a role for RNA damage in 5-Azacytidine-induced cytotoxicity.

papers.title: Hyperosmotic stress induces rewiring of 3D chromatin interactions
papers.abstract: Flores et al. show that hyperosmotic stress temporarily rewires three-dimensional chromatin structure, causing widespread loss of existing loops and formation of promoter-enriched loops that require cohesin but not CTCF. These structural changes precede delayed expression of genes located at stress-induced loop anchors.

papers.title: Plagl2 reprograms adult mouse retinal Müller glia for proliferation and injury-enhanced neurogenic competence
papers.abstract: Masaki et al. show that Plagl2 reprograms quiescent adult mouse Müller glia into a proliferative, late retinal progenitor-like state. Retinal injury further promotes neurogenic competence toward inner retinal neuronal identities. These findings indicate Plagl2 as a regulator capable of activating regenerative programs that mammalian Müller glia normally fail to engage.

papers.title: Temporal shifts in post-asthmatic immune responses define tumor outcomes via strain-specific monocyte reprogramming
papers.abstract: While acute asthma uniformly accelerates tumor growth, its resolution triggers strain-dependent divergence. Wang et al. show that post-asthmatic recovery reprograms hematopoietic progenitors, imprinting divergent monocyte functionality: BALB/c monocytes engage an mTOR-glycolysis axis to clear tumors, whereas C57BL/6 counterparts rely on oxidative phosphorylation that promotes progression.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial characterization of the human pancreas in cystic fibrosis
papers.abstract: Mummey et al. combine single-cell multiome and spatial transcriptomic profiling to reveal how cystic fibrosis affects cellular regulation in the human pancreas. They identify altered cellular signaling in areas of tissue damage that promotes beta cell dysfunction and loss, highlighting therapeutic opportunities.

papers.title: Perivascular macrophages restrict CXCR4-dependent accumulation of stem-like CD8+ T cells in tumors and limit chemotherapy efficacy
papers.abstract: Cheung et al. show that HO-1 expressed by PvTAMs restricts the post-chemotherapy accumulation of stem-like CD8+ T cells in the TME. These cells enter tumors through a CXCR4-dependent pathway associated with chemotherapy-expanded CXCL12+ PvCAFs. Once within the TME, they differentiate into anti-tumor effectors, contributing to durable anti-tumor immunity.

papers.title: Astrocytes drive stroke-induced glioma progression
Linking kinase inhibitors for greater selectivity
Innate immune memory in mucosa: where is it encoded?
papers.abstract: Trained immunity describes the capacity of innate immune cells to develop memory-like responses following a prior challenge. Early studies focused on myeloid cells and bone marrow progenitors. Extension of this concept to mucosal tissues, however, presents a more complex picture. These barrier sites harbor diverse, long-lived immune populations that interact with structural cells and neuronal circuits to actively shape immune responses. Emerging evidence suggests that memory-like programs extend beyond immune cells to include epithelial, stromal, and neuronal compartments. We propose that trained immunity in mucosal surfaces is distributed across the tissue ecosystem, encompassing progenitors, tissue-resident populations, and the tissue niche. This expanded framework redefines innate immune memory and has important implications for infections and chronic inflammatory diseases.

papers.title: Tracing the spread of Germanic languages using ancient genomics
papers.abstract: Germanic languages, including German, English, Frisian, Dutch and the Nordic languages, are widely spoken across northwest Europe. However, the timing and location of the prehistoric arrival of this Indo-European linguistic phylum, as well as its Iron Age diversification, remain contentious1–3. Here, by sequencing 712 ancient human genomes and analysing them alongside 4,009 previously published genomes, we identify an archaeologically elusive population that entered Sweden, likely from the Baltic region, by around 4000 bp. This population, which became widespread throughout Scandinavia by 3500 bp, offers a potential vector for the introduction of the Germanic language group to Scandinavia4–6, some 800 years later than traditionally assumed7–9. Following the Late Iron Age disintegration of Germanic into its descendant languages, we observe by 1650 bp a southward migration from southern Scandinavia into presumed Celtic-speaking areas, including present-day Germany, Poland and the Netherlands. During the subsequent Migration Period (1575–1375 bp), we see this ancestry among Germanic-speaking Anglo-Saxons in Britain and Langobards in southern Europe. In the same time period, we identify a related large-scale northward back-migration into Denmark and southern Sweden, coinciding with the rise of Danish influence and the linguistically documented emergence of Old Norse. These findings indicate that multiple migrations and geographical locations had a major role in the arrival and formation of Germanic, as well as in its divergence into historical and modern descendant languages. Analysis of newly sequenced and previously published ancient human genomes identifies migrations associated with the spread of the Germanic language group, from its arrival in Scandinavia 4,000 years ago, through to its diversification during the historical period.

papers.title: Varied forms of mutant tRNA mistranslation produce distinct phenotypes across multiple model organisms
papers.abstract: Mutant tRNA mistranslation is a phenomenon in which specific tRNA gene mutations cause translational errors wherein amino acids incorporated during translation differ from those coded by mRNA sequences. The biological consequences of mutant tRNA mistranslation are highly complex and contextual, but are often deleterious. Importantly, many variables exist that are likely to affect the outcomes of any one mutant mistranslating tRNA; biochemical characteristics of the exchanged amino acids, frequency of use, identity of mistranslated products, and so on. Here, we generate a carefully curated array of tRNA mutants to assess which characteristics of mistranslating tRNA variants are most predictive of deleterious phenotypes. We find that toxicity often arises from mutant tRNAs that induce dramatic changes in biochemical properties between exchanged amino acids, as well as mistranslation that occurs more frequently. Importantly, exceptions are also observed to each of these general rules, implying instead that some deliriousness may arise from more granular, product-specific mechanisms. Additionally, quantification of mistranslation via mass spectrometry demonstrates a weak relationship between quantity of mistranslated products and severity of toxic phenotypes. Lastly, despite previous establishment of mutant mistranslating tRNA models in Drosophila melanogaster, incorporation of higher frequency mistranslating tRNA variants was largely unsuccessful, and incorporation of lower frequency mistranslating tRNA variants produces no detectable developmental phenotypes. These experiments support the notion that although general rules may be capable of reasonably predicting their consequences, each mistranslating tRNA variant warrants individual consideration and investigation for thorough understanding of its biological outcomes and precise mechanisms of toxicity.

papers.title: Perturbation-induced gene programs map the hidden regulatory architecture of complex diseases
papers.abstract: Steady-state molecular profiles incompletely capture the regulatory programs through which genetic variation influences complex disease, particularly programs that emerge only when cells are perturbed. Here, we introduce Perturbscape, a computational framework that learns multiscale gene programs for individual perturbations in a CRISPR Perturb-seq screen using linear and nonlinear contrastive approaches alongside complementary program-learning methods, and integrates them with human genetics to prioritize disease-relevant genes, perturbations and downstream regulatory pathways. Across 15,859 perturbation-by-context profiles from 7 Perturb-seq systems and 53 complex diseases and traits (mean GWAS N=291K), perturbation-induced programs showed up to 4.3-fold higher heritability informativeness than analogous steady-state multi-tissue gene prioritization, and retained significant conditional heritability informativeness across all 34 matched cell system-trait comparisons after accounting for steady-state prioritization. Preserving perturbation-specific programs further yielded 2.5-5.3-fold higher trait relevance scores than programs derived from control cells, pooled perturbations or differential-expression summaries. In K562, Perturbscape-prioritized genes showed stronger enrichment for rare-variant burden genes than steady-state prioritization and were supported by orthogonal enhancer CRISPRi screens. In HepG2, LDL cholesterol-associated perturbation-induced programs specifically revealed statin-responsive pathways not significantly enriched by steady-state PoPS prioritization, supported by pharmacological transcriptional responses and population plasma proteomics. Perturbscape also recovered blood-related trait-conditioned trans-regulatory relationships that were specifically supported by population trans-eQTLs in IFN-gamma-stimulated monocytes (OR = 1.30, P=1.6e-05). Perturbscape further revealed developmental-stage-specific convergence between monogenic diabetes regulators and polygenic T2D risk during pancreatic islet differentiation, and neuronal-subclass-specific autism-associated regulatory programs in vivo. Together, these findings establish perturbation-induced gene programs as a complementary layer of disease-relevant regulatory information, revealing genetically informative pathways and context-specific regulatory relationships incompletely represented by steady-state molecular atlases.

papers.title: Urban enrichment of molestus ancestry and opposing temperature clines in a metropolitan Culex pipiens hybrid zone
papers.abstract: Hybridization between ecologically distinct lineages can fuel rapid adaptation when introgressed alleles are locally favored. The North American Culex pipiens assemblage, a principal West Nile virus vector east of the Mississippi, comprises three lineages---temperate Cx. pipiens f. pipiens, urban-specialist Cx. pipiens f. molestus, and subtropical Cx. quinquefasciatus---that meet in a mid-Atlantic hybrid zone where temperature and urbanization gradients intersect. Using whole-genome Pool-seq of 24 field populations and three lineage-reference pools across the Baltimore--Washington corridor, we find a weakly differentiated, Cx. pipiens f. pipiens-like background, richer in molestus- and quinquefasciatus-like ancestry toward the warmer end of the corridor. Urbanization impacts allele frequencies across the genome: molestus-like ancestry rises with impervious surface, independently of temperature and position, while Cx. quinquefasciatus-like ancestry does not. An 11.6 Mb chromosome 3 inversion is molestus-like in every population, most of all in urban ones, and tracks genome-wide molestus-like ancestry. Temperature acts locus by locus. On chromosome 1, a cluster of six CYP6 paralogs, a family implicated in insecticide resistance and thermal-stress response, shows rising Cx. quinquefasciatus-like ancestry and read depth with temperature. A chromosome 2 interval centered on a Yan ortholog, a repressor of cell differentiation, shows non-quinquefasciatus ancestry increasing with temperature, consistent with selection against Cx. quinquefasciatus-like introgression. Urban populations therefore carry more ancestry from the human-commensal lineage, while temperature moves Cx. quinquefasciatus ancestry both ways at individual loci. Both molestus and Cx. quinquefasciatus donors carry human-contact traits, so these patterns bear on how warming and urbanization will reshape arboviral risk.

papers.title: LplA-mediated rescue of lethal myopathy and cardiomyopathy in mitochondrial lipoylation-deficient mammalian caused by Lipt1
papers.abstract: Inherited mitochondrial metabolic disorders impair cellular energy generation and often lead to fatal metabolic crises. Mitochondrial lipoylation defects represent a severe case of such disorders that can lead to lethality but lacks effective treatment so far. In this study, we generated a viable mouse model with muscle-specific deficiency of the lipoyltransferase coded by Lipt1 to provide an in vivo preclinical model that overcomes embryonic lethality. Using this model, we examined a bacterial lipoate protein ligase A (LplA)-mediated gene therapy via adeno-associated virus (AAV) delivery. By introducing LplA alongside lipoic acid supplementation, we reconstituted a salvage pathway that bypasses the mammalian endogenous lipoylation pathway. The intervention rescued premature lethality, recovered motor function and reversed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in the Lipt1-deficient mouse model. Mechanistically, AAV-LplA reconstitutes mitochondrial protein lipoylation and oxidative phosphorylation in situ. This energetic rescue suppresses phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)-Akt hyperactivation, thereby restoring autophagic clearance and subsequently contributing to the recovery of the pathological phenotype. This study established AAV-LplA as a promising gene-delivery strategy for rescuing lethal mitochondrial lipoylation disorders.

papers.title: A noncanonical function of Dicer fuels self-dsRNA-driven inflammation
papers.abstract: Self-derived double-stranded RNAs (self-dsRNAs) can drive autoinflammation, but how structurally constrained self-dsRNAs become immunostimulatory remains unclear. We identify a noncanonical role for Dicer and a broad requirement for LGP2 in this process. Dicer is required for responses to self-dsRNAs, but not exogenous dsRNAs, that arise from defects in RNA editing, splicing, epigenetic silencing, or mitochondrial RNA degradation in multiple cell types, including a human stem cell-derived model of neuroinflammation. Independently of microRNA biogenesis, Dicer promotes activation of MDA5, PKR, and OAS-RNase L. Dicer binds immunostimulatory dsRNAs and uses its catalytic activity to generate shorter duplexes with accessible ends that are available for LGP2 end-binding, enabling MDA5 filament assembly. Thus, Dicer converts short, structurally constrained self-dsRNAs into inflammatory ligands, thereby facilitating their recognition as danger-associated signals.

papers.title: Squalene as a Candidate Signalling Molecule: Computational Evidence for a Predicted KEAP1 Interaction and Implications for Stress-Induced Altruistic Stem-Cell Niche Protection
papers.abstract: Stem and progenitor cells exposed to cytotoxic stress must preserve both their own viability and the functional integrity of their surrounding niche. Previous investigations from our laboratory have described stress-adapted altruistic stem-cell phenotypes and demonstrated the cytoprotective potential of squalene in normal haematopoietic and mesenchymal progenitor cells through preservation of glutathione homeostasis. More recent studies have associated hypoxia-driven changes in squalene metabolism with intracellular squalene accumulation and protection against lipid peroxidation, while independent experimental evidence has implicated NRF2 in squalene-mediated cytoprotection. However, the molecular basis through which squalene may engage the NRF2 regulatory pathway remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the structural feasibility of a potential interaction between squalene and the KEAP1 Kelch domain using molecular docking across three human KEAP1 crystal structures (PDB IDs: 6TYM, 6SP4 and 5CGJ). The docking protocol was evaluated through native-ligand redocking, yielding RMSD values of 0.826, 0.277 and 0.303 A, respectively. Squalene was consistently accommodated within the canonical hydrophobic cavity, with predicted docking scores of 7.905, 7.513 and 6.756 kcal/mol. The predicted interaction environment was predominantly hydrophobic and involved residues including Arg415, Arg380 and Asn414, without conventional hydrogen-bond formation. These findings support the structural feasibility of squalene accommodation within the KEAP1 Kelch domain and provide a testable hypothesis connecting stress-responsive squalene metabolism with potential KEAP1 NRF2 regulation. However, docking alone does not establish direct binding, physiological accessibility, KEAP1 inhibition or functional NRF2 activation. Further biophysical, molecular-dynamics and cellular investigations are required to establish the biological significance of the predicted interaction.

papers.title: Aggregate Deep Visual Proteomics reveals selective organization of α-synuclein inclusions
papers.abstract: -Synuclein inclusions, the lesions typical of Parkinson's disease, have been interpreted as protective deposits, toxic species or failed degradation products, each predicting a different composition and correlating that enrichment with neuron dysfunction and eventual degeneration. Distinguishing them requires measuring what an inclusion concentrates relative to the cell that built it. Here we developed Aggregate Deep Visual Proteomics, which uses ultrasensitive mass spectrometry to profile laser-microdissected inclusions against the remainder of the same cell or a matched host. In HEK293 cells, iPSC-derived dopaminergic neurons and post-mortem patient brain, each inclusion concentrated a selective subset of its cell's proteome, independent of abundance and dominated by membrane, in neurons largely presynaptic. Inclusions took up whole assemblies, with subunits moving together in 421 of 438 complexes, and the V-ATPase alone was enriched in all three systems. Degradation cargo stayed with the receptors that route it, consistent with sequestration and failed degradation acting together. Neuritic and somatic inclusions differed, the former rich in UBQLN2 and the latter in intermediate filaments. In the cell line, phosphorylated -synuclein was tenfold higher in the inclusion than in the rest of the cell, with about one third of the rise already present before an inclusion was visible. Measured against its host, the composition of an inclusion becomes a readout of how it formed and a source of candidate markers and therapeutic targets.

papers.title: COSMOS: integrated vector-pathogen metagenomics for mosquito-borne disease
papers.abstract: By 2050, almost half of the global population will be at risk of mosquito-borne disease. Effective response requires monitoring both pathogen transmission and vector abundance, yet these are typically assessed using separate assays with limited taxonomic breadth. Here we present COSMOS (COmprehensive Sequencing for MOSquito-borne disease), a targeted metagenomics workflow designed to reconstruct pathogen genomes and mosquito community composition directly from mixed field-collected samples. Over three annual rounds of a major Australian surveillance program, we evaluated >120,000 mosquitoes in 219 traps, with 98.7% agreement with surveillance data across seven monitored arboviruses, and additional detections of Sindbis virus and the state's first detection of encephalitic Little Sussex virus. Of 137 viral detections, 101 yielded near-complete genomes (>90% coverage) at median 95x depth. Using an accompanying computational workflow, COSMOS quantified mosquito composition, matching entomological estimates of reported vector species (CCC 0.78-0.89). Joint analysis of virus and vector composition identified structured mosquito communities associated with spatial and temporal environmental variation, allowing the ecological context of arbovirus detections to be characterised. Detections during the Murray Valley encephalitis virus outbreak in 2023 were concentrated within a narrowly defined mosquito-community space corresponding to rural communities dominated by the inland S-AUS sub-lineage of Culex annulirostris. Integrated vector-pathogen metagenomics provides ecological and evolutionary context for arbovirus activity within a single scalable workflow for surveillance and outbreak response.

In vitro–reconstituted Drosophila Arc capsids deliver gene editors to dystrophic muscle
papers.abstract: The intracellular delivery of therapeutic macromolecules remains a major challenge in biomedicine. Capsid-forming proteins are one promising vehicle, but to date, these have required cellular assembly or rely on fusogens for cell entry, limiting their scalability and utility. Here we reconstitute the Drosophila melanogaster Arc1 (dArc1) retroelement-derived capsid entirely from purified recombinant protein components and in vitro transcribed RNA, creating a fully defined, cell-free assembled protein nanoparticle system. We engineered the dArc1 RNA-binding domain to efficiently encapsulate both mRNA payloads and Cas9 ribonucleoproteins. We show that dArc1 capsids bind mammalian cells through a direct interaction with the surface receptor SORCS2. Leveraging this interaction, we demonstrate that intramuscular injection of dArc1 capsids carrying Cas9 gene editors achieves up to 18% exon skipping and restores dystrophin expression in muscle fibers of mdx mice, a model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy. This work demonstrates the potential of in vitro-assembled protein nanoparticles for delivery of molecular cargoes. Capsid-forming proteins are promising vehicles for macromolecule delivery, but have required cellular assembly or fusogens for entry. Here, authors assemble Drosophila Arc1 capsids cell-free, show entry via the receptor SORCS2, and deliver Cas9 editors that restore dystrophin in mdx mice.

papers.title: Precision probabilistic mapping reveals personalized functional topography in the early postnatal human brain
papers.abstract: Human adults exhibit remarkable individual differences in the brain’s functional topography, yet how such individualized topography emerges and shapes long-term cognition remains unknown. Using multimodal neuroimaging data of 419 infants (367 term-born; 52 preterm-born) from the Developing Human Connectome Project, we characterize personalized functional topographies in the neonate brain and evaluate their ability to predict 18-month neurocognitive outcomes. We find that typical functional topographies are present at birth, with interindividual variability organized along a sensorimotor-to-association hierarchy. These individualized maps encode early brain maturity and predict cognitive, language, and motor outcomes in early childhood, with the most predictive features localized to sensorimotor network boundaries. This functional refinement is structurally anchored by concurrent maturation in cortical myelination and sulcal depth. Preterm birth is associated with topographic alterations featuring atypical association network maturation. Our findings establish a foundational framework for precision modelling of early brain development and its influences on long-term cognitive trajectories. Using resting-state fMRI, this study maps individualized functional topographies in the neonatal brain that encode early maturity, predict neurocognitive outcomes at 18 months, parallel cortical structural maturation, and are altered by preterm birth.

papers.title: MMC-seq enables efficient long-read eccDNA profiling from low-input samples
papers.abstract: Extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA) comprises diverse DNA circles outside chromosomes, yet limited material constrains their analysis. Here, we present Multi-Modal Circle-seq (MMC-seq), integrating optimised enrichment with PacBio HiFi sequencing, and CircleSeeker for reconstructing and classifying unique-locus, multi-locus and chimeric circles. Workflow optimisation increases detection 38.7-fold in matched 300,000-cell preparations; CircleSeeker achieves F1 scores above 96% in platform-matched human unique-locus simulations. MMC-seq profiles single-cell preparations and frozen tumour tissue, and supports a size-based readout from 100 μL of plasma. One gliosarcoma yields over a million eccDNAs, including nested circles within an EGFR amplification region. In cell lines, ≤5-kb unique-locus circles show largely replicate-specific junctions but reproducible density landscapes and cell-line-specific hotspots. Multi-locus circles reflect host repeat architecture; intra-chromosomal chimeric circles have median genomic spans of 8.0 Mb in human but 31–94 kb in three plant species. This framework makes eccDNA diversity accessible from limited material and biologically interpretable through structural classification. Comprehensive eccDNA profiling remains constrained by differences in protocol, input requirement and sensitivity. Here, the authors present Multi-Modal Circle-seq (MMC-seq), an efficient long-read approach for profiling and classifying eccDNA from low-input samples.

papers.title: Podocyte-derived palmitic acid drives p53 S-palmitoylation and CD103+ CD4+ T cell differentiation in humanized mouse model of systemic lupus erythematosus
papers.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) involves massive immune cell infiltration and progressive renal injury, yet the mechanisms by which the local niche programs T cell residency remain unclear. Here, by combining analysis of single-cell datasets from LN patients and studies in humanized SLE chimeras, we report a marked accumulation of pathogenic CD4+CD103+ T cells that strongly correlates with disease activity. Mechanistically, SLE-associated podocytes undergo aberrant fatty acid oxidation (FAO) and transfer soluble palmitic acid to infiltrating CD4+ T cells, thereby promoting p53 S-palmitoylation, p53-dependent Runx3 transcription and CD103+ T cell differentiation, ultimately amplifying local immune responses. Notably, targeted inhibition of podocyte FAO reduces CD103+ T cell accumulation and alleviates renal inflammation in humanized chimeras. Collectively, our findings define a stromal-immune metabolic axis within the autoimmune kidney microenvironment, positioning podocyte fatty acid metabolism as a potential therapeutic target for LN. CD103+ CD4+ T cells mediate renal tissue injury in lupus nephritis (LN). To date, the mechanism instructing pathogenic CD103+ CD4+ T cell differentiation remains elusive. Here, the authors show that LN-associated podocytes undergo fatty acid oxidation reprogramming and release palmitic acid, thereby promoting p53 S-palmitoylation and Runx3 transcription in CD4⁺ T cells, ultimately sustaining pathogenic CD103⁺ T cell differentiation.

Systematic screen of RNA binding proteins that enhance circular RNA translation
papers.abstract: Translatable circular RNAs (circRNAs) have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional mRNA therapy due to their improved stability that results in a prolonged expression window. The translation of circRNAs is mainly driven by internal ribosome entry site (IRES) or IRES-like elements, which is tightly regulated by various trans-acting RNA binding proteins (RBPs). Here we develop a cell-based system to systematically screen RBPs that enhance translation of circRNAs, identifying 68 proteins as putative activators of noncanonical translation. These translation activators are involved in a broad range of biological processes including RNA processing, ribosomal biogenesis, and translation initiation. We further design a machine learning algorithm to extract common sequence features of these activators and predict more potential RBPs with translation activator activities. The newly identified and predicted activators are subsequently validated to promote the IRES-mediated circRNA translation in a context-dependent fashion. Overall, this study provides new insights into IRES-related trans-acting factors and expands the toolbox for engineered RBPs in RNA synthetic biology. Circular RNAs are promising therapeutics due to their stability. Here, the authors identified 68 RNA-binding proteins that enhance circRNA translation, built a predictive machine learning model, and showed these activators promote IRES-driven translation in a context-dependent manner, expanding tools for circRNA therapeutics.

papers.title: Highly efficient and durable Ga-doped Ni/Al2O3 catalyst enhanced by interfacial Ga3+ for low-temperature ammonia decomposition
papers.abstract: Ammonia is a promising hydrogen carrier for producing COx-free hydrogen. However, its decomposition suffers from high reaction temperatures. This study reveals that trace Ga doping markedly boosts the low-temperature activity of Ni/Al2O3 catalyst for ammonia decomposition. The Ga-doped Ni/Al2O3 catalyst achieves 92.0% ammonia conversion at 500 oC and weight hourly space velocity (WHSV) = 30,000 mL gcat−1 h−1. Kinetic experiments demonstrate that the introduction of Ga species alleviates catalyst hydrogen poisoning. Further studies confirm that Ga preferentially segregates on the catalyst surface and disperses around Ni nanoparticles. Interfacial Ga species facilitate hydrogen spillover from Ni to the Al2O3 support, which promotes the enrichment of adsorbed N* species and reduces their recombination temperature on the Ni surface. This work develops an efficient and stable Ni-based catalyst for low-temperature ammonia decomposition and provides a strategy for optimizing catalytic performance via the regulation of interfacial hydrogen transfer. Ammonia could enable carbon-free hydrogen production, but efficient decomposition at low temperatures remains difficult. Trace gallium helps nickel catalysts remove surface hydrogen, markedly boosting low temperature activity.

papers.title: Seagrass sediment organic carbon burial rates are globally significant
papers.abstract: Crucial for coastal carbon sequestration, global seagrass organic carbon (OC) burial rates remain uncertain as early estimates were derived from mixed methodologies across geographically and taxonomically biased datasets. Here, we present a data-driven reassessment from a synthesis of 332 sediment cores spanning the last century. Results show that seagrasses bury OC at 25 ± 3 g OC m−2 yr−1 (geometric mean), with an area-weighted global average of 33 ± 9 g OC m−2 yr−1. Rates reflect a balance between sediment OC content and sediment accumulation, which share a negative exponential relationship driven by mineral dilution. Based on a revised mapped seagrass extent (247,700–366,400 km2), global burial scales to 6–15 Tg C yr−1. Although one-fourth of earlier benchmarks, seagrasses account for 3–4% to 3–6% of total oceanic OC burial despite covering <0.1% of the seafloor. Combined with mangroves and tidal marshes, vegetated coastal ecosystems contribute 8–13% of oceanic OC burial. Reassessing global seagrass carbon burial via 332 sediment cores reveals an area-weighted average of 33 ± 9 g OC m-2 yr-1 (6-15 Tg C yr-1 globally). Despite covering <0.1% of the seafloor, seagrasses drive 3-6% of total oceanic organic carbon burial.

Driving catalysts to the intrinsic optical selectivity limit for accelerating photothermal catalysis
papers.abstract: Optimizing the photothermal conversion (maximized solar absorption, minimized mid-infrared emissivity) and catalytic activity is essential for constructing highly efficient photothermal catalysts. However, most catalysts lack intrinsic optical selectivity (i.e., high αsolar and low εMIR) and fail to suppress εMIR, which significantly compromises their catalytic performance. Herein, we propose an optical depth strategy to drive catalysts to their intrinsic optical selectivity limit. Demonstrated in metal oxides, this approach simultaneously maximizes αsolar and minimizes εMIR without compromising intrinsic catalytic activity. Demonstrated in the photothermal Sabatier and Bosch processes, our strategy increases methane production by ~590% and carbon nanotube yield by ~200%. Notably, the optimized Co2.85Ru0.15O4 optically selective catalyst exhibits a ~ 26.7% increase in photothermal conversion efficiency. This enhancement leads to a record CH4 production rate of 3375.5 mmol gcat−1 h−1 at a light intensity of 2.8 W cm−2. This innovative strategy highlights the prospects for achieving intrinsic optical selectivity in photothermal catalysts. Optimizing photothermal conversion and catalytic activity is crucial for developing highly efficient photothermal catalysts. Here, the authors propose an optical-depth strategy to drive catalysts toward their intrinsic optical selectivity limit, thereby enhancing the efficiency of photothermal catalysis.

Autoantibodies associate with clinical outcome in patients with melanoma treated with a dendritic cell-based vaccine
papers.abstract: Increased B cell receptor signaling pathways in patients with melanoma correlates with a favorable clinical response to a cancer vaccine expressing multiple tumor-associated antigens. Here, we utilize phage immunoprecipitation sequencing (PhIP-seq) and Rapid Extracellular Antigen Profiling (REAP) assays to analyze the autoantibody profiles of patients with melanoma from a dendritic cell vaccine trial (NCT01622933), before and after vaccination. Patients have significantly elevated breadth and titer of autoantibodies compared to healthy donors. Vaccination results in the induction of de novo autoantibodies, particularly those with a favorable clinical outcome. Reduced serum SDF1-alpha, MIP-1ß, MCP1 and increased circulating monocytes are associated with development of autoantibodies. We identify plasma autoantibody signatures separating melanoma from healthy subjects as well as clinical responders vs non-responders to vaccination treatment. These findings demonstrate the potential for autoantibodies as diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers that predict clinical outcomes in cancer. NCT01622933 was a clinical trial of an autologous dendritic cell-based vaccine in patients with melanoma. Here the authors show that the vaccine results in the induction of de novo autoantibodies associated with a favourable clinical outcome.

papers.title: UNMASC: modelling non-monotonic dose responses to cytokine combinations
papers.abstract: Computational and mathematical models are frequently used in the design of appropriate experimental protocols for in vitro cell differentiation assays. However, models are limited by typical monotonic dose-responses, preventing them from being used for cytokine effects that are largely non-monotonic. To address this shortcoming, we developed Uncovering Non-Monotonic Antagonistic and Synergistic Combinations (UNMASC), a mathematical model describing non-monotonic dose-response surfaces of cytokine interactions that distinguishes synergy of efficacy and potency. We demonstrate that our approach successfully recapitulates non-monotonic observed dose-response surfaces characterizing in vitro T cell progenitor differentiation. Our results show that interleukin (IL)3 and IL7 have antagonistic effects alone but are synergistic in combination. Altogether, UNMASC can aid in the efficient design of cell generation assays and extends drug interaction surfaces to a broader range of dose-responses. The authors present UNMASC, a model that captures non-monotonic cytokine combination effects. Applied to T cell development, UNMASC extends drug interaction surfaces to a broader range of dose-responses.

papers.title: Pressure-driven regime shifts in graphitization rewrite carbon fate during metamorphism
papers.abstract: The fate of organic carbon at convergent margins depends in part on its transformation into relatively inert graphite, yet the influence of precursor composition remains poorly constrained. Here we show that two organic precursors, vitrinite and liptinite, follow distinct graphitization pathways under high-pressure and high-temperature conditions. Vitrinite undergoes progressive structural ordering, whereas liptinite transforms more slowly at intermediate pressures owing to inherited defects and inhibited structural coalescence. Although both precursors respond strongly to pressure, their chemistry governs transitions between the processes that ultimately limit transformation rates. In this work, we develop a precursor-specific kinetic framework that integrates graphitization along geological pressure-temperature histories. Applications to representative Alpine tectonic units indicate that graphitization can continue during post-peak decompression or reheating. Precursor-dependent path integration further influences the modeled partitioning between graphite-like carbon and low-order reactive carbon fluxes. These results highlight how precursor chemistry and geological history jointly control carbon ordering, retention potential, and flux partitioning at convergent margins. This study demonstrates that pressure, metamorphic duration and organic precursor type are key controls on graphitization. The resulting kinetic framework provides constraints on carbon retention and structural partitioning during metamorphism and subduction.

papers.title: Nanoscopic cation heterogeneity dictates the ambient stability of halide perovskites
papers.abstract: Ambient instability in formamidinium-caesium mixed-cation perovskites limits the efficiency and long-term durability of solar cells, yet its nanoscopic origin remains unclear. Using quasi-in situ scanning transmission electron microscopy, we identify Cs-enriched grain triple junctions as intrinsic weak points under ambient exposure, where Cs⁺ segregation and phase separation initiate. This localized instability induces structural disordering and δ-CsPbI3 crystallization, which propagates into neighboring grains, progressively degrading the perovskite matrix and interfacial optoelectronic properties. To suppress cation heterogeneity, we introduce N-Octylsulfobetaine, which regulates crystallization kinetics, promotes homogeneous cation distribution, and passivates grain boundaries, thereby enhancing resistance to water and oxygen intrusion. The resulting n-i-p perovskite solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.37% and retain 96.47% of initial performance after 2,200 h under ISOS-L-1l protocol. Our findings elucidate the nanoscopic ambient degradation pathways in FA-Cs perovskites, establishing a promising strategy for achieving robust perovskite photovoltaics combining high efficiency with long-term durability. The nanoscopic origin of the ambient instability in mixed-cation perovskites is unclear. Wang et al. identify Cs-enriched grain junctions as weak points and introduce N-Octylsulfobetaine to regulate crystallization kinetics. The resulting device achieves a power conversion efficiency of 26.37%.

papers.title: Alpha-aminoadipate in the saccharopine pathway promotes cancer metastasis through sumoylation of transcription machinery
papers.abstract: Despite studies linking metabolism and cancer, our understanding of the metabolite network that drives metastasis remains incomplete. Through a metabolic RNAi-based screen for cell invasion, we identify alpha-aminoadipate (2-AAA), the intermediate metabolite of aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase (AASS) in the saccharopine pathway, as a common pivotal factor in metastasis of human cancers. Metabolite-protein connectivity mapping reveals that 2-AAA binds to SAE1, a crucial component of the SUMO-activating enzyme E1, and enhances SAE1 recruitment to UBA2, facilitating sumoylation. 2-AAA-mediated sumoylation of the RNA polymerase subunit POLR2A then partially promotes cancer cell invasion by inducing the expression of metastasis-promoting genes, including SPG11 and KCTD7. Targeting AASS with cetalkonium chloride, a newly identified small molecule inhibitor against AASS, attenuates cancer cell invasion and tumor metastasis. Our study highlights the mechanism by which metastasis is mediated by metabolite-driven sumoylation and indicates AASS as an effective therapeutic target for mitigating metastatic cancer progression. The role of metabolism in metastasis remains unclear. Here, a metabolic RNAi-based screen for cell invasion and metabolite-protein connectivity mapping reveals a mechanism by which sumoylation driven by alpha-aminoadipate, the intermediate metabolite of aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase, drives metastasis.

Perioperative ivonescimab with or without chemotherapy in resectable non-small cell lung cancer: a phase 2 trial
papers.abstract: Resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) carries a high risk of postoperative recurrence, underscoring the need for effective perioperative therapies. This nonrandomized, noncomparative phase 2 trial evaluated neoadjuvant ivonescimab monotherapy (cohort 1) or in combination with chemotherapy (cohort 2), followed by surgery and adjuvant ivonescimab. In cohort 2, the major pathological response (MPR) rate was 70.1% (47/67; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 57.7–80.7); the lower bound of the 80% two-sided CI exceeded the historical control rate of 41% and the primary endpoint was met. The MPR rate in cohort 1 was 60.0% (6/10; 95% CI = 26.2–87.8). Among patients who achieved MPR, 83.3% (5/6) in cohort 1 and 97.9% (46/47) in cohort 2 had residual viable tumor (RVT) of ≤5%, respectively. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events (AEs) occurred in 36.4% (4/11) patients in cohort 1 and 30.4% (24/79) of those in cohort 2, with no grade 3 or higher hemorrhage or treatment-related death. Treatment-related surgery delay occurred in one (1.3%) patient. Surgery-related AEs related to ivonescimab occurred in 10.0% (1/10) and 10.4% (7/67) patients in the two cohorts, respectively, with no grade 3 or higher events reported. These data support perioperative ivonescimab with or without chemotherapy as a promising strategy for resectable NSCLC. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05247684 . In a nonrandomized phase 2 trial, patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer received perioperative ivonescimab as monotherapy or with chemotherapy, leading to encouraging pathological response rates in both cohorts, and sustained circulating tumor DNA negativity throughout neoadjuvant therapy may be predictive of response.

papers.title: RobPicker: a meta-learning framework for robust identification of macromolecules in cryo-electron tomograms
papers.abstract: Accurate particle picking of macromolecules of diverse types, shapes and sizes in cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) is critical for understanding the molecular architecture of biological systems in their native state. Current deep learning methods have shown potential for identifying macromolecules in tomograms; however, they are vulnerable to annotation noise in the training data and to imbalanced distributions of macromolecule species. Here, to address these limitations, we developed RobPicker, a meta-learning framework that effectively mitigates these issues by automatically learning to correct label errors and by placing greater emphasis on smaller and rarer macromolecule species. In evaluations across diverse cryo-ET datasets with noisy labels and imbalanced species distributions, RobPicker substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods, particularly in identifying small and rare macromolecules. The robustness and efficiency of RobPicker led to improved resolution in 3D density maps of protein structures, enabling high-resolution cellular structural biology analysis. RobPicker improves cryo-ET particle picking by correcting noisy labels and reweighting rare species, enabling robust detection of small macromolecules across diverse datasets.

Longitudinal single-cell profiling of breast tumors highlights immune and epigenetic mechanisms associated with sensitivity to aromatase inhibitors
papers.abstract: Estrogen receptor (ER)-positive breast cancer treatment is based primarily on endocrine therapy. To dissect mechanisms of sensitivity to aromatase inhibitors in ER-positive breast cancer, we profiled tumor biopsies from 25 patients during neoadjuvant therapy using single-cell RNA sequencing, immune receptor sequencing and enhancer activity mapping. Malignant cells with high ER signaling and elevated activity of enhancers with ER binding sites were sensitive to treatment. Resistance was associated with androgen receptor signaling, dedifferentiation and epithelial–mesenchymal transition. Poor responders preferentially used the androgen receptor cis-regulome under treatment pressure. The baseline tumor microenvironment was associated with tumor downstaging. Poor responders exhibited a ‘hot’, yet ineffective immune landscape enriched for naive lymphoid and undifferentiated myeloid cells. Good responders showed an active immune microenvironment with sustained clonal expansion of T cells. Our longitudinal single-cell analyses elucidate the genetic, cellular and epigenetic mechanisms driving sensitivity and resistance to neoadjuvant aromatase inhibition in ER-positive breast cancer. This longitudinal single-cell study of estrogen receptor (ER)-positive breast cancer suggests that strong estrogen signaling, ER-linked enhancers and active T cell responses could predict sensitivity to aromatase inhibitors, whereas resistance involves androgen signaling though hormone-sensing enhancer activity.

papers.title: The Participant Engagement and Cancer Genome Sequencing Network to accelerate research in rare and understudied cancers
authors: On behalf of the Participant Engagement and Cancer Genome Sequencing (PE-CGS) Network
papers.abstract: The genomic characterization of cancers has considerably advanced research and clinical practice. However, critical gaps remain, including limited knowledge of tumor profiles in rare cancers and populations understudied in genomic research and insufficient integration of genomic, clinical and epidemiologic data. This Perspective highlights the Participant Engagement and Cancer Genome Sequencing (PE-CGS) Network, established by the US National Cancer Institute to address knowledge gaps in rare and understudied cancers. PE-CGS comprises five research centers supported by a coordinating center and guided by an external advisory panel. Collaborations across PE-CGS are grounded in shared values of participant-centeredness, engagement, access, collaboration and innovation. Activities emphasize participant engagement throughout the research process, including the return of results and collection of clinical and epidemiologic data alongside paired tumor/germline sequencing. PE-CGS demonstrates how engagement, return of results and comprehensive data collection can be integrated to support participant-centered cancer genomics research and accelerate research in rare and understudied cancers. The Participant Engagement and Cancer Genome Sequencing (PE-CGS) Network integrates participant engagement, return of genomic results and comprehensive data collection to advance cancer genomics research involving rare and understudied cancers.

Bringing peroxisomes within reach
PerCap isolates native peroxisomes to reveal peroxisomal proteins and regulators
papers.abstract: Peroxisomes are highly heterogeneous organelles with remarkable functional diversity across species and tissues. Isolating peroxisomes is essential for proteomic investigating their biological roles and regulatory mechanisms. Here, we discover that the N-terminal region of ATF6α interacts directly with peroxisomal membrane protein ABCD1 and ABCD3 in vitro and develop an affinity-based strategy PerCap, leveraging these interactions to rapidly purify native peroxisomes. Using this approach, we isolated peroxisomes from human cells, validated their intactness and identified the potential peroxisomal proteins by proteomic analysis. We show that AKAP1, CPT1A and CYB5R1 also localize to peroxisomes and loss of AKAP1 affects peroxisome morphology. Peroxisomes were also isolated from mouse tissues to compare tissue-specific peroxisomal proteins. By monitoring peroxisomal proteome dynamics during Torin1-induced pexophagy, we identified UBE2V1 as a contributor to this process. In summary, PerCap enables isolation of native peroxisomes from human cells and mouse tissues for proteomic and functional analyses. Peroxisomes are organelles with remarkable functional diversity across species and tissues. A peroxisome capture method to enrich native peroxisomes from human cells and mouse tissues enables functional and proteomic analysis.

papers.title: Large-scale RNA-binding protein tethering screen discovers modulators of circular RNA metabolism
papers.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are emerging as important regulators in mammalian cells and promising substrates for RNA therapeutics, yet the trans-acting factors governing their metabolism remain poorly defined. Here we systematically evaluate 730 RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) using a tethered reporter assay and identify 281 RBPs that significantly modulate circRNA activity. Follow-up assays implicate these RBPs across key stages of the circRNA life cycle, including biogenesis, nuclear export, degradation and translation. We identify seven RBPs for tethered translation enhancement of therapeutically applicable circRNA vectors and highlight LARP4B as a potent enhancer of exogenous circRNA translation across multiple internal ribosomal entry sites and cell types. We uncover an evolutionarily conserved role for RBM15 in circRNA biogenesis in fly, mouse and human, further demonstrating a role in circRNA nuclear retention, and that perturbing RBM15 sites with dCasRx or antisense oligonucleotides modulates endogenous circRNA expression. Together, our study provides a global view of circRNA trans-regulation and describes practical entry points for therapeutic development. This study systematically evaluates proteins that control circular RNA production, stability and translation, revealing new regulators and strategies to enhance or suppress circular RNA activity for therapeutic development.

papers.title: Facet-dependent molecular adsorption modulates zinc anode work function for the favourable orientation of zinc electrocrystallization
papers.abstract: Additive-mediated orientation of Zn electrocrystallization is generally attributed to selective facet adsorption of the additives, yet this conventional wisdom is increasingly challenged by mounting literature counterexamples. Here we unravel the relationship between oriented Zn electrocrystallization and the atomic-scale physical variations of different Zn facets upon additive adsorption through extensive case-by-case experimental and computational investigations covering 29 additives. We confirm that the variation of work function upon facet-dependent additive adsorption is the governing factor for crystallographic orientation, achieving a prediction accuracy of 93.1%. This finding suggests a fundamental criterion for additive screening towards favourably oriented Zn electrocrystallization. In addition, further electrochemical investigations reveal that Zn electrocrystallization featuring preferred (100) orientation delivers outstanding cyclability even under harsh conditions of high current density (up to 20 mA cm−2) and deep cycling (depth of discharge >85%), which challenges the consensus that the (002) is the optimal orientation for practical Zn anodes. While additives direct Zn electrocrystallization and impact battery performance, the mechanism remains disputed. Now it has been shown that facet-dependent work function modulation upon additive adsorption governs Fermi-level equilibration and Zn crystallographic texture across 29 additives with 93.1% accuracy, providing an interfacial electronic descriptor for additive screening towards favourable Zn electrodeposition.

Scale-dependent pathways of the graphite-to-diamond transition
papers.abstract: The transformation from graphite to diamond is a paradigmatic pressure-induced structural phase transition in solids with fundamental insights in condensed matter physics, geoscience, and materials science. However, the atomistic pathway remains a subject of longstanding debate due to the challenge in observing the ultrafast nucleation process. To overcome the limitations of traditional high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) experiments, which rely on post-mortem analyses that obscure early-stage dynamics, here we combine metadynamics simulations with HPHT synthesis using dimensionally distinct carbon precursors to elucidate the microscopic nucleation and growth mechanisms. Our simulations reveal scale-dependent transformation pathways in which fluctuations in interlayer bonding precede the formation of persistent sp3-bonded diamond-like nuclei. Experimentally, by exploiting the radial confinement of multi-walled carbon nanotubes to suppress growth kinetics, we successfully capture the elusive nucleation stage, identifying 2–6 nm diamond nuclei. Using highly oriented pyrolytic graphite, we demonstrate a temperature-driven shift from interlayer to intralayer growth, which subsequently governs the genesis of twin boundaries and hexagonal diamond lamellae during final grain coalescence. These findings not only reconcile disparate theoretical models regarding the kinetic pathway but also establish a robust, precursor-mediated framework for the microstructural design of high-performance diamond materials. The study uncovers a scale-dependent graphite to-diamond pathway, showing that interlayer bonding fluctuations precede nucleation and precursor confinement captures nanoscale nuclei and regulates growth, providing a unified view of this transition.

papers.title: DNA-driven dimerization of Ku70/Ku80 regulates the synapsis of double-strand breaks by APLF
papers.abstract: Repair of double-strand breaks via non-homologous end joining requires the synapsis of DNA ends. APLF is emerging as an important repair factor, capable of forming synaptic bridges in the presence of the Ku70/Ku80 heterodimer. However, only a single one-to-one interaction between Ku70/Ku80 and APLF has been reported to date, which is fundamentally insufficient for synapsis. Moreover, it remains unclear how APLF-mediated bridging of Ku70/Ku80 heterodimers is prevented in the absence of double-strand breaks. Using a combination of single-molecule techniques, including Mass Photometry, Atomic Force Microscopy, and Magnetic and Optical Tweezers, we demonstrate that APLF-mediated synapsis requires threading of at least two Ku70/Ku80 heterodimers per DNA end. We show that this requirement stems from the need for a simultaneous interaction of two poly(ADP-ribose) binding Zinc Fingers in APLF with threaded poly(ADP-ribosyl)ated Ku70/Ku80s on a single DNA. We further provide evidence that long non-coding RNA NIHCOLE cooperatively binds up to four Ku70/Ku80, consistent with a synapsis efficiency enhancement mechanism based on the bridging of two Kus70Ku80s bound on both sides of the break. Our results propose a model for the physiological significance of Ku70/Ku80 threading and a regulatory mechanism based on multivalency that restricts APLF-mediated bridging to DNA-bound Ku70/Ku80. DNA synapsis is a crucial step in Non-Homologous End Joining. Through molecular-level quantification of the underlying interactions, this work reveals a regulatory mechanism for how APLF-mediated DNA synapsis is restricted to Ku when it is bound to damaged DNA.

papers.title: Neural autoantibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with schizophrenia spectrum disorders
papers.abstract: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders have substantial genetic liability, but their stable incidence and clinical heterogeneity leave open contributions from non-genetic mechanisms. Though autoimmune encephalitis demonstrates that anti-neural antibodies can cause psychosis, encephalitis antibodies are uncommon in schizophrenia. Here we show that multi-platform autoantigen profiling of cerebrospinal fluid and plasma detects rare, anti-neural autoantibodies in schizophrenia spectrum disorders. By antibody profiling the cerebrospinal fluid of 32 schizophrenia spectrum participants and 32 neuropsychiatrically unaffected controls by brain tissue immunostaining, immunoprecipitation–mass spectrometry, phage display immunoprecipitation sequencing, and plasma by complementary protein microarrays, we identify three autoantibodies, including to alpha-crystallin B. The anti-alpha-crystallin B antibody preferentially recognizes phosphorylated serine-45 and is absent from the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with untreated multiple sclerosis, a disease with frequent antibodies to unphosphorylated alpha-crystallin B. These findings do not define autoimmune psychosis as a new disease but support broader autoantibody searches in psychotic disorders. Autoimmunity has long been hypothesized in schizophrenia spectrum disorders, but antibodies diagnostic of autoimmune encephalitis are uncommon. Here, the authors show that multi-platform profiling detects rare anti-neural autoantibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with schizophrenia spectrum disorders.

papers.title: In vivo ultrasound–MRI 3D mapping of neuromuscular compartments reveals the neuromechanical architecture of finger-specific control
papers.abstract: Neuromuscular compartments provide the functional substrate for finger-specific motor control, yet their in vivo three-dimensional (3D) architecture remains unresolved because of the absence of clear fascial landmarks for imaging. Here, we present a multimodal imaging framework combining ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to provide volumetric compartment segmentation and in vivo architectural reconstruction of the flexor digitorum superficialis. During isolated finger flexion, tissue movement directions estimated from dynamic ultrasound delineate compartment contours, which are mapped into a 3D MRI reference to generate volumetric compartment masks. Using these masks as constraints, tractography reconstructs 3D fiber trajectories and yields compartment-specific architectural measurements. In ten healthy individuals, compartment topology and fiber orientations were consistent with classic cadaveric anatomy, and estimated compartments accurately predicted surface electromyography amplitude distributions. This framework provides 3D fiber trajectories and quantitative parameters for finger-specific computational models, establishing a foundation for subject-specific neuromuscular digital twins and next-generation neuromuscular interfaces. Finger-specific motor control depends on neuromuscular compartments whose architecture has remained unresolved. Here, the authors combine dynamic ultrasound and MRI to map the compartments in 3D, reconstruct fibre level architecture, and validate them with anatomy and electromyography.

papers.title: A geospatial approach to measuring economic activity
papers.abstract: We introduce a methodology to detect and measure economic activity using geospatial data and apply it to steel production, a major industrial pollution source worldwide. Combining plant output data with geospatial data, such as ambient air pollutants, nighttime lights, and temperature, we train machine learning models to predict plant locations and output. We identify about 88% (94%) of plants missing from the training sample within a 1 km (5 km) radius and achieve R2 above 0.8 for output prediction at a 1 km grid and at the plant level, as well as both regional and time series validations. We use the model trained on Chinese steel data to reliably detect the location and measure the total annual output of steel plants in South Korea and Iran. Our approach can be adapted to other industries and regions, and used by policymakers and researchers to track and measure industrial activity in near real time. Satellite signals of pollution, heat and night lights reveal where steel plants operate and how much they produce. Trained on Chinese plants, the method transfers to other countries, tracking industry in near real time.

papers.title: Tailoring modulus and hardness of AuAgCu alloys via three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures
papers.abstract: Tailoring elastic modulus of alloys or composites is typically achieved through composite or solute effects. In this work, we demonstrate that simultaneous enhancement of elastic modulus and hardness in Au50Ag20Cu30 alloys can be realized via elastic strain engineering, enabled by three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures (3D-CDSs) which was self-organized through spinodal decomposition. Microstructural characterization and nanoindentation testing confirm the alternating hydrostatic compressive or expansion strains associated with the coherent dual-phase structure. This strain modulation leads to significant enhancements in elastic modulus (by 27%) and hardness (by 37%) compared to solid solution phase. These results are consistent with theoretical predictions and molecular dynamics simulations. Our study presents a rational and effective strategy to simultaneously tailor high elastic modulus and mechanical strength through 3D elastic strain engineering. By simultaneous tuning of modulus and hardness via three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures, this work reveals the relationship between nanoscale phase structures, lattice strain, and mechanical response, enabling high-modulus and hardness within a model AuAgCu alloy.

papers.title: A critical role for the ER membrane complex (EMC) in lipid homeostasis
papers.abstract: The ER membrane complex (EMC) facilitates insertion of integral membrane proteins into the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) lipid bilayer. Recent years have seen significant progress in understanding the structural aspects of EMC, but the identity of EMC-client proteins and EMC’s functional roles throughout evolution remain less well understood. Here we delete the essential EMC3 subunit in the liver and adipose tissues of mice and examine the impact of EMC loss-of-function in a range of metabolic and lipid homeostasis models. The absence of EMC3 in either the liver or adipose tissues results in defective storage of triglycerides and perturbations in lipid droplet (LD) homeostasis. EMC-deficient adipose tissues have reduced ability to mediate fat storage in mice on a high-fat diet and are unable to support non-shivering thermogenesis. Proteomic analyses of EMC3-deficient tissues show reduced levels of FITM2, a key regulator of LD biogenesis and ER homeostasis, identifying FITM2 as an EMC client. Deletion of EMC3 in the Drosophila fat body reveals similar defects in LD homeostasis, which can be rescued by a FITM2 mutant whose biogenesis was EMC-independent. Together, our results indicate that the EMC plays a key evolutionarily conserved role in the biogenesis of machinery maintaining triglyceride storage in metazoans. The ER membrane complex inserts proteins into ER membranes, but its physiological roles are unclear. Here the authors show that it has an evolutionarily conserved role in fat storage, mediating insertion of the lipid droplet protein FITM2.

papers.title: Biphasic enzymatic reaction in coacervate-containing droplets
papers.abstract: Spatiotemporal compartmentalization is a powerful cellular strategy for concentrating biomolecules, buffering noise, and creating local niches, that enable robust information-processing and reaction cascades. While compartments formed by coacervation are known to modulate catalytic activity, how reaction kinetics and interphase mass transfer between the coacervate and the surrounding phase jointly regulate catalysis within these dynamically evolving compartments remains poorly understood. Here we introduce synthetic coacervate-containing droplets (CCDs)—microfluidically generated arrays of single droplets containing single coacervates in equilibrium with the dilute phase—to investigate coupled reaction-diffusion dynamics under confinement. Using CCDs formed by complex coacervation of oppositely charged polyelectrolytes, we quantify guest molecular partitioning and enzymatic dephosphorylation reactions within single droplets. By integrating spatiotemporal imaging, bulk kinetics, and mathematical modeling, we quantitatively link enzymatic activity to dynamic molecular redistributions across phases, revealing how reaction-driven fluxes regulate enzymatic reactions within biphasic droplets and demonstrating the noise buffering capability of the coacervate phase. Living cells organize biochemical processes through spatial compartmentalization, which concentrates key components and suppresses molecular noise. Here, the authors develop a synthetic coacervate-based model to dissect the dynamic equilibrium between condensed phases and their surroundings. By quantitatively linking reaction-diffusion behavior with molecular partitioning, they establish a unified framework connecting enzymatic kinetics to redistribution of substrates and products in confined mesoscopic environments.

papers.title: Spatial protein interactomics in solid primary human tissue
papers.abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) in diseased tissues represent a promising class of potential drug targets. However, PPIs are typically identified in live cells, lysate, and genetically engineered model organisms, limiting their translational value to human disease. Here we describe MAP-IT, an optimized photocatalytic carbene-based proximity labeling method for direct PPI mapping in primary human tissue sections, which bypasses the need for model organisms in the initial discovery step. We use MAP-IT to profile PPIs in situ for cell surface and nuclear target proteins, identify and orthogonally validate new interactors of EGFR in colon cancer, and couple light-powered MAP-IT labeling with spatially patterned visible light irradiation guided by neural network image segmentation to map location-specific protein interactomes. Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) represent a promising class of drug targets. Here, the authors describe MAP-IT, a photocatalytic carbene-based proximity labeling method for direct PPI mapping in primary human tissue sections.

papers.title: Endocannabinoid-mediated rescue of somatosensory cortex activity, plasticity and related behaviors following an early-life concussion in male mice
papers.abstract: Due to the assumed plasticity of the immature brain, early-life brain alterations are thought to lead to better recoveries in comparison to the mature brain. Despite clinical needs, how neuronal networks and associated behaviors are affected by early-life brain stresses, such as pediatric concussions, have been overlooked. Here we provide first evidence in male mice that a single early-life concussion durably increases neuronal activity in the somatosensory cortex into adulthood, disrupting neuronal integration while the animal is performing sensory-related tasks. This represents a clinically relevant mechanism that was previously unappreciated for understanding impairment of sensory-related behavior performance. We also demonstrate that pharmacological modulation of the endocannabinoid system a year post-concussion is well-suited to rescue neuronal activity and plasticity, and normalizes sensory-related behavioral performance. These findings identify persistent alterations in cortical sensory processing following early-life concussion and demonstrate that neuronal and behavioral deficits remain amenable to pharmacological intervention long after injury. Here authors show that a single pediatric concussion causes long-lasting disruptions in brain activity, plasticity and sensory behavior in mice. However, they show deficits can be reversed by targeting the endocannabinoid system after the initial injury.
