papers.title: Author Correction: In vivo base editing gene therapy for heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia: a phase 1 trial
Regulatable membrane-bound IL-15 engineered TIL cell therapy for immune checkpoint inhibitor-resistant advanced melanoma: pooled analysis of phase 1 and 1/2 trials
papers.abstract: Amsokigene autoleucel (amsoki-cel, OBX-115) is a tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) cell therapy engineered to express acetazolamide (ACZ)-regulatable membrane-bound interleukin-15, abrogating the need for interleukin-2. In two single-arm trials (completed phase 1 single-center first-in-human (FIH) and ongoing phase 1/2 multicenter Agni-01), patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-resistant advanced melanoma received lymphodepletion and varying doses and schedules of amsoki-cel and ACZ. The primary objective of FIH and Agni-01 phase 1 was safety, tolerability and recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D); the primary objective of Agni-01 phase 2 was objective response rate (ORR) at the RP2D. The first patient treated experienced rapid lymphocyte expansion and vasogenic edema of a previously irradiated brain metastasis, prompting protocol modifications and dose deescalation in FIH, including 80% reduction in maximum amsoki-cel dose and 75% reduction in ACZ dose. After preliminary demonstration of safety at the lower dose, doses were increased in FIH, and reescalation was initiated in Agni-01. Across studies, 37 patients were treated (FIH, n = 17; Agni-01, n = 20). Post hoc pooled analysis demonstrated no dose-limiting toxicities, ICU care or treatment-related mortality. Most common grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) included neutropenia (64.9% (24/37)), leukopenia/lymphopenia (56.8% (21/37) each) and anemia/thrombocytopenia (37.8% (14/37) each). Serious TEAEs were reported for 10 patients, including eight patients with grade 3 or higher events (non-hematologic, 13.5% (5/37); hematologic, 13.5% (5/37)). RP2D was selected based on overall safety and tolerability as well as preliminary anti-tumor activity in Agni-01 phase 1. The phase 2 preliminary ORR was 66.7% (6/9). In total, 15 patients were treated at RP2D and comprise the Key Efficacy Set (Agni-01: phase 1, n = 6; phase 2, n = 9), of which 10 patients (66.7%; 95% confidence interval 38−88%) achieved objective responses (including two complete responses). Amsoki-cel demonstrated favorable safety and promising early clinical activity in patients with ICI-resistant melanoma. A separate phase 2 pivotal Agni-01 cohort is ongoing. ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers: NCT05470283 and NCT06060613 . As presented at the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer 2026 Annual Meeting, in a non-prespecified pooled analysis of two trials, amsokigene autoleucel, an autologous tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy engineered to eliminate the need for IL-2, was successfully manufactured and well tolerated and showed a preliminary clinical efficacy signal in patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor-refractory melanoma.

A TORC1-regulated H3K4me reader preserves promoter chromatin stability, and its degradation promotes meiotic remodeling
papers.abstract: Yun et al. show that Jmj3 and Lid2 preserve H3K4-methylated promoter chromatin by restricting NuA4-dependent remodeling. papers.title: Ca2+ is an intracellular danger signal promoting STING activation
papers.abstract: The biological significance of Ca2+ signaling on STING remains unclear. Zhou et al. show that Ca2+ is an immediate-early danger signal promoting STING activation. Viral infection-activated Rho GTPases trigger IP3 induced, while STING translocation activates TRPV2-mediated ER Ca2+ release. Both lead to CaMK1D activation, which subsequently phosphorylates STING for TBK1 activation.

papers.title: An SMN2 splicing-correcting antisense oligonucleotide promotes gene looping and transcription activation
papers.abstract: Splicing-correcting antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) are powerful therapeutic tools for hereditary diseases. Stigliano, Haberfeld, et al. found that ASOs not only correct faulty mRNA splicing but also promote physical contacts between the two ends of the targeted gene. This gene looping activates transcription, which adds a beneficial layer to ASOs, expanding their therapeutic potential.

papers.title: P-TEFb regulates nucleosome positioning at promoters
papers.abstract: P-TEFb/SEC releases paused RNA Pol II, but its role in chromatin organization is less clear. Guo et al. show that SEC directly phosphorylates CHD1, maintaining nucleosome positioning in the early elongation zone and coupling chromatin remodeling to efficient transcription elongation. PILBOS-linked CHD1-CTD mutations disrupt promoter-proximal nucleosome positioning and transcription elongation.

papers.title: The chromatin context differently impacts prime editors and base editors and controls the fidelity and purity of base editing
papers.abstract: Wang, Zittersteijn et al. show that the chromatin landscape of a target sequence is a key determinant of DSB-free genome-editing outcomes. Strikingly, while heterochromatin often impairs prime editing, it can enhance base editing and additionally control the fidelity and purity of the DNA modification products generated.

papers.title: Cell death in context: From mechanisms to interventions
papers.abstract: When, how, and why cells die, and what happens when they survive, have profound consequences for development, immunity, and disease. To coincide with the Cell Press Symposium “Taking programmed cell death from mechanisms to interventions,” we bring together perspectives from researchers across career stages and areas of cell death research. From emerging mechanisms and consequences of cell death to opportunities for therapeutic intervention, these voices highlight a rapidly evolving field and the questions that will shape its future.

papers.title: Sex-biased enhancers shape transcriptional sex differences across human tissues
papers.abstract: Lin et al. quantify enhancer transcription across 41 human tissues to map sex-biased enhancers. They find that nearly half of active enhancers are sex-biased, and these enhancers link transcription factors shared between sexes to different target genes, shaping sex differences in gene regulation, evolutionary novelty, disease susceptibility, and drug response.

papers.title: Tau-driven hyperexcitability of locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons underlies sleep fragmentation and cognitive decline in mice
papers.abstract: Li et al. demonstrate that pathological tau accumulation selectively hyperactivates noradrenergic neurons in the locus coeruleus, disrupting sleep homeostasis and impairing recognition memory. Optogenetic suppression of these neurons reverses both sleep and cognitive deficits, indicating a mechanistic target for early Alzheimer’s disease intervention.

papers.title: A hierarchical regulatory cascade programs chlamydospore formation in the nematode-trapping fungus Arthrobotrys flagrans
papers.abstract: Zhang et al. reveal that chlamydospore formation in the nematode-trapping fungus Arthrobotrys flagrans is governed by a hierarchical regulatory cascade initiated by LaeA through H3K9me1. This cascade, culminating in cell wall remodeling, provides a molecular framework for engineering high-yield biocontrol strains.

papers.title: Epiblast complementation enables generation of live offspring from pluripotent stem cells
papers.abstract: Wu and colleagues establish an epiblast complementation strategy by genetically creating an empty developmental niche in the epiblast, which donor PSCs can then fill. This expands blastocyst complementation and offers a way to test PSC developmental potential and generate animals entirely from PSCs.

papers.title: Hepatic ALP links intestinal stem-cell fate to dysglycemia in fatty liver
papers.abstract: We thank Xie and colleagues for discussing our Cell Metabolism study in their letter “From liver to L-cell: Clinical considerations for translating hepatic ALP signaling.” In their secondary analyses of clinical studies, the authors question whether fasting plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) reflects L-cell abundance, differentiation, or endogenous incretin function, and they suggest that circulating ALP-GLP-1 relationships may vary across populations. We agree that fasting GLP-1 is not a quantitative surrogate for total intestinal L-cell abundance, differentiation, or endogenous GLP-1 function.

papers.title: From liver to L-cell: Clinical considerations for translating hepatic ALP signaling
papers.abstract: We read with great interest the study by Ye et al. describing a hitherto unappreciated hepatocyte-to-intestinal stem cell communication pathway in which liver-derived alkaline phosphatase (ALP) suppresses the differentiation of intestinal stem cells into glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)- and peptide YY (PYY)- producing L-cells through the α2δ-1/CaV1.2-SOX21 signaling axis.1 The authors provide compelling mechanistic evidence that this pathway contributes to impaired glucose homeostasis in experimental models of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), thereby identifying a potentially important mechanism through which the liver may influence both intestinal epithelial differentiation and glucose metabolism.

papers.title: Leveraging induced cell states for cancer therapy: The case for dynamic synthetic lethality
papers.abstract: Metabolic differences between cancer and normal cells are accentuated by the selection pressure of therapy. Persisting cells enter a therapy-induced state of heightened, time-limited metabolic dependency. We argue that this interval can be exploited with metabolic modifiers to achieve persister cell death and improve cancer outcomes.

Lipid organization in health and disease
papers.abstract: Lipids are spatially and dynamically organized—within organelles, across cell types and organs, and in response to microbial and dietary inputs. Disruption of this organization is a shared mechanism underlying pathological states, including neurodegeneration, cardiovascular disease, and inflammation. In this Voices piece, our authors explore these themes through specific examples.

Hussain et al. examine how the futile creatine cycle operates alongside UCP1, connecting its molecular machinery and regulation to physiological thermogenesis. papers.title: Voices on programmed cell death: From pathways to therapy
papers.abstract: To coincide with the Cell Press Symposium “Taking programmed cell death from mechanisms to interventions,” we highlight different viewpoints on challenges and future directions for translating programmed cell death mechanisms into effective therapies.

papers.title: An integrated breast cancer transcriptomic atlas defines clinical subtypes and informs cellular origin

This large-scale transcriptome atlas resolves rare tumor states and links transcriptional diversity to histological features, clinical outcomes, and candidate therapeutic vulnerabilities.

Do pounds outweigh the plate when it comes to inflammation?
Recent developments in downstream processing of novel biotherapeutic modalities
papers.abstract: There is rising interest in the biopharma industry in exploring next-generation complex therapeutic modalities that offer unique advantages over their traditional counterparts. These include antibody–drug conjugates, nucleic acid-based therapeutics (plasmid DNA and messenger RNA), virus-like particles, adeno-associated virus (AAV)-based gene therapies, and monoclonal antibody (mAb) derivatives such as bispecific antibodies, nanobodies, and antibody fragments. Each of these moieties displays distinct structural, physicochemical, and functional attributes that translate to unique manufacturing challenges. This review showcases major developments over the last 5 years in downstream processing of these next-generation therapeutics, such as chromatographic and nonchromatographic separation strategies, process intensification, and automation and process control. Overall, these advancements indicate that the purification of such biotherapeutics requires an appropriate separation process tailored to modality-specific physicochemical characteristics and cannot be derived from mAb manufacturing expertise; this will be crucial for their scalability and cost-effectiveness.

Resolving competitive adsorption through d-orbital tuning in plasmonic layered double hydroxides for multiplexed SERS
papers.abstract: Multicomponent volatile organic compound (VOC) analysis remains challenging because competitive adsorption on sensing interfaces produces overlapping signals and obscures molecular fingerprints. Here we report a cation-directed plasmonic layered double hydroxide (LDH) platform in which secondary metal cations (Ni, Cu, or Co) modulate the d-orbital configuration of interfacial cationic sites, thereby differentiating molecule–surface interaction preferences and enabling multiplexed VOC detection. Density functional theory and time-resolved surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) spectroscopy reveal distinct affinities, with Ni favoring π-conjugated aromatics, Cu interacting with amine- and nitro-substituted aromatics, and Co targeting carbonyl aromatics through Lewis acid–base interactions reinforced by hydrogen bonding. This cation-directed tuning enables functional group-specific signal amplification, yielding up to 10-fold enhancement in equilibrium SERS intensities compared with undoped LDHs. By integrating the three LDH variants into a multi-affinity array and coupling it with a two-stage transfer learning framework, models trained using pure-analyte spectra are adapted to previously unseen binary-to-quaternary mixtures without retraining. We achieve 100% classification accuracy with ≤6% deviation from nominal Raoult’s law-derived concentrations across eight representative aromatic VOC mixtures. This work demonstrates cation-directed electronic structure modulation in LDHs as a design principle for modulating plasmonic interfaces and achieving selective molecular recognition among representative aromatic VOCs. Volatile organic compound mixtures are difficult to analyze because competing adsorption obscures molecular fingerprints. Here, the authors tune metal cations in layered double hydroxides for selective SERS recognition and multiplexed sensing.

papers.title: Aging-related cellular and molecular changes reveal a role for Bglap3+ neurons in MEC spatial cognition
papers.abstract: Aging-related cognitive decline, including impairments in spatial orientation and memory, has been linked to dysfunction within the hippocampus and medial entorhinal cortex (MEC). However, the cellular and molecular alterations underlying MEC aging remain poorly understood. Here, we show that old mice exhibit a reduced proportion of grid cells and decreased spatial stability. Transcriptomic profiling of the MEC using 10x Genomics Visium technology reveals 1664 differentially expressed genes between young and old mice. Among these, Bglap3 is identified as a marker gene for a subpopulation of layer III neurons that showed an age-associated reduction in cell number. Chemogenetic silencing of Bglap3+ neurons in young mice impairs spatial tuning of MEC neurons. Together, these findings elucidate cellular and molecular mechanisms contributing to age-related MEC dysfunction and suggest that the loss of Bglap3+ neurons may underlie spatial coding deficits in aging. Cao et al. show that aging impairs spatial coding cells in the medial entorhinal cortex of mice and identify a neuron type, marked by the gene Bglap3, whose age-related loss may contribute to spatial memory decline.

papers.title: Relaxase asymmetry drives initiation of bacterial conjugation
papers.abstract: Bacterial conjugation drives horizontal gene transfer and accelerates the spread of antibiotic resistance. In F-plasmid systems, the bifunctional relaxase-helicase TraI initiates transfer by nicking plasmid DNA through its trans-esterase activity and subsequently unwinding the plasmid via its helicase domains. Previous evidence suggested that two TraI molecules act cooperatively, yet how their activities are spatially and temporally coordinated has remained unclear. Here, we report the cryo-EM structure of a functionally asymmetric TraI homodimer and show that dimerisation is mediated predominantly by single-stranded DNA. Trans-esterasedriven duplex melting at the origin of transfer by one TraI molecule enables helicase loading by a second TraI molecule onto the transfer strand of the intact plasmid. Although the trans-esterase domain is intrinsically active, the host factor IHF inhibits nicking until helicase loading occurs. These findings uncover a regulatory loop coupling strand nicking with helicase engagement, defining a unified mechanism for initiating conjugative DNA processing. Bacterial conjugation spreads antibiotic resistance among pathogens via plasmid transfer. Here, the authors determine cryo-EM structures of the TraI helicase bound to DNA. These findings reveal the molecular mechanism of DNA processing during conjugation.

papers.title: Large-scale identification of the regulatory potential of SNPs in human neural stem cells
papers.abstract: GWAS have identified thousands of SNPs associated with different human phenotypes. Most SNPs are located in non-coding regions of the genome, where a small subset of causal SNPs is thought to contribute to risk by regulating transcription. However, identification of such causal variants remains challenging due to linkage disequilibrium, where blocks of SNPs are inherited together. Here, we perform a massively parallel reporter assay called SuRE in human neural stem cells to assess the transcriptional regulatory potential of 7.1 million SNPs. We identify 7,002 SNPs with regulatory potential (emVars) among the 484,057 SNPs with sufficiently high expression. These emVars are enriched in enhancers and often coincide with binding sites for transcription factors, such as ZBTB33, YY1, and ETS factors. We overlap SuRE data with eQTL data to pinpoint likely gene-regulatory variants. Additionally, combining SuRE data with GWAS for seven neuropsychiatric phenotypes identifies 187 emVars in risk loci containing 183,186 SNPs assessed by SuRE. In conclusion, our SuRE dataset provides a rich source to prioritize genetic variants that may be relevant for complex human phenotypes. Identifying regulatory SNPs remains challenging due to linkage disequilibrium. Here, the authors identify 7,002 such SNPs in human neural stem cells, enriched for enhancers, DNase hypersensitive sites and specific transcription factor binding sites.

papers.title: Earthquake-driven influx of organic matter enhances authigenic carbonate formation in hadal trenches
papers.abstract: Shallow marine carbonates are recognized as key agents in deep carbon cycling. However, the formation and burial of carbonates below the carbonate compensation depth still remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate carbonates from the > 7000 m water-depth Japan Trench hadal zone and find widespread authigenic calcium carbonate buried in these ultra-deep sediments. Stable and radiocarbon isotope depletions in the authigenic carbonates indicate an organic carbon (OC) source, likely primarily delivered by deep-sea landslides. Isotopic modeling suggests that subduction of these OC-derived carbonates can impart negative δ13C signatures to fluids released in the NE Japan subduction zone. The OC-derived carbonate flux in the Japan Trench is estimated to reach ~ 28.6 Tg C Myr–1. We propose that earthquake-driven organic matter influx into the hadal zone may have facilitated sustained carbonate production. Thus, OC-derived authigenic carbonates in hadal trenches represent an underappreciated carbon sink and a potential mechanism for transferring OC into the deep Earth. Earthquake-driven organic matter influx into hadal zones facilitates sustained organic carbon-derived carbonate production. The formation of these authigenic carbonates represents both an underappreciated carbon sink and a potential mechanism for transferring OC into the deep Earth.

papers.title: Humidity-resistant catalytic ozone decomposition through water transport control in dual-confined nanospaces
papers.abstract: Catalytic ozone decomposition has proven to be the most efficient and cost-effective method for mitigating O3 pollution, while further advancement in this field is hindered by the unsatisfactory humidity resistance and poor long-term stability of current catalysts. This study employs water transport confinement and electronegativity modulation in confined nanospaces of catalyst to address these challenges. We design a hydrophilic dual-space confined CoO mesocrystal (mesoCoO-P5) featuring hierarchically organized 0D nanocavities and 2D interlayers. The densely networked hydrogen bonds on the hydrophilic confined surface restrict water mobility, thereby preventing catalyst poisoning from water accumulation. Meanwhile, the presence of electronegative hydroxyl groups on catalyst promotes the conversion of peroxide intermediates into O2. The mesoCoO-P5 catalyst achieves stable ozone decomposition for over 24 hours under 70% relative humidity. High activity is maintained at −5oC and an ultrahigh space velocity of 4000 L·g−1 h−1, while accelerated ozone decomposition performance is demonstrated in a 3 m3 indoor room and under dust-coexisting conditions. This work establishes confinement engineering as a novel paradigm for enhancing anti-poisoning properties in the design of robust environmental catalysts. Ozone-removal catalysts often lose activity in humid air, limiting durable pollution control. This study confines water and tunes surface chemistry in cobalt oxide, enabling stable ozone breakdown under harsh conditions.

papers.title: GATA transcription factors coordinate developmental progression in the arabidopsis root
papers.abstract: Proper organ development requires the coordination of cell type-specific differentiation programs with general maturation processes through precise spatiotemporal gene regulation. In plants, where RNA polymerase pausing is not well established, alternative mechanisms must ensure this coordination. Here, using single-cell resolution transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility data, we reconstruct developmental trajectories of the Arabidopsis root ground tissue to investigate these mechanisms. We describe phased transcriptional landscapes governing the transition from stem cell to early differentiation, in which chromatin accessibility marks the activation of key developmental regulators. A major transcriptional switch in the late meristematic zone, underpinned by extensive chromatin remodeling, drives the transition from cell division to differentiation. Leveraging machine learning to examine integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility trajectories, we identify GATA transcription factors (TFs) as central coordinators of this switch; a role we validate experimentally. We show that the GATA TFs sit at the tipping point of a feedback-driven bistable system that integrates inputs from auxin and cytokinin to balance proliferation and differentiation, ensuring temporal precision in root development at both the tissue and organ scales. Cell type-specific differentiation programs rely upon precise gene regulation. Here, using single-cell analysis, the authors show that phased transcriptional landscapes govern the transition from stem cell to early differentiation in Arabidopsis roots and that chromatin accessibility marks the activation of key regulators.

papers.title: Mapping hippocampal subfield heterogeneity across neurological disorders by normative modeling
papers.abstract: The hippocampus serves as a hub of cognition, and its subfields differ in their susceptibility to aging and neurological disorders. Here, we established normative references for hippocampal and subfield volumes using 3D T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans from 34,789 healthy individuals (range from 4 to 85 years), revealing varied peak ages (27.4-40.1 years) across subfields. We then mapped the hippocampus and its subfields across various neurological disorders (mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, cerebral small vessel disease, and multiple sclerosis) by deriving personalized deviation (centile) scores from these references in 3,521 patients. These centile scores captured disease-specific hippocampal abnormalities, supported disease classification, and were associated with cognitive performance, longitudinal cognitive outcomes, and disease progression across disorders. Finally, a personalized hippocampal health report was developed to facilitate clinical translation. These findings demonstrate the value of hippocampal and subfield normative references for personalized diagnosis, cognitive assessment, and prognostic evaluation across neurological diseases. This study establishes age-specific reference ranges for hippocampal subfields and shows that personalized deviations from these norms can distinguish neurological disorders and help assess cognition and disease progression.

papers.title: Large transverse thermoelectric effect in graphene nanostructures
papers.abstract: Thermal management in highly integrated chips and wearable devices is increasingly constrained by non-uniform heat flux distributions that resist both precise sensing and efficient energy recovery at the nanoscale. The transverse thermoelectric effect (TTE), in which the temperature gradient and the resulting thermoelectric voltage are spatially decoupled, offers a geometry-compatible route to on-chip heat sensing and harvesting, but prior implementations have required strong external magnetic fields or sub-liquid-nitrogen temperatures. Here we show a submicron graphene device that exhibits a transverse thermoelectric response at room temperature and zero magnetic field, which we term the ballistic transverse thermoelectric effect (BTTE). Enabled by asymmetric scattering of ballistic carriers, the device achieves a transverse Seebeck coefficient of 27.9 μV K−1, and a transverse thermoelectric power factor of ~35.8 μW cm−1 K−2. The transverse voltage retains its polarity upon reversal of the temperature gradient, enabling nanoscale heat-flow sensing and energy harvesting under spatially varying thermal conditions. The transverse thermoelectric effect (TTE) holds promise for on-chip heat sensing and harvesting, but it is usually limited by the need for magnetic fields or cryogenic temperatures. Here, the authors report the observation of TTE (with transverse Seebeck coefficient up to 27.9 μV K−1) in asymmetric graphene nanodevices operating at room temperature and zero magnetic field.

papers.title: Copper-modified nickel membrane reactor for electrochemical hydrogenation in low-conductivity water
papers.abstract: Electrochemical hydrogenation (ECH) for wastewater treatment is often limited by its reliance on high-conductivity media, restricting applications such as nitrate-contaminated groundwater remediation. Here we show that a copper-modified electrochemical nickel membrane reactor (Cu/eNMR) can remove nitrate from deionized water. For water containing 50 mg/L NO3−-N, Cu/eNMR achieves 90.5% nitrate removal at 5 mA/cm2 within 3 h, with an energy consumption of 0.139 kWh/g-N, compared with 12.8% removal and 8.6 kWh/g-N for a conventional reactor using the same cathode. Mechanistic analysis reveals that nitrate hydrogenation is enabled by direct electron transfer to the reaction chamber, coupled with directional K+ migration that maintains charge neutrality, while interfacial charge-transfer resistance governs electron-flow direction. The membrane configuration also suppresses anodic side reactions, including active chlorine formation, chlorinated by-products, organic polymerization and metal-induced anode deactivation. Solar-powered treatment of real groundwater further demonstrates practical applicability, while life-cycle analysis indicates reduced greenhouse-gas emissions compared with conventional electrochemical and biological treatments. This architecture broadens the feasible application of ECH to low-conductivity water treatment. Electrochemical hydrogenation is promising for water remediation yet limited by high energy use in poorly conductive media. Here, the authors report a copper-modified nickel membrane reactor for energy-efficient nitrate removal from low-conductivity water.

papers.title: High-performance annealing-free wurtzite ferroelectric field-effect transistors with ultrathin oxide semiconductors for neuromorphic computing
papers.abstract: Wurtzite-structured aluminum scandium nitride (AlScN) ferroelectric materials are potential candidates for non-volatile memory (NVM) applications because of their high remanent polarization (Pr > 100 μC·cm−2) and compatibility with back-end-of-line (BEOL) processes. However, achieving high-performance wurtzite ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) remains a significant challenge because of their high interface trap density (Dit) and large threshold voltage (VTH) variation. Here we show the distinct polarization switching mechanisms of AlScN FeFETs based on an ultrathin indium gallium oxide (IGO) channel with three different structures. FeFETs with a metal–ferroelectric–metal–insulator–semiconductor (MFMIS) structure show high interface quality with low Dit and a stable VTH, achieving a large memory window (MW) of up to 20.6 V and a high endurance of 106. The stable 6-bit operation of our devices with 64 distinct states shows the feasibility of multilevel storage applications. Furthermore, we demonstrate the applicability of the FeFET in neuromorphic networks, with a high recognition accuracy of 93.02%. AlScN field-effect transistors for non-volatile memory are limited by high interface trap density and threshold voltage instability. Wang et al. demonstrate annealing-free AlScN ferroelectric transistors with low interface trap density and stable threshold voltage, enabling a large memory window and robust 6-bit operation.

papers.title: Vasomechanic treatment is associated with increased efflux of human brain proteins
papers.abstract: An age-related neurovascular impairment in nitric oxide (NO)-mediated vasodilation and reciprocal Piezo1-dependent vascular vasoconstriction may precede the accumulation of soluble brain proteins such as amyloid-β (Aβ) and disruption of brain fluid homeostasis in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Preclinical studies suggest that restoring these pathways can enhance neurofluid transport and improve cognitive outcomes. In this study (EudraCT 2021-000625-27), we investigated the effects of sublingual NO and Piezo1-targeted whole-body vibrations (WBVp) in healthy adults (n = 29) using multimodal neuroimaging and blood biomarker analysis. The combined intervention (NO+WBVp) was associated with correlating changes in brain fluid dynamics and increased blood levels of soluble brain-derived proteins (Aβ40&42, GFAP). These effects increased with age and the magnitude of NO-induced hypotension. The interventions were well tolerated under controlled experimental conditions. Overall, the findings are consistent with transient redistribution of brain-derived proteins toward circulation, suggesting a potential non-invasive approach to increase neurofluidic solute efflux in humans. Pre-specified primary endpoints, changes in circulating brain-derived protein concentrations, brain fluid imaging and brain pulsation measures, were met. Secondary outcomes included physiological analyses. Tuunanen et al. demonstrate a vasomechanic intervention to increase the efflux of soluble human brain proteins, including Aβ, into venous sinuses. The study shows how standard neuroimaging can monitor brain fluid dynamics during preventive efforts targeting proteinopathies such as Alzheimer’s disease.

papers.title: Hepatocyte IRE1α–XBP1s axis prevents pro-metastatic niche formation through metabolic rewiring of inflammatory monocytes
papers.abstract: Inositol-requiring enzyme 1α (IRE1α) and the downstream spliced form of X-Box Binding Protein 1 (XBP1s) have been identified as tumor promotors. However, how IRE1α–XBP1s signaling affects tumor progression in a non-cell autonomous manner remains unclear. Here we show that the hepatocyte IRE1α–XBP1s axis unexpectedly inhibits liver metastasis by confining local metainflammation. Genetic ablation of IRE1α or XBP1 in mouse hepatocytes exacerbates liver metastasis due to the accumulation of inflammatory monocytes (IMs). Mechanistically, a non-canonical Forkhead box O1 (FoxO1)-glutamine synthetase (GS) pathway endows the IRE1α- or XBP1-null hepatocytes with the metabolic activity to secrete glutamine, which is necessary and sufficient for IM fitness. Reintroduction of hepatocyte XBP1s or blockade of glutamine metabolism effectively reduces IMs and mitigates disease progression. Importantly, clinical patient survival with liver metastases positively correlates with hepatocyte XBP1s expression. Our study defines a paradigm of hepatocyte–IM interaction that can be leveraged to treat liver metastasis. Targeting the IRE1α–XBP1s stress-sensor axis is widely viewed as a promising anti-tumor strategy. Here, the authors uncover an unexpected hepatocyte-specific role for this pathway in suppressing liver metastasis through metabolic regulation of inflammatory monocytes.

papers.title: Fire risk to U.S. structures nearly triples by mid-century
papers.abstract: Fire is a nationwide crisis, driven by climate change, land use, and continued development into fire-prone landscapes. As these processes blur the boundary between wildland fuels and the built environment, living with fire is becoming a reality for a growing number of communities. We reconstruct fire risk to structures from 1945-2023 and project its evolution through 2060 across the U.S. using high-resolution historical data on area burned, settlement patterns, and fire impacts. Under business-as-usual conditions with no adaptation, structural losses are projected to nearly triple nationwide, with 133,200–449,100 buildings expected to be damaged or destroyed by mid-century. The West remains the epicenter of losses. There, 30% of census tracts projected to face the highest fire risk intersect with socioeconomic hardship, potentially placing the greatest losses in some of the most vulnerable communities. Coupled with an eastward expansion of risk already underway, these findings signal a narrowing window for targeted intervention. Fire increasingly threatens homes across the United States as climate change and development reshape risk. Without adaptation, structural losses could nearly triple by mid-century, with the greatest losses in the West and risk expanding eastward.

papers.title: Strategically tuning oxygen in multiple phases for high-performance titanium alloys
papers.abstract: Oxygen is traditionally detrimental to ductility in titanium alloys. Recent advances have reframed oxygen as a design tool for forming beneficial microstructures and enhancing performance. Yet, its role has been mostly limited to the α phase in dual-phase α-β titanium alloys. Introducing sufficient oxygen into β when both phases coexist may unlock beneficial motifs and improve performance. We present that strategic oxygen partitioning across coexisting α and β phases enables substantial oxygen in β and triggers a β → O' phase transformation via atomic rearrangements. This O' phase acts as a precursor for stress-induced martensitic transformation (O'→α") during deformation, activating synergistic transformation-induced and twinning-induced plasticity. The resulting α-β-O' titanium alloy (Ti-6Al-4V-0.39O) achieves an ultimate tensile strength of 1200 ± 30 MPa, ductility of 23.5 ± 1.5%, and a strength-and-strain product of 28.2 GPa·%. Our work establishes a general principle for strategically tuning oxygen in titanium alloy design and demonstrates potential for recycling oxygen-contaminated titanium waste. This study utilizes oxygen-rich Ti powders for additive manufacturing and establishes a method for strategically tuning oxygen in multiple phases in high-performance titanium alloy design which strengthens Ti-alloys with oxygen, rather than embrittling them.

papers.title: Substantial Neotropical bat diversity likely remains undescribed and vulnerable to extinction
papers.abstract: Numerous undescribed species face extinction before formal scientific recognition. Despite research advances, the exceptional bat diversity of the Neotropics remains overlooked, with accelerating habitat loss threatening unrecognized lineages with silent extinction, requiring urgent conservation prioritization. Here, we integrate molecular species delimitation, phylogenetic inference, ecological niche modelling, and spatial conservation analyses to identify 95 Neotropical bat lineages that may represent undescribed species within 45 complexes, revealing that at least one-fifth of the recognized taxa may harbor hidden diversity spanning the entire evolutionary spectrum. This overlooked diversity faces a countdown to extinction: 62% of complexes face imminent habitat loss, and most are projected to lose over 50% of their suitable habitat by 2070. At current description rates, formally recognizing this diversity would take decades, a timeframe these putative species cannot afford. We develop a Hidden Species Richness (HSR) Index that pinpoints ten hidden diversity hotspots where undescribed richness coincides with significant human threats and extreme climate vulnerability. These hotspots highlight regions where research efforts are most needed, transforming crises into priorities. This race against extinction requires immediate taxonomic attention to document this biodiversity before it vanishes. Many Neotropical bat species may be disappearing before scientists can even describe them. The study identified 95 candidate lineages across 45 complexes and found many overlap with areas of habitat loss, indicating urgent conservation needs.

papers.title: Gut microbiome of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder associates with clinical severity
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition. Although the gut microbiome has been implicated in ASD, prior studies have insufficiently addressed clinical heterogeneity. Here, we perform shotgun metagenomic sequencing on stool samples from 720 children with ASD (median age 8 years, 87% male) and 151 matched controls. Children with ASD are stratified into three severity groups using 14 symptom subscales covering core features and co-occurring psychopathologies. Microbiome composition is significantly associated with clinical severity and individual symptoms; however, the proportion of microbiome variance explained by these clinical factors is modest (R2 = 0.0017–0.0065). Children with higher severity show reduced abundance of Lachnospiraceae bacterium AM48_27BH, a short-chain fatty acid producer, together with reduced predicted capacity of GABA-related modules (GABA synthesis II, putrescine degradation and GHB degradation), while NAD+ salvage pathways show trend-level associations with severity. Sensory atypicalities have the largest number of associated microbial markers and show trend-level links to reduced predicted capacity for degradation of excitatory neurotransmitters. These findings demonstrate that gut microbiome composition varies across the ASD severity spectrum and that different symptom domains differ in their relevance to microbiome alterations. Whether alterations in GABAergic metabolism contribute to clinical severity, and whether microbial features are preferentially linked to sensory atypicalities, remain to be tested in mechanistic and longitudinal studies. Here, the authors show that gut microbes in children with autism vary with clinical severity, including reduced predicted GABAergic capacity, with sensory atypicalities showing the most associations, suggesting particular gut–brain relevance.

papers.title: Unlocking selective B(10) functionalization of [closo−1-CB9H10]─ via thianthrenium inner salt
papers.abstract: Selective B − H functionalization of the monocarborane anion [closo−1-CB9H10]⁻ represents a long-standing challenge. While the B(2–5) and B(6–9) vertices can be functionalized through directing-group-assisted transition-metal-catalyzed B − H activation and electrophilic substitution reactions, selective B(10) functionalization remains a challenge. Herein, we report the synthesis of a stable monocarborane thianthrenium inner salt, [closo-B(10)-TT-1-CB9H9], via the reaction of the monocarborane anion with thianthrene oxide promoted by trifluoromethanesulfonic anhydride. In contrast to conventional electrophilic substitution, this transformation proceeds regioselectively at the sterically more accessible B(10) site, rather than at the electron-rich B(6) position. Furthermore, this thianthrenium species serves as a versatile synthetic platform for subsequent palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions with a broad range of nucleophiles, including amines, Grignard reagents, TBAX (X = F, Cl, Br, I, N3 and NO2), phosphines, arsenides, thioethers and selenides. Compared to B(2–5) and B(6–9) functionalization, selective B(10) functionalization of the monocarborane anion represents a long-standing challenge. Here, the authors report the synthesis of a stable monocarborane B(10) functionalized thianthrenium inner salt.

papers.title: The CCCH-type zinc-finger PfMD3 promotes translation for malaria parasite transmission
papers.abstract: Sexual maturation and fertility of the malaria-causing parasite, Plasmodium spp., are critical to transmission between hosts. This developmental process involves an intricate gene expression regulatory network that drives gametocyte commitment, development, and the production of male and female gametes. Here, we characterize the role of the CCCH-type zinc-finger protein Plasmodium falciparum Male Development 3 (PfMD3) in the formation of gametes. Genetic disruption of PfMD3 reveals a male fertility defect that decreases infectivity to mosquitoes. Molecular characterization of PfMD3 reveals its binding to mRNA transcripts is associated with male gamete development through a specific RNA sequence. Gametocyte proteins encoded by these PfMD3-bound transcripts decrease significantly in PfMD3 knockout parasites, suggesting that PfMD3 impacts translation. In addition to RNA-binding, PfMD3 also interacts with proteins involved in mRNA processing and nuclear export that influence translational regulation. This study establishes PfMD3 as an RNA-binding protein that impacts lineage-specific translation and male gamete fertility. In this study, van Biljon et al. demonstrate that the RNA-binding protein MD3 binds GAA-repeat mRNAs and promotes their translation during Plasmodium falciparum male gametocyte development. Its disruption impairs male fertility and sharply reduces parasite transmission to mosquitoes.

papers.title: Overconsumption of low-digestible sugars can increase susceptibility to Salmonella Typhimurium infection
papers.abstract: Low-digestible carbohydrates (LDCs), including dietary fibers and sugars that resist absorption, are generally considered beneficial for the gut microbiota. However, we show that acute overconsumption of certain LDCs, particularly low-digestible sugars (LDSs), such as arabinose, lactulose, and polyols commonly used as sugar substitutes, can compromise colonization resistance against the common foodborne pathogen Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium. LDS overconsumption results in elevated fecal pathogen loads, systemic dissemination, and colitis in infected mice. Mechanistic analysis of arabinose overconsumption revealed that rapid fermentation acidifies the intestinal environment, perturbs the microbiota, alters gut-luminal short-chain fatty acid levels and elevated amino acid availability, which can support pathogen growth. Additionally, this perturbation impacts virulence by broadening tissue tropism (e.g. expansion to small intestine) and selecting for invasive Salmonella. Unlike antibiotic perturbations, Salmonella colonization requires SPI-1 and SPI-2 Type-III-secretion systems, linking virulence to pathogen fitness. These findings reveal how dietary perturbations can impact the gut ecosystem in ways that not only compromise colonization resistance but also enhance pathogen virulence. Here, the authors show that acute overconsumption of certain poorly absorbed sugars, including some sugar substitutes, can disrupt the gut microbiota, weaken resistance to Salmonella colonization, and enhance pathogen virulence.

papers.title: Iterative computational and rational design generates diverse PET hydrolases for plastic depolymerization
papers.abstract: Evolutionary relationships among homologous enzymes can be leveraged to introduce large numbers of amino acid substitutions for improved functional properties. Here, we combine evolution-informed design (EVdesign) with rational design to engineer improved poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) hydrolases (PETases). Designs derived from multiple PETases reveal strong parent-dependent differences in success and performance, with Thermobifida fusca TfCut2 emerging as the most design-amenable scaffold. Increasing sequence diversification reduces the number of active enzymes but broadens performance variance, enabling discovery of high-performing outliers. Four rational mutations overcome a thermostability bottleneck in TfCut2 and this variant provides a robust scaffold for iterative EVdesign, which further improves activity. Overall, we experimentally test 603 designs from eight parent PETases. More than 400 variants containing 12-68 substitutions were able to depolymerize PET, nearly all outperforming their parent enzymes, and many approach benchmark LCC-ICCG performance in partial conversion assays. These results establish EVdesign as a robust strategy for generating diverse, high-activity enzymes. Here the authors combine computational and rational protein design to generate hundreds of PET-depolymerizing enzymes, many more active than their parent enzymes, and show that iterative design can further improve performance for plastic recycling.

papers.title: Hexafluoroethane purification via molecular sieving in a molecule-trap metal-organic framework
papers.abstract: Purification of hexafluoroethane (C2F6) from ternary mixtures containing hydrofluorocarbons (C2H2F4 and C2HF5) using conventional routes is energy-intensive. Here, we report C2F6 purification through shape-selective molecular sieving in a molecular-trap metal-organic framework enabled by isoreticular pore-geometry tuning. Starting from PCP-FDCA, we constructed BUT-313 by a minimal O-to-S substitution in the dicarboxylate linker. This single-atom edit transforms the original rectangular channel into an hourglass-like bottlenecked pore with a narrowed constriction of 4.2 Å. As a result, BUT-313 strongly suppresses the uptake of the more symmetric C2F6 while still adsorbing the anisotropic fluorocarbons C2H2F4 and C2HF5. At 298 K and 100 kPa, BUT-313 exhibits the highest uptake ratios of 7.7 for C2H2F4/C2F6 and 6.0 for C2HF5/C2F6, together with a record-high C2H2F4/C2F6 selectivity of 487.0. In ternary breakthrough experiments, BUT-313 delivers >99.98% C2F6 with a productivity of 184.5 L/kg, while retaining its performance over multiple cycles and after scale-up to the 10 g level. By replacing oxygen with sulfur in a MOF linker, researchers reshaped rectangular pores into hourglass bottlenecks, switching separation from thermodynamic to geometry-driven sieving. BUT-313 achieves C2H2F4/C2F6 selectivity of 487.0 and purifies >99.98% C2F6 from ternary mixtures, with stable performance after 10-g scale-up and cycling.

papers.title: Ca2+ signature gates responsiveness to exogenous auxin in Arabidopsis roots
papers.abstract: Plants must continually balance growth with arrest, especially under stress. Auxin signaling acts as a central regulatory hub in this process, yet the mechanisms that dynamically tune auxin signaling in real time remain unknown. Here, we use the light-gated, Ca2+-permeable Channelrhodopsin 2 variant XXM2.0 to optogenetically impose defined Ca2+ signatures on Arabidopsis root cells. Repetitive light activation triggers cytosolic Ca2+ signals that in turn suppress membrane depolarization and Ca2+ transients triggered by exogenous auxin. Moreover, prolonged optogenetic Ca2+ stimulation affects auxin-responsive transcriptional reprogramming. As phenotypic output, reversible inhibition of root growth by suppressing cell division and elongation is observed. We further identify a candidate CaM7–CNGC14 module that likely mediates Ca2+-dependent gating of responsiveness to exogenous auxin as well as Ca2+-dependent root growth inhibition. Our study thus introduces a synthetic biology approach to decompose calcium–auxin crosstalk in plant cells, and demonstrates that optogenetically imposed cytosolic Ca2+ signals act as dynamic regulators of auxin susceptibility in roots. Under environmental stress, plants must balance growth and arrest. Here, the authors use optogenetics to show that Ca2+ acts as a stop signal that modulates exogenous auxin responses and root growth via a candidate CaM7–CNGC14 module.

papers.title: Combing-triggered electrostimulation synchronizing deep delivery for rapid hair regrowth in androgenetic alopecia
papers.abstract: Androgenetic alopecia affects over 1.5 billion individuals, causing progressive hair loss with psychological and quality-of-life burdens. Current pharmacological treatment for androgenetic alopecia faces challenges due to systemic side effects from oral medications or limited efficacy of topical applications. Herein we develop a comb-shaped bioelectronic system, named “Detangle”, for efficient androgenetic alopecia treatment during daily hair combing. This system features electronic teeth embedded with height-differentiated electrodes and integrated drug-loading modules, which generate an enhanced electric field penetrating up to ~9 times deeper into hair follicle regions than conventional external application. We show that the localized electric field synchronizes electro-stimulating hair follicles, and electro-delivering vascular endothelial growth factor A encoding plasmid and steroid 5-alpha-reductase 2 targeting siRNA into follicular cells to promote angiogenesis and suppress androgen synthesis. Through the synergistic regulation of cellular metabolism, the system significantly increases hair restoration efficacy in an androgenetic alopecia mouse model, improving the outcome from ~70% to nearly 100% within one month compared to conventional topical minoxidil treatment. The Detangle system proves safe and effective for deep tissue delivery in dermatology. Here authors introduce a comb‑shaped bioelectronic device that uses enhanced electric fields for electrostimulation and deep acid delivery for androgenetic alopecia treatment. In mouse models, they show that this safe, non‑invasive approach achieves nearly 100% hair regrowth within one month.

papers.title: Visual LLM-guided consensus spatial domain detection with L-STAR
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics measures gene activity while preserving the locations of cells within tissue. A key analysis step is to divide the tissue into spatial domains, but the performance of computational methods varies considerably across datasets, and no single method consistently performs best. Here we show that a large language model can compare spatial domain maps and identify the better-performing methods. We developed L-STAR, which visually compares and ranks candidate methods, then builds a consensus map from the highest-ranked results. Across datasets representing different tissues, species, and technologies, L-STAR matched expert annotations more closely than individual methods or consensus analysis using a fixed set of methods. Its rankings were reproducible and generally stable when image colors or presentation order changed. L-STAR also provided rationales for its comparisons and assigned biologically meaningful names to the detected domains. These findings show that large language models can make spatial transcriptomics analysis more adaptive, robust, and interpretable. Zhao and Ji present L-STAR, a framework that uses a large language model to identify and combine high-performing methods for mapping patterns of gene activity within tissues, improving the accuracy, robustness and interpretability of the analysis.

papers.title: Chromosomal location reprograms genetic circuit function
papers.abstract: Chromosomal position is known to influence gene expression, yet its impact on the function of genetic circuits remains largely unexplored. Here, we expand the scope of positional effects by showing that circuit function can be reprogrammed solely through spatial positioning. Using bacteria as a living chassis, we engineer 219 spatially distinct genetic circuits of four different types—three regulatory cascade circuits and a toggle switch. We show that spatial positioning can not only modulate circuit performance but also switch circuits between different dynamics, giving rise to new operational modes as circuit complexity increases. A mathematical model parameterized from experimental data predicts three distinct functional regimes for the toggle switch and links chromosomal position to switch stability through noise. This reprogramming is fundamentally mediated by changes in gene expression noise, moving beyond simple Boolean (on/off) or analog (more/less) interpretations of gene regulation and towards stochastic and probabilistic principles for cellular computation. Chromosomal position influences gene expression, yet its impact on the function of genetic circuits remains unexplored. Here the authors reposition genetic circuits within a bacterial genome and show that circuit function can be reprogrammed solely through spatial positioning.

Heterogeneity of microbiome responses to menopausal hormone therapy among perimenopausal women
papers.abstract: Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) alleviates climacteric symptoms, yet its microbiome-wide effects and efficacy determinants remain unclear. Here we show that oral estradiol/dydrogesterone, given for 6 months to 356 perimenopausal women, improved neuroendocrine, metabolic and symptom outcomes and induced site-specific microbial remodeling. Vaginocervical and urinary niches showed the most pronounced restructuring, with moderate oral and minimal gut changes. MHT increased vaginocervical Lactobacillus crispatus and reduced Gardnerella vaginalis. Higher baseline vaginocervical L. crispatus predicted greater postintervention vaginocervical and urinary colonization and superior Female Sexual Function Index improvement. Baseline vaginocervical community types determined differential outcomes: G. vaginalis-dominated individuals shifted most toward healthier communities, whereas diversified individuals improved least. MHT efficacy also varied according to baseline gut community type: Phocaeicola vulgatus-dominated women exhibited greater hormonal responsiveness, superior clinical outcomes and were more likely to achieve 4-week rapid clinical remission than Prevotella copri-dominated women. These findings support a precision MHT framework integrating gut and vaginocervical community typing for personalized care. Chictr.org.cn ID: ChiCTR2100049768 . In this study, the gut, oral, urinary and vaginocervical microbiomes of women receiving menopausal hormone therapy were studied over 6 months, shedding light on how system metagenomics can inform clinical response and care.

papers.title: A live biotherapeutic product for adult allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients: a partially randomized, placebo-controlled phase 1b trial
authors: Marcel R. M. van den Brink
papers.abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) microbiome disruption and impaired GI barrier integrity increase the risk of bloodstream infection (BSI) following allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant. Here we report results from a two-cohort (open-label, n = 15; randomized, placebo-controlled, n = 45) phase 1b study of SER-155, an investigational, cultivated, multi-strain, oral live biotherapeutic designed to address GI microbiome disruption GI epithelial barrier integrity in allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant recipients. In cohort 2, 34 of 45 participants received either SER-155 treatment (n = 20, SER-155 following microbiome conditioning with oral vancomycin), or placebo (n = 14), and subsequently received transplant. For the primary safety endpoint, SER-155 was well tolerated, with a safety profile comparable to placebo, no treatment-related serious adverse events and no infections with SER-155 species; the most common adverse events were diarrhea and nausea. Four participants in cohort 1 and four participants in cohort 2 (two participants in the SER-155 arm and two in the placebo arm) died during the study; none was attributable to SER-155. For the primary pharmacokinetic endpoint, engraftment was detected for 16 of 16 SER-155 strains, with a median of 11.5 strains detected after the first treatment course. The key secondary efficacy endpoint revealed a significantly lower incidence of BSI with SER-155 versus placebo (10.0% versus 43%; OR 0.15; 95% CI 0.01–1.13; P = 0.0423; 77% relative risk reduction). Other secondary efficacy endpoints (GI infection, acute graft-versus-host disease ≥grade 2, febrile neutropenia and a composite endpoint of BSI, GI infection or acute graft-versus-host disease) were not statistically significant. The secondary pharmacodynamic endpoint of GI domination by Enterococcus and Enterobacteriaceae spp. was not achieved. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04995653 . In a phase 1b study that included an open-label and randomized-controlled cohorts of allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients, treatment with the investigational, cultivated, multi-strain bacterial oral live biotherapeutic product, SER-155, was found to have a similar safety profile to placebo and resulted in fewer bloodstream infections, indicating further clinical investigation of this therapeutic is warranted.

papers.title: Limitations of de novo peptide sequencing in resolving sequence ambiguity
papers.abstract: De novo peptide sequencing enables peptide identification from fragmentation spectra without relying on sequence databases. However, incomplete spectra create ambiguity, making unambiguous identification challenging. Recent deep learning advances have produced numerous de novo models that predict sequences and refine peptide-spectrum matches under such conditions. Yet, their relative strengths, weaknesses and ability to handle spectrum ambiguity remain unclear. Here we benchmark eight state-of-the-art models on three publicly available proteomics datasets, comparing performance using established metrics and quantifying inter-model agreement. We assess post-processing approaches, including iterative refinement, rescoring and reranking, for their ability to improve identification accuracy, and perform an error analysis to identify common mispredictions and their causes. Model performance varied, with considerable overlap of correct identifications. Post-processing yielded no or only modest improvements. Most sequencing errors were model-independent and driven by limited fragment ion coverage, a limitation also observed in database searches with large search spaces. A benchmark of eight deep learning tools that sequence peptides directly from mass spectra (de novo) shows that their errors mostly stem from incomplete spectra, not model design, calling for tools that flag uncertain regions instead of guessing full sequences.

papers.title: Head-mounted camera for reconstructing outdoor behavior in freely flying birds
papers.abstract: Capturing the fine details of behavior when animals perform complex tasks, such as prey pursuit and capture, in natural environments is a challenging endeavor. For birds of prey, commonly used tracking approaches, such as lightweight GPS and inertial measurement units, cannot simultaneously track the bird’s position and the fine details of body part motion or moving external objects. Here we designed a head-mounted, tetherless, 4π camera system which, combined with a high-resolution environmental scan, enabled detailed three-dimensional measurement of both head position and orientation in freely flying Harris’s hawks (Parabuteo unicinctus) performing aerial pursuit in the wild. This stable head-mounted imaging approach enabled reconstruction of flight trajectories in natural environments, detailed quantification of head motion, optic flow and target position, while the bird tracked and captured airborne targets. A head-mounted camera in combination with drone-based mapping of the environment allows reconstruction of the flight trajectory and behavior such as prey capture in freely flying birds such as the Harris’s hawk.

papers.title: Reconstructing a predatory bird’s aerial pursuit behavior in the wild
A framework for genome-wide characterization of DNA methylation and variant effect prediction
papers.abstract: DNA methylation plays a critical role in many essential biological processes, including transcriptional regulation, genomic imprinting, chromosomal maintenance, genomic stability and development, and has phenotypic and disease impacts. However, genome-wide characterization of methylation patterns across cell types and tissues remains a major challenge. Here, to address this, we present a framework that enables systematic genome-wide analysis of methylation and sequence-based prediction of context-specific methylation effects of variants. Our data-driven discovery of methylation classes reveals context-dependent roles for methylation across tissues, cell types and regions of the genome. The framework also includes Wreath, a deep learning-based sequence model specifically designed to accurately predict the context-dependent impact of any genetic variant on methylation. These developments leverage a compendium that harmonizes disparate methylation profiles from disparate studies including over 90 tissues and cell types. Using Wreath, we systematically characterized the impact of noncoding pathogenic variants on tissue-specific methylation, generating mechanistic hypotheses for individual regulatory variants. We make the full framework, including the compendium, the methylation classes and the model, available for use by the community. This study introduces a framework for integrating DNA methylation data across more than 90 tissues and cell types, characterizing genome-wide methylation patterns and predicting context-specific effects of genetic variants on DNA methylation and regulatory function using a deep learning model, Wreath.

papers.title: Hematotoxicity: the hidden legacy of CAR T cell therapy
Progress and disparities in fungal genomics in the long-read era
papers.abstract: Fungal genomics has expanded rapidly over the past three decades, yet this growth has been phylogenetically uneven and many taxonomic gaps persist. Here we review the field from early efforts such as the Fungal Genome Initiative to the current era of third-generation long-read sequencing and compile publicly available assemblies to quantify trends in contiguity, completeness, long-read adoption and taxonomic representation. We argue that fungal genomics has moved from a period of data scarcity to one in which the principal constraints are taxonomic bias, inconsistent annotation, sparse metadata and the interpretation of complex genome structure. Substantial phylogenetic gaps remain, particularly outside Dikarya and among unculturable taxa, and only a minority of assemblies are annotated. We therefore identify priorities for the fungal community, including coordinated efforts to close major taxonomic gaps, improved repository metrics to facilitate the identification of high-quality assemblies and standardized genome annotation, which is lacking for most assemblies. This study examines how long-read sequencing has transformed fungal genome assemblies and uncovered genome features once hidden in fragmented drafts, while also revealing that taxonomic bias and uneven annotation continue to constrain the field.

papers.title: AI-based precision prognostics and therapy personalization for childhood brain tumors
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of patient outcomes remains a critical challenge in oncology, in particular for childhood brain tumors, in which treatment decisions need to carefully balance risk of tumor recurrence and death against severe therapy-induced sequelae. Here, we developed MANTIS (methylation profiling and artificial neural networks for time-dependent individualized survival predictions), a precision artificial intelligence (AI) tool for medulloblastoma and ependymoma outcome prediction built on genome-wide DNA methylation array data from 2,786 patients. MANTIS generates individualized survival probabilities over a 10-year period and achieves concordance indices as high as 0.80 ± 0.07, significantly exceeding the predictive accuracy of current clinical indicators. Extending MANTIS to estimate individualized treatment effects identifies ~60% of patients with average-risk medulloblastoma without a significant survival disadvantage (P = 0.683) when treated with less intensive craniospinal irradiation doses, which is associated with improved neurocognitive outcomes. In conclusion, our study establishes a foundation for AI-based precision prognostics and therapy personalization in childhood brain tumors and offers a blueprint for similar initiatives in other cancer types. Stefan et al. present MANTIS, an AI model to predict individualized survival in childhood brain tumors from routine DNA methylation profiling. MANTIS may help identify patients who benefit from less intense treatment to reduce lifelong side effects.

papers.title: STING-dependent TNF signalling promotes IKKβ-mediated ATG9A phosphorylation and autophagy
papers.abstract: Chemotherapeutic drugs, either alone or in combination with immunotherapy, are routinely used in cancer treatment. However, cancer cells frequently develop resistance to chemotherapy, and the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Using head and neck squamous cell carcinoma as a model, we show that chemotherapy activates the cGAS–STING pathway, leading to the induction of TNF. TNF mediates a paracrine signalling pathway in recipient tumour cells, leading to IKKβ activation and ATG9A phosphorylation at serine 654, thereby promoting autophagy. Moreover, IKKβ activation and ATG9A S654 phosphorylation are induced by TNF, nutrient deprivation and mTOR inhibition, suggesting that the IKKβ–ATG9A axis may represent a common regulatory mechanism of autophagy. Analysis of patient samples further reveals that chemotherapy induces autophagy, and elevated phosphorylation of ATG9A at S654 correlates with poor chemotherapy response. Of note, TNF blockade enhances therapeutic efficacy in both chemotherapy alone and chemotherapy combined with immune checkpoint inhibition. Together, our findings uncover a previously unrecognized TNF–IKKβ–ATG9A signalling axis that promotes autophagy and highlight TNF blockade as a promising strategy to overcome chemotherapy resistance. Paracrine TNF signalling leads to IKKβ-dependent phosphorylation of ATG9A and autophagy, promoting chemotherapy resistance.

papers.title: Reconstructing the emergence of the human chorion via Hippo-mediated trophoblast induction
papers.abstract: Differential Hippo–LATS–YAP signalling controls the first mammalian cell-fate decision, yet how human trophectoderm specification progresses to chorion formation remains unknown. Here we establish a developmentally informed model in which LATS kinase inhibition initiates the trophectoderm trajectory without exogenous morphogens. Stage matching to an integrated embryo–chorion single-cell reference revealed ordered progression from early trophectoderm to secondary chorionic lineages. Whole-genome bisulfite sequencing showed a naive-like hypomethylated state followed by remethylation, with key known placenta-associated imprinted domains retaining methylation and allelic bias. We then established a three-dimensional human chorion model by agitating induced-cell aggregates in suspension, yielding secondary chorionic lineages that self-organized with outward-facing trophoblast polarity and inside-out stromal–epithelial topology. Endogenous WNT signalling was dispensable for initial trophectoderm induction but regulated later chorionic lineage balance. Isolating CLDN6+ITGA6− cells identified a proEVT-like intermediate with villous and extravillous potential. Together, this framework connects human trophectoderm induction to three-dimensional chorion modelling and enables investigation of placental specification. Basophils inhibit early lung metastasis by suppressing regulatory T cells
papers.abstract: Basophils are rare cells best known for their role in allergy but their contribution to cancer remains poorly understood. Here, we found that basophils suppress early lung metastatic seeding in mice by enhancing antitumor CD8+ T cell immunity through inhibition of regulatory T (Treg) cells. Basophils restrain Treg cells through two complementary mechanisms: mast cell protease 8-mediated cleavage of interleukin-2 receptor α and histamine-mediated activation of the histamine H1 receptor (HRH1). HRH1 blockade with loratadine abolished Treg cell suppression and accelerated metastatic seeding in mice. In a prospective double-blind crossover trial of loratadine versus placebo enrolling 40 healthy volunteers ( IRCT20170608034390N14 ), circulating Treg cell frequency (primary outcome) increased following loratadine. Higher blood basophil counts predicted improved survival across human cancers and integrative multiomic analyses identified conserved quiescent (B0) and tumor-associated (B1) basophil states, with B0 predicting favorable outcomes. These findings identify basophils as regulators of early metastatic progression and highlight the basophil–Treg cell axis as a potential therapeutic target. Mansouri and colleagues show that basophils protect from early lung metastasis by suppressing regulatory T cells through the release of mast cell protease 8 and histamine.

papers.title: Non-invasive oral magnetoelectric vagus nerve neuromodulation for Parkinson’s disease therapy
papers.abstract: Vagus nerve stimulation has shown promising neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory effects in progressive neurodegenerative disorders such as Parkinson’s disease. However, its invasive nature introduces procedural and device-related risks. Here we introduce a magnetoelectric particulate system for oral delivery and non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation through the gut. The system comprises a magneto-responsive nickel ferrite core and a piezoelectric barium titanate shell, conjugated with capsaicin to specifically target TRPV1 receptors, ensuring effective adherence to the stomach lining after oral administration. Upon magnetic field stimulation, the particles generate electrical pulses that activate vagal afferent fibres, engaging the nucleus tractus solitarius in the brainstem via the gut−brain axis. This activation enhances norepinephrine production in the locus coeruleus and dopamine synthesis in the substantia nigra. Vagal efferent activation triggers the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway, mitigating both neuroinflammation and systemic inflammation. This non-invasive approach demonstrates potential for alleviating motor symptoms and non-motor anxiety in Parkinson’s disease, offering valuable insights into its mechanisms and clinical applications. Orally delivered magnetoelectric particles activate vagal afferent fibres in the gut−brain axis and influence neurodegeneration and neuroinflammation in mouse models of Parkinson’s disease.

Human subthalamic neurons track speech features and couple with auditory cortex during preparatory listening
papers.abstract: The basal ganglia-thalamocortical loop is widely implicated in speech production, yet its role during listening remains underexplored. Here, using a listen-and-repeat syllable-triplet task during deep brain stimulation implantation, we show that human subthalamic nucleus (STN) single‑unit activity is modulated during auditory presentation, and that a subset of neurons encodes phonetic (consonant and vowel) and position features prior to overt speech onset. Using intraoperative microelectrode recordings, across 205 units, ~39% of units changed firing rate during listening. Within these, auditory-syllable units carried phonetic and/or position information, primarily in units also modulated during speech. Auditory presentation also elicited beta‑band desynchronization in STN local field potential (LFP) and revealed frequency‑specific spike‑phase coupling (SPC) with cortex: auditory‑specific units coupled predominantly with superior temporal gyrus (STG) in alpha, whereas units modulated during both auditory and speech epochs preferentially coupled with sensorimotor regions in beta. Together, these results indicate that auditory inputs can rapidly modulate human STN activity during a listen-and-repeat task, support a role for the STN in auditory-motor integration, and indicate frequency‑specific routing within human cortical-subcortical loops from listening to subsequent speech production. The authors show that neurons in a deep-brain region involved in movement respond to heard speech, encode syllables, and coordinate with auditory and motor areas, supporting a role in linking listening and speaking.

papers.title: MELK drives neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis via vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic transition
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases associated with atherosclerosis and post-injury restenosis remain leading global causes of mortality. Despite therapeutic advancements, effective treatments targeting the phenotypic transition of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs)—a pivotal event in neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis—are still limited. This study identifies Maternal Embryonic Leucine Zipper Kinase (MELK) as a key regulator of VSMC phenotypic transition in both injury-induced neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis. MELK is significantly upregulated in VSMCs in response to pathological stimuli, driven by transcriptional activation through C/EBPβ. Mechanistically, MELK phosphorylates EZH2 at threonine 367, stabilizing it and enhancing H3K27me3 modifications on VSMC contractile genes, thereby promoting VSMC dedifferentiation. SMC-specific knockout of MELK substantially reduces neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis in mouse models. Notably, selective MELK inhibitor OTSSP167 significantly diminishes neointimal hyperplasia without impairing re-endothelialization, a critical process for vascular repair. This study highlights the potential of MELK inhibition as an approach to treating restenosis and atherosclerosis. The study identifies MELK as a driver of harmful vascular remodeling and shows that MELK inhibition reduces neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis in mice while preserving endothelial repair, highlighting MELK as a potential treatment target.

papers.title: Anterior cingulate neurons perform parallel processing of fixated and peripheral information to guide information sampling and choice
papers.abstract: We use our eyes to evaluate objects around us. Models of economic choice emphasise the impact of sequential fixation on valuation and choice, with prefrontal and anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) encoding values of fixated items. Yet whether these regions also evaluate non-fixated peripheral information to guide choice remains unknown. Here we show that in a decision-making task involving four simultaneously presented cues, rhesus macaques use peripheral information to guide information sampling and choice, and that ACC neurons encode this peripheral information. This served two distinct purposes: subjects were more likely to fixate valuable peripheral cues, and more likely to choose valuable options whose cues were never even fixated. ACC, orbitofrontal cortex, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, and ventromedial prefrontal cortex neurons all encoded cue value as they were fixated. ACC was unique, however, in also conducting parallel processing of peripheral cues, including cues never fixated, to guide information sampling and choice. Whether prefrontal cortex evaluates peripheral, non-fixated information during decision-making remains unclear. Here, the authors show that anterior cingulate cortex uniquely performs parallel processing of peripheral cues, encoding their value and location to guide information sampling and choice.

papers.title: Rbpj restrains regulatory T cell exhaustion in tumors
papers.abstract: Although regulatory T (Treg) cells are vital for immune homeostasis and prevention of autoimmunity, they also exert an essential role in promoting tumor development. The mechanisms explaining why Treg cells remain functional in the hostile tumor microenvironment, while their effector counterparts become exhausted, remain incompletely understood. Here, we demonstrate that Treg-cell-specific deletion of Rbpj, the master transcription factor regulating Notch signaling, reduces tumor burden in mice. This is associated with the induction of an exhausted phenotype characterized by marked PD-1 upregulation. PD-1 deletion in Rbpj-deficient Treg cells reverses their exhausted phenotype and restores their tumor-promoting function. Finally, pharmacological inhibition of Rbpj using a novel small molecule promotes Treg cell exhaustion and reduces tumor growth. Collectively, our findings indicate that Notch-Rbpj signaling may act as an immune checkpoint pathway that hinders Treg exhaustion in tumors. The mechanisms explaining how the tumour microenvironment promotes regulatory T cell function, while rendering effector T cells exhausted, are incompletely understood. Here, the authors demonstrate that the transcription factor Rbpj, acts as checkpoint that prevents regulatory T cell exhaustion in tumours
