papers.title: Recruitment of TEX15 by HUSH2 drives repression of multicopy gene families in fertility regulation
papers.abstract: Chromatin-associated proteins are key regulators of fertility. While the testis-specific protein TEX15 and a HUSH2 component TASOR2 have established roles in early germ cells and somatic cells respectively, this study identifies their cooperative role during spermiogenesis. Postnatal loss of either TEX15 or TASOR2 in mice causes teratozoospermia without retrotransposon de-repression. Mechanistically, TEX15 complexes with TASOR2 but not its paralogue TASOR in the testis. The resulting TEX15-HUSH2 complex localizes to nuclear foci in round spermatids, particularly at XY chromatin, with TASOR2 acting as the recruiter. TASOR2 and MPP8 preferentially bind to multicopy gene families in round spermatids. Consequently, many of these families—including the X-linked H2al histone-like genes—are upregulated in both TEX15-deficient spermatids and TASOR2-deficient testis. Together, these findings show that the TEX15-HUSH2 complex represses multicopy gene families during spermiogenesis, revealing a molecular mechanism underlying postmeiotic repression of sex chromatin critical for male fertility. In this study, Yang et al showed that the TEX15-HUSH2 complex represses multicopy gene families in haploid spermatids. Their study revealed a molecular mechanism underlying postmeiotic repression of sex chromatin (PMSC) critical for male fertility.

papers.title: Minimally invasive topological light manipulation with lensless fiber endomicroscope
papers.abstract: Topological light fields, with their robust properties, offer transformative potential across photonics. However, achieving flexible manipulation and practical deployment of topological light fields in hard-to-reach areas remains challenging. To overcome this limitation, we propose an adaptive topological light endoscopic system (ATLES) and pioneer an integrated transceiver design based on a multi-core fiber, enabling minimally invasive detection with topological light field manipulation. Leveraging the ATLES framework, we reconfigure a 10,000-core fiber into a high-resolution modulator for phase, amplitude, and coherence control. This enables the on-demand creation of both coherent and incoherent topological light fields, tailored in their structures, directly from a bare fiber tip of just 350 μm in diameter. We demonstrate the power of this approach by performing highly precise rotational velocity measurements under endoscopic conditions, achieving a relative error below 0.055%. Our work establishes a versatile platform for the implementation of topological photonics in hard-to-reach areas, thereby paving the way for their application in biomedical imaging and optical computing. This study presents a 350 μm-wide lensless fiber endoscope that creates tailored topological light and measures rotation with relative errors below 0.055%, enabling precise optical control and sensing in hard-to-reach spaces.

papers.title: Structural basis for curvature generation and functional specialization in spirochete flagella
papers.abstract: Spirochetes are spiral-shaped bacteria whose curved periplasmic flagella drive corkscrew-like motility through viscous environments. Despite their clinical importance, molecular mechanisms underlying flagellar assembly remain poorly understood. Here, we combine cryo–EM of flagellar filaments natively isolated from oral pathogen Treponema denticola, with proteomics and comparative genomics to characterise the molecular organisation. We resolve two filament types to sub-3 Å resolution: thin FlaB3-only cores, and thick filaments with a FlaB1/2 core asymmetrically decorated by a sheath comprising FlaA1/2/3 and lattice proteins FlaL1/2. We show sheath asymmetry imposes differential axial compaction on the FlaB1/2 core, generating convex and concave filament faces and establishing curvature. FlaB sequence and glycosylation differences at sheath–core interfaces correlate with selective incorporation into distinct filament types, supporting a mechanism for regulated filament architecture. Phylogenetic analysis reveals FlaL conservation across spirochete lineages, suggesting modular sheath lattices provide an adaptable mechanism for tuning flagellar mechanics across diverse pathogenic lifestyles. Spirochetes twist through tissues with a powerful corkscrew motion driven by curved internal flagella. Here, authors use cryo-EM to show that an asymmetric protein sheath on a conserved flagellin core shapes these flagella, setting the filament curvature needed for motility.

papers.title: Lamprey and hagfish VLRB signalling complex VLRB-GPIbβ-GPIX originates from lymphocyte-specific duplication of a platelet adhesion module
papers.abstract: Unlike jawed vertebrates relying on Ig-based adaptive immunity, jawless vertebrates utilize variable lymphocyte receptors (VLR) for antigen recognition. Despite extensive studies into VLR diversity and antigen recognition, how VLR engagement activates lymphocytes remains unexplored. Integrating single-cell and full-length transcriptomic data of lamprey and hagfish with functional studies, we identify a VLRB cell-specific tripartite VLRB-GPIbβ-1-GPIX-1 complex transducing activation signals via an ITAM motif in GPIbβ-1. Phylogenetic reconstruction reveals its origin from lineage-specific duplication of ancestral platelet GPIb-IX complex in agnathans, yielding two functionally divergent paralogs retained in thrombocytes or co-opted by VLRB lymphocytes. Transcriptional profiling demonstrates BHLHE41 and FOS as potential regulators of complex-expression. scRNA-seq reveals that VLRB cells, analogous to mammalian B cells, transition from pre-activated to post-activated states with proliferative, plasma cell-like features and VLRB complex up-regulation. Collectively, these findings reveal repurposing of a platelet-adhesion module into a VLRB cell-specific signalosome, unveiling a missing link in VLR-mediated adaptive immunity. The jawless vertebrate antigen receptor VLRB functions analogously to the B cell receptor, despite bearing no structural similarity to it. Here the authors identify the signalling complex downstream of VLRB and show that the origin of the genes encoding the signalosome is an ancient platelet unit that has been duplicated in the lymphocyte lineage.

papers.title: Synthetic tools to redirect the ubiquitin E3 ligase activity of a plant-specific N-recognin
papers.abstract: The Arg/N-degron pathway regulates important agronomic traits. In plants, the PROTEOLYSIS 1 (PRT1) protein binds to aromatic amino-terminal residues and recruits ubiquitin (Ub) conjugating enzymes to ubiquitinate substrate proteins. Here, we demonstrate that PRT1 recruits the UBC35-UEV1A complex via RING1 of PRT1. This stimulates UBC35 to produce K63-linked Ub chains. To afford chemical control over Ub signalling, we construct a synthetic substrate of PRT1 with an N-terminal calmodulin-binding peptide (CBP). The addition of the CBP sequence to the substrate creates an off switch for PRT1-dependent ubiquitination that is regulated by calcium and calmodulin. Finally, we produce a set of nanobodies that are recognised by PRT1 and induce the ubiquitination of a reporter protein. Altogether, we introduce and biochemically validate several tools to both redirect and chemically control the Arg/N-degron pathway. The Arg/N-degron pathway plays a central role in plant development, germination, and submersion tolerance. Here, the authors show that PRT1 recruits the UBC35-UEV1A complex via RING1 of PRT1, demonstrate an off-switch for calmodulin-controlled ubiquitination, and engineer nanobodies that can redirect PRT1.

papers.title: Npl4 decodes polyubiquitin length and undergoes D1-gated exchange on p97/VCP
papers.abstract: Human p97 binds the Npl4–Ufd1 heterodimer adapter to extract polyubiquitinated substrates for proteasomal degradation, but how it decodes K48-linked chain length and how D1-coupled events license downstream D2 power strokes remain unclear. Here we introduce smUbiRAD, or single-molecule ubiquitin recognition and dynamics, and identify a sharp chain-length threshold: Npl4 binds transiently to short chains but switches to long-lived, multivalent engagement on tetra- and penta-ubiquitin. Ufd1 and p97 further stabilize these complexes mainly by suppressing Npl4 dissociation without affecting the initial encounter. In fully assembled p97-Ufd1-Npl4-substrate complexes, D1 ATP hydrolysis—rather than D2—drives rapid Npl4 exchange. These results support a model in which D1-powered conformational changes promote cofactor Npl4, but not Ufd1, turnover and gate iterative coupling to downstream D2-driven substrate processing. Finally, we show that multisystem proteinopathy variants R155H and A232E bias p97 toward a high-affinity resting state and accelerate Npl4 exchange, implicating hyperactive cofactor cycling in disease. p97 maintains protein quality by processing ubiquitin-tagged proteins. This report shows how Npl4 reads ubiquitin-chain length and how p97 ATPase activity controls Npl4 exchange, which is altered by disease-linked variants

papers.title: Genomic surveillance meets clinical practice: rule-based individualized treatment prediction for gonorrhoea using SensiTyper
papers.abstract: Extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains threaten the current empirical gonorrhoea treatment. We designed and analytically validated SensiTyper, a rule-based framework that predicts antimicrobial susceptibility from whole-genome sequencing data and generates susceptibility-guided individualized treatment recommendations. SensiTyper was applied to 13,701 gonococcal genomes from 68 countries in 1928-2024, including cultured isolates and clinical molecular samples, and benchmarked predictions against previous genomic and phenotypic data. Susceptibility predictions for ceftriaxone, ciprofloxacin, spectinomycin, and zoliflodacin had 98.9-100% sensitivity and specificity. Azithromycin susceptibility predictions had 92.5% sensitivity and 97.1% specificity, and gepotidacin susceptibility prediction 100% sensitivity, but 0% specificity, illustrating that low-level phenotypic gepotidacin resistance is not caused by the only known resistance determinants (GyrA A92T plus ParC D86N). The SensiTreat module integrates antimicrobial susceptibility profiles into sequential treatment logic, providing susceptibility-guided individualized treatment recommendations while also enabling alternative stewardship strategies prioritizing, e.g., ciprofloxacin. SensiTyper flags XDR isolates for expert follow-up, test-of-cure and comprehensive contact tracing. In conclusion, SensiTyper is a robust and adaptable approach for gonococcal antimicrobial susceptibility prediction, individualized gonorrhoea treatment and antimicrobial stewardship. Golparian et al. designed and validated (13,701 global gonococcal genomes) SensiTyper, a rule-based framework predicting antimicrobial susceptibility from whole-genome sequencing data and susceptibility-guided individualized gonorrhoea treatment.

papers.title: Process-dependent shifts in conspecific negative density dependence during boreal forest succession
papers.abstract: Conspecific negative density dependence (CNDD)—the stronger negative effects of conspecific than heterospecific neighbours on plant demographic performance—is a key process proposed to stabilize forest diversity, yet how it changes during succession remains poorly understood. Using a 25-year spatially explicit dataset from 148 post-fire plots in boreal forests, we show that species richness increases with stand age and that CNDD varies in process- and abundance-dependent ways across recruitment, survival, and growth. Plot-level CNDD shows no significant change with stand age in recruitment or survival, but mean relative effects are generally stronger for recruitment, and CNDD shifts from destabilizing to stabilizing for growth as stands mature. Species-level CNDD is strongly associated with species abundance, with rare species consistently experiencing stronger CNDD in recruitment and growth, whereas common species tend toward neutral or destabilizing effects. For survival, by contrast, CNDD is stronger in common than in rare species. These abundance-related differences remain broadly consistent across stand development, except in recruitment, where CNDD intensifies in rare species but remains consistently weak or near-neutral in common species. This shifting balance of density-dependent pressures highlights succession-driven trade-offs as central to species coexistence and increases in diversity in disturbance-driven forests. Conspecific negative density dependence may maintain diversity, but its role during succession is unclear. This study shows that changes depend on demographic processes and species abundance rather than following a uniform community-wide trend.

papers.title: Ligand hardness as a key feature differentiating base- versus noble-metal mechanisms of nickel-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-couplings
papers.abstract: Nickel-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions that engage alkyl electrophiles provide potential routes for synthesis of molecules with high Fsp3. However, development of these reactions remains a challenge since the impact of ligand identity on competing mechanistic pathways is not yet well understood. To address this knowledge gap, we establish structure-reactivity trends across >550 Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reactions with known mechanistic pathways. We evaluate reaction outcome by ligand features including heteroatom identity, hybridization, bite angle, geometry, and buried volume. The most important determinant of reactivity is heteroatom identity: nitrogen-based ligands support open-shell reactions while phosphorus-based ligands support closed-shell reactions. Here we report that experimental and calculated reduction potentials and charge density analysis correlate with catalytic activity and propose a rationale for these observations based on hard-soft acid-base theory. The authors establish structure-reactivity trends across <550 Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reactions with known mechanistic pathways. They evaluate reaction outcome by ligand features including heteroatom identity, hybridization, bite angle, geometry, buried volume, reduction potential and APT charge.

papers.title: Ancestry-specific and multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies of restless legs syndrome
papers.abstract: Restless legs syndrome is a neurological disorder that disrupts sleep and quality of life, but its genetics have mostly been studied in individuals of European ancestry. Here, we perform GWAS of restless legs syndrome using data from individuals of African, Latin American, and European ancestry, followed by a multi-ancestry meta-analysis. We leverage biobank-based cohorts that established RLS diagnosis using validated clinical criteria, allowing for precise phenotypic characterization. We perform ancestry-specific association studies and post-GWAS analyses to prioritize candidate genes. Our analyses reveal ancestry differences in the genetics of restless legs syndrome. At the MEIS1 and BTBD9 loci, lead variants showed lower allele frequencies and did not reach genome-wide significance in African ancestry. We identify ancestry-specific and shared risk loci, including novel associations near GYPC/TEX51 and PRIMA1 in African ancestry and ISX in Latin American ancestry. The European meta-analysis identifies 11 additional loci and replicates 50 previously reported associations. The combined multi-ancestry analysis finds ten new loci. This multi-ancestry study broadens the genetic understanding of restless legs syndrome, and the absence or reduced frequency of key European restless legs syndrome alleles in individuals of African ancestry provides insights into known epidemiological differences. The genetics of restless legs syndrome have mostly been studied in European populations. Here, the authors perform a multi-ancestry genetic study of the condition, revealing differences in genetic risk across populations with different ancestries.

papers.title: Performance of artificial intelligence-assisted cytology and high-risk human papillomavirus testing for cervical cancer screening
papers.abstract: Evidence comparing cervical cancer screening strategies that combine artificial intelligence-assisted liquid-based cytology (AI-LBC) and high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) testing in large-scale populations is limited. This study includes 284,002 women who underwent AI-LBC and HR-HPV genotyping in community-based screening in Wuhan, China. We evaluate the performance of nine hypothesized screening strategies in detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) and their colposcopy referral rates. After correcting for verification bias, HR-HPV testing alone (Strategy 4) demonstrates higher sensitivity (94.93% vs. 83.88%) and a higher Youden’s index (0.864 vs. 0.789) than AI-LBC alone (Strategy 1), but requires a higher referral rate (9.05% vs. 5.49%). Among the triage-based strategies, Strategy 3 (AI-LBC with reflex HR-HPV) achieves a sensitivity of 82.90%, a referral rate of 2.67%, and a Youden’s index of 0.807. HR-HPV genotyping with reflex AI-LBC (Strategy 7) demonstrates a sensitivity of 92.68%, a Youden’s index of 0.899, and a referral rate of 3.34%. Co-testing of AI-LBC and HR-HPV genotyping (Strategy 9) achieves the highest Youden’s index (0.932), with a sensitivity of 96.37% and a referral rate of 3.70%. These findings suggest that AI-LBC performs well as a standalone screening method, triage tool, or a component a co-testing strategy in cervical cancer screening. When HR-HPV genotyping is available, Strategy 7 or Strategy 9 may be considered, depending on the trade-off between detection performance and referral burden. The authors prove AI-assisted cytology effective for cervical cancer screening. When combined with HPV testing, it detects more precancerous lesions and maintains low referral rates.

papers.title: Interfacial reinforcement relieves mechanical mismatch for stable perovskite photovoltaics
papers.abstract: Long-term operational durability under realistic day-night cycling remains a critical bottleneck for the commercialization of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). While significant progress has been made in managing thermo-mechanical stress within the perovskite layer, day-night cycling tolerance remains far from real-world applications, as cycling-induced interface degradation at adjacent functional layers has largely been overlooked. Here, we identify a failure mechanism at the C60/atomic layer deposition (ALD)-SnO2 interface in inverted PSCs, where a severe mismatch in mechanical properties leads to substantial internal stress accumulation, readily causing interfacial delamination and accelerating device degradation. To address this, we introduce graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) as a multifunctional buffer layer between C60 and ALD-SnO2. This two-dimensional material acts as a compliant mechanical bridge, effectively alleviating stress and suppressing microcrack formation, while simultaneously facilitating electron transport across the interface. As a result, the target PSCs achieve a remarkable efficiency of 27.05% and exhibit superior robustness. Notably, the devices retain over 90% of their initial efficiency after 1056 h of maximum power point tracking under day-night cycling. Our findings advance the understanding of interfacial failure mechanisms and provide a practical strategy to support the commercialization of durable PSCs. The day-night cycling durability remains a bottleneck for the commercialization of perovskite photovoltaics. Li et al. introduce g-C3N4 as a buffer layer between C60 and SnO2 to alleviate stress and suppress microcrack. The resulting device achieves a power conversion efficiency of 27.05%.

papers.title: Sequence Display generates large-scale sequence–activity datasets for reprogramming SlugCas9 toward difficult-to-access PAMs
papers.abstract: Protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) requirements constrain the targeting scope of CRISPR-Cas9 systems and limit genome editing applications that require precise nuclease positioning. Although broad-PAM and near-PAMless Cas9 variants have expanded the editable genome, robust targeting across certain PAM families remains difficult, particularly at NNAN PAMs. Here, we apply Sequence Display to generate multiplexed, large-scale sequence–activity datasets for Staphylococcus lugdunensis Cas9 (SlugCas9) across the NNAN PAM family, including NNAA, NNAT, NNAC and NNAG. These datasets quantitatively resolve how individual and combinatorial mutations reshape nuclease activity across distinct PAM contexts. By integrating Sequence Display-derived datasets with protein language models, we construct fine-grained activity landscapes and identify SlugCas9 variants with enhanced and broadened activity across NNAN PAMs. The resulting variants reprogram PAM recognition beyond the native G-compatible landscape of SlugCas9 and enable improved base editing at selected endogenous NNAN-constrained sites in cultured mammalian cells, including disease-relevant sites in APOC3 and PCSK9. Together, our results establish a strategy for reprogramming PAM preference in compact Cas9 nucleases and highlight Sequence Display as a general platform for evolving genome editors toward specific and difficult-to-access PAM spaces. Compact CRISPR-Cas9 enzymes are easier to deliver but recognize few targets. Here, authors use Sequence Display to generate large-scale SlugCas9 sequence–activity datasets and apply protein language models to engineer variants that recognize difficult NNAN PAMs and edit selected human genomic sites.

papers.title: Memristive crossbar architecture for programmable and scalable terahertz metasurface
papers.abstract: Programmable terahertz (THz) metasurfaces have emerged as a versatile platform for dynamic wavefront control, offering possibilities for high-capacity wireless communication and advanced sensing. Realizing full wavefront control requires scaling to large-format arrays with pixel-level reconfigurability, but this is fundamentally limited by inter-pixel crosstalk and the increasing complexity of electrical interconnections. Here, we present a scalable, pixel-level programmable metasurface addressing architecture inspired by the crossbar architecture of memristor arrays, and implement it in the THz regime. By integrating VO2-based snapback selectors, this design effectively suppresses sneak path currents, allowing low-crosstalk addressing of each pixel. A modular row-column tiling scheme facilitates scaling to large arrays while preserving per-pixel programmability. We further demonstrate independent two-dimensional phase modulation and non-volatile THz beam steering. This work provides a theoretical framework and design paradigm for a versatile and scalable photonic platform spanning the THz to optical regimes. Guo and colleagues develop a programmable terahertz array based on phase-change materials and crossbar addressing, enabling scalable control of individual elements, retention of programmed states and beam steering.

papers.title: A motion vector sensor-enabled 3D spinal morphology monitoring suit for intelligent scoliosis identification
papers.abstract: Early identification of scoliosis is important for timely clinical intervention. However, conventional static screening methods rely on subjective assessments, resulting in limited accuracy and insufficient continuity. Here, we propose a motion vector sensor-enabled 3D spinal morphology monitoring suit for intelligent scoliosis identification. We engineer a highly anisotropic mesh with orderly aligned conductive fibers, enabling the motion sensors to precisely perceive motion amplitude and direction. The suit integrates motion sensors positioned at symmetrical body locations to quantify 3D spinal motions bz capturing skin-surface deformation amplitude and direction. We achieve dynamic scoliosis identification through machine learning-powered evaluation of spinal kinematic symmetry. We test performance on a multi-center cohort comprising four hospitals and one school-based screening program, demonstrating 92.63%, 71.05%, and 82.76% accuracy for scoliosis detection, curvature degree quantification, and curvature location identification, respectively. This radiation-free alternative has the potential to support longitudinal follow-up and reduce repeat radiographs in scoliosis management. Early detection of scoliosis is critical for timely intervention, but current screening lacks accuracy. Here the authors develop a motion vector sensor-enabled 3D spinal morphology monitoring suit for accurate, intelligent scoliosis identification.

papers.title: Intruding delta waves during REM sleep are associated with tau, amyloid, and forgetting in aging
papers.abstract: Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep degrades with age, and more severely in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). REM sleep comprises about twenty percent of adult sleep, alternates between phasic and tonic periods, and includes delta waves (1-4 Hz) in two forms: fast sawtooth waves and slower, NREM-like waves, whose expression dynamically varies across REM periods. Yet, the functional relevance of these REM sleep delta waves remains unknown. Here, using two independent cohorts, we show that aging is associated with a shift from fast sawtooth to slow NREM-like delta waves, particularly during phasic REM sleep - a period typically marked by high cortical activation. Beyond chronological age, this shift is associated with amyloid-β and tau burden, suggesting that AD pathology is associated with REM-specific oscillatory patterns. Furthermore, this shift in REM oscillations is linked to impaired overnight memory consolidation, independent of NREM sleep quality. Moreover, variation in APOE alleles, a major genetic risk factor for AD, was independently associated with a reduction in fast sawtooth wave density, thereby linking a genetic predisposition for AD to these specific REM microstructural changes. These findings identify a signature of memory decline in aging and implicate REM sleep as a distinct vulnerable substrate through which AD pathology may impair brain function. Desel et al. report that memory loss in aging is associated with a shift from fast sawtooth to slow delta waves during REM sleep. This shift correlates with amyloid and tau burden, marking a REM sleep signature of impaired memory consolidation.

papers.title: Genomic heterogeneity inflates the performance of variant pathogenicity predictions
papers.abstract: Recent studies have reported unprecedented accuracy predicting pathogenic variants across the genome, including in noncoding regions, using large deep-learning models trained on vast genomic data. To verify and understand the basis of these reports, we systematically evaluated the prediction accuracy of frontier models over single-nucleotide variants, focusing on general models capable of scoring multiple variant types across coding or noncoding regions. Our evaluations reveal that the performance of genome-wide predictions is severely inflated by mixing variant categories with different baseline prevalences of pathogenic variants. We constructed a benchmark stratified by variant type to identify the best-performing models for each genomic context, determine where reliable predictions remain out of reach, and establish rigorous standards to guide future evaluations. Evaluations of AI models predicting disease-causing single nucleotide variants reveal that the performance of genome-wide predictions is inflated by mixing variant types, e.g. canonical splice and 5’ UTR variants. The authors introduce a stratified benchmark to accurately identify the most robust models.

papers.title: Equipositioning of chromosomes in the polyploid archaeon Haloferax volcanii by HpaAB
papers.abstract: Proper genome segregation is essential for cellular survival, yet this process is poorly understood in archaea. Archaea show considerable variability in genome ploidy and organization. Haloferax volcanii DS2 is a polyploid archaeon with a fragmented genome consisting of a main chromosome, three secondary chromosomes and a plasmid. Due to high ploidy, genomic segregation in H. volcanii is typically considered random. However, we identified four two-gene operons encoding ParA-like proteins and uncharacterized partners. Here we characterized HpaA and HpaB, encoded on the secondary chromosome pHV3. HpaA contains conserved ATPase walker motifs and is a ParA protein with a bacterial origin. Mutation of key residues in HpaA alters its localization, while HpaA is necessary for proper HpaB spatial distribution. HpaB forms cytosolic foci and functions as a centromere-binding protein, analogous to bacterial ParB. Deletion of the genes hpaA and hpaB results in severe growth defects when xylose is the sole carbon source, consistent with the location of xylose degradation genes on pHV3. It also reduces the pHV3 to main chromosome ratio. Single-particle tracking suggests that HpaB influences HpaA dynamics. Together, these findings demonstrate an equipositioning of pHV3, likely supporting maintenance in the different cell morphologies observed in H. volcanii. How the archaeon Haloferax volcanii segregates its multi-copy chromosomes during cell division is unclear. Here, the authors identify two proteins required for an equidistant positioning mechanism, maintaining uniform spacing between chromosomes.

papers.title: Host diet may shape bat RNA viromes within geographic and phylogenetic constraints at a global-scale
papers.abstract: Bats are key models for studying the ecological mechanisms driving viral community structure, yet the role of diet remains unclear. By integrating 1627 RNA virome libraries from 78 bat species across 13 countries, we recovered 309,546 vOTUs spanning 66 recognized RNA virus families, whereas 82.74% remained unclassified, suggesting extensive viral “dark matter”. Classified viruses were associated with vertebrates, invertebrates, plants and plant-associated fungi, with invertebrate-associated viruses contributing prominently to overall diversity. Viral community composition differed significantly among feeding guilds, with sanguivorous bats exhibiting a specialized viral community structure. However, sampling site and host phylogeny explained substantially more variation than feeding guild, indicating that broad-scale bat virome structure is primarily shaped by geography and host evolutionary history. Analyses restricted to vertebrate-associated viruses further showed that feeding guild was associated with community composition but not viral species diversity. Viral sharing was more strongly structured by sampling site and host phylogenetic distance than by shared diet. Together, these findings indicate that geography and host phylogeny dominate broad-scale viral community structure, whereas diet plays a secondary role by modulating exposure to viruses through predation. This improves our understanding of bat viral assemblages and informs assessments of host–virus associations and spillover risk. By analyzing 1,627 bat RNA viromes from 78 species worldwide, the study shows that geography and host evolution shape bat viral communities more strongly than diet, while feeding ecology plays a secondary role in viral exposure.

papers.title: IDPForge: deep learning of proteins with global and local regions of disorder
papers.abstract: Although machine learning has transformed protein structure prediction of folded protein ground states with remarkable accuracy, intrinsically disordered proteins and regions (IDPs/IDRs) are defined by diverse and dynamical structural ensembles that are predicted with low confidence by algorithms such as AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold. We present a machine learning method, IDPForge (Intrinsically Disordered Protein, FOlded and disordered Region GEnerator), that exploits a transformer protein language diffusion model to create all-atom IDP ensembles and IDR ensembles that maintains the folded domains. IDPForge does not require sequence-specific training, back transformations from coarse-grained representations, nor ensemble reweighting. The created IDP/IDR conformational ensembles show good agreement with both NMR and SAXS solution experimental data, and options for biasing with experimental restraints are available if desired. IDPForge with these diverse capabilities facilitates integrative and structural studies for proteins that contain intrinsic disorder, and is available as an open source resource for general use. Intrinsically disordered proteins and regions (IDPs/IDRs) are defined by diverse structural ensembles. We present IDPForge that exploits a transformer protein language diffusion model to create all-atom IDP and IDR ensembles that maintain folded domains with options to conform to experimental data.

papers.title: Phylogeny and intraspecific variability dominate nitrogen fixer biomass responses to nitrogen enrichment
papers.abstract: Anthropogenic nitrogen (N) enrichment profoundly influences the growth of N-fixing plants, but the drivers underlying their highly variable biomass responses remain poorly quantified. Through a meta-analysis of 2,110 paired observations across 76 N-fixing plant species from 121 experiments, we demonstrate that N enrichment increases N-fixing plant biomass by 14.2% on average, with responses ranging from −99.4% to 1301.3%. Intraspecific variability (26.9%; i.e., variation among individuals within species) and plant phylogeny (21.1%) represent substantial yet frequently overlooked sources of uncertainty in biomass responses of N-fixing plants to N enrichment, even though environmental conditions (climatic and edaphic factors) and experimental design (N enrichment rate and duration) account for a significant portion of biomass response variation. Intraspecific variability, phylogeny, and experimental design collectively explain a larger proportion of variance in root than in shoot biomass responses, whereas environmental conditions show the opposite trend. These results provide quantitative evidence that phylogeny and intraspecific variability are indispensable for accurately predicting the response of N-fixing plants to global change. Nitrogen enrichment alters the growth of nitrogen-fixing plants, but responses vary widely. This meta-analysis shows that phylogeny and intraspecific variation are major contributors to that variability.

papers.title: Real-time quantification of skeletal muscle metabolism in healthy men using hyperpolarised [1-¹³C]pyruvate reveals training-dependent adaptation
papers.abstract: Skeletal muscle undergoes rapid and dynamic changes in energy demand during exercise, limiting the physiological relevance of resting-state measurements. Here, we demonstrate the feasibility of combining hyperpolarised ¹³C magnetic resonance spectroscopy (¹³C-MRS) with ³¹P-MRS to non-invasively measure real-time metabolic responses in exercising human skeletal muscle. Sedentary and endurance-trained men perform plantar-flexion exercise inside a magnetic resonance scanner. Dynamic hyperpolarised [1-¹³C]pyruvate spectra from the medial gastrocnemius show that increasing exercise intensity escalates pyruvate-to-lactate conversion relative to mitochondrial pyruvate utilisation. Endurance training is associated with greater bicarbonate labelling, consistent with increased mitochondrial pyruvate utilisation, and reduced lactate production. These metabolic signatures are accompanied by intensity- and training-dependent differences in phosphocreatine degradation and intracellular pH decline measured by ³¹P-MRS. Together, these findings demonstrate the feasibility of combining hyperpolarised ¹³C- and ³¹P-MRS to phenotype skeletal muscle metabolism during exercise, providing a platform for investigating metabolic adaptations in ageing, disease and therapeutic intervention. This study combines hyperpolarised ¹³C- and ³¹P-MRS to non-invasively measure human muscle metabolism in real time, revealing training-dependent metabolic adaptations and linking ¹³C metabolite ratios to established measures of muscle energetics.

papers.title: Foundation models unlock robust phenotypic representations from Cell Painting images
Decoder-FFPE-seq enables sensitive, genome-wide spatial transcriptomics of archival tissues at single-cell resolution
papers.abstract: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue–compatible spatial transcriptomics (ST) is transforming biology and histopathology, but achieving high sensitivity, genome-wide coverage, single-cell resolution, and researcher accessibility remains challenging. To address these challenges, we here present a dendrimeric DNA coordinate barcoding design for FFPE tissue–adapted spatial RNA sequencing (Decoder-FFPE-seq) by integrating RNA-to-DNA probe conversion with blotting-assisted barcoding. Decoder-FFPE-seq provides single-cell resolution with a >2.6-fold sensitivity increase in whole-transcriptome mouse brain and archived human sample profiling over existing platforms, resolving potential cellular identity of low-abundance genes, finer tissue architecture, and capturing an epithelial-mesenchymal transition–associated signature for prognostic value. With expanded probe libraries, Decoder-FFPE-seq captures long noncoding and viral RNAs, revealing their spatial coregulatory networks with messenger RNAs in oral squamous cell carcinomas (OSCCs). In an OSCC immunotherapy cohort, two CD8 + T cell subpopulations were respectively identified in pre- and postchemoimmunotherapy samples, potentially linked to treatment response. Decoder-FFPE-seq establishes a robust, high-resolution, and accessible framework for sensitive ST profiling of archival tissues in fundamental and translational studies.

papers.title: Graph-based pangenome analysis uncovers structural and functional impacts of allopolyploidization events
papers.abstract: The emergence of graph pangenomes has advanced the study of structural variants (SVs) across diverse species, yet the impact of complex ploidy on SV landscapes remains poorly explored. Brettanomyces bruxellensis , a yeast shaped by multiple allopolyploidization events, offers a compelling model due to its well-characterized genomic and phenotypic diversity. Here, we integrated subgenome-resolved assemblies with population-scale genomic and transcriptomic datasets to characterize SV distribution and functional impact at the species level. Leveraging a reference graph pangenome, we detected 5972 unique SVs across 1060 isolates. Allopolyploid genomes harbored significantly more SVs (320 on average) than diploids (116), reflecting hybridization’s extensive impact on genome architecture. Functional association analysis revealed that 27.5% of SVs locally influence gene expression. Furthermore, a subset of SVs originating from ancestral divergence between subgenomes (hybridization-associated SVs) formed hotspots of structural diversity and disproportionately affect gene expression, with larger effect sizes than other SVs. These findings underscore allopolyploidization as a driver of structural and functional genomic diversification, highlighting the value of graph-based approaches in dissecting complex genome evolution.

papers.title: A nematic framework for sprouting angiogenesis
papers.abstract: Sprouting angiogenesis is critical for embryogenesis, wound healing, and tumor growth. Here, we show that the liquid crystal framework, which has recently been leveraged to study various morphogenetic events, provides unique insight into angiogenic sprouting. In response to vascular endothelial growth factor, a potent proangiogenic factor, endothelial cells cultured on the surfaces of soft collagen hydrogels form elongated cell streams that coexist with more polygonal cell regions. Angiogenic sprouting initiates preferentially at cell stream tips, where nematic order gradients are most pronounced. We demonstrate that cell streams are associated with large traction forces that lead to three-dimensional deformations of the underlying hydrogel and that stream formation results from a delicate balance between microtubule polymerization and actomyosin contractility. Last, we show that active control of nematic order allows modulation of sprout formation, highlighting the key role of endothelial cell orientation gradients in angiogenic sprouting and paving the way for new therapeutic avenues.

papers.title: Oxygen-dependent constraint of glycolysis through the mitochondrial electron transport chain
papers.abstract: Hypoxia-inducible factors (HIFs) are constitutively active in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) cells. Here, we investigated whether these cells could still respond to hypoxia independently of canonical HIF activation. We found that hypoxia provokes a NADH reductive stress that attenuates lactate release when the supply of extracellular pyruvate becomes limited, a response that was restored by the ectopic expression of the cytosolic and mitochondria-targeted NADH oxidase ( Lb NOX). Suppression of the mitochondrial electron transport chain (mtETC) alone is sufficient to attenuate glycolytic flux when extracellular pyruvate is limited, a situation consistent with metabolomic data from human ccRCCs. Furthermore, this response can be mimicked by pharmacological or genetic inhibition of mitochondrial complex IV (CIV) activity and restored by the mitochondrial-targeted alternative oxidase (AOX). Therefore, our data suggest that cells can respond to low oxygen tension through a mitochondrial-dependent elevation of NADH/NAD + , resulting in the suppression of glycolysis when pyruvate availability is compromised.

papers.title: Robust pan-junctional reinforcement preserves the gut epithelial barrier under mechanical stress
papers.abstract: Epithelia are specialized tissue barriers that safeguard the organism’s internal milieu from the external environment, a function critically dependent on intercellular junctions. In the colon, this barrier is repeatedly challenged by mechanical distension from feces, but it is unknown whether and how the colon adapts to this stress, which could otherwise compromise barrier integrity. Here, we show that feces-mediated mechanical distension triggers coordinated remodeling at cell and tissue scales, consistent with a mechanoadaptative response. This response includes recruitment of junctional proteins at all three types of adhesive cell-cell junctions (tight junctions, adherens junctions, and desmosomes). We identified protein-specific temporal profiles of junctional enrichment during distension, with ZO-1, E-cadherin, desmocollin 2, and plakoglobin exhibiting sustained junctional enrichment, whereas desmoplakin and keratin 8 showed progressive accumulation peaking at 15 min of distension. Distension was also accompanied by perijunctional recruitment and activation of nonmuscle myosin II (NMMII). Through genetic, pharmacological, and mechanical perturbations, we demonstrated that NMMII activation is required for epithelial mechanoadaptation. This process depends on extracellular calcium availability and mechanosensitive ion channel activity, supporting a role for calcium-dependent mechanosensitive signaling in NMMII-mediated junctional reinforcement. Loss of NMMII function impaired the junctional response to distension across all three junctional complexes, including desmosomes, resulting in disorganized junctions and barrier breach. Together, our findings uncover a robust physiological mechano-adaptive response of the adult colonic epithelium to an extrinsic mechanical stress, whereby coordinated reinforcement of all junctional complexes, requiring myosin II activity and calcium-dependent mechanosensitive signaling, preserves intestinal barrier integrity.

papers.title: Chirality-selective second-harmonic response with Floquet engineering
papers.abstract: Symmetry breaking profoundly influences the macroscopic physical properties of materials. For instance, inversion symmetry breaking in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides enables the emergence of chiral selection rules, featuring distinct optical chirality-selective electronic properties. Here, we demonstrate ultrafast, coherent manipulation of chirality-selective nonlinear optics in monolayer molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ) through time-reversal symmetry breaking via Floquet engineering. By using sub-bandgap, circularly polarized ultrafast optical pulses, we introduce nondegenerate, chirality-selective optical Stark and Bloch-Siegert shifts. This approach effectively lifts the energy degeneracy, leading to pronounced chirality-selective second-harmonic generation. Furthermore, we reveal that the Floquet-engineered chirality-selective states can be finely tuned using optical parameters such as intensity and chirality. Our results show a method for manipulating the energy degree of freedom, paving the way for ultrafast nonlinear photonics.

papers.title: RNA binding by ADARs prevents RNA interference from attacking self-produced dsRNA
papers.abstract: The ability of an organism to distinguish between self and foreign double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) is central to eliciting an immune response when needed while preventing autoimmunity. Using Caenorhabditis elegans , we investigated the interplay between two host pathways that regulate dsRNA expression and function, adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing by adenosine deaminases that act on RNA (ADARs), and RNA interference (RNAi). We found that the number of small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) targeting edited genes is significantly up-regulated in ADAR mutant animals. In addition, despite an almost complete depletion of primary siRNAs generated from editing sites in wild-type animals, secondary siRNAs are generated from edited transcripts, suggesting that ADARs antagonize only the first step of RNAi processing. We show that ADARs interfere with the efficacy of exogenous RNAi in vivo, likely to prevent trans-silencing, and provide evidence that ADR-2 binding to dsRNA is required for efficient RNAi suppression. This work sheds light on how RNA editing safeguards self-dsRNAs against immune recognition and by-product degradation.

papers.title: Monsoon zonal seesaw: Development of the South Asian monsoon aridified North Africa in the Cenozoic
papers.abstract: North Africa experienced a pronounced transition from humid to arid conditions during the early Cenozoic. Meanwhile, the South Asian monsoon underwent substantial intensification, largely driven by the uplift of the Himalayan-Tibetan Plateau. Here, we demonstrate that the two events, which greatly shaped the paleoenvironment and modern regional climate, are not independent responses to paleogeography changes; rather, the former is primarily driven by the latter through the monsoon-desert mechanism, in which South Asian monsoon diabatic heating produces large-scale subsidence and aridity over North Africa. Using multiple ensembles of paleoclimate simulations and a model for the atmospheric response to imposed diabatic heating, we show that the intensification and poleward shift of Asian monsoon rainfall each make comparable contributions to the aridification of North Africa. Our findings identify a persistent dynamical pathway linking the South Asian and North African monsoons and suggest that it played a major role in early Cenozoic North African aridification, while its climatic expression at other times depended on the relative strengths of competing forcings.

papers.title: Enhanced room-temperature spin transport in a deuterated molecular single crystal
papers.abstract: Achieving high-efficiency spin transport at room temperature remains a central challenge in spintronics. Molecular single crystals are ideal candidates for addressing this challenge because their highly ordered lattices and uniform transport pathways intrinsically suppress spin scattering and enable long spin lifetimes. However, integrating these intrinsic advantages into practical devices has remained challenging, primarily because molecular single crystals are extremely fragile during device fabrication. Here, we design a molecular single-crystal system with uniform spin-transport pathways and suppressed spin-relaxation channels, resulting in a substantially enhanced room-temperature spin lifetime, as confirmed by both theoretical analysis and experimental characterizations. By applying a damage-free crystal-handling method with an optimized electrode-transfer technique, we fabricate high-quality single-crystal spintronic devices and achieve a spin-transport efficiency of 15.17% at room temperature, nearly twice the previous benchmark (∼8%). This work establishes a generalizable strategy for designing long-spin-lifetime molecular spintronic materials and demonstrates the practical viability of molecular single crystals as a platform for efficient room-temperature spin transport.

papers.title: Evidence of active whole-genome doubling (WGD) subclones in non-WGD tumors
papers.abstract: Whole-genome doubling (WGD) occurs frequently in human cancer and influences tumor evolution, metastasis, and treatment response. Here, we integrate bulk, single-cell, and spatial data to dissect the subclonal dynamics of WGD. Single-cell data analysis shows that WGD cells are prevalent even in tumors that are classified as non-WGD (nWGD). WGD subclones actively acquire somatic copy number alterations as they expand, suggesting ongoing evolution. We developed and rigorously validated a gene expression–based method, WAGES, to map WGD cell clonal fraction in bulk tumors. Applying WAGES to nWGD tumors, we reveal genomic correlates including TP53 mutations and chromosomal instability that are consistent with the presence of WGD subclones. Clinically, WAGES scores are strongly correlated with tumor metastatic potential, response to treatments including chemotherapy and immunotherapy, and patient prognosis. These findings reveal widespread WGD subclones in nWGD tumors and demonstrate their substantial impact on cancer evolution and therapeutic outcomes.

papers.title: A soft wireless bioelectronic patch for noninvasive modulation of cavernosal microenvironment in diabetic erectile dysfunction
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus–induced erectile dysfunction is difficult to reverse due to long-term impairment of cavernosal microenvironment. Conventional oral or intracavernosal injection therapies suffer from poor targeting, uneven drug distribution, and potential complications. Here, we propose a soft, wireless electronic patch for treating erectile dysfunction (SWEED) in diabetes mellitus, which enables safe, noninvasive, and controllable modulation of penile microenvironment. With its “microelectrode–drug reservoir–nanopore” configuration, SWE intensifies local electrical field nanoscopically and achieves uniform transdermal drug delivery. Through the enhanced local delivery of prostaglandin E1 (PGE1), SWEED demonstrates high efficiency in promoting the expression of vascular factors for endothelial repair and enhancing cavernosal blood perfusion. In both in vitro and in vivo settings, the platform achieves vascular regeneration and functional recovery comparable to clinical intracavernosal injection therapy. Moreover, it activates proerectile signaling pathways (EP2/PKA/CREB) and suppresses the TGF-β/Smad pathway, markedly alleviating cavernosal fibrosis. This work presents a paradigm for noninvasive diabetes mellitus–induced erectile dysfunction therapy.

papers.title: Human hair–bearing skin organoids reveal cell type–specific susceptibility and innate immune responses to herpes simplex virus 1
papers.abstract: Epithelial surfaces are the primary sites of lytic herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) infection following initial exposure or reactivation from latency. To model this complex environment, we used human hair–bearing skin organoids and combined single-cell spatial transcriptomics with imaging to map viral spread and host responses across skin architecture. Our data suggest delayed progression of the HSV-1 life cycle in epidermal keratinocytes and hair follicle cells compared to the dermis. Infection triggered spatially organized host responses, including induction of IER3 in papillary fibroblasts. In basal keratinocytes, IRF3 was up-regulated in both infected and neighboring uninfected cells, consistent with paracrine activation of antiviral signaling. Inflammatory responses were compartmentalized in a cell type–specific manner, with TNFSF9 (4-1BBL) induced in papillary fibroblasts and tumor necrosis factor–α (TNF-α) induced in keratinocytes. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays confirmed secretion of these cytokines and the TNF-α–responsive chemokines CXCL2 and CXCL10. CXCL2 expression was enriched in cells adjacent to TNF-α–expressing cells, highlighting spatial coordination of inflammatory signaling. While interferon-β reduced viral replication, TNF-α and 4-1BBL did not, suggesting that their primary role is to orchestrate immune cell recruitment and activation. These findings establish human hair–bearing skin organoids as a physiologically relevant model for investigating spatial host–HSV-1 interactions.

papers.title: General prediction of T cell receptor antigen specificity from sequence using AlphaFold 3
papers.abstract: The major histocompatibility complex (MHC):peptide:T cell receptor (TCR) complex is the most diverse trimolecular interface known in nature and a key trigger for adaptive immunity. TCRs are now routinely sequenced at scale; however, decoding their specificity for antigens remains a bottleneck. While in silico approaches have advanced considerably, none enables prediction against “unseen” epitopes, limiting their applicability to a tiny fraction of cases. Here, we show that AlphaFold 3 (AF3) predicts the structures of MHC:peptide:TCR triads with unprecedented accuracy. By applying AF3 to >9000 TCRs mapped to >1000 distinct epitopes restricted by >70 MHC class I/II alleles, we identify features that distinguish cognate triads from controls. The resulting model achieves median areas under the curve of 0.81 to 0.92 on validation triads unseen by AF3 or during feature selection. Our results reveal that generalized prediction of TCR specificity from sequence is possible, with the potential to greatly accelerate the decoding of immune responses.

papers.title: Photosynthetic chimeric stem cells function as mitochondrial batteries
papers.abstract: Therapies built on mitochondrial transfer hold promise for repairing dysfunctional, energy-deficient cells. Still, mesenchymal stem cells used as mitochondrial donors are limited by poor engraftment, risk of aberrant differentiation, and low transfer efficiency. Herein, we constructed photosynthesis-empowered cross-kingdom chimeric stem cells (PCSs; “mitochondrial battery”) by introducing plant-derived thylakoid-based artificial nuclei plus FGF21 -encoding messenger RNA (mRNA) into enucleated bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. Photosynthetic activity enhances mitochondrial transfer to restore metabolism in damaged cells and elevates anabolism to increase FGF21 production. Sustained FGF21 release promotes mitochondrial biogenesis and sustains long-term cellular energy homeostasis. Mouse and porcine wound healing models demonstrate that PCSs recharge cellular energy to accelerate wound repair. This light-activated cellular photosynthetic platform supports modular mRNA programmability, shows no engraftment or aberrant differentiation, and allows repeated administration for diverse therapeutic applications.

papers.title: Intrinsic cellular persistent firing sustains hippocampal spatial representations during working memory
papers.abstract: Neurons are the fundamental units of cognitive processing. The prevailing view holds that neurons are input-output units that fire action potentials only upon receiving sufficient synaptic input. Here, we demonstrate that this may not be the sole operational mode of neurons in vivo during cognitive tasks, by showing that hippocampal place cells actively maintain firing and preserve spatial information through molecularly defined intrinsic mechanisms. Using in vitro and in vivo recordings coupled with molecular manipulation in mice, we reveal that hippocampal persistent firing during spatial working memory is supported by individual neurons via TRPC4 ion channels. Despite the general belief that persistent activity maintains working memory content, we demonstrate that persistent firing instead maintains immediate spatial representations, potentially supporting the encoding of spatial information to guide behavior. These findings position individual neurons as active contributors to information retention, extending their traditional role as passive input-output units and potentially broadening our understanding of neural computation.

papers.title: Tunneling spectroscopy of topological insulator Josephson junctions
papers.abstract: In the seminal proposal by Fu and Kane, the superconducting proximity effect is used to realize topological superconductivity in the topological surface state (TSS) of a 3D topological insulator (TI). In a Josephson junction made on the TI surface, the spin-momentum locking of the TSS guarantees the existence of spin nondegenerate, perfectly transmitted Andreev modes. These modes lead to gap closing as a function of the superconducting phase difference φ. Here, we report the observation of highly transmissive Andreev modes in a TI Josephson junction, probed via tunnel contacts and φ controlled by a flux loop. Within our experimental resolution, they could indicate a gap closing and reopening. This phenomenon is observed for a wide range of chemical potentials, supporting its TSS origin. Under an applied magnetic field, highly transmissive modes are observed locally, matching theoretical predictions for Josephson vortices in the TSS. Our results support the fundamental role of spin-momentum locking in the Andreev physics in the TSS.

papers.title: LAMP2A gene therapy mitigates Parkinson’s disease–related pathology in nonhuman primates
papers.abstract: Chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA), regulated by its lysosomal receptor LAMP2A, is a key pathway for αSynuclein (αSyn) clearance and a direct target of αSyn-related neurotoxicity. Rodent studies show that LAMP2A enhancement reverses neurodegeneration, whereas its deficiency accelerates pathology. To test translational relevance, we examined whether increasing LAMP2A expression in nonhuman primates could mitigate α-synucleinopathy induced by injections of Parkinson’s disease patient-derived Lewy body (LB) extract. Increasing LAMP2A expression protected nigral dopaminergic neurons from LB-induced αSyn neurodegeneration, delayed the formation and release of pathology-related αSyn species, and evoked a beneficial effect on motor behavior and on cognitive functions of the primate model. Our findings provide preliminary preclinical evidence supporting CMA enhancement as a therapeutic strategy for αSynucleinopathies.

papers.title: PDS5A and TOP2B cooperate for chromatin recruitment via CTCF
papers.abstract: PDS5A, a cohesin regulatory subunit, and topoisomerase IIB (TOP2B), an enzyme resolving DNA topological problems, interact with CTCF and regulate transcription and genome organization. We ascertained that PDS5A and TOP2B are recruited to CTCF-bound chromatin cooperatively and that catalytically active TOP2B increases PDS5A occupancy genome wide. Notably, the amino-terminal 95 to 116 amino acids of CTCF interacts with PDS5A, giving rise to CTCF-PDS5A-TOP2B interaction in vitro and to PDS5A chromatin enrichment via active TOP2B in vivo. PDS5A-TOP2B function together in moderating the resultant gene expression and genome organization. Loss of CTCF (95 to 116 amino acids) led to dysregulated gene expression and mildly reduced chromatin loops. In gliomas, PDS5A and TOP2B expression levels vary, but correlate, contributing to distinctive gene expression patterns. Inducible PDS5A knockdown led to reduced TOP2B occupancy and altered gene expression. Furthermore, PDS5A mediated sensitivity to TOP2 cancer drugs in glioma cells. This functional interaction between PDS5A and TOP2B at CTCF boundaries expands upon the mechanisms affecting gene regulation through genome organization, with implications for glioma therapeutics.

papers.title: The Fireside Database: Large-scale evidence from 25,419 psychedelic support interactions
papers.abstract: Most psychedelic experiences occur outside clinical settings, yet as policy frameworks rapidly expand to accommodate nonclinical use, no systematic data exist on who seeks psychedelic support, under what circumstances, or what makes that support effective. We present the Fireside Database, a US-based dataset comprising 25,419 peer support interactions conducted by 220 trained volunteers at Fireside Project’s Psychedelic Support Line between April 2021 and February 2026. The released resource integrates structured interaction logs with volunteer-coded metadata and 2777 caller satisfaction surveys across five outcome dimensions. Psilocybin was the most commonly reported substance (59.9% of coded interactions), while cannabis produced the highest distress rate (47.2%). The nested data structure—with 50 supporters each completing ≥10 surveyed interactions—supports multilevel modeling of individual supporter effects on caller outcomes. This resource enables research in psychedelic epidemiology, evidence-based training design, and the investigation of what makes psychedelic psychological support effective.

papers.title: Augmenting intercellular mitochondrial transfer for tissue repair and rejuvenation
papers.abstract: Cells exhibit innate reparative communication, enabling the exchange of bioactive molecules and, in some cases, entire organelles. Harnessing this endogenous process of intercellular organelle transfer represents an emerging therapeutic paradigm for restoring cellular function in diseases driven by organelle dysfunction. Mitochondrial transfer has gained prominence for its ability to restore bioenergetic capacity, mitigate oxidative stress, and rescue metabolic function in cells with impaired mitochondrial activity. Given that genetic or acquired defects in mitochondrial function are associated with diverse pathologies, including neurodegeneration, cardiovascular diseases, metabolic disorders, skeletal muscle defects, immune dysregulation, and age-associated decline, mitochondrial transfer offers broad therapeutic potential. Mitochondrial transfer seeks to deliver functional mitochondria to injured cells to reestablish metabolic competence. However, insufficient organelle trafficking and limited control over transfer dynamics remain critical barriers to clinical translation. Recent biotechnological developments aimed at enhancing donor-recipient connectivity, increasing mitochondrial availability, and modulating transfer machinery have begun to address some of these key challenges. This review highlights recent advances in mitochondrial transfer bioengineering, emerging therapeutic applications, and key challenges that must be resolved to enable clinical deployment.

papers.title: C:H:N:O:P stoichiometry and oxygen demand of marine organic matter are driven by phytoplankton ecophysiology
papers.abstract: Although the hydrogen and oxygen content of marine phytoplankton plays a critical role in determining oceanic O 2 consumption rates, shaping habitat for anaerobic metabolism, they are often assumed to be constant in biogeochemical studies, resulting in biased estimates of respiration rates. Here, by simulating phytoplankton allocation in a general circulation model, we predict latitudinal variations in phytoplankton C:H:N:O:P composition and corresponding O 2 demand. These patterns are driven by physiological adaptation to environmental conditions and are consistent with observations. Subtropical phytoplankton have more C─O bonds and lower O 2 demand, as they contain more carbohydrates than higher-latitude populations. We test the sensitivity of O 2 inventory and regenerated C via the biological pump (C soft ) to plausible bounds of cellular allocation and find that the global O 2 inventory and C soft decrease by ∼11 and 14%, respectively, when a cell shifts from carbohydrate-rich to protein-rich biomass. Our findings demonstrate that biochemical remodeling of phytoplankton composition mediates large-scale patterns and oceanic budgets of O 2 and C.

papers.title: Cryo-EM structure of a protein nanopore reveals lipid acyl chains as integral components
papers.abstract: Nanopore-based technologies are revolutionizing nucleic acid sequencing and molecular sensing, yet the structural basis by which pore-forming proteins interact with lipid membranes remains poorly defined. The mycobacterial porin MspA is a benchmark biological nanopore owing to its exceptional stability and uniquely narrow constriction, but accurate structural information is limited to protein-only models. Here, we present a 2.5-angstrom resolution cryo–electron microscopy structure of the M2 mutant of MspA embedded in a phospholipid nanodisc, providing a high-resolution experimental observation of MspA in a lipid environment. The structure reveals an annular arrangement of extended lipid acyl chains surrounding the MspA oligomer and contacting the transmembrane barrel. Their resolved densities indicate a substantially more ordered annular lipid environment than would be expected from a largely heterogeneous and nonspecific protein-lipid interface. The structure also demonstrates how specific M2 MspA mutations modulate pore polarity, influencing ion selectivity and transport. By determining the membrane-embedded structure of MspA and revealing an ordered arrangement of acyl chains forming extensive hydrophobic interactions with the protein, this study demonstrates the importance of the surrounding lipid environment in the design of protein nanopores.

papers.title: A-site cation–pseudohalide co-design for tin halide perovskite transistors
papers.abstract: Tin halide perovskites are promising lead-free semiconductors for next-generation electronics; however, their implementation is constrained by a fragile crystal framework, facile Sn 2+ oxidation, and rapid crystallization kinetics. Here, we establish a molecular design principle for non-metallic thiocyanate (SCN − ) additives that stabilizes the formamidinium tin iodide (FASnI 3 ) lattice and enables high-performance, stable p-channel thin-film transistors (TFTs). Density functional theory calculations reveal that the Sn–X–Sn bond strength in the lattice and the halide migration barriers can be tuned by the size of the A-site cation and its hydrogen-bonding capability with SCN − and I − . In particular, we find that both the Sn–SCN–Sn bonding interaction and the iodine migration barrier are maximized when guanidinium thiocyanate (GuaSCN) is employed. Consistently, GuaSCN enhances the crystallinity and grain size of tens-of-nanometer-thick FASnI 3 films, prolongs carrier lifetimes, and suppresses Sn 4+ formation, without altering the intrinsic bandgap. TFTs incorporating GuaSCN achieve a field-effect mobility above 88 cm 2 V −1 s −1 , an I on/off ratio exceeding 4 × 10 9 , negligible hysteresis, and superior operational and shelf stability across hundreds of devices.

papers.title: Electric field–controlled spin transport in a topological insulator interfaced with a ferroelectric antiferromagnet
papers.abstract: Topological insulators have been explored extensively for spin-charge interconversion via magnetic interfaces, yet the true response of their spin-charge conversion, particularly in the absence of an external magnetic field, remains to be studied. Here, we report electric field control of spin-charge conversion in the topological insulator Bi 2 Te 3 with the antiferromagnetic multiferroic BiFeO 3 , using a nonlocal spin transport device. A systematic thickness dependence of the spin transport across the interface between Bi 2 Te 3 and BiFeO 3 reveals a signature of topological surface-state–dominated spin transport in the bilayer system. The spin-charge conversion remains robust for thicknesses above 10 nanometers but falls rapidly with reducing thickness and vanishes at 5 nanometers. This is consistent with hybridization-induced emergence of a trivial insulating phase, which is supported by the coherency factor estimated from the magnetoconductance of Bi 2 Te 3 . These results establish that spin-momentum–locked surface states dominate interfacial spin transport in the decoupled regime. Beyond presenting efficient spin-charge interconversion at an entirely insulating magnetic interface, this work also highlights sputter-deposited Bi 2 Te 3 as a high-quality and scalable platform for integrating quantum materials onto the devices. The nonlocal spin transport approach presented here provides a simple and unprecedented direct evidence of spin-charge conversion and opens an efficient and practical pathway toward designing energy-efficient spin-based devices.

papers.title: Rashba-induced intersubband interference in high-harmonic generation
papers.abstract: High-harmonic spectroscopy is exquisitely sensitive to the electronic structure and dynamics of quantum materials, yet quantum interference between spin-orbit-split bands has remained experimentally elusive. We observe this interference between Rashba-split bands in bismuth tellurium iodide (BiTeI) driven by strong mid-infrared laser fields. The sixth harmonic exhibits intensity-scaling kinks and an M-shaped ellipticity dependence. Theoretical simulations attribute these features to spin-orbit–mediated multichannel quantum interference, which arises from Landau-Zener-Stückelberg–type intersubband tunneling between Rashba-split bands. The suppression of harmonic yield under linearly polarized pulses arises from destructive interference among electron-hole recombination pathways, whereas increasing ellipticity modifies their relative phase and induces a distinct spectral redshift. These results establish high-harmonic spectroscopy as a probe of spin-textured band dynamics and ultrafast spin-polarized currents.

papers.title: Mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming by a glutamine antagonist radioenhancer conjugate drives pyroptosis and antitumor immunity
papers.abstract: Aberrant glutamine metabolism undermines the efficacy of cancer radiotherapy (RT) by promoting DNA repair, increasing oxygen consumption, and imposing metabolic stress that compromises the viability and function of cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs). Here, we report a mitochondria-enriched, metabolism-regulating monolayered metal-organic framework (MOF) nanoplatform, Hf-Ir/DON, constructed by incorporating the glutamine antagonist 6-diazo-5-oxo- l -norleucine (DON) into a radiosensitizing hafnium-iridium (Hf-Ir) MOF to inhibit glutaminolysis. This design markedly sensitizes tumor cells to RT and, upon x-ray irradiation, enables mitochondria-targeted RT-radiodynamic therapy with substantially enhanced reactive oxygen species accumulation. The resulting oxidative stress induces extensive DNA damage, mitochondrial dysfunction, and immunogenic tumor cell pyroptosis. Concurrently, Hf-Ir/DON alleviates metabolic constraints on activated T cells, preserving CTL viability while sustaining effector and memory functions. In a murine colon cancer model, low-dose RT combined with Hf-Ir/DON achieved >95% tumor growth inhibition. Further combination with anti–PD-L1 therapy induced regression of bilateral triple-negative breast tumors and prevented lung metastasis. These results establish a radiometabolic MOF nanoplatform that potentiates RT while promoting durable antitumor immunity.

papers.title: Metazoan diversification characterized by elevated rates of evolution during the middle Ediacaran to earliest Cambrian
papers.abstract: To test causal hypotheses for the emergence of animal body plans, we analyze rates of molecular and phenotypic evolution across Opisthokonta, focusing on divergences within the Tonian-Ordovician interval. Both molecular and phenotypic rates increase through the Ediacaran, peaking in an Ediacaran and earliest Cambrian interval before declining thereafter. Partitioning phenotypic characters into categories relating to development, feeding, fossilization potential, locomotion, and nervous systems reveals distinct temporal patterns, with developmental traits contributing disproportionately to elevated rates in the metazoan stem lineage. Rate patterns show a temporal lag between the ecological changes integral to hypotheses of developmental evolution and the Cambrian agronomic, substrate, and information revolutions and earlier peaks in the evolution of the associated phenotypic characters. These patterns are largely independent of the timescale used. Overall, our results indicate that the primary phase of elevated evolutionary novelty occurred during the Ediacaran and culminated in the late Ediacaran-earliest Cambrian, providing the foundation for later ecological and taxonomic innovation.

papers.title: A dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle delivery system for precision phage therapy against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria
papers.abstract: The escalating crisis of antimicrobial resistance, particularly among Gram-negative bacteria, demands innovative therapeutic strategies. Here, we present a dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle-chimeric phage (AbLCP) system engineered to combat multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacteria. Our design integrates a genetically modified M13 phage displaying anti–lipopolysaccharide (LPS) antibodies with polymyxin B conjugation, which is further encapsulated within anti-LPS antibody–functionalized lipid nanoparticles. This system overcomes the fundamental limitations of conventional phage therapy, enabling efficient cellular internalization, endosomal escape, and potent intracellular bactericidal activity. In murine models of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, AbLCP achieved superior bacterial clearance and up to 10 3 -fold reduction in bacterial burden at a 10 3 -fold lower effective dose than free polymyxin B, with 67-fold selective accumulation at infection sites, and attenuated systemic inflammation and preservation of gut microbiota. Mechanistically, AbLCP neutralized LPS to suppress inflammation and induced a lethal bacterial stress response. This work establishes a transformative nanophage platform that merges synthetic biology with nanomedicine, offering a promising strategy against MDR bacterial infections.

papers.title: Monolithic and scalable capacitive electrodes leveraging parasitic capacitance for full-body pressure mapping
papers.abstract: Scaling capacitive pressure sensor arrays to large areas remains challenging due to electrode alignment errors, fabrication complexity, and limited dynamic range inherent in conventional parallel-plate architectures. Here, we present a scalable capacitive pressure sensor array based on a monolithic electrode architecture, where transmitter and receiver electrodes are co-integrated into a single substrate. A deformable dielectric and a floating ground (GND) layer are positioned above, eliminating alignment errors and reducing the layer-stacking process by 20%. The parasitic capacitance between the electrodes and GND layer is intentionally incorporated into the sensing mechanism, enabling stable pressure detection with effective electromagnetic interference shielding. The resulting 2911-cell array (1.7 m by 1.0 m) achieves 30 Hz full-body pressure mapping with high linearity (R 2 = 0.994). Demonstrations in sleep posture classification, pressure injury prevention, and exercise monitoring validate the platform’s versatility for healthcare and human-machine interfaces.

papers.title: A skin-like, all-in-one hydrogel engineered via a supramolecular entangled network reinforced with hydrogen-bond–associated nanodomains
papers.abstract: Hydrogels hold substantial promise for artificial skin in bionic robotics and biomedical devices. However, few hydrogels have a combination of properties comparable to natural human skin. Here, we report a skin-like, all-in-one hydrogel based on a supramolecular entangled network reinforced with hydrogen-bond–associated nanodomains. Within this architecture, hydrogen-bond–associated self-assembled nanodomains, polymer-chain entanglement, dynamic electrostatic interactions, and reversible metal-ligand coordination operate cooperatively to endow the network with mechanical robustness and dynamic adaptability. Consequently, the hydrogel reconciles the intrinsic trade-offs among mechanical properties, multiple functions, and multimodal perception. Its integrated performance compares favorably with that of other advanced hydrogels and even biological skin. To demonstrate its potential applications, we constructed an artificial skin using our hydrogel, which facilitates interaction with the surrounding environment, including monitoring respiration, detecting motion, and manipulating robotic grippers. These results pave the way for versatile hydrogels that replicate the unparalleled combinatory properties of natural skin more precisely for diverse intelligent applications.

papers.title: Alleviating the stability-energy density dilemma via electron-donor-mediated orbital symmetry regulation in sodium phosphate cathodes
papers.abstract: Manganese-based sodium super ionic conductor-type cathode materials, leveraging the multielectron redox activity of manganese, represent a promising pathway toward high-energy-density sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). However, the unavoidable generation of Mn 3+ (3d 4 ) species during charge-discharge processes, characterized by asymmetric e g orbital occupancy, triggers octahedral symmetry breaking. This inherent electronic structural instability creates a fundamental contradiction between achieving high energy density and ensuring long cycle life that remains inherently difficult to reconcile. Here, we report an electron-donor–mediated (EDM) mechanism that suppresses Mn 3+ -induced octahedral distortion while preserving high-spin functionality. As electron-donating Fe 3+ and V 3+ are incorporated, Mn 3+ 3d electrons undergo partial delocalization. This electronic redistribution promotes orbital interactions between neighboring transition metal sites through the transition metal-oxygen framework, driving the e g orbitals toward a more symmetric occupation and suppressing octahedral distortion. The EDM-modified cathode demonstrates a high energy density of 492.06 Wh kg −1 . It delivers 178.8 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C and retains 80.2% of its capacity over 2000 cycles at 10 C, paving a novel pathway toward next-generation high-performance SIBs cathode materials.
