papers.title: GPR183 senses 7α,25-OHC to drive T reg differentiation and tumor immune evasion via AXL-JAK2-STAT5 signaling
papers.abstract: Regulatory T cell (T reg ) accumulation within the tumor microenvironment is a major contributor to immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance. However, the metabolic signals orchestrating T reg lineage commitment remain poorly defined. We identify that the oxysterol 7α,25-dihydroxycholesterol (7α,25-OHC), produced by Vimentin + stromal cells, acts through GPR183 to promote T reg differentiation and suppressive identity. In patients with gastric cancer (GC), GPR183 + T reg infiltration correlates with advanced disease and poor survival. In syngeneic tumor models, conditional GPR183 deletion, specifically in CD4 + T cells or T reg cells, demonstrates its cell-intrinsic requirement for high-cholesterol-diet–induced T reg expansion and tumor growth, thereby abrogating immune evasion and restoring CD8 + T cell effector function. Mechanistically, 7α,25-OHC–GPR183 signaling activates the AXL-JAK2-STAT5 pathway to reinforce Foxp3 expression. Last, GPR183 antagonism modestly enhances anti-PD-1 efficacy in a model-dependent manner and prevents therapy-induced T reg expansion. These findings identify the 7α,25-OHC–GPR183–AXL axis as a potential metabolic checkpoint linking cholesterol metabolism to immune suppression, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy to enhance antitumor immunity.

papers.title: Integrative discovery and functional dependency mapping uncover essential chimeric RNAs in the active transcriptome
papers.abstract: Chimeric RNAs are a class of molecules defined as RNA transcripts containing genetic information for multiple genes. While their expression patterns across tissue types and disease states have been well documented, the biological function of these transcripts remains poorly understood. In this study, we developed an integrative prediction pipeline to establish an atlas of 569,640 chimeric RNAs across 1019 cancer cell lines. Leveraging this resource, we performed a systematic functional dependency screen by integrating our predictions with perturbation datasets from The Cancer Dependency Map project. This approach moves beyond prediction to identifying high-confidence functional chimeric RNAs essential for cellular processes, including a subset of recurrent chimeric transcripts generated by cis - splicing of adjacent genes. We demonstrate that depletion of selected candidate chimeras disrupts cell cycle progression and cellular fitness and that these transcripts are frequently dysregulated in primary breast tumors. Together, these results demonstrate that chimeric RNAs constitute a previously underappreciated layer of gene expression, expanding the functional genome beyond conventional genetics.

papers.title: Competing charge and spin instabilities and giant magnetoelastic coupling in CrSb
papers.abstract: Electronic, magnetic, and lattice degrees of freedom are often strongly intertwined in quantum materials, giving rise to competing ordered states and emergent collective phenomena. Understanding how these interactions evolve across symmetry-breaking transitions is essential for identifying new mechanisms of electronic ordering. Here, we show that the antiferromagnet chromium antimonide provides an ideal platform to investigate this interplay and uncover short-range charge-order fluctuations at the M point of the Brillouin zone, q * = ( 1 2 0 ) , persisting well above the Néel temperature, T N . These fluctuations collapse upon entering the magnetically ordered phase, revealing a direct competition between charge and spin order parameters. At T N , the phonon dispersion at q * develops a pronounced Kohn-like anomaly, signaling strong electron-phonon coupling in the vicinity of the magnetic transition. Below T N , exchange striction markedly renormalizes the associated soft phonon mode by ∼6 milli–electron volts, corresponding to the largest spin-phonon coupling reported to date. First-principles calculations show that the relevant phonon branch is unstable at the harmonic level only in the absence of magnetic order, highlighting the remarkable sensitivity of the lattice to magnetic symmetry breaking. The suppression of charge correlations upon magnetic ordering, together with the abrupt reconstruction of the phonon spectrum at T N , demonstrates an exceptional coupling between charge, spin, and lattice degrees of freedom in chromium antimonide. With its chemically simple structure and symmetry-protected altermagnetic state, chromium antimonide emerges as a model system for exploring giant spin-phonon coupling, competing electronic instabilities, and emergent broken symmetries in altermagnetic materials.

papers.title: Extracellular vesicle-mediated restraint of hepatic CD74–NF-κB repairs diabetic neuropathy
papers.abstract: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) affects up to half of people with diabetes and lacks disease-modifying therapy. Here, we profiled MSC-EV biodistribution and multiomic programs across diabetic models, with key nerve repair established in db/db mice and corroborated in high-fat diet/streptozotocin- and methionine-choline–deficient mice. Systemically administered EVs predominantly accumulated in the liver and improved peripheral nerve structure and function, with benefits supported by glycemia-controlled or glycemia-adjusted analyses rather than being fully explained by systemic glycemic changes. EV treatment was associated with reduced circulating injury markers, attenuated spinal inflammatory responses, and improved endothelial junction integrity. Mechanistically, EV-encapsulated miR-24-3p repressed hepatic CD74, coinciding with reduced MHC II/NF-κB activity in macrophages. Hepatic CD74 overexpression promoted systemic inflammation and peripheral nerve injury, whereas pharmacologic NF-κB inhibition recapitulated EV-associated benefits. Together, these data define a liver-to-nerve causal axis and support EV-mediated restraint of hepatic CD74–NF-κB signaling as a cross-organ strategy for DPN repair.

papers.title: The true scale of global wildlife trade is obscured by data gaps
papers.abstract: Overexploitation of wildlife is one of the greatest global drivers of biodiversity loss. Yet, despite this well-established risk, data on extraction and trade are both incomplete and highly fragmented. The IPBES Global analysis estimated 50,000 species to be in trade, yet our review of wildlife trade monitoring programs found at least double that, at 107,356 species in use and trade globally. This included up to 47,685 animal species, covering 42% of all described vertebrate species. Most countries lack any systematic data on trade for species not listed in Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), with the exception of the US-specific dataset Law Enforcement Management Information System, which frequently had higher diversity of species in trade than global databases. This highlights the importance of national monitoring efforts and the need for standardized collation of wildlife trade data beyond CITES-listed species. Without these changes, global indicators on trade meant to guide sustainability and conservation will continue to focus on less than 2% of traded species.

papers.title: ANME-2a perform methane oxidation in brackish coastal sediments via multiple pathways
papers.abstract: Methane is a powerful greenhouse gas. Typically, a large fraction of methane formed in coastal sediments is removed via anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM). Here, we demonstrate the potential for a range of AOM pathways in brackish coastal sediments by ANME-2a archaea. At our study site, geochemical profiles indicate that AOM is primarily restricted to a shallow, metal oxide–rich sulfate-methane transition zone (SMTZ). ANME-2a were the sole methanotrophs detected, and metatranscriptomics showed the highest expression levels of the ANME-2a genes in the SMTZ. AOM activity was observed in sediment incubations with various electron acceptors, including sulfate, metal oxides, and the organic matter analog graphene oxide. Highest potential rates were observed in sediments from below the SMTZ, pointing toward fast stimulation of the deeper methanotrophic community when alleviating the electron acceptor limitation. The variety of AOM pathways and persistence of methanotrophs below the SMTZ likely contribute to the resilience of the microbial methane filter in brackish coastal sediments.

papers.title: Fluid-driven robotic micromanipulation for assembloid fabrication
papers.abstract: The assembly of cellular spheroids into spatially organized assembloids represents a transformative paradigm for modeling complex biological systems. However, the lack of standardized fabrication strategies fundamentally limits the precision and reproducibility of these models, hindering their widespread application. Here, we present a robotic micromanipulation platform—Fluid-Driven Tweezer with Visual Servo Control (FDT-VSC). By integrating multidimensional visual perception with microfluidic control, our system enables the gentle and programmable assembly of diverse cellular spheroids. Leveraging this platform, we achieve the bottom-up construction of structurally defined, heterogeneous multicellular tissues, and the programmed orchestration of multilineage models that recapitulate the complex microenvironments of early organogenesis. Crucially, the system improves consistency during the scalable fabrication of tumor-stroma assembloids, supporting reliable drug screening. These results demonstrate that FDT-VSC advances assembloid-based applications across modular tissue engineering, developmental biology, and drug discovery.

papers.title: Crystalline three-dimensional membranes enable chromatography-free purification of natural products
papers.abstract: Chromatographic purification of natural products is solvent intensive and energy-demanding and remains a major bottleneck in the sustainable production of pharmaceutical compounds. Here, we show that crystalline three-dimensional membranes enable chromatography-free purification of complex natural product mixtures by organic solvent nanofiltration. The rigid, nanomechanically robust channels of the membrane sustain continuous 6-day operation with commercial Taxus crude extracts, achieving ∼96% retention and fourfold enrichment of paclitaxel while allowing valuable precursors to permeate. The membranes exhibit high solvent permeance with negligible swelling, enabling stable molecular sieving in methanol across extended operation. Scalable fabrication via nanosphere-assembled interfacial polymerization produces continuous crystalline membranes over large areas. Life cycle assessment reveals nearly an order-of-magnitude reduction in carbon emissions compared with liquid chromatography. These results demonstrate a membrane platform that can replace chromatographic steps in natural product drug purification, offering a sustainable route for active pharmaceutical ingredient production.

papers.title: Elevated CO 2 mitigated warming-enhanced carbon loss from northern peatland
papers.abstract: Peatlands store one-third of the global soil carbon (C) on only ∼3% of Earth’s land surface but risk becoming C sources to accelerate climate change due to warming-induced C loss. Elevated CO 2 (eCO 2 ) may mitigate this loss by boosting plant C uptake. However, how eCO 2 and climate warming interact to influence peatland C dynamics remains unclear. Here, we investigated peatland C fate at five warming levels (+0°, +2.25°, +4.5°, +6.75°, and + 9°C), each under ambient CO 2 (aCO 2 ) and eCO 2 (+500 parts per million), by model-guided synthesis of 18 measured variables for each of the 10 treatments from an experiment. Our results showed that the peatland C loss increased with warming at a rate of 62.6 g C m −2 year −1 °C −1 , reaching 476.5 ± 104.7 g C m −2 year −1 at +9°C under aCO 2 , primarily because of increased Sphagnum mortality and accelerated decomposition. eCO 2 reduced the loss rate to 17.3 g C m −2 year −1 °C −1 , nearly halving the C loss at +9°C (269.4 ± 80.5 g C m −2 year −1 ), mainly due to enhanced tree and shrub growth. Methane emissions increased with warming, similarly under aCO 2 and eCO 2 . Our findings suggest that northern peatlands likely become major C sources under climate warming, although rising atmospheric CO 2 concentration may partially slow down the C loss. Climate-driven shifts in plant community structure, rather than peat decomposition alone, play a critical role in regulating peatland C fate and may threaten the stability of peatland ecosystem functions and services in the future.

papers.title: Super-resolution mapping of nuclear stress signaling by probiotic-derived extracellular vesicles in UV-induced skin photodamage
papers.abstract: Ultraviolet (UV)-induced photodamage drives oxidative stress, DNA damage, and chronic inflammation, leading to progressive cellular ultrastructure and skin function degeneration. Despite the potential of probiotics as anti-photodamage agents, their nanoscale action mechanism remains unexplored. Here, we utilize super-resolution fluorescence microscopy to investigate the cellular and molecular basis of Lactobacillus plantarum -derived extracellular vesicles ( L. plantarum EVs) in mitigating photodamage. We showed that UV irradiation triggered extensive organellar remodeling along with elevated reactive oxygen species production, DNA damage signaling, and inflammatory activation. Remarkably, pre- and posttreatment with L. plantarum EVs preserved organelle integrity and restored native nanoscale architecture. Additionally, EV treatment delayed UV-induced PARP-1 activation and nuclear condensate clustering, while suppressing NF-κB translocation and downstream inflammatory cytokine expression. These findings establish probiotic-derived EVs as modulators of stress-responsive signaling and structural homeostasis during UV-induced photodamage. By providing a super-resolution mechanistic framework for understanding probiotic EV-mediated modulation of cellular photodamage responses, this study provides a basis for future investigation of EV-based strategies for skin protection.

papers.title: Coarse climate model grids underestimate coastal humid-heat extremes
papers.abstract: Humid-heat extremes reach intensities close to the limit of human survivability around the Arabian Peninsula. Here, we analyze fully coupled kilometer-scale Icosahedral Nonhydrostatic (ICON) and Integrated Forecasting System–FinitevolumE Sea ice-Ocean Model (IFS-FESOM) simulations from the nextGEMS project, with original resolutions of around 9 kilometers, and compare them with station observations, ERA5, and CMIP6 projections. IFS-FESOM reproduces well the observed upper-tail wet-bulb temperature (TW) and lies near the high end of the CMIP6 distribution over coastal regions, while ICON simulates weaker extremes. Spatial smoothing suppresses localized coastal maxima, reducing daily-maximum TW extremes by up to 8°C and lowering exceedance frequencies across multiple thresholds. Native resolution fields also show stronger mid-century increases in exposure under SSP3-7.0 than their coarse-gridded counterparts. These results suggest that conventional coarse resolution projections may underestimate localized coastal humid-heat risk, although the magnitude of this effect remains model dependent.

papers.title: Antibodies to distinct epitopes on MPXV enveloped virion provide additive and complete protection
papers.abstract: The continuing evolution of monkeypox virus (MPXV) clades capable of sustained human-to-human transmission poses an escalating global health risk, yet no effective therapy exists for poxvirus infection. Here, we investigate a panel of human monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), derived from an antibody library, which targets A35 and B6 antigens located on the extracellular enveloped virion (EV). Four high-affinity mAbs target the central groove of the A35 dimer, whereas one targets a previously unidentified epitope on the A35 protruding loop. Three other mAbs recognize distinct, previously unmapped epitopes on the multidomain B6 antigen. Those epitopes are conserved across most orthopoxviruses. A combination of an anti-A35 and an anti-B6 antibody provides additive and complete protection from both morbidity and mortality in a lethal VACV mouse model, challenging the previous assumption that targeting both the EV and mature virion (MV) forms is required for full protection. These studies uncover critical information for next-generation therapeutics and vaccines against emerging MPXV as well as other Orthopoxvirus threats.

papers.abstract: In the aging Drosophila brain, Orb2 amyloids required for long-term memory undergo structural remodeling, shifting from translation-promoting assemblies to destabilization-resistant, translation-deficient states. Rebalancing Orb2 toward youthful, translationally active assemblies improves memory in old flies.

papers.title: Mitochondrial DNA abundance is a determinant of immunogenic cell death in cancer
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial stress can trigger either immunogenic or apoptotic cell death. Tanaka et al. find that mitochondrial DNA abundance, shaped by oncogenic KRAS signaling and mitophagy, determines the immunological outcome of mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization, providing a mechanistic basis for targeting mitochondrial stress to augment antitumor immunity.

papers.title: Structural basis for the non-canonical nucleosome remodeling by ATRX
papers.abstract: Wang et al. show that ATRX remodels chromatin through an unusual mechanism that favors nucleosome disassembly over repositioning. ATRX also captures histones and cooperates with ASF1 for tetrasome assembly, linking chromatin remodeling to histone chaperoning for reassembly and helping explain how ATRX functions at accessible chromatin regions.

papers.title: Macrophages iron out cancer cells’ vulnerability
Conserved disordered regions and ubiquitin-binding motifs within HUWE1 contribute to substrate targeting plasticity
papers.abstract: Ge et al. develop a combinatorial cell-based system to map functional domains within HUWE1. Conserved disordered regions and ubiquitin-binding motifs contribute to substrate targeting, and HUWE1 engages both disordered and structured domains of its targets, explaining how a single ligase recognizes structurally diverse proteins.

papers.title: A hyper-IgM2 AID mutation limits IgH break formation but preserves affinity maturation
papers.abstract: Belcheva et al. describe a mouse carrying an AID mutation that causes hyper-IgM syndrome in patients. The mutation blocks antibody class switching while largely preserving antibody fine-tuning, and it does so through a role of AID that is independent of its enzymatic activity, explaining the immunodeficiency.

papers.title: Rheb in central amygdala somatostatin neurons regulates chronic itch and anxiety-like behaviors
papers.abstract: Qi et al. show that central amygdala somatostatin-expressing (SST) neurons are activated during DCP-induced chronic itch and contribute to scratching and anxiety-like behaviors. Rheb knockdown reduces SST neuronal hyperexcitability and alleviates these behaviors, whereas Rheb overexpression promotes scratching and anxiety-like behaviors.

papers.title: Clusterin, through exercise-mediated liver-heart crosstalk, promotes heart regeneration after myocardial infarction
papers.abstract: Wang et al. identify hepatic clusterin as the exercise-inducible circulating factor that drives cardiomyocyte proliferation and functional recovery following myocardial infarction. These findings reveal a liver-heart communication axis and establish clusterin as a potential therapeutic target for post-infarction heart failure.

papers.title: Pot1a maintains mesenchymal stem cell niche function to support hematopoietic stem cells
papers.abstract: Esaki et al. show that Pot1a preserves LepR+ MSC abundance and function by limiting DNA damage response and reactive oxygen species, thereby maintaining hematopoietic support. Pot1a deficiency impairs HSC quiescence and long-term reconstitution, whereas Pot1a supplementation improves MSC-mediated hematopoietic support.

papers.title: A competitive PDLIM1-USP14 axis destabilizes ACTN4 to disturb the invasive homeostasis of trophoblast in preeclampsia
papers.abstract: Zhang et al. identify PDLIM1 as a regulator of trophoblast invasive homeostasis in preeclampsia. Elevated PDLIM1 competitively displaces USP14 from ACTN4, shifting ACTN4 toward ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation thereby limiting trophoblast invasion. Placenta-targeted PDLIM1 silencing restores ACTN4 abundance and alleviates preeclampsia-like maternal and fetal phenotypes, highlighting therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Arbitrium crosstalk enables shared signaling among phages
papers.abstract: Lomeli-Ortega et al. review how peptide-mediated arbitrium signaling enables communication both within and between bacteriophage populations, highlighting how viral crosstalk may influence phage competition, cooperation, and microbial community dynamics while creating opportunities for phage-based technologies.

papers.title: How expansive and flexible is the matrix of life?
From poppies to pain relief
Engineered receptor-biased IL-2–drug immunoconjugates selectively expand Tregs and suppress effector cells for autoimmune therapy
papers.abstract: Li et al. identify Y31-20K-KU, a receptor-biased, site-specifically PEGylated IL-2-mTOR inhibitor immunoconjugate that selectively expands Treg cells, suppresses effector T cell activation, and ameliorates autoimmune inflammation in preclinical models.

papers.title: Mechanisms and regulation of proteolytic DNA–protein crosslink repair
papers.abstract: DNA–protein crosslinks (DPCs) are one of the most complex and deleterious forms of DNA damage. DPCs arise from the stabilization of covalent enzyme–DNA intermediates, such as topoisomerase cleavage complexes, or from exposure to bifunctional crosslinking agents, and they differ in protein identity, DNA context and chemical linkage. Because of their bulky nature, DPCs obstruct essential chromatin processes such as DNA replication and transcription, making their timely removal by dedicated DPC repair pathways crucial for genome stability and cellular homeostasis. In this Review, we discuss the origin and properties of the major classes of DPCs. We also describe key enzymes involved in DPC repair, with a particular focus on the proteasome and the specialized DPC protease SPRTN. Next, we synthesize recent advances in the understanding of proteolytic DPC repair across replication-coupled, transcription-coupled and global genome repair pathways and explain how these pathways converge on ubiquitylation of the crosslinked protein to license proteolysis by the proteasome or SPRTN. Finally, we discuss how defective DPC proteolysis contributes to genome instability, premature ageing and cancer predisposition. DNA–protein crosslinks (DPCs) obstruct essential chromatin processes, and their removal is crucial for genome stability. This Review discusses the origin and properties of DPCs, mechanisms of proteolytic DPC repair, and how defective DPC proteolysis contributes to genome instability, premature ageing and disease.

papers.title: Codon optimization as a design variable in biotherapeutics
papers.abstract: Codon optimization (CO) is a key design variable in biotherapeutics that is used to enhance expression of recombinant proteins, gene therapies, and vaccines. Although synonymous codon substitutions were historically considered neutral, codon choice can influence messenger RNA (mRNA) stability, translation kinetics, cotranslational folding, and immunogenicity. Current optimization strategies integrate computational parameters including codon adaptation indices, tRNA availability, mRNA structure, cytosine–phosphate–guanine dinucleotide content, codon pair bias, and machine learning approaches to balance expression and product quality. Additionally, dynamic tRNA modifications within the epitranscriptome modulate codon-biased translation in a context-dependent manner. While CO has not been implicated in adverse clinical outcomes, its context-dependent effects on protein conformation, post-translational modifications, and immune responses necessitate rigorous characterization. This opinion article presents our viewpoint on mechanisms, applications, and regulatory considerations for CO in biologics.

papers.title: Microbial production of the low-caloric sweetener d-allulose from d-glucose by evolutionary engineering
papers.abstract: Lehnert et al. combine adaptive laboratory evolution and metabolic engineering to enable microbial d-allulose production from d-glucose at 30°C with 18–19% yield. Evolved glucose isomerases and sugar transporters in strains deficient in glucose-dependent growth provide a microbial chassis for producing d-allulose and possibly other d-fructose-derived compounds under mild process conditions.

papers.title: Daily briefing: The three red flags of suspicious journals
VoroTIDE: Protein domain segmentation through independent hierarchical searches using Voronoi tessellation and physical self-containment
papers.abstract: Protein domains are commonly regarded as structurally separated, functionally relevant, and evolutionarily separable units. Although classification systems may assign different domain boundaries to the same structure, structural separation remains a shared criterion, and many domain parsers assess it through inter-residue distances, contact numbers, or contact densities. However, the Voronoi contact area, which is widely used to study protein-protein interactions and predict contact sites, has seen limited use in domain parsing. There are two potential challenges to this problem. First, unlike in protein-protein interaction, partitions are not known in advance and must be identified before their interface can be evaluated. Second, the contact area depends on fragment size and internal packing, making it difficult to compare candidate partitions. Here, we introduce VoroTIDE (Voronoi-based Two-way Independent Domain Exploration), a domain parser based on all-heavy-atom Voronoi contact areas. By normalizing the contact area for fragment size and internal packing, and incorporating residue hydropathy, we define a pairwise self-containment score F. VoroTIDE applies F in two independent hierarchical searches: top-down recursive splitting until no admissible division remains, and bottom-up merging of secondary-structure elements until the entire structure becomes a single fragment. Intermediate partitions from both searches are ranked by a global partition quality score G, derived on the same principle. On two CATH-ECOD consensus benchmarks, under balanced evaluation, VoroTIDE achieved the strongest performance among all tested criterion-based parsers and was comparable to Chainsaw, the best-performing deep learning method tested. These results show that the Voronoi-based criterion can yield competitive domain parsing.

papers.title: Validated backbone assignments for natural-abundance 1H,15N spectra of commercial hen egg white lysozyme and example applications thereof
papers.abstract: Although backbone 1H and 15N assignments for hen egg white lysozyme (HEWL) have been reported in the literature and several related entries are available in the BMRB, these resources differ in sequence, experimental conditions, and the nuclei represented. In particular, there is no BMRB entry with an explicit set of 1H,15N backbone assignments applicable to spectra that can now be collected at natural 15N abundance on concentrated samples of commercial HEWL as shown by Bruker and reproduced here using a 800 MHz magnet with a cryoprobe. Therefore, here I make available the backbone 1H,15N chemical shifts of commercial (Sigma) HEWL at pH 3.8 and 308 K parsed from previous papers and checked against 1H,1H NOESY, 1H,1H TOCSY and 1H,15N correlation spectra of HSQC and SOFAST-HMQC types, acquired on a 3 mM sample at natural 15N abundance. I also provide backbone 1H,15N assignments transferred to pH 6 and 308 K via a pH titration, closer to physiological conditions as used by others. I discuss details about sample preparation and spectra acquisition, including the measurement times involved, and possible reasons for a few residues lacking assignments. The usefulness of these assignments and of detecting 1H,15N correlations at natural abundance are proven by (i) application to a titration with a small molecule, (ii) studies of hydration and dynamics via Het-SOFAST-HMQC experiments, and ultimately (iii) by their utilization in published papers even if without attribution. I deliver ready-to-use assignments as text-format Sparky files, and make selected spectra available on the PDB Manipulation Suite's WebNMR app for straightforward visualization online, useful also for swift educational demonstrations. Overall, I expect the data and methods presented here will be of use in protein biophysics and structural biology research and education, by enabling the interpretation of modern NMR-based studies on inexpensive samples of this widely studied protein.

papers.title: Somewhere over the transcontinental burrito tunnel
Patrick Stewart dies: how Captain Picard inspired today’s science leaders
Are dinosaur fossils hogging top journals? Analysis sparks debate over ‘charismatic’ finds
A combinatorial genetics approach reveals limits to redundancy within Plasmodium falciparum invasion ligand families
papers.abstract: To maintain infection in the human bloodstream, Plasmodium falciparum parasites undergo repeated cycles of invasion of and multiplication inside red blood cells (RBCs). Two protein families, the Erythrocyte binding-like (EBA) and Reticulocyte binding-like (Rh) proteins, are known to play a key role in invasion, mediating early stages of attachment of the P. falciparum merozoite to the host RBC. There is a degree of redundancy within these families, such that disrupting the function of individual EBA/Rh proteins in vitro is not sufficient to prevent invasion. By employing a novel approach to disrupt multiple EBA and Rh genes in combination, we systematically assess functional interdependency across these families for the first time. This analysis, and further characterisation of mutant parasites, reveals that disruption of some pairs of EBA/Rh ligands significantly impacts P. falciparum invasion, whereas others do not. Disruption of PfEBA175 in combination with either PfRh2b or PfRh4 significantly reduces parasite multiplication in vitro, indicating that the remaining EBA/Rh proteins cannot fully compensate for the absence of these three key invasion ligands. PfEBA175, PfRh2b and PfRh4 may therefore represent a critical nexus of the parasite invasion machinery, and combinatorial approaches that target these specific ligands could be a beneficial therapeutic approach. The authors use a genetic approach to explore redundancy within two multigene families important for Plasmodium falciparum invasion of human red blood cells, revealing that not all family members function equivalently.

papers.title: Hydrogen-bond-mediated quasi-two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks for ultrahigh gold extraction
papers.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are ideal for precious metal recovery due to their high surface areas and tunable binding sites. However, the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer, resulting in poor site accessibility and limited extraction capacities. Herein, we report a quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) topology-directed strategy to construct exposed binding sites for highly efficient gold recovery. By incorporating outward-pointing hydroxyl groups, the local conformation of the imine-linked skeleton is effectively locked via inter-chain hydrogen bonding (ICHB), which suppresses molecular torsion and promotes ordered assembly of the 1D chains into a quasi-2D crystalline architecture. This structural rigidification creates unobstructed ion-diffusion pathways and maximizes the exposure of active sites for rapid [AuCl4]− capture and reduction. Remarkably, under mild thermal and vibratory stimulation, gold nanoparticles form in situ and aggregate, yielding a high gold extraction capacity of 5082.32 mg g−1. Theoretical calculations demonstrate that ICHB-induced structural planarization creates a cooperative coordination environment and optimizes the energetic landscape for dechlorination, synergistically promoting guest enrichment and interfacial gold reduction. This work establishes a new blueprint for creating COFs with exposed active sites via inter-chain assembly, offering a scalable approach to maximize site accessibility and electron transfer for selective gold capture. Covalent organic frameworks are ideal for precious metal recovery but the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer and limits extraction capacities. Here, the authors report a quasi-2D topology-directed strategy to construct exposed binding sites for highly efficient gold recovery.

papers.title: Weakened association between sequential phenological events corresponds to interphase extension
papers.abstract: The sequential occurrence of leaf unfolding, flowering, fruiting, foliar senescence and other life-cycle events constitutes a full cycle of plant phenology. Temporal shifts in the seasonal timing of these phenophases have been regarded as key evidence of global environmental change. Most previous studies, however, have focused on the timing of individual phenophases. Little is known about the relationships between changes in timing across sequential phenophases. Here, using in-situ phenological records of major European tree species between 1980 and 2017, we show strong positive associations between consecutive phenophases. In particular, the statistical relationship between the timing of consecutive phenophases is comparable to that of temperature for spring phenological events and substantially exceeds the relationship with climatic factors for late-season phenological events. However, the associations themselves have shifted across years, with a significant decrease in the association between the timing of fruit ripening and autumnal coloration, corresponding to the largest extension of interphase duration. Current process-based phenological models largely overlook associations between consecutive phenological events and their interplay with climate change, potentially leading to biased projections of phenological changes and ecosystem adaptation to future climate change. Seasonal events in temperate deciduous trees, from leaf-out to leaf fall, follow a fixed annual sequence. This study shows that the timing of consecutive events is statistically associated in European trees, but that the association between fruiting and leaf coloration has weakened in some species as the interval between these phases has increased.

papers.title: B7-H4‒directed antibody-drug conjugate AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan) in patients with advanced/metastatic solid tumors: the Phase 1/2a (BLUESTAR), first-in-human study
papers.abstract: B7-H4 is a promising antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) target with high expression in several solid tumors and limited expression in normal tissue. B7-H4 negatively regulates T-cell function, and high expression of B7-H4 is associated with disease progression. AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan [Puxi-Sam]) is a novel B7-H4–directed ADC with a stable cleavable linker and a bystander-capable topoisomerase-1 (TOP1) inhibitor payload. In this first-in-human study, 47 patients with advanced/metastatic B7-H4−positive endometrial cancer, ovarian cancer, breast cancer or cholangiocarcinoma received intravenous Puxi-Sam at 0.8–3.2 mg/kg every 3 weeks. The primary objectives were to evaluate the safety and tolerability of Puxi-Sam (incidence of adverse events [AE], serious AEs and dose-limiting toxicities), and to determine the maximum tolerated dose and/or recommended phase 2 dose of Puxi-Sam. Secondary objectives included characterizing the pharmacokinetics, assessing the antitumor activity (objective response rate [ORR]), and determining the pharmacodynamics of Puxi-Sam. The most common treatment-related adverse events were nausea (51.1%), neutropenia (48.9%) and anemia (38.3%). At 3.2 mg/kg, dose-limiting neutropenia and thrombocytopenia were observed. In patients treated at ≥1.6 mg/kg (predicted efficacious range), partial responses were observed in ovarian, endometrial and breast cancer (ORR 20.5% [9/44]). Translational data indicated selective localization of the TOP1 inhibitor payload to B7-H4–expressing tumor cells and induction of target-dependent DNA damage. Our findings demonstrate manageable safety and promising efficacy with Puxi-Sam in heavily pretreated patients; further development is ongoing. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05123482. B7-H4 is a promising therapeutic target in solid tumors because of its frequent expression in cancer cells, limited normal tissue distribution, and immunosuppressive functions. In this first-in-human trial, the authors report safety and efficacy outcomes for B7-H4–directed antibody-drug conjugate AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan) in patients with heavily pretreated ovarian, endometrial, and breast cancers, and cholangiocarcinoma.

papers.title: One Health genomic surveillance identifies potential genetic links of antimicrobial-resistant foodborne pathogens across sectors
authors: Foodborne AMR Research Group of Public Health Institutes
papers.abstract: Foodborne pathogens and antimicrobial resistance are major global health concerns. The integration and analysis of genomic surveillance data across human, animal, and environmental sectors remain a critical challenge in the study of foodborne bacteria. Here we investigate potential cross-sector genetic links between antimicrobial-resistant isolates from food (mainly chicken meat), animals (mainly cecal and rectal samples), and humans (clinical cases) by comparing whole-genome sequences of non-typhoidal Salmonella (n = 1,613), Campylobacter (n = 682), and Enterococcus (n = 72) collected from these sectors across Japan. For Salmonella, we identify closely related human- and food-derived S. Blockley isolates carrying blaCTX-M-15, with pairwise SNP distances of 6–10 SNPs, as well as S. Agona isolates carrying fosA7.2, with pairwise SNP distances of 13–15 SNPs, suggesting that resistant Salmonella strains are shared between human and food sectors. For Campylobacter, we identified closely related human- and food-derived ST-22 isolates carrying a tetracycline resistance gene and a fluoroquinolone resistance-conferring gyrA mutation, with a pairwise SNP distance of 4 SNPs. These findings highlight potential genetic links of antimicrobial-resistant foodborne bacteria between food and humans. In this study, the authors use nationwide genomic data collected across sectors in Japan to identify closely related antimicrobial-resistant Salmonella and Campylobacter isolates in food and humans, highlighting the value of integrated One Health surveillance.

papers.title: Genome-scale eCLIP mapping of SARS-CoV-2 RNA interactions with NSP8, NSP12, and N reveals regulatory sites
papers.abstract: The global impact of the COVID-19 pandemic highlights the need for a deeper understanding of SARS-CoV-2 replication. Although the essential roles of the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (NSP12), primase (NSP8), and nucleocapsid (N) proteins are established, their contact points with the full-length viral RNA genome during active infection require further characterization. Here, we used enhanced crosslinking and immunoprecipitation (eCLIP) to map direct interactions of NSP8, NSP12, and N across the SARS-CoV-2 genome during live virus infection at early and late stages of replication. We mapped NSP8 and NSP12 binding to the 5′ and 3′ ends of positive- and negative-sense RNA, consistent with their roles in viral replication, transcription, and translation. We also observed an NSP12 binding site within the conserved Y1 domain of NSP3 that modulates RNA and protein abundance. In addition, N binds the 5′ untranslated region (UTR), supporting a role in translational regulation early in infection, and associates with the frameshift element, where it modulates ribosomal frameshifting. Together, these findings map SARS-CoV-2 RNA–protein interactions across the viral genome and delineate specific regulatory regions for potential antiviral intervention. In this study, the authors map how SARS-CoV-2 proteins NSP8, NSP12 and N interact with viral RNA during infection, revealing regulatory sites that control viral replication and translation, and offering potential targets for antiviral strategies.

papers.title: Spatial patterning of hierarchical lamellar-cellular structured hydrogels for programmable deformation-coupled information encryption
papers.abstract: Inspired by organisms capable of adaptive morphological regulation, hydrogel actuators with softness and large deformability are attractive for biomedical devices and information encryption, yet remain limited by the lack of hierarchically oriented structures simultaneously enabling rapid actuation and high-order complex deformation. Here, we report a multiscale lamellar-confined assembly polymerization strategy for fabricating synchronous programmable shape-morphing and information-encoding hydrogels with hierarchically periodic lamellar-cellular structure. Owing to the periodic asymmetric stresses that amplify deformation and hierarchical porous channels that accelerate water transport, the obtained hydrogel exhibits large three-dimensional deformation with the rapidest recovery speed of 112.5°/s among the reported thermo-responsive hydrogels, facilitating programmable shape morphing by orchestrating localized curvature. Furthermore, a spatial orientation-patterning strategy is developed to precisely regulate the site-specific arrangement of lamellar-cellular structures for diverse cooperative sophisticated deformations at high speed. Importantly, the highly oriented architecture endows the hydrogel with tunable birefringence, enabling a dynamic encryption platform that couples programmable deformation with information encoding. This work provides a flexible structural strategy for preparing hydrogels with biomimetic dynamic information encryption. Hydrogel actuators have potential in a range of applications, but combining rapid actuation and complex deformation is challenging. Here, the authors report a lamellar confined assembly polymerisation strategy for preparing programmable shape-morphing and information-encoding hydrogels.

papers.title: Sequential protonation and deprotonation reactions govern alternating access in a Major Facilitator Superfamily proton/multidrug antiporter
papers.abstract: Drug/proton antiporters of the Major Facilitator Superfamily are key drivers of antimicrobial resistance. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying proton-coupled drug efflux are inherently complex and remain unresolved. Here, we dissect the timing and mechanism of proton coupling in the multidrug transporter LmrP, a prototypical exporter of clinically relevant antibiotics and toxins. By directly tracking chamber opening in the native plasma membrane, we capture functionally relevant conformational transitions within a lipid environment and map them onto the catalytic carboxylates that govern transport. Our results suggest that earlier DEER distance measurements in detergent solution captured a restricted subset of conformational states, which our pH 8.0 data extend and place into a broader framework. Complementary pH 5.0 measurements reveal additional mechanistic features and, together, these datasets define the transport cycle in a membrane-embedded context. Supported by molecular dynamics simulations, the results reveal a coordinated, transport cycle-dependent mechanism in which paired catalytic carboxylates act sequentially in substrate binding, proton relay, gate control, and transporter resetting. The molecular mechanisms underlying proton-coupled drug efflux are not fully resolved. Here the authors assess the timing and mechanism of proton coupling in the multidrug transporter LmrP, a prototypical exporter of clinically relevant antibiotics and toxins.

papers.title: Enzymes can activate and mobilize dense biomolecular condensates across scales
papers.abstract: Biomolecular condensates have so far been studied in terms of their structural, compositional, and functional properties. However, condensate enzymatic activity - a key aspect of cellular metabolism - remains unexplored due to the complexity of the system. In this study, using a combination of experimental, computational and theoretical techniques, we have discovered that the non-equilibrium activity which originates from catalytic reactions couples with the environment through various feedback mechanisms across five orders of magnitude of length scales. We observe that condensed enzymes catalyze more rapidly in the presence of crowding proteins and show that the increased enzymatic activity within these droplets stems from the emergence of lower-energy protein conformations induced by the highly crowded environment. Despite the crowding in the environment of the droplet, which might suggest an effective increase in its overall viscosity, we find that it becomes more agile, as evidenced by the observation of enhanced diffusion and macroscopic flow, due to the enzymatic activity. These findings shed light on the dynamic interplay between enzymatic activity, composition and crowding in condensates, and their roles on the mobility and accessibility of various functional units in these environments, expanding our understanding of liquid-liquid phase separation in metabolically active conditions. Enzymes operate in highly crowded cellular environments, yet the impact of crowding on their function remains poorly understood. Here, the authors demonstrate that enzyme activity increases molecular mobility in crowded protein droplets, suggesting a feedback mechanism between catalysis and the physical properties of the surrounding environment.

papers.title: Canopy nutrient balance predicts autumn senescence across U.S. forests
papers.abstract: Terrestrial ecosystems are changing rapidly under global nutrient enrichment, yet how canopy nutrients balance shapes the seasonal end of photosynthesis, a critical control on ecosystem carbon cycling, remains unclear. Rising anthropogenic nitrogen inputs are shifting many ecosystems towards relative phosphorus limitation, with uncertain consequences for autumn phenology. Here, we combined airborne imaging spectroscopy with remotely sensed phenology to test whether canopy nutrient ratios predict spatial variations in autumn senescence across National Ecological Observatory Network sites in the United States. Higher canopy N:P is consistently associated with earlier senescence in 20 out of 25 sites, whereas higher N:K has opposite effects in 19 sites after controlling for climate, elevation, dominant species, and canopy structure. Growing-season productivity is generally related to later senescence, but only modestly mediates the direct nutrient-phenology associations. These findings add a phenological dimension to the functional impacts of nutrient imbalance on terrestrial ecosystems and demonstrate that nutrients provide predictive power beyond climate alone. Continued nitrogen deposition is expected to increase relative phosphorus limitation, a shift that could be associated with earlier senescence and shorter growing season. Incorporating canopy nutrients into phenological models may therefore improve forecasts of canopy duration and carbon fluxes under ongoing nutrient enrichment. Canopy nutrient balance helps sustain leaf activity through the growing season. The study finds that higher canopy N:P is linked to earlier autumn senescence, whereas higher N:K is linked to later senescence across U.S. forests.

papers.title: Video-rate volumetric chemical imaging via mid-infrared photothermal optical diffraction tomography
papers.abstract: Label-free vibrational microscopy provides chemically specific access to cellular structures, yet quantitative volumetric imaging of intracellular dynamics remains challenging on subsecond timescales. Here, we demonstrate video-rate mid-infrared photothermal optical diffraction tomography (MIP-ODT) by combining high photothermal sensitivity with rapid angular scanning. The system achieves 19.2 volumes per second, nearly 400 times faster than previous MIP tomography implementations, with a signal-to-noise ratio exceeding 70 and no temporal averaging. We track lipid droplets in living cells and quantify anomalous diffusion from three-dimensional trajectories, revealing heterogeneous intracellular transport behaviors obscured in two-dimensional measurements. Rapid mid-infrared wavenumber sweeping further enables broadband multi-wavenumber volumetric chemical imaging across a 300 cm⁻¹ spectral window within 1 s. These results establish MIP-ODT as a platform for high-speed, label-free volumetric chemical imaging of single cells and quantitative investigation of dynamic intracellular organization. Chemical imaging can reveal cellular structures without labels, but capturing their rapid 3D dynamics remains challenging. papers.title: Towards the real diamond formation conditions: insights and perspective
papers.abstract: Pressure and temperature conditions of diamond formation provide valuable insights for reconstructing paleo-geotherms and the deep carbon cycle. These conditions can be determined by investigating mineral inclusions in diamonds using elastic geobarometry, which can be applied to any mineral inclusion in a diamond. However, it assumes purely elastic host-inclusion behaviour throughout exhumation. In reality, almost all mineral inclusions in diamonds are surrounded by cracks. Here, we combine in situ high-temperature micro-Raman spectroscopy with thermo-elastic modelling to evaluate the pressure-release process in one of the most common diamond inclusions, olivine [(Mg,Fe)2SiO4]. Our results indicate that a diamond can sustain pressures of ~2.5 GPa before undergoing minor fracturing, which induces only partial loss of inclusion pressure rather than a complete reset. The estimated pressure loss can lead to an underestimation of up to 2.5 GPa in the entrapment pressure at 1150 °C, a typical temperature for diamond formation. This study shows that olivine in diamond can undergo partial release of pressure during kimberlite eruptions due to fast adiabatic decompression, leading to cracked olivine inclusions and entrapment pressures underestimated by up to 2.5 GPa at 1150 °C

papers.title: Liquid-metal physical unclonable functions resistant to both physical and digital cloning
papers.abstract: Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) leverage device-specific randomness for hardware security, yet their static, persistently accessible responses allow attackers to collect sufficient data for digital cloning. We present a liquid-metal PUF (LM-PUF) that integrates physical unclonability with material-driven resistance to digital attacks. Randomly mixed, visually indistinguishable LM particles form thermally unique microstructures, ensuring physical unclonability. Digital protection arises from two concealment mechanisms: time-limited accessibility restricts meaningful data collection, while decoy obscuration prevents reliable key identification. At equilibrium, the device remains cryptographically silent, but heating through a transient non-equilibrium window reveals thermal patterns convertible to cryptographic keys. Outside the predefined temperature range, misleading thermal patterns conceal the authentic key among decoys. LM-PUF supports scalable patterning, demonstrated in secure labels and QR codes, highlighting its potential for secure supply chains and physical unclonable authentication. Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) secure hardware identity but can be digitally cloned by machine-learning attacks. Here, authors report a liquid-metal PUF whose thermal keys appear only briefly during heating and are hidden among decoys, resisting both physical and digital cloning.

papers.title: Observation of quantized charge accumulation in a quantum anomalous Hall system
papers.abstract: The quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetically doped topological insulators exhibits a quantized Hall conductance σxy = e2/h arising from the two-dimensional surface states. While conventional transport probes confirm this quantization, they remain insensitive to the field-induced surface charge accumulation as a direct manifestation of σxy. Here, we experimentally validate an out-of-plane capacitive method that directly detects this quantized charge accumulation in a quantum anomalous Hall system. Using Corbino and simple disk devices, we measure charge accumulation proportional to field variation ΔB, with dissipation characterized by longitudinal conductance σxx and frequency f. A quantitative dissipation model extracts the intrinsic quantized charge density η0 = (e2/h)ΔB, which is confirmed through f- and σxx-dependent measurements. Under ultra-low dissipation (σxx ≈ 10−9 S), we directly resolve the fully quantized charge accumulation. This methodology establishes a direct charge-accumulation probe and provides a pathway toward detecting the topological magnetoelectric effect, a condensed matter manifestation of the four-dimensional quantum Hall effect. The quantum anomalous Hall effect in a magnetically doped topological insulator exhibits a quantized Hall conductance. Here, the authors demonstrate an out-of-plane capacitive method that directly measures field-induced quantized charge accumulation originating from the quantized Hall conductance.

papers.title: Ultrahigh strength aluminum alloy by green laser additive manufacturing
papers.abstract: Infrared laser additive manufacturing of high-strength 7××× aluminum (Al) alloys is hindered by low absorptivity, high cracking-susceptibility, and insufficient precipitation strengthening. Herein, we investigate a new approach to process high-performance AA7075 by integrating green laser directed energy deposition (L-DED) with nano-TiC embedded composite AA7075 powder. The green laser achieves better energy-material coupling, enabling high-quality deposition at a lower laser power than conventional infrared lasers. The green laser also stabilizes the melt pool, reduces thermal gradients and elemental evaporation, and promotes more uniform grains with lower dislocation density. Heat treatment yields an ultra-high density of nano-scale η′ precipitates and GP zones (~2.13×1016 m−2) in the green laser deposited Al alloy, achieving a tensile yield strength of ~600 MPa, which is higher than forged AA7075 and almost all L-DED-processed Al alloys hitherto reported. This work presents an integrated material-process strategy for additive manufacturing of highly reflective, hot-crack-susceptible alloys using short-wavelength lasers. Cracking and poor laser absorption curbed additive manufacturing of high-strength aluminium alloys. Using a TiC/AA7075 composite powder and a green wavelength laser, researchers produced crack-free aluminum alloy with a yield strength of nearly 600 MPa.

papers.title: A multilamellar organelle for chemosymbiosis in an aplacophoran mollusc adapted to anoxic cold seep sediment
papers.abstract: Symbiosis with chemoautotrophic bacteria has evolved in many animal lineages inhabiting reducing habitats such as hydrothermal vents, allowing these holobionts to thrive in dark biospheres. In certain cases, the symbionts have become intracellular, residing within specialised bacteriocytes. Although the integration of microbial symbionts with eukaryotic cells varies across known animals, no specialised organelle dedicated to chemosynthesis has been identified. Here, we report a mode of symbiosis where sulphur-oxidising bacteria are cultured within spherical multilamellar compartments ( ~ 12 μm) in the cold-seep aplacophoran mollusc Chaetoderma shenloong. This organelle, which we name ‘dracosphera’, is ubiquitous within the hypertrophied and intricately reticulate digestive gland of C. shenloong, which has otherwise lost most of its gut. Given that the symbionts are microaerobic and the host resides in anoxic sediments tens of centimetres below the surface, the dracosphera may minimise oxygen diffusion to the bacteria, akin to mechanisms observed in microbial diazotrophs and termite hindguts, as supported by our genomic and spatial transcriptomic analyses. Hypoxia is known to induce radical adaptations in meiofauna, exemplified by the acquisition of hydrogenosomes. Our discovery of similar adaptations in C. shenloong provides insights into the evolution of such organelles in larger animals. Animals living in the deep sea often form symbiotic partnerships with chemosynthetic bacteria. Here authors discover a multilamellar organelle in the worm-mollusc Chaetoderma shenloong containing bacteria and name it dracosphera (‘dragon ball’).

papers.title: Climate change threatens malaria elimination in the Asia Pacific
papers.abstract: Climate change threatens decades of progress toward malaria elimination across the Asia Pacific. In recent years, reported cases have increased sharply in several regions, including Pakistan following the 2022 floods. However, current research and adaptation strategies have largely focused on gradual warming and shifting transmission seasons and may not fully capture acute operational disruptions in endemic settings. Here we examine how climate change influences malaria through cascading disruptions to health systems, population displacement and ecological change. As a multidisciplinary group of policymakers and researchers, we identify priority actions: integrating malaria control into disaster response, deploying adaptive vector control for displaced populations, strengthening cross-border data sharing, linking early warnings to anticipatory action, and incorporating land-use data into surveillance. Leveraging existing advances in climate policy, digital surveillance and community engagement will be critical. Sustaining elimination will require complementing long-term projections with preparedness for near-term system shocks. A multidisciplinary group of policymakers and researchers discusses the impacts of climate change on malaria in the Asia Pacific, identifies gaps in national adaptation strategies and outlines five priority actions for the region.

Spatial single-cell mapping of transcriptional differences across genetic backgrounds in mouse brains
papers.abstract: Genetic variation can alter organ structure and function. Comparative statistical analysis of organs across genetic backgrounds requires spatial, single-cell, atlas-scale data in replicates. Here we introduce atlas-scale transcriptome localization using aggregate signatures (ATLAS), a scalable tissue mapping method that learns transcriptional signatures from single-cell RNA sequencing data, encodes them in situ with tens of thousands of oligonucleotide probes and decodes them to infer cell types and imputed transcriptomes. We validated ATLAS against direct MERFISH measurements of marker genes and through quantitative comparisons to four other technologies. We profiled 40 million cells across more than 400 coronal sections from central brains of five male and five female C57BL/6J mice and five male BTBR T+tf/J mice, an idiopathic autism model. Our analysis revealed more than 40 significant differences in cell-type distributions and identified 16 regional composition changes across male–female and B6–BTBR comparisons. ATLAS thus enables systematic comparative studies, facilitating organ-level structure–function analysis of disease models. ATLAS is a highly scalable tissue profiling method that leverages existing atlas data and in silico decoding to generate imputed cell maps.

papers.abstract: Here we constructed a genotype imputation reference panel from whole-genome sequencing data from 490,319 UK Biobank (UKB) participants1 and enabled both standalone and cloud-based phasing and imputation through EagleImp2 and EagleImp-RAP within the UK Biobank Research Analysis Platform. The UKB reference panel achieves lower phasing switch error rates than the widely used TOPMed r3 panel (133,597 individuals) for all global superpopulations except AMR and for 25 of 26 1000 Genomes Project subpopulations. Imputation accuracy, measured by MAE, improved for 4 of 5 superpopulations and 12 subpopulations for variants with minor allele frequencies down to 0.01%. Estimated squared correlation further improved across all 5 superpopulations and 22 subpopulations, with the largest gains in East and South Asian populations. Reimputation of COVID-19 genome-wide association study datasets from Italy, Germany, Spain and Norway3,4 demonstrated that common-variant imputation remains unsaturated, enhancing the discovery of genome-wide significant loci and improving fine-mapping resolution. A haplotype reference panel constructed from whole-genome sequencing data from 490,319 UK Biobank participants improves genotype imputation accuracy across diverse populations and achieves lower phasing switch error rates than existing approaches.

Phase separation of SMARCAL1 orchestrates epigenetic reprogramming and methionine metabolism to foster radioresistance and immunosuppression
papers.abstract: Liquid–liquid phase separation has emerged as a key mechanism governing cellular organization and function, but its role in pathological processes and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely elusive. Here we show that SMARCAL1 forms nuclear condensates via liquid–liquid phase separation to enhance histone H4 lactylation and chromatin accessibility. This SMARCAL1‑driven epigenetic reprogramming not only facilitates the recruitment of DNA repair proteins, leading to radiotherapy resistance, but also regulates methionine adenosyltransferase transcription, thereby promoting the methionine cycle and inducing T cell exhaustion and immune therapy tolerance. Intriguingly, SMARCAL1 is identified as a biomarker for predicting therapy response and patient stratification. Importantly, pharmacological disruption of SMARCAL1 condensates by digoxin sensitizes tumours to both radiotherapy and anti-PD1 therapy in multiple models. These findings highlight the crucial role of condensates centred on SMARCAL1-histone H4 in governing DNA repair and immune microenvironment remodelling, as well as propose an innovative strategy to overcome radioimmunoresistance. Zheng, Cui, Li et al. demonstrate a role for SMARCAL1 in modulating histone lactylation and chromatin remodelling via phase separation, thereby impacting the antitumour efficacy of radiotherapy and immunotherapy.

papers.abstract: Heterotrimeric G proteins, activated by G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), are central mediators of cellular signaling. Activation requires GDP release from the Gα subunit, a step attributed largely to the C-terminal α5 helix, the primary GPCR-interacting region. Contributions from other Gα regions have remained unclear. Here we show that the N-terminal helix (αN) of Gαs promotes GDP release through a rotational conformational change. Diffracted X-ray tracking revealed that engagement with an active GPCR increases αN conformational displacement. Biochemical assays and molecular dynamics simulations showed that counterclockwise rotation of αN, viewed from the extracellular side, facilitates GDP release, whereas clockwise rotation does not. Mechanistically, this αN-mediated pathway acts synergistically with α5 conformational changes and propagates through the β-sheet network within the Ras homology domain to the P-loop and the αG helix. These findings identify an αN-driven activation pathway and extend the mechanistic framework for GPCR-triggered G protein activation. Receptor engagement rotates the N-terminal helix of the G protein alpha subunit, and this motion is relayed through the protein to release bound GDP, revealing an activation pathway that works together with the long-studied C-terminal route.

papers.title: GALE is a tumor-intrinsic checkpoint of Vγ9Vδ2 T cell-mediated killing
papers.abstract: Vγ9Vδ2 T cells mediate HLA-independent targeting of tumor cells, offering unique opportunities for cancer immunotherapy, yet their therapeutic efficacy remains limited. Here, using a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we identify UDP-galactose 4-epimerase (GALE) as a tumor-intrinsic checkpoint that restricts Vγ9Vδ2 T cell-mediated killing. GALE is a key nucleotide-sugar metabolic enzyme that controls the interconversion of UDP-galactose and UDP-glucose, thereby supporting protein glycosylation and cell-surface glycan remodeling. Mechanistically, GALE promotes complex N-glycosylation of CD155 and CEACAM1, favoring their engagement with the inhibitory receptors TIGIT and TIM3, respectively, while limiting CD155 binding to the activating receptor CD226. GALE loss potentiates Vγ9Vδ2 T cell-mediated tumor killing in multiple mouse models and colorectal cancer patient-derived organoids. Together, these findings reveal how nucleotide-sugar metabolism shapes tumor–immune communication through complex N-glycan remodeling and identify GALE and its downstream receptor–ligand interactions as potential therapeutic targets for enhancing Vγ9Vδ2 T cell antitumor activity. papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR-T) cell therapy shows limited efficacy in solid tumors, partly owing to poorly defined tumor-intrinsic resistance mechanisms. Here we show that the epigenetic regulator BAZ2A drives resistance to CD70-targeted CAR-T therapy by reprogramming tumor lipid metabolism. papers.abstract: In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), the fibroblastic stroma constitutes most of the tumor mass and is remarkably devoid of functional blood vessels, leaving unresolved how PDAC cells obtain essential metabolites and water-insoluble lipids. We find that cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) acquire and transfer lipids from blood-borne particles to PDAC cells through trogocytosis of CAF plasma membranes, a process requiring the CAF-expressed phospholipid scramblase anoctamin 6 (ANO6) to promote PDAC cell survival. Cancer cells and CAFs form synapse-like contacts that induce cytosolic calcium influx in CAFs through Orai channels, activating ANO6 and driving phosphatidylserine exposure on CAF membranes, which initiates trogocytosis and transfer of membrane lipids, including cholesterol, to PDAC cells. This ANO6-dependent phosphatidylserine externalization also supports CAF-mediated immunosuppression of cytotoxic T cells through trogocytosis. Blockade of ANO6 antagonizes tumor growth, partly by disrupting cholesterol delivery to cancer cells, and attenuates immune suppression, identifying ANO6 as a candidate therapeutic target in PDAC. papers.abstract: Gastrointestinal fistulas (GFs) represent one of the main causes of morbidity and mortality. While endoscopic techniques provide a minimally invasive approach to GF repair, offering advantages over conventional surgical approaches, the integration of endoscopic delivery with hydrogel sealants in user-friendly and easy processes approaches remains a great challenge. Here we develop a thermoresponsive positively charged poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM)/Ga3+ (PGaIII) hydrogel sealant, formed by slug-inspired biomimetic self-assembly. The proposed PGaIII holds potential for the repair of fistulas in other organs in vivo, thereby promoting the establishment of safer and more effective clinical treatment options for related diseases. papers.abstract: Nearly half of the ~5,000 human membrane proteins need to assemble into stoichiometric complexes as part of their biogenesis at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane. Here we demonstrate that the human ER membrane protein complex (EMC) insertase additionally acts as a chaperone to facilitate the assembly of heterotrimeric voltage-gated calcium channels (Cav). Using function-separating mutations and inhibitory nanobodies, we show that nascent Cav channels are degraded prematurely when EMC’s chaperone function is selectively perturbed. EMC engagement of the pore-forming Cav α-subunit occurred cotranslationally and required the Cav α-subunit’s first transmembrane domain bundle to protrude from the nascent ribosome–multipass translocon complex. Our findings establish a chaperone function for the EMC and suggest that biogenesis of multibundle membrane proteins may require a highly orchestrated, cotranslational interplay among ER biogenesis factors. Layer-wise Prediction for Interpretation of Hidden Representations in Deep Neural Networks through Evolving Probability Distributions
papers.abstract: The sequential architecture of DNNs enables accurate predictions by encoding input features, yet their limited interpretability and transparency during forward propagation undermine the credibility of predictions. Therefore, we propose layer-wise prediction for interpretation method (LPI), which involves mapping the representation from each layer to a probability distribution, explaining the hidden-layer prediction process. To ensure interpretation fidelity to DNN mechanisms, we employ a reconstruction strategy to map probability distributions back to hidden layer features while reducing their influence on model prediction. Meanwhile, we define a rank-index metric to quantify the consistency of probability distribution evolution. Furthermore, we show how each hidden layer probability distribution evolves consistently during DNN forward propagation. Experiments on various models show that LPI achieves superior performance in consistency, stability, fidelity and certainty, outperforming AdditionalLayer, SDN, MetaGF, and DFS. Notably, LPI not only enhances deep learning interpretability but also provides valuable insights into reliable and credible model security assessment. Here, the authors introduce a hidden-layer interpretation method that maps intermediate DNN representations to probability distributions and reconstructs features to ensure faithful explanation.

papers.title: Resolving the Kay–Dunn limit and the speed–endurance dilemma in ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 for DRAM-class sub-volt capacitors
papers.abstract: Ferroelectric hafnium zirconium oxide can increase charge density in scaled capacitors, but its high coercive field limits the low-voltage, high endurance switching required for dynamic random-access memory and embedded ferroelectric memories. Here we show that plasma-engineered (111)-textured TiN electrodes with N-rich, oxidation-resistant surfaces suppress interfacial oxidation and enable robust switching in 5 nm Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 capacitors. The devices exhibit saturated hysteresis at 0.6 V, with 2Pr = 31.5 μC cm−2 and Ec = 0.62 MV cm−1, and no hard electrical breakdown through 1012 bipolar cycles. Their nucleation-limited switching kinetics extrapolate to sub-nanosecond polarisation reversal at DRAM-relevant capacitor areas. At 1.1 V, circuit simulations of a common plate 1T–1 C cell yield short- and long-term stand-by sensing margins of 482 and 201 mV under a 20 fF bit line load. Electrode texture and interface engineering therefore enable low-voltage, high speed switching without compromising endurance, mitigating the practical Kay–Dunn scaling penalty and the speed–endurance dilemma. Ferroelectric hafnium zirconium oxide could improve scaled memory capacitors, but high switching fields limit low-voltage endurance. Park et al. engineered textured titanium nitride electrodes, enabling fast switching at 0.6 volts without breakdown after one trillion cycles.

papers.title: Wavelength selective fragmentation of metastable photoresponsive platelets via light irradiation
papers.abstract: Polymer lamellar crystals commonly consisting of folded chains are frequently formed since they are kinetically favorable. Hence, the metastability of polymer crystals can be regulated by crystallization pathways, and the thinner lamellar crystals display a tendency to transform into thicker crystals via lamellar thickening process. Herein, we report that photoresponsive two-dimensional (2D) platelets with low metastability undergo controllable fragmentation upon light irradiation. Mechanistic studies indicate that the metastability within a single platelet particle is heterogeneous across different domains. Light irradiation triggers lamellar thickening preferentially within less stable domains decorated with photoresponsive molecules, leading to site-specific fragmentation. To illustrate the utility of light-stimulated fragmentation, wavelength selective fragmentation of 2D segmented platelets with spatially defined photoresponsive molecules is achieved upon light irradiation, yielding 2D hollow platelet structure. This important feature holds significant promise for advanced applications such as spatially resolved therapeutic delivery systems, thereby broadening the functional scope of 2D nanomaterials. Two-dimensional platelets are typically formed from polymer lamellar crystals, with metastability regulated by crystallization pathways. Here, the authors report photoresponsive platelets with low metastability, which undergo controllable fragmentation on light irradiation.

papers.title: Increasing prevalence and expanding diversity of tet(X4)-carrying Salmonella in China
papers.abstract: The plasmid-mediated tigecycline resistance gene tet(X4) threatens the efficacy of tigecycline. While prevalent in Escherichia coli across diverse ecological niches, its evolutionary trajectory in Salmonella remains underappreciated. Here, we conducted nationwide genomic surveillance of 42403 clinical nontyphoidal Salmonella isolates collected from diarrheal patients in China between 2014 and 2025, of which 102 were tet(X4)-positive. Although the overall prevalence remained low, detection showed a statistically significant upward trend over 2019-2025. Importantly, the newly accrued 2025 data were broadly consistent with short-term forecasts generated by the beta regression model, providing partial support for short-term trend consistency. Genomic analyses showed that tet(X4) remained concentrated in ST34 but was also detected in additional sequence types, including ST469, ST8971, ST11 and one isolate with an unassigned ST, across multiple provinces, indicating broader geographic representation and genetic diversification. Plasmid analyses likewise revealed broader replicon diversity, with the dominant IncHI1A/IncHI1B/IncFIA background accompanied by less frequent IncHI2/IncHI2A, IncI1(Alpha) and IncFIA/IncFIB/IncFIC. Phylogenetic analyses further revealed shared clustering of the dominant plasmid background across host species and bacterial genera, consistent with cross-host and cross-genus circulation. Here, they determine that tet(X4)-carrying Salmonella remains rare in China but is being detected more often and in a wider range of bacterial sequence types and plasmids, supporting continued surveillance.

papers.title: Secondary organic aerosol formation from sequential oxidation of toluene and cresols
papers.abstract: Cresols are important urban emissions that can form multiple oxygen containing condensable vapors when they react with OH radicals in the atmosphere. These molecules contribute to secondary organic aerosols that have strong implications on climate and human health. In this work, we present flow reactor oxidation experiments demonstrating the rapid (sub-second) formation of condensable vapors with up to 10 oxygen atoms from the three cresol isomers (ortho-, para- and meta-cresol) under atmospheric conditions. Our quantum chemical calculations reveal that initial OH additions to the hydroxyl containing carbon atom lead to geminal diol intermediates that are critical to the rapid formation of condensable vapors from cresols and their key oxidation product, 3-methylcatechol. Incorporating these autoxidation mechanisms into model simulations shows that they contribute significantly to secondary organic aerosol composition. These results could explain the strong multi-generational contributions to aerosol from toluene and cresol, enabling a more accurate assessment of their climate and health impacts. Cresols and their oxidation products contribute to secondary organic aerosol, but their role in atmospheric oxidation remains poorly quantified. The authors report rapid formation of highly oxygenated organic molecules from cresols, identifying autoxidation mechanisms that could explain substantial multi-generational contributions to toluene and cresol secondary organic aerosol.

papers.title: Exaiptasia diaphana core microbiome members are lost under climate change conditions despite host thermal tolerance
papers.abstract: Acute and chronic exposure to elevated temperatures associated with Global Climate Change (GCC) threatens the structure and function of host-associated microbiomes, yet predicting microbial responses to heat stress remains challenging. We exposed two lines of the sea anemone, Exaiptasia diaphana, to acute and chronic thermal stress to quantify the impacts on cnidarian physiology and microbiome composition. Acute exposure caused rapid algal bleaching that was paired with pronounced shifts in bacteriome structure in both lines within 14 days of thermal exposure. Chronic exposure significantly affected the population structure, photo-physiology and bacteriome composition in only one host line, suggesting acclimation capacity depends on host-algal genetic backgrounds. Using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing of 493 individuals sampled across 180 days, we found that sampling date explained nine-fold more variation in the microbiome composition than temperature exposure. Despite this temporal variation, we identified 16 indicator taxa that consistently changed in relative abundance under thermal stress. These taxa became central hubs in microbial association networks with increasing levels of thermal stress, suggesting they played key roles in bacteriome reorganization. As many of these taxa were present in other cnidarians, including reef-building corals, they may represent targets for conservation strategies that aim to enhance resilience on reefs. In this study, the authors show that thermal stress impacts the microbiome of the sea anemone Exaiptasia diaphana differentially. Chronic and acute stress strongly affects the more sensitive line’s microbiome while the temperature tolerant line’s microbiome changed over time but not with temperature exposure.
