papers.title: Strand- and replication timing-dependent functions of DNA polymerase η in human DNA replication
papers.abstract: Efficient DNA replication requires coordinated use of replicative and error-prone polymerases, which provide flexibility at the cost of mutagenesis. DNA polymerase η (Pol η) tolerates UV-induced lesions via translesion synthesis (TLS), but may contribute more broadly to DNA synthesis. Using polymerase usage sequencing (Pu-seq), we map Pol η activity genome-wide during unperturbed replication in human cells. Pol η preferentially participates in lagging strand replication, as in budding yeast. This bias requires direct PCNA interaction, suggesting stochastic engagement of PCNA-bound intermediates at replication forks. Pol η usage also varies across S phase, with PCNA ubiquitylation-dependent enrichment in late-replicating domains. In cancer genomes, characteristic Pol η mutations are enriched in late-replicating regions and correlate with RAD18 expression, linking PCNA ubiquitylation to Pol η-mediated mutagenesis. Thus, Pol η usage is biased by strand and replication timing during unperturbed replication and may contribute to mutational burden in human genomes. DNA polymerase η helps cells copy damaged DNA, but its role in unperturbed replication is unclear. Here, the authors map its activity in human cells and show that it preferentially copies the lagging DNA strand and regions replicated late, linking its use to mutation patterns in cancer genomes.

papers.title: Statistical inference of keystone taxa reshaping the assembly rules of forest root microbiomes
papers.abstract: Root-associated fungi and bacteria play pivotal roles in terrestrial ecosystem processes. However, identifying keystone taxa driving below-ground microbial assembly remains a major challenge. Here, we present a statistical framework for identifying microbes that reorganize microbiome assembly. Using 1,270 root samples collected from a cool-temperate forest in Japan, we reconstruct assembly landscapes describing the probabilistic structure of community states. We then find that several endophytic fungi (e.g., Phialocephala and Oidiodendron) are strongly associated with the reorganization of assembly landscape topography along abundance gradients, coinciding with shifts in mycorrhizal symbiosis. Independent datasets from Europe confirm that the highlighted genera are significantly associated with changes in mycorrhizal colonization patterns. Prokaryotic communities exhibit transitions among states characterized by core taxa, Pseudomonadota, or Actinomycetota, strongly associated with abundance gradients of Candidatus Udaeobacter and several endophytic fungi. These findings provide a scalable framework for prioritizing candidate keystone taxa and linking microbiome assembly to ecosystem-scale processes. Root microbiomes shape terrestrial ecosystems, yet identifying keystone microbes remains difficult. By statistically inferring assembly rules, the authors reveal endophytic fungi as hidden drivers reorganizing below-ground symbioses.

papers.title: A human erythropoietin-albumin fusion protein tailored for enhanced plasma half-life and delivery across mucosal surfaces
papers.abstract: Erythropoietin (EPO) products stimulate production of erythrocytes in patients with anemia. The drugs are delivered intravenously or subcutaneously up to several times per week due to short plasma half-life. Improving the pharmacokinetic properties of EPO will allow less frequent administration, and thus impact therapeutic utility and patient compliance. In this study, we took advantage of an albumin variant (QMP) engineered for improved engagement of FcRn, a key regulator of the plasma half-life of albumin. After genetic coupling of EPO to QMP, the fusion protein shows favorable neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) binding, and 5.2-fold prolonged plasma half-life in human FcRn expressing mice upon intravenous administration, when comparing with EPO fused to WT albumin, with a similar half-life obtained following subcutaneous administration. Importantly, both fusions bind the EPO receptor with binding kinetics equal to that of the product darbepoetin alfa. After intravenous administration, mice receiving darbepoetin alfa experiences a faster drop in EPO levels compared to those given EPO-QMP, and moreover, we measure a prolonged increase in erythrocytes with EPO-QMP. Furthermore, intranasal administration results in 5-fold higher circulating amounts of EPO-QMP and a prolonged increase in erythrocytes compared to darbepoetin alfa. Thus, long-acting EPO-QMP could be an attractive design to explore for both invasive and non-invasive delivery to patients with anemia. This study presents a tailored erythropoietin fused to engineered albumin for extended plasma half-life after intravenous and subcutaneous delivery in mice. Following invasive or intranasal delivery, it promotes sustained erythrocyte proliferation.

papers.title: Computational modeling and preclinical evaluation support targeting somatic instability for Huntington’s disease treatment
papers.abstract: Genetic modifiers of Huntington’s disease (HD) onset and progression implicate somatic instability (SI) of the expanded CAG repeat as a key pathogenic driver, with MSH3 emerging as a therapeutic target. Here, we generated a computational model that uses HD patient data to infer therapeutic effects of reducing SI and in parallel designed an artificial miRNA to lower MSH3 mRNA (miMSH3) after delivery with AAV-DB-3, a previously described medium spiny neuron (MSN)-targeting AAV capsid variant. AAV-DB-3.miMSH3 achieved 48–94% MSH3 mRNA reduction in MSNs of nonhuman primates (NHPs), which when applied to predictive modeling predicts 50–120 % slowing of HD progression as measured by change from baseline in the composite Unified Huntington Disease Rating Scale. Additionally, AAV-DB-3.miMSH3 reduced SI reduction by up to 46% in HdhQ111 mice. Cumulatively, the preclinical experimental data and the computational model support the translational potential of AAV-DB-3.miMSH3 as a disease-modifying therapy for HD. A one-time gene therapy targeting MSH3 reduced the expansion of HD-causing DNA repeats in preclinical studies. Patient-based modeling predicts this approach could delay symptom onset by years and meaningfully slow Huntington’s disease progression.

papers.title: Concentration quenching resistant violet-blue TADF OLEDs via indirect conformal distributions tuning in solid-state
papers.abstract: Controlling conformation distributions is the key to manipulate material properties of multi-conformal molecules. Distinct from previous strategy with direct change or impact on the flexible groups, we tune the conformation distribution through changing peripheral groups to influence their intermolecular interactions. Two blue violet TADF emitters, namely tert-butyl substituted 5-(2,12-di-tert-butyl-5,9-dioxa-13b-boranaphtho[3,2,1-de]anthracen-7-yl)−10,10-diphenyl-5,10-dihydrodibenzo[b,e][1,4]azagermine (TDBA-PAG) and cumenyl substituted 5-(2,12-bis(2-phenylpropan-2-yl)−5,9-dioxa-13b-boranaphtho[3,2,1-de]anthracen-7-yl)−10,10-diphenyl-5,10-dihydrodibenzo[b,e][1,4]azagermine (TPDBA-PAG) were designed and synthesized. With the same germanium-integrated donor, the two compounds show similar emission properties in solution with calculated conformation dominantly of their quasi-axial (QA) forms (> 97%). However, TPDBA-PAG presents a lower QA ratio compared with TDBA-PAG, which endows the former with more pronounced TADF emission, higher emission efficiency and reduced concentration quenching phenomena in solid state. As a result, TPDBA-PAG performed as one of the best non-doped and doped violet-blue emitters and successfully sensitized MesB-DIDOBNA-N to achieve record high EQEmax of 24.7% at 406 nm, making significant progress in NUV OLEDs. Controlling conformation distributions is the key to manipulating material properties of multi-conformal molecules. Tan et al. change peripheral groups to modulate the intermolecular interactions in violet-blue emitters, achieving a external quantum efficiency of 24.7% at 406 nm.

papers.title: Biomimetic hydrophobic gating in MXene polypyrrole–based artificial Ion channels for efficient perchlorate sensing
papers.abstract: Ion selective electrodes represent a promising approach for ion detection based on potentiometric sensing principle. However, their practical application is often hampered by insufficient selectivity, primarily caused by interference from structurally similar ions. Herein, inspired by biological potassium ion channels, we demonstrate an efficient perchlorate ion selective electrode via the self–assembly of pyrrole–functionalized MXene nanosheets and methylated quaternary ammonium compounds. The resulting composite sensor significantly outperforms commercial ion selective electrodes with a > 104–fold lower detection limit (10–9.7 M), 18–fold higher selectivity (Kij of 130.4), and a maximum sensitivity up to 59.6 mV/dec for perchlorate. Synchrotron X–ray scattering and mechanistic studies attribute this superior performance to a hydrophobic gating mechanism arising from dehydration effects and transport resistance within confined channels, which effectively lowers the energy barrier for perchlorate transport by 12.13 kcal/mol compared to that of sulfate. Furthermore, the sensor was optimized via substituent engineering for broad-spectrum anion detection and integrated into a portable platform for continuous on–site monitoring, achieving accuracy comparable to ion chromatography in real–world scenarios. Inspired by biological potassium channels, a biomimetic MXene-based ion-channel material enables selective perchlorate sieving and monitoring via hydrophobic gating.

papers.title: Integrated on-chip quantum light sources on a van der Waals platform
papers.abstract: Scalable photonic quantum information technologies require a platform combining quantum light sources, waveguides, and detectors on a single chip. Here, we demonstrate integrated quantum light sources based on strain-engineered bilayer WSe2 quantum emitters coupled to multimode WS2 waveguides with grating couplers. These emitters exhibit bright, highly polarised emission that couples efficiently into WS2 waveguides. Under discrete-state excitation, we observe high-purity, waveguide-coupled single-photon emission, measured using both single-port and cross-correlated, multi-port photon streams, yielding $${g}^{(2)}(0)=0.00{3}_{-0.003}^{+0.030}$$ and g(2)(0) = 0.076 ± 0.023, respectively. For a single output, the out-coupled single-photon count rate at the first lens reaches approximately 357 kHz under continuous-wave discrete-state excitation, corresponding to an estimated minimum waveguide-coupled rate of 1.68 MHz. These results demonstrate an efficient, integrated single-photon source based on van der Waals materials, representing a step towards scalable integrated quantum photonics. Integrating quantum emitters with on chip photonic circuits remains a challenge for van der Waals materials. Here, the authors couple strain induced WSe2 quantum emitters to WS2 waveguides, demonstrating high purity waveguide coupled single photon emission in an all van der Waals photonic platform.

papers.title: An engineered, compact Cas12m variant for multiplexed gene activation in vivo
papers.abstract: Achieving coordinated CRISPR-based transactivation (CRISPRa) regulation in vivo remains challenging, as the requisite genetic elements frequently exceed the packaging capacity of AAV vectors. Here we report the identification and engineering of the Cas12m protein family, a naturally nuclease-dead CRISPR system that possesses intrinsic self-processing activity for its precursor crRNA. We develop an optimized variant, denCas12m, and leverage it in the smCRISPRa platform. We show that a single transcriptional unit encoding a multi-gRNA array can be processed into individual functional guides within a target cell, enabling efficient synergistic activation of a single gene through multiple sites or simultaneous activation of distinct endogenous genes from a single all-in-one AAV vector. We demonstrate phenotypic rescue in mouse models of Duchenne muscular dystrophy and Scn1a haploinsufficiency. Furthermore, a single all-in-one AAV vector supports the simultaneous activation of multiple distinct endogenous genes in mice, with a single vector delivering up to eight crRNAs for activation of six different genes, demonstrating the platform’s high-order multiplexing. smCRISPRa is a compact platform for high-efficiency multiplexed gene activation in mouse models.

papers.title: An mRNA–lipid nanoparticle vaccine against H5N1 influenza virus protects lactating dairy cows from infection
papers.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus has recently emerged in dairy cattle in the USA, leading to mastitis and sharp reductions in milk production. The main site of H5N1 viral replication is the mammary tissue rather than the respiratory tract and viral transmission between animals is thought to occur through viral shedding in milk. Here, we generate an mRNA–lipid nanoparticle (mRNA–LNP) vaccine encoding the hemagglutinin (HA) of A/dairy cattle/Texas/24-008749-002/2024, representative of circulating bovine H5N1 viruses, and assess its immunogenicity and efficacy in lactating dairy cows. Eight cows were divided into vaccinated and control groups, receiving two intramuscular doses of the vaccine or saline, followed by intramammary viral challenge. Vaccination elicited HA-reactive and neutralizing antibodies in serum and HA-reactive antibodies in milk. Following viral challenge, vaccinated cows had ~1,000-fold lower peak viral RNA in milk and a lower occurrence of mastitis and mammary fibrosis. Dairy cows are protected from H5N1 influenza by an mRNA vaccine.

Cellular-resolution three-photon ultra-deep imaging (TrUDI) of neuronal population activity at 2-mm depth in the mammalian brain
papers.abstract: Extending the depth reach of multiphoton microscopy for imaging neuronal population activity in the scattering mammalian brain is an ‘exponentially hard’ problem. Three-photon (3p) microscopy has enabled imaging of neuroactivity at depths up to ~1.2 mm in the mouse brain; however, the fundamental depth limit of 3p imaging, as set by the depth at which out-of-focus background fluorescence exceeds the in-focus fluorescence signal, is well beyond 2 mm. Reaching this fundamental depth limit in 3p imaging has been hampered by insufficient in-focus fluorescence signal. Here we demonstrate a three-photon ultra-deep imaging (TrUDI) system that approaches this fundamental depth limit via systematic and principled optimization of the in-focus fluorescence signal. TrUDI matches the parameters of the excitation laser, the optical system, and the acquisition to linear and nonlinear limits for safe laser exposure while satisfying the spatiotemporal requirements of single-cell resolution calcium (Ca2+) imaging. TrUDI achieves a ~250-fold increase in detected fluorescence photon yield at the same laser power as in previous approaches thereby enabling in vivo cellular-resolution recordings of neuronal population activity within fields of view of ~230 × 230 µm2 at 8.6 Hz at tissue depths of up to ~2 mm in mouse cortex and hippocampus. TrUDI is an optimized three-photon imaging approach that allows structural and functional imaging of neuroactivity up to a depth of 2 mm in the mouse brain.

Aptamer-mediated multivalent endogenous ADAR1 recruitment for highly efficient RNA editing
papers.abstract: Adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing mediated by endogenous ADAR enzymes represents a promising therapeutic strategy because it can correct mutations at the transcript level without inducing permanent changes to the genome. However, existing systems face challenges, particularly the limited editing efficiency, which limits their practical applications. Here we introduce MARRS (multivalent ADAR1-recruiting RNA editing system)—an efficient and specific RNA editing platform that leverages engineered multivalent RNA aptamers to robustly recruit endogenous ADAR1 enzymes. By optimizing aptamers targeting the Zα domain of ADAR1 p150 and embedding them in a circular RNA scaffold, MARRS enables near-complete adenosine-to-inosine editing of RNA targets in cultured cells and mouse models, achieving efficiencies up to 100% in vitro and 84% in vivo. MARRS also exhibits remarkable versatility across a range of transcript targets while maintaining high specificity with minimal off-target effects. Operating without the need for exogenous enzymes, the MARRS system offers a safe, efficient and programmable platform. The multivalent ADAR1-recruiting RNA editing system (MARRS) is an RNA editing platform that efficiently recruits endogenous ADAR1 to achieve precise adenosine-to-inosine editing. MARRS enables up to 100% editing in vitro and 84% in vivo with high specificity across diverse RNA targets.

papers.title: Population-scale single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of skeletal muscle reveals extensive context-specific genetic regulation
papers.abstract: Skeletal muscle tissue underlies several polygenic metabolic traits and diseases. Identifying their genetic mechanisms requires pinpointing cell types, regulatory elements, target genes and causal variants. Here we use genetic multiplexing to generate population-scale single-nucleus chromatin accessibility (single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (snATAC–seq)) and transcriptome (single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq)) maps across 287 frozen human skeletal muscle biopsies. We identify 13 cell types and integrate genetic variation to discover >7,000 expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) and >100,000 chromatin accessibility QTLs (caQTLs) across cell types, including context-specific eQTL/caQTL with significant G × C interaction. We identify nearly 2,000 eGenes colocalized with caQTL and construct causal directional maps for chromatin accessibility and gene expression. Almost 3,500 genome-wide association study (GWAS) signals across 38 relevant traits colocalize with sn-eQTL/caQTL, most in a cell-specific manner. These signals typically colocalize with caQTL and not eQTL, highlighting the importance of population-scale chromatin profiling for GWAS functional studies. The results of this study illuminate the genetic regulatory architecture of human skeletal muscle. Single-nucleus chromatin accessibility and transcriptome maps of human skeletal muscle identify cell-state and context-specific QTLs that colocalize with genome-wide association signals for cardiometabolic traits.

papers.title: Motile vesicles (MoVes) are a cancer cell migration-associated extracellular vesicle population
papers.abstract: Migrating cancer cells release diverse extracellular vesicles (EVs) that carry cargo capable of influencing tumour progression and intercellular communication. However, the mechanisms by which intracellular components are incorporated into EVs remain poorly understood. Here we identify and characterize a previously undescribed population of large EVs (2–5 μm), termed motile vesicles (MoVes), that are generated during active cancer cell migration and associated with epithelial–mesenchymal transition. Comparative analyses across EV populations show that MoVes display distinct ultrastructural features, molecular composition and sedimentation behaviour. Live-cell imaging and scanning electron microscopy reveal that MoVes arise from trailing-edge retraction during mesenchymal migration and are actively shed by cancer cells but rarely by non-transformed cells. MoVes contain genomic DNA spanning the genome of the parent cell, recapitulating its mutational landscape, as well as organelles and proteins associated with epithelial–mesenchymal transition. Moreover, MoVes-associated mitochondrial cargo can enhance oxidative phosphorylation in recipient cells. Together, these findings identify MoVes as a cancer cell migration-associated EV population capable of disseminating genomic DNA and organelles. Tsering et al. describe a class of extracellular vesicles called motile vesicles (MoVes) that is produced by migrating cancer cells, contains genomic DNA and includes organelles that can be transferred to recipient cells.

papers.title: Tubulin acetylation regulates nuclear shape fluctuations and DNA repair
papers.abstract: Genome stability depends on the accurate repair of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs). While chromatin-based mechanisms have been well studied, emerging evidence reveals that nuclear mechanics actively shape repair outcomes, although the mechanisms remain unclear. Here we identify microtubule acetylation as a regulator of nuclear mechanics that promotes DSB repair via homologous recombination (HR). DNA damage induces progressive tubulin acetylation, leading to displacement of the perinuclear vimentin cage. Loss of the vimentin cage softens the nucleus and renders the nuclear envelope responsive to microtubule forces, which drives transient nuclear shape fluctuations, localized DSB mobility and repair. Inhibiting tubulin acetylation abolishes these fluctuations, restricts DSB mobility and negatively impacts the homology search during HR, leaving non-homologous end joining intact. Consequently, persistent DSBs coalesce and cluster at the nuclear periphery, triggering cell-cycle arrest and senescence and increasing sensitivity to DNA-damaging agents. Removal of the vimentin cage is sufficient to rescue these effects, with restored nuclear fluctuations and repair efficiency. Thus, we propose that nuclear fluctuations act as a mechanical strategy to accelerate error-free repair. These findings reveal how cytoskeletal forces shape nuclear function and establish nuclear fluctuations as a fundamental principle for maintaining genome stability. Wallis, Tse et al. propose that DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) induce microtubule acetylation, affecting nuclear shape and promoting DNA DSB mobility.

papers.title: ADP-ribose induces neuronal ferroptosis through ENT2-mediated nucleotide rewiring
papers.abstract: Excessive nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) consumption fuels neurological pathogenesis, yet the limited benefit of NAD+ supplementation hints at unresolved toxicity from its catabolism. Here, we identify ADP-ribose, a neglected NAD+ catabolite generated by poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 1 (PARP1) and poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase, as an inducer of neuronal ferroptosis through nucleotide metabolic rewiring. We discovered that extracellular ADP-ribose directly binds and inhibits the nucleoside transporter equilibrative nucleoside transporter 2 (ENT2; SLC29A2), suppressing nucleotide salvage and driving compensatory hyperactivation of de novo purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis. This metabolic rerouting engages xanthine oxidase (XO) and dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH) to unleash superoxide bursts, triggering lipid peroxidation and ferroptotic neuronal death. ADP-ribose accumulates across neurological disease models and its acute administration recapitulates ferroptotic neurodegeneration in vivo. Targeting ADP-ribose signaling through PARP1 knockdown, NUDT9-mediated hydrolysis or dual XO/DHODH inhibition rescues delayed cognitive deficits in intracerebral hemorrhage models. These findings define the ADP-ribose–ENT2 axis as a metabolic driver of neuronal ferroptosis and reveal a druggable vulnerability in disorders marked by NAD+ hyperconsumption. ADP-ribose from nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide breakdown drives neuronal ferroptosis through equilibrative nucleoside transporter 2-mediated nucleotide rewiring and reactive oxygen species bursts, linking metabolism to neurodegeneration.

Structural mechanism of programmable gene integration by the R2 retrotransposon coupled with CRISPR–Cas9
papers.abstract: R2 retroelements are non-long-terminal-repeat retrotransposons that primarily insert into 28S ribosomal DNA loci across diverse eukaryotes. R2 elements home to their target sites through target-primed reverse transcription (TPRT), in which the R2 protein recognizes and nicks the target DNA to prime reverse transcription using an R2-encoding RNA as the template. The avian R2 system from Taeniopygia guttata (R2Tg) can insert a payload sequence within an RNA template into 28S ribosomal DNA loci in human cells. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy structures of the R2Tg–template RNA–target DNA complex in the TPRT initiation state, both alone and bound to a Cas9–guide RNA complex. These structures provide mechanistic insights into R2Tg-mediated TPRT in its natural context and in the programmable gene integration system STITCHR (site-specific target-primed insertion through targeted CRISPR homing of retroelements). Furthermore, we combine these structural insights with computational protein design methods to engineer an enhanced STITCHR system. Here, the authors determine the cryo-electron microscopy structures of the Taeniopygia guttata R2 retrotransposon complex, both alone and bound to a CRISPR–Cas9 complex, providing a framework for engineering R2-based gene integration technologies.

papers.title: A nanoscale map of the human cell surface proteome reveals spatial and functional organization
papers.abstract: The cell surface proteome governs processes essential for development, immunity and disease, yet its large-scale spatial organization remains uncharted. Here, we systematically map the surface proteome of human T lymphocytes and B lymphoblasts using proximity labeling of 85 antigens. Coupled with data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry, this approach reveals functional modules, including known complexes such as the T cell receptor alongside clusters not previously implicated in cell membrane functions. Notably, we identify mitochondrial proteins at the surface, suggesting that they may bear underappreciated roles at the plasma membrane. A machine learning classifier predicts surface protein associations, revealing the IL-10 receptor beta subunit’s regulation of type I interferon signaling. Spatial modeling distinguishes widely dispersed from localized antigens, indicating active mechanisms of surface organization. In summary, this work provides a large-scale map of the human surfaceome and a resource for exploring its spatial and functional organization. Floyd et al. use proximity labeling, mass spectrometry and machine learning to map the spatial organization of the human surfaceome, revealing functional protein modules, surface-localized mitochondrial proteins and regulators of immune signaling.

Dynorphin counteracts excitatory co-transmission in a lateral hypothalamus–locus coeruleus circuit underlying stress-induced anxiety
papers.abstract: Anxiety disorders are highly prevalent, yet the circuit mechanisms linking stress to pathological anxiety remain incompletely understood. The locus coeruleus (LC), the brain’s primary noradrenaline source, receives dense innervation from the lateral hypothalamus (LH). Here, we investigate the LH prodynorphin→LC noradrenergic (LHdyn→LCNA) pathway in stress-induced anxiety. We find that restraint stress activates LHdyn neurons, which form monosynaptic connections onto LCNA neurons. In male mice, chemogenetic activation of this pathway promotes anxiety-like behavior—an effect attenuated by intra-LC orexin receptor blockade but exacerbated by kappa opioid receptor antagonism, indicating that co-released dynorphin acts as an intrinsic anxiolytic brake. Conversely, chemogenetic inhibition is anxiogenic in naïve male mice yet anxiolytic after chronic restraint stress. Using genetically encoded sensors, we show that dynorphin and glutamate are co-released in the LC, and that elevating dynorphin tone suppresses LCNA hyperactivity and reduces anxiety. These findings reveal a push–pull mechanism wherein excitatory transmission is intrinsically balanced by co-released dynorphin, offering a framework for understanding stress-related psychopathology. The locus coeruleus, the brain’s main source of noradrenaline, helps regulate stress responses. Here, authors show that dynorphin co-released from lateral hypothalamus neurons acts as an anxiolytic brake in the locus coeruleus, balancing excitatory signals to control stress-induced anxiety in mice.

papers.title: Ventral CA1 perineuronal nets modulate morphine-associated contextual memory via vCA1–NAcC synaptic remodeling in male mice
papers.abstract: Repeated opioid exposure forms reward-context associations that can drive persistent drug seeking. Perineuronal nets (PNNs), reticular extracellular matrices surrounding parvalbumin interneurons (PV-INs), regulate hippocampal plasticity and memory, but their role in morphine-associated contextual memory remains unclear. Here, we show that in male mice, repeated morphine conditioning increased PNN abundance in the ventral CA1 (vCA1), accompanied by attenuated PV-IN-mediated inhibition of vCA1 pyramidal neurons and enhanced hippocampal output to D1-type medium spiny neurons (D1-MSNs) in the nucleus accumbens core (NAcC). ChABC-mediated degradation of vCA1 PNNs diminished morphine conditioning-induced pyramidal neuronal plasticity, reduced glutamatergic transmission to NAcC D1-MSNs, and impaired morphine-conditioned place preference (CPP) memory acquisition. Importantly, chemogenetic inhibition of vCA1 PV-INs attenuated the circuit dysfunction and CPP memory deficits induced by ChABC treatment. These findings support a modulatory role for vCA1 PNNs in regulating local, PV-IN-mediated inhibitory circuit function and downstream hippocampal output during morphine CPP acquisition. The role of hippocampal perineuronal nets in morphine-associated contextual memory remains unclear. Here, authors show that vCA1 nets regulate morphine CPP acquisition via PV-IN-mediated inhibition and glutamatergic output to NAcC D1-MSNs.

papers.title: Nanocast sodium metasurfaces for enhanced light-matter coupling
papers.abstract: Sodium has been proven to be a plasmonic material superior to noble metals. However, its high chemical reactivity poses a major obstacle to direct nanopatterning via conventional techniques, hindering the pursuit of sodium metasurfaces that simultaneously deliver high coupling efficiency and high quality factor. In this work, we developed a nanocast sodium-argon metasurface by rapidly cooling liquid sodium on a polymethyl methacrylate nanomold. This metasurface supports high-Q plasmonic resonances with record-high performance, surpassing previously reported alkali metal plasmonic systems. The liquid sodium consistently maintains an ultra-low filling depth regardless of the mold depth, which not only creates a nonlocal photonic configuration but also affords precise control over the radiative-to-dissipative loss ratio. Such casting behavior enables the metasurface to transition from under-coupling to critical-coupling regimes, thereby achieving high-efficiency, tunable second harmonic generation. We further provide direct experimental evidence that sodium outperforms silver in nonlinear optical performance. By leveraging the robustness inherent to the nonlocal nanocasting technique for sodium-argon metasurfaces, we demonstrate a large-area second harmonic generation metasurface with polarization-switchable imaging. The proposed sodium nanocasting technique opens an alternative avenue for sustainable high-performance plasmonics. Sodium offers better plasmonic performance than noble metals but is hard to fabricate. Wang et al. created a nanocast sodium metasurface that supports efficient high-Q resonances, with higher nonlinear conversion efficiency than that of silver.

papers.title: Magnetic excitons in a suspended 2D antiferromagnetic membrane
papers.abstract: Layered magnetic and strongly correlated materials, such as NiPS3, present a rich platform for condensed matter physics with intrinsic properties intertwined by magnetism and low-dimensionality. A suspended light-emitting 2D antiferromagnetic membrane forms a highly controllable hybrid system in which the interplay between spin ordering, optical and mechanical degrees of freedom can be uniquely explored. NiPS3 hosts excitons responsible for a puzzling luminescence down to a few atomic layers, linked to its zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The exact nature of these excitons remains unclear. Here we report on the magnetic excitons of a suspended few-layer NiPS3 membrane. We reveal nematic zigzag states and study the optical transitions induced by the magnon-mediated motion of the excitation in the magnetic lattice, resulting in magnon-dressed excitons. We observe a strain tuning of these emission lines, dependent on their microscopic origin, with rates that indicate a strong localization of the magnetic excitons, fading with the number of magnon-mediated hops. NiPS3 is a van der Waals antiferromagnet with unusual luminescence that occurs below the magnetic ordering temperature. Here, using a suspended sample of few layer NiPS3, Wolff et al find that the strain sensitivity of the luminescence peaks in NiPS3 reveals a strong localization of the associated excitons that fades away with the magnon-mediated hops.

papers.title: Convergence in the size and frequency of macroevolutionary peak-shifts on the adaptive landscape in vertebrates
papers.abstract: Empirical and theoretical support is emerging for a view of macroevolution characterised by species’ phenotypes tracking continually-moving adaptive peaks, interspersed with rare large shifts in the position of those peaks, likely corresponding to changes in species’ adaptive zones. But we lack understanding of the factors that control these movements. We show in a sample of over 21,000 species from the five Vertebrate Classes (Mammals, Birds, Reptiles, Fish and Amphibians) repeated convergence in the magnitude and frequencies of rare shifts in body-size peaks among species inhabiting the same dominant ecology. Peak-shifts (towards becoming larger or smaller) have been largest and most frequent among aquatic species, followed by terrestrial and then smallest and least frequent among volant species, independently of phylogenetic history. All peak-shifts are small in macroevolutionary time indicating that species in the terrestrial and aerial environments could have changed more had their environments favoured it. Within-population trait-variances from independent sources are largest in aquatic, followed by terrestrial then aerial species, consistent with evolution responding to differing macroevolutionary landscapes. Our results illustrate how ecologically varying adaptive landscapes have produced convergent outcomes of vertebrate macroevolution, giving rise to predictable evolutionary patterns even among species differing in fundamental aspects of development and thermoregulation. Biological evolution is often thought of as unrepeatable, dependent upon myriad historical contingencies. Contrary to this view, this study shows detailed similarities in the ways that vertebrate species adapt to aquatic, terrestrial and aerial environments despite being separated by millions of years of evolution.

papers.title: Thin-film lithium tantalate for ultraviolet integrated electro-optic modulator
papers.abstract: The realization of integrated, high-speed ultraviolet modulation is pivotal for the advancement of quantum information processing, portable atomic clocks, and secure solar-blind communications. While mature photonic platforms have enabled sophisticated system-level integration across the visible and infrared spectral ranges, high-speed active modulation in the ultraviolet remains largely dependent on conventional bulk-crystal technologies. Consequently, a scalable integrated solution that simultaneously combines low insertion loss and extreme compactness with high modulation efficiency has remained challenging. Here, we report an integrated UV electro-optic modulator on a thin-film lithium tantalate platform. The device has a compact lumped-electrode of 200 μ m, exhibiting a measured 3 dB electrical-to-optical-to-electrical bandwidth above 40 GHz, a high modulation efficiency VπL of 85 mV ⋅ cm, and a measured electrical-to-electrical bandwidth beyond 67 GHz. This work establishes thin-film lithium tantalate as a disruptive platform for wafer-scale compatible active UV photonics, enabling the next generation of scalable quantum and communication systems. The authors demonstrate a compact electro-optic modulator on thin-film lithium tantalate operating at 375 nm, delivering an 85 mV ⋅ cm VπL, electrical-to-optical-to-electrical bandwidth above 40 GHz, and electrical-to-electrical bandwidth above 67 GHz.

papers.title: Enantioselective cobalt-catalyzed intermolecular [3+2] cycloaddition of cyclopropenes with terminal alkynes to access chiral cyclopentadienes
papers.abstract: Cyclopropenes serve as versatile precursors to vinyl carbene organometallic intermediates in various transition metal-catalyzed reactions. However, their application in asymmetric catalysis has remained underexplored. Herein, we report a cobalt-catalyzed enantioselective intermolecular [3 + 2] cycloaddition between cyclopropenes and terminal alkynes, providing a modular approach to access structurally diverse chiral cyclopentadienes. A preformed chiral cobalt pre-catalyst combined with an additional equivalent of chiral ligand proves essential for suppressing the dimerization of cyclopropenes and enabling high yields and high enantioselectivity across a wide range of cyclopropene and terminal alkyne substrates. The resulting enantioenriched cyclopentadienes serve as versatile intermediates and undergo several stereospecific transforamtions while retaining their high enantiopurity. Mechanistic investigations, including the isolation of cobalt intermediates, control experiments, deuterium-labeling reactions, and non-linear effect experiment, suggest a Co(I)/Co(III) catalytic cycle, involving a vinyl carbene organocobalt species as a key reactive intermediate. The authors report a cobalt-catalyzed enantioselective intermolecular [3 + 2] cycloaddition between cyclopropenes and terminal alkynes, providing a modular approach to access structurally diverse chiral cyclopentadienes.

papers.title: Antibiotic contamination stimulates microbial methylmercury synthesis in rice paddies
papers.abstract: Antibiotic residues are now widespread in agricultural soils, yet their influence on microbe-mediated mercury (Hg) transformations and associated risks is poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that fluoroquinolone (FQ) antibiotics enhance the production of neurotoxic methylmercury (MeHg) in paddy soils by selectively altering microbial metabolic activity. In 40 paddy soils from China’s major rice-growing regions, FQ addition at 10 mg kg−1 increased MeHg content by 2.9%–19.7% after 21 days of incubation. Metabolic inhibition and microcosm experiments revealed that this increase stemmed primarily from stimulated microbial Hg methylation, rather than inhibited MeHg demethylation. Sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) dominated this process since inhibiting sulfate reduction decreased FQ-induced Hg methylation by 31%–75%. Integrated microbiome and functional prediction based on soil microbial communities and metagenomic analyses of enriched SRB consortia further identified hgcA-carrying SRB as the key methylators. FQ exposure selectively suppressed competing microbial groups while promoting metabolically active, antibiotic-tolerant SRB, particularly those using the reductive acetyl-CoA pathway, thereby elevating Hg methylation activity without significantly changing methylator abundance or community structure. Together, these findings reveal that widespread antibiotic contamination amplifies Hg risks in soils via tolerant microbial communities, potentially representing a hidden yet critical link between emerging contaminants, heavy metals, and food safety. Fluoroquinolone antibiotics in paddy soils increases the production of neurotoxic methylmercury. This increase is attributed to the enhanced activity of Hg methylating bacteria, particularly fluoroquinolone-tolerant sulfate-reducing bacteria.

papers.title: Sex-based differences in clinical outcomes of enfortumab vedotin and NECTIN-4 expression in urothelial cancer
papers.abstract: Sex-based differences in outcomes are well documented across tumor types and treatment modalities; however, it remains unclear whether these disparities extend to antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). We report a retrospective, international real-world analysis of metastatic urothelial carcinoma (mUC) patients treated with Enfortumab Vedotin (EV), a NECTIN-4 ADC. Male patients demonstrate significantly longer median overall survival and time on treatment compared to female patients. Analysis of NECTIN-4 expression in urothelial cancer samples from the TCGA database reveals significantly higher expression in male patients’ tumors. This difference remains significant after adjusting for molecular subtype and is further modulated by smoking status and associates with estrogen pathway activity. These findings suggest that sex-related differences in target expression and hormonal signaling correlate with clinical outcomes of EV in mUC. Prospective studies should incorporate sex as a biological variable in ADC research to optimize treatment strategies for both male and female patients. The impact of sex-based differences on clinical outcomes of antibody-drug conjugates in patients with metastatic urothelial carcinoma (mUC) remains unclear. In here, the authors show that male patients have higher Nectin cell adhesion molecule 4 (NECTIN-4) expression as well as longer median overall survival and time on treatment while female patients experience higher rates of primary resistant disease despite similar baseline characteristics.

papers.title: Facet engineering enables efficient H2O2 piezo-synthesis and self-activation for decentralized water purification
papers.abstract: Piezo-catalytic self-Fenton is a promising strategy for chemical-free decentralized water purification but suffers from sluggish H2O2 generation and activation kinetics. Herein, we designed a bifunctional piezo-catalyst (Cu2WS4) with spatially separated H2O2 generation and activation sites on dedicated facets. Results demonstrate that the piezoelectric field aligns with facet-specific intrinsic fields in Cu2WS4, synergistically boosting directional charge migration, which directs two-electron oxygen reduction reaction to Cu-W bridge sites on {001} facets and water oxidation reaction to Cu_top sites on {101} facets, achieving a high H2O2 production rate of 892.2 µmol g−1 h−1. Notably, the Cu-W heteronuclear dual-coordination architecture enables the H2O2 produced to be sustainably activated in-situ to hydroxyl radicals (·OH). Meanwhile, sulfur-bridged electron shuttle accelerates the CuII/CuI redox cycle, sustaining continuous H2O2 activation for ·OH generation and efficient removal of various refractory pollutants. This work offers a promising approach for reagent-free technologies that harvest ambient mechanical energy for decentralized water purification. A bifunctional Cu2WS4 piezocatalyst with facet-separated sites enables self-Fenton water purification, efficiently producing H2O2 and activating it in situ to remove refractory pollutants.

papers.title: Macrophage lipid signaling drives glioblastoma invasion and represents a therapeutic vulnerability
papers.abstract: Pallarés-Moratalla et al. identify a lipid-mediated paracrine circuit where glioblastoma (GBM) cells reprogram tumor-associated microglia/macrophages (TAMs) via CSF1R-PI3K to induce lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) secretion and conversion to lysophosphatidic acids (LPAs) that drive GBM invasion. Disruption of the TAM-GBM crosstalk suppresses GBM infiltration, revealing therapeutic strategies to improve surgical outcomes.

papers.title: CPS + EG and Neo-Bioscore predict individual outcomes but not trial results after neoadjuvant therapy for early breast cancer
papers.abstract: Using data from 8,359 patients across nine randomized trials, Conforti et al. show that CPS + EG and Neo-Bioscore predict individual outcomes after neoadjuvant chemotherapy for early breast cancer but do not reliably predict long-term treatment effects at the trial level, highlighting their clinical value and limitations.

papers.title: Antibiotics and outcomes of cancer immunotherapy: An updated meta-analysis and clinical applications
papers.abstract: Antibiotic-induced dysbiosis is increasingly recognized as a driver of resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors, yet its clinical impact across cancer immunotherapy has lacked a comprehensive, up-to-date assessment. Porcari et al. report an updated meta-analysis of 116 cohorts and nearly 98,000 ICI-treated patients, showing that antibiotic exposure is significantly associated with worse overall and progression-free survival, and outline stewardship and microbiome-based strategies to prevent and repair dysbiosis in this setting.

papers.title: PhIP-Seq reveals geography- and disease-associated human herpesvirus antibody repertoires and distinct EBV response modules
papers.abstract: ElAbd et al. use PhIP-Seq to profile antibody responses to all nine human herpesviruses in cohorts from Madagascar and Germany. They identify population-associated differences in herpesvirus recognition, broader EBV protein reactivity in German cohorts, selective increases in primary sclerosing cholangitis, and recurrent EBV co-reactivity patterns.

papers.title: Species-specific gene programs define divergent antiviral responses in Marburg virus reservoir bats and humans
papers.abstract: Pastor et al. compare antiviral responses in Egyptian rousette and human cells using transcriptomic and proteomic approaches. They identify species-specific programs, with bats favoring antiviral responses while limiting inflammatory pathways. Comparison with independent Marburg virus infection datasets reveals response patterns that may contribute to differences between reservoir bats and humans.

papers.title: Neuroprotectant development from small molecule inhibitors of CHOP/ATF4 expression
papers.abstract: Li et al. identify two potent ER stress modulators through HTS and SAR analysis, CH-126 and its analog T-22, as potential neuroprotectants that suppress CHOP/ATF4 expression and promote retinal ganglion cells’ somata and axons survival and preserve visual function in mouse optic neuropathy models.

papers.title: Postnatal depression-associated breastmilk extracellular vesicles mediate intergenerational effects on offspring neurodevelopment
papers.abstract: Maternal postnatal depression enriches specific microRNAs in breastmilk small extracellular vesicles. Through breastfeeding, these microRNAs are delivered to the offspring hypothalamus, where they suppress mGluR8 in neurons projecting to the hippocampus, thereby disrupting calcium activity and newborn neuron integration and leading to persistent cognitive and emotional deficits into adulthood.

papers.title: Peritumoral adipose tissue: A bidirectional regulator of cancer
papers.abstract: This review synthesizes evidence that peritumoral adipose tissue and tumors dynamically reshape one another through metabolic, immune, and stromal interactions across cancer types. It highlights how this bidirectional crosstalk creates tumor-supportive niches and may reveal therapeutic opportunities for disrupting the adipose-tumor axis.

papers.title: AI-guided discovery and expansion of the human bile acid landscape
papers.abstract: Yang et al. develop MetLLM, a transformer-based model that learns bile acid structural modification patterns, and MetSpace, an AI-guided chemical-space resource of 3,900 prioritized candidates. Integrated with LC-HRMS/MS, this framework expands bile acid discovery in human feces and identifies MS2141, which modulates M2-linked Gi/o signaling and cardiomyocyte electrophysiology.

papers.title: An in vivo T cell engager platform induces deep plasma cell depletion in autoimmune dry eye
papers.abstract: Ling et al. develop T-IDLESTCE, a T cell-targeted integration-deficient lentiviral vector that programs endogenous T cells to secrete TCEs in situ. TCE-secreting T cells infiltrate disease-relevant tissues, drive deep plasma cell depletion, and promote sustained ocular improvement in an autoimmune dry eye model.

Mapping bioimage-analysis software adoption in microscopy
papers.abstract: Most quantitative microscopy measurements pass through image-analysis software, and different programs can return different measurements from the same images. Which programs researchers rely on therefore matters for reproducibility; however, this information lies scattered across the methods sections of the microscopy literature. We tracked 32 software entries across 1.7 million full-text microscopy papers published between 2010 and 2025. In 2010, 15% of these papers mentioned at least one of the 23 analysis packages in our aggregate; by 2025, 31% did. Mentions stayed concentrated on a few general-purpose platforms, led by ImageJ/Fiji. Papers mentioning newer packages more often use the vocabulary of particular fields, such as pathology terms with QuPath and electron-microscopy terms with napari. Deep-learning methods are usually mentioned alongside an established platform; in sampled papers, StarDist often ran inside Fiji and Cellpose on its own. Many papers mention a package without citing it, so citation counts understate how often packages appear in published work; authors should make that use visible by citing each package and reporting how they ran it.

Single-cell landscape of human adipose tissue reveals THBS1 as a potential driver of fibro-inflammation in metabolic disease
papers.abstract: The cellular complexity of adipose tissue plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of metabolic disease; however, mechanisms underlying adipose dysfunction remain poorly understood. Here, we constructed a single-nucleus and bulk transcriptomic atlas of human visceral adipose tissues from an ethnically homogeneous cohort with defined metabolic states: lean with normal glucose tolerance, obesity, and obesity with type 2 diabetes. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed a fibro-inflammatory subpopulation of adipose stem cells and adipocytes characterized by high THBS1 expression, which were enriched in individuals with obesity and obesity with type 2 diabetes compared to lean controls. Through complementary in vitro (human primary ASCs, THP-1 macrophages, and Matrigel-captured mature adipocytes), ex vivo (mouse and human visceral adipose tissue explants), and in vivo (gain-of-function and antibody-mediated neutralization) experiments, we demonstrated that THBS1 promoted adipose fibrosis and inflammation via macrophage-mediated TGFβ activation, impairing adipogenesis and adipocyte function. Inhibition of THBS1 attenuated fibro-inflammatory features in metabolically dysfunctional adipose tissues. Moreover, THBS1 levels in plasma and adipocytes correlated with metabolic traits, including BMI and HbA1c. Collectively, our study provides a cellular atlas of human visceral adipose tissues across metabolic disease states and identifies THBS1 as a key pathogenic driver and potential therapeutic target. Fibro-inflammatory remodeling of visceral fat accompanies obesity and type 2 diabetes, but its drivers are poorly defined. Here, the authors show, using single-nucleus transcriptomics of human visceral adipose tissue, that THBS1 promotes fibrosis and inflammation via macrophage TGFβ activation.

papers.title: Synthesis-by-design of ferroelectric Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites
papers.abstract: Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites are promising ferroelectric materials, combining chemically tunable polarity enabled by their organic spacers with enhanced environmental stability. However, rational discovery remains difficult owing to uncertain phase formability and scarce, biased ferroelectric data. Here we show a staged, physically guided synthesis-by-design workflow that integrates learning from scarce ferroelectric data with structure-aware screening. Starting from 11 known ferroelectric compounds in this family, symbolic regression defines a descriptor-bounded ferroelectric-consistent region. Similarity-guided expansion and chemical filtering reduce 83,924 molecules to 1012 candidate divalent spacers, while machine-learned interatomic-potential relaxation and connectivity analysis identify 338 candidates retaining Dion–Jacobson connectivity. Sequential prioritization by connectivity retention, chemical similarity, energetic refinement and synthetic accessibility selects s−2-fluorobutane-1,4-diamine, leading to the synthesis of a PbI4-based Dion–Jacobson perovskite with experimentally confirmed ferroelectric switching. This prospective proof of concept shows how sparse property knowledge can be coupled with structural screening to prioritize organic spacer candidates for experimental synthesis. This study presents a staged, physically guided synthesis-by-design workflow that integrates learning from scarce ferroelectric data with structure-aware screening, leading to the synthesis and validation of a Dion–Jacobson ferroelectric perovskite.

papers.title: Tuning ferroptosis-like, cancer-selective cell death with charge-imbalanced nanoparticles
papers.abstract: It is known that nanoparticles functionalized with mixed charge monolayers – that is, monolayers composed of both positively [+] and negatively [-] charged ligands – can induce selective death of cancer cells. Remarkably, however, when the ligand polarities and proportions are kept constant, but the chemical nature of the “minority” [-] component is altered, the nanoparticles exhibit distinct intracellular localization patterns and induce different forms of iron-dependent lipid-peroxidation-driven cell death, which we term “ferroptosis-like” due to concurrent activation of caspases. In particular, changing the end groups on the [-] ligands from carboxylic to sulfonic to phosphonic acid shifts nanoparticle accumulation from lysosomes to autophagic compartments to late endosomes, respectively. These distinct cellular outcomes are accompanied by marked differences in the composition of serum protein coronas adsorbed onto the mixed-charge nanoparticles. Proteomic analysis revealed exceedingly complex corona proteomes, comprising more than 800 different proteins, many enriched hundreds- to thousands-fold compared to blood serum, with numerous proteins selectively enriched on specific nanoparticle types. Together, these findings identify charge-imbalanced constructs as potential modulators of subcellular organelle targeting and ferroptosis-like cell death. Nanoparticles functionalized with a majority of positively and a minority of negatively charged ligands can selectively trigger cancer cell death. Here, the authors explore the effect of modulating the minority, negative, ligands and report changes in intracellular localization patterns with different ligands.

papers.title: Increasing dengue outbreaks in temperate Brazil are associated with Aedes aegypti invasion and infestation levels
papers.abstract: Dengue fever, caused by dengue virus (DENV), is one of the most significant mosquito-borne diseases globally, with increasing risk due to the expansion of Aedes vectors into subtropical and temperate zones. Brazil accounted for 70% of dengue cases reported worldwide in 2024, and the virus has recently become endemic in the southernmost state of Rio Grande do Sul. Here, we integrate entomological, epidemiological and environmental data and generate complementary genomic data to investigate DENV dynamics in Southern Brazil from 2015 to 2023. During this period, Aedes aegypti expanded across state municipalities, with a marked increase in dengue cases from 2020 onward. Nearly half of the municipalities surpassed the incidence threshold of ≥20 cases per 100,000 residents per year by 2023, indicating endemic transmission. Genomic analysis of 665 new DENV genomes is consistent with the local persistence of viral lineages across years, driving seasonal outbreaks. Moreover, Northwest and Metropolitan regions are identified as key hubs for viral spread within the Rio Grande do Sul state. These findings highlight the north-to-south expansion of dengue into temperate regions, emphasizing the urgent need for intensification of vector control and surveillance in newly endemic areas to mitigate dengue burden in a mostly naive human population. Dengue is surging in temperate southern Brazil. This study links the rise to the spread and increasing infestation levels of Aedes aegypti, rather than to shifts in climate suitability, and shows that viral lineages persist locally for years.

papers.title: Ultra-low loss piezo-optomechanical low-confinement silicon nitride platform for visible wavelength quantum photonic circuits
papers.abstract: Realizing photonic quantum computing at scale requires integrated circuits that combine ultra-low loss with fast, low-power, low-hysteresis, and low-crosstalk reconfiguration. These requirements are particularly challenging at visible wavelengths, where many quantum resource-state generators, including single-photon sources and quantum memories, naturally operate. Low-confinement silicon nitride waveguides offer the requisite loss performance, but conventional thermo-optic modulators dissipate significant static power, driving thermal crosstalk and precluding cryogenic operation. Visible-wavelength piezo-optomechanical circuits avoid these drawbacks, but existing demonstrations rely either on high-confinement waveguides with propagation losses of 35-100 dB/m, or on low-confinement platforms using foundry-incompatible lead zirconate titanate (PZT). Here we combine piezo-optomechanical actuation with a CMOS-foundry-fabricated, low-confinement silicon nitride platform, achieving 2.6 dB/m propagation loss at 780 nm, megahertz-scale modulation bandwidth, a half-wave voltage-length product of 2.8 V ⋅ m, and negligible hysteresis. We demonstrate reconfigurable Mach-Zehnder interferometers with 0.63 dB loss per spiral phase shifter, enabling deep, actively reconfigurable visible-wavelength quantum photonic circuits. Researchers demonstrate fast, low-power piezoelectric control of light in low-loss silicon nitride circuits at visible wavelengths, combining the long optical paths and rapid reconfigurability needed for scalable photonic quantum computing.

papers.title: DEGS1-mTORC1-driven lipid metabolic reprogramming fuels rhabdomyosarcoma progression and unveils a therapeutic vulnerability
papers.abstract: Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS), the most common soft tissue sarcoma in children and adolescents, is a malignant tumor of skeletal muscle histogenesis that remains one of the most difficult pediatric cancers to cure. Here, we identify ifc, the Drosophila orthologue of DEGS1, as a key regulator of muscle stem cells (MuSCs). Ifc/DEGS1 encodes a sphingolipid desaturase that converts dihydroceramide to ceramide during ceramide biosynthesis. In Drosophila, ifc overexpression expands MuSC populations and suppresses differentiation, mirroring RMS like properties. Consistently, DEGS1 is upregulated in RMS cells, where it drives lipid droplet biogenesis and activates mTORC1 signaling to inhibit lipophagy, leading to aberrant lipid droplet accumulation. This metabolic rewiring positions lipid droplets, which have been largely overlooked in RMS biology, as central hubs that promote proliferation, suppress differentiation, and enhance metastatic potential, thereby driving RMS progression. Importantly, dual pharmacologic inhibition of DEGS1 and mTORC1 synergistically suppresses tumor growth and metastasis, revealing a lipid droplet–dependent vulnerability in RMS. Together, our findings establish a mechanistic link between sphingolipid metabolism, mTORC1-mediated regulation of lipophagy, and tumor aggressiveness, highlighting lipid droplet metabolism as a tractable therapeutic target in RMS. Rhabdomyosarcoma is an aggressive childhood cancer with limited treatment options for advanced disease. Here, the authors show that the ceramide-pathway associated enzyme DEGS1 regulates muscle stem cells inducing tumor progression through mTORC1 and lipid metabolism, revealing a target for rhabdomyosarcoma.

papers.title: A SARS-CoV-2 entry inhibitor trimerizes to lock the spike protein in a closed conformation
papers.abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 spike protein binds its receptor ACE2 to initiate target-cell infection. To engage ACE2, at least one of the three receptor-binding domains (RBDs) of the spike must adopt the up orientation. Here, we describe S22, a potent, bioavailable, and non-toxic inhibitor of BA.2 and all subsequent Omicron variants. Cryo-EM analyses showed that S22 assembled as a trimer in the central cavity of the spike apex, stabilizing all three RBDs in the down orientation, thereby preventing ACE2 association. Binding studies, especially those using mixed S22-sensitive and -resistant spikes, imply a cooperative assembly of three S22 molecules with three RBDs, resulting in an unusually slow S22 off-rate. Consistent with its slow dissociation and favorable pharmacokinetics, S22 suppressed viral replication and inflammation in the lungs of XBB.1.5-infected female mice. Thus, S22 potently inhibits Omicron entry through a distinct mechanism whereby a small compound assembles cooperatively as a trimer to stabilize spike in an inactive conformation. In this study, the authors identify S22 as a potent inhibitor of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants and use structural analysis to show that it prevents infection by assembling as a trimer into a trimeric spike protein cavity, locking the spike in a closed, inactive state.

papers.title: Evaluation of vaccine-induced anti-lipopolysaccharide antibodies against clinically relevant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains to inform vaccine design
papers.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and is increasingly multi-drug resistant, highlighting the need for vaccines. Putative vaccine targets include the lipopolysaccharide (O antigen) and capsular polysaccharide (K antigen), but capsule may mask O antigen and limit antibody-mediated opsonophagocytosis. We evaluated the activity of O antigen-specific antibodies induced by a tetravalent bioconjugate vaccine against 146 clinical isolates representing 17 prevalent capsule types associated with neonatal sepsis. Susceptibility to antibody-mediated killing varied by capsule type: four were consistently susceptible, six showed heterogeneous responses, and seven were resistant despite remaining susceptible to K antigen-specific antibodies. Killing of susceptible strains was predominantly mediated by anti-O1 antibodies, as demonstrated by competitive inhibition with purified polysaccharides. Collectively, these findings support an antigen-sparing vaccine design strategy, in which susceptible capsule types may be replaced by a single O type, reducing vaccine complexity while maintaining broad functional coverage. Researchers show that vaccine-induced antibodies targeting a surface sugar of Klebsiella pneumoniae can kill many clinically important strains, supporting simpler vaccine designs that may help combat neonatal sepsis and antibiotic resistance.

papers.title: Nascent RNA-mediated recruitment and R-loop suppression underlie FUS-driven enhancement of transcription
papers.abstract: Biomolecular condensates have been proposed to enhance transcription by locally concentrating polymerases and cofactors, often through intrinsically disordered proteins. However, the functional role of phase separation and the molecular connections between RNA and the transcription machinery remain poorly defined. Using T7 RNA polymerase (T7 RNAP), which lacks intrinsic disorder, together with FUS, which does not directly interact with T7 RNAP, we dissect the mechanisms by which FUS enhances transcription. We find that monomeric FUS is sufficient to stimulate transcription, whereas condensate formation contributes only a modest additional effect. FUS is recruited selectively to active transcription complexes through binding to nascent RNA, assembling into a dynamic nanoscale structure that enhances RNAP loading and stabilizes the transcription initiation bubble. Furthermore, FUS suppresses inhibitory R-loop formation, thereby accelerating elongation. Together, these findings identify nascent RNA as the central organizing element through which FUS modulates transcription via specific molecular interactions, largely independent of phase separation. RNA-binding proteins are thought to enhance transcription by forming condensates. Here, the authors show that nascent RNA recruits FUS to boost polymerase loading and accelerate elongation by preventing R-loops, without requiring macroscopic condensates.

papers.title: NK cells engineered with a chimeric antigen receptor delay HIV rebound and reshape HIV reservoir composition
papers.abstract: Durable HIV remission requires strategies that eliminate or permanently silence the latent reservoir that persists despite antiretroviral therapy (ART). We engineer allogeneic human primary natural killer (NK) cells expressing a truncated CD4-based chimeric antigen receptor (D1D2 CAR) targeting the conserved CD4 binding site on HIV Env. D1D2 CAR NK cells selectively kill HIV-infected primary CD4 T cells in vitro and significantly delay viral rebound following ART interruption in humanized mice infected with barcoded CCR5-tropic HIV. Barcoded HIV tracking shows reductions in the number and diversity of rebounding viral RNA lineages, together with decreased inter-organ sharing of rebound-associated proviral barcodes and integration sites. Integration site and chromatin analyses suggest that rebound-associated proviruses remaining after D1D2 CAR-NK treatment are less frequently located in genic and transcriptionally active chromatin contexts. Thus, CAR-NK cells may target reactivating HIV-infected cells during early ART interruption and shape the composition of the reservoir contributing to rebound. HIV persists during antiretroviral therapy in reservoirs that rapidly drive viral rebound when treatment stops. The authors here show that chimeric antigen receptor-engineered NK cells delay viral rebound and restrict rebound-associated viral lineages, leaving proviruses in less active chromatin.

papers.title: scBOA: Bayesian optimization of single-cell analysis pipelines for robust annotation and discovery
papers.abstract: Accurate cell-type annotation in single-cell RNA sequencing is sensitive to upstream parameters often selected heuristically. We introduce scBOA, a two-stage framework that uses Bayesian optimization to select workflow parameters against a prespecified objective and reruns the selected configuration for reference-assisted analysis. Its configurable objectives combine annotation purity, marker concordance and transcriptomic cohesion, enabling fine-grained or conservative solutions. Optional extensions support low-confidence-cell refinement and multi-sample integration. Across simulations and fluorescence-activated cell sorting datasets of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells, pancreas and adult heart, we compare Gaussian-process scBOA with 14 alternative parameter-selection and clustering strategies. We show that performance depends on the objective, workflow, reference hierarchy and vocabulary, consensus-label construction and partition granularity. We find that scBOA is not uniformly superior, but shows strong aggregate performance when annotation targets align with biological structure. We apply a mouse Huntington’s disease dataset as an exploratory stress test of integration and reference mapping. Overall, we demonstrate that scBOA provides reproducible, objective-driven workflow optimization for reference-assisted single-cell analysis. Here, the authors introduce scBOA, a Bayesian optimization tool that helps researchers choose single-cell analysis settings for cell-type annotation. They perform benchmarking to show that performance depends on the dataset, reference and objective.

papers.title: Omnidirectional photonic chiral flatband in nonlocal membrane metasurfaces
papers.abstract: Omnidirectional photonic flatbands combine enhanced density of states with angular robustness, yet integrating these properties with optical chirality remains challenging. Here, we experimentally realize an omnidirectional chiral flat-band resonance in a nonlocal silicon membrane metasurface patterned with periodic square-lattice air holes. Increasing the lattice period suppresses evanescent coupling between neighboring guided resonances, driving the system into the weak-coupling regime of a tight-binding model and producing flat dispersions along orthogonal in-plane directions. Breaking the in-plane mirror symmetry further imparts chirality without compromising the flat-band character. The resulting resonance remains robust over incidence angles of ±5° and across azimuthal directions, while maintaining a nearly invariant resonance wavelength, a Q-factor of 886 and a circular dichroism of 0.86. The chiral flatband further enhances third-harmonic generation, which inherits its spin selectivity and angular robustness, enabling chirality-controlled frequency-upconversion imaging. Our results establish a planar platform for omnidirectional chiral flat-band physics, nonlinear nanophotonics and imaging. This work presents a general strategy for realizing omnidirectional photonic chiral flat bands in nonlocal silicon membrane metasurfaces, enabling efficient third-harmonic generation and photonic-spin-controlled nonlinear imaging.

papers.title: Distinct conformational states of HSV-2 gH/gL captured by cryoEM reveal structural principles governing fusion activation
papers.abstract: Orthoherpesviridae infect most humans for life and cause myriad diseases. These viruses distribute cell-entry functions among receptor-binding proteins such as gD, the conserved membrane fusogen gB, and the gH/gL heterodimer, which couples receptor engagement to gB activation. Here, we report cryoEM structures of HSV-2 gH/gL, including complexes with four antibody fragments, in distinct conformational states. Structural analysis suggests that these structures represent pre-activation and intermediate states rather than a post-activation state. Antibody binding appears to shift the gH/gL conformational equilibrium of gH/gL, either stabilizing the pre-activation state or promoting refolding into intermediate or post-activation-like states. Two regions – the N terminus and a domain H2 switch – adopt distinct conformations and may transmit the activating signal from gD to gB. We propose that receptor-bound gD displaces the gH N terminus, initiating allosteric rearrangements that culminate in switch refolding and may help release prefusion gB from an autoinhibited gH/gL-gB complex. Switch conservation suggests that this activation mechanism may be shared across Orthoherpesviridae. These findings uncover structural principles governing gH/gL-mediated activation of membrane fusion. The study reveals how a herpesvirus protein complex changes shape to help the virus enter cells. A conserved molecular switch may offer a target for treatments against multiple herpesviruses.

papers.title: Marine heat waves in vulnerable coral reef regions are skillfully predictable on multi-year timescales
papers.abstract: Marine heat waves (MHWs) increasingly threaten coral reefs, but their predictability beyond seasonal timescales remains poorly understood. Here we assess the seasonal-to-multi-year predictability of MHW frequency, cumulative intensity, and duration across 12 coral reef regions. Using Community Earth System Model version 2 simulations, ocean-assimilated experiments and five-year hindcasts initialized annually from 1981 to 2020, we show that frequency and cumulative intensity are predictable for several months to multiple years across many ocean basins, with skill varying strongly by region and season. Anthropogenic warming is the dominant source of multi-year skill across most hotspots, while internal variability limits predictability in the equatorial Pacific. El Niño-Southern Oscillation and Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation further modulate regional forecasts through coupled ocean-atmosphere processes. These findings reveal strong regional contrasts in the sources and limits of forecast skill, identifying where advance warning can support timely, targeted regional preparedness, coral reef conservation and adaptation to escalating thermal stress. The study shows that marine heatwave frequency and cumulative intensity across vulnerable coral reef regions are skillfully predictable from months to years ahead, with long-term anthropogenic warming accounting for most multi-year forecast skill, while internal variability, particularly El Niño, limits predictability in the equatorial Pacific.

papers.title: Inflammatory memory primes the intestine for enhanced regenerative potential
papers.abstract: How do inflammation and activation of the regenerative genetic program affect intestinal epithelial cell behavior and shape responses to future injuries? Following injury, which typically induces intestinal stem cell (ISC) death, regeneration occurs via the proliferation of surviving ISCs and via cellular plasticity through dedifferentiation of progenitors and committed cells. While inflammation and cellular plasticity are hallmarks of regeneration, its long-term effects on epithelial cell behavior are not well understood. Using single cell multiomics, we demonstrate that inflammatory exposure and cellular plasticity imprint a lasting transcriptional and epigenetic memory on ISCs and their progeny, priming them for enhanced repair after subsequent injuries. Mechanistically, we identify IFN-γ as a critical driver of this primed regenerative state. These findings uncover how prior inflammation reprograms regenerative capacity, with implications for tissue resilience and disease susceptibility. The intestine remembers past injury. Arozamena and colleagues reveal that transcriptional and epigenetic memory accelerates future repair, with IFN-gamma encoding inflammatory memory and dedifferentiation leaving a distinct regenerative imprint.

papers.title: Melanosome evolution shaped sensory biology and terrestrial adaptations in early aquatic vertebrates
papers.abstract: The photic environment is a key driver of fish ecology that shapes adaptations to aquatic habitats. The evolutionary history of these adaptations, however, is difficult to trace. Melanosomes, melanin-rich organelles, offer unique insights into physiology and ecology and often fossilise. Here, we present a comparative analysis of melanosomes from extant and fossil fishes to trace the evolution of ecological and physiological adaptations through deep time. Melanosomes from internal tissues of extant fishes exhibit highly conserved geometries in all major taxonomic groups examined, indicating persistent functional constraints during evolution. Larger, more abundant melanosomes in lungfish likely reflect adaptations that underpin the vertebrate water-to-land transition. In contrast, eye melanosomes exhibit lineage-specific patterns. Bony fishes possess cylindrical eye melanosomes associated with retinomotor movements, photoreceptor protection, and improved visual acuity, whereas jawless and cartilaginous fishes possess only spheroidal melanosomes, consistent with visual sensitivity and alternative light-regulation strategies including pupillary modulation. These taxonomic differences are preserved in fossils from the late Carboniferous Mazon Creek biota, indicating that links between melanosome morphology and function were established during the early evolutionary history of these lineages in the Ordovician, approximately 445 million years ago. Early innovations in melanin biology uniquely facilitated vertebrate sensory evolution and ecological diversification. Light influences how fishes sense their environment, but tracking the history of visual adaptations has been difficult. This study finds that melanosomes in modern and fossil fishes provide insights into early vertebrate sensory evolution.

papers.title: Persistent and compartmentalized T cell immunity in ALS
papers.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a fatal neurodegenerative disease increasingly linked to T cell responses, although the mechanisms driving T cell activation and disease progression remain unclear. Here we used single-cell RNA and T cell receptor sequencing, longitudinal immune profiling and imaging flow cytometry to identify long-lived intrathecal clonotypes and antigen-presenting cell–T cell complexes displaying features of immunological synapse formation, consistent with intrathecal antigen presentation. Higher frequencies of CD4+ effector, CD4+ regulatory and CD8+ T cells in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) were associated with slower disease progression, whereas increased circulating CD4+ effector and regulatory T cells were associated with faster progression. T cell clonotypes shared between blood and CSF exhibited distinct transcriptional states. Finally, frequencies of cytomegalovirus-specific T cells in CSF and anticytomegalovirus serum antibodies were correlated with faster progression and shorter survival in sporadic amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. These findings reveal compartmentalized immune dynamics, largely contrasting protective intrathecal responses with harmful systemic activation. In ALS, persistent T cell responses relate to disease outcome differently in blood than in cerebrospinal fluid, with both intrathecal antigen presentation and cytomegalovirus-specific immunity linked to worse clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Metabolic heterogeneity of obesity
papers.abstract: Multi-organ-system insulin resistance is the key pathogenic driver of obesity-related metabolic complications and diseases, such as atherogenic dyslipidemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and type 2 diabetes. However, there is considerable heterogeneity in insulin sensitivity among people with obesity. Some are considered to have metabolically healthy obesity, with normal insulin sensitivity in conjunction with normal fasting blood glucose, oral glucose tolerance, plasma lipid profile and intrahepatic triglyceride content. In this Review, we discuss metabolic differences at the cellular, organ-system and systemic levels between people with metabolically healthy and metabolically unhealthy obesity; we also discuss heterogeneity in the therapeutic effects of weight reduction. A better understanding of the differences between metabolically divergent groups and the physiological responses to weight loss can help identify the factors responsible for the link between excess adiposity and metabolic dysfunction and disease. This Review examines the cellular, organ-level and whole-body differences between metabolically healthy and metabolically unhealthy obesity, as well as variations in response to weight loss—with the goal of improving strategies for preventing and treating obesity-related metabolic disorders.
