A three-dimensional human co-culture system reveals reciprocal embryo–endometrial adaptation at implantation onset
papers.abstract: Human embryo implantation begins with dynamic, tightly coordinated interactions between embryonic and endometrial compartments, yet the earliest trophoblast–endometrial interface dynamics remain poorly resolved in vivo. Here, using an endometrial assembloid-based three-dimensional co-culture system with human blastoids and natural blastocysts, we analyse implantation-like progression by time-series single-cell transcriptomics and functional perturbation. Importantly, we identify co-culture-induced trophoblast subsets marked by SDC1+MMP7+ and enriched for transcriptional features associated with extracellular matrix remodelling and cell migration. These subsets are reproducibly detected across independent implantation-like systems, emerge specifically within a decidualized stromal co-culture context, and are further linked to stromal-derived CSF3 signalling by intercellular communication analysis and targeted perturbation. In parallel, the endometrium displays transcriptional changes associated with enhanced decidualization and a glandular hypersecretory transition. Together, our study provides a tractable framework for dissecting reciprocal embryo–endometrial adaptation at the onset of implantation. Bi, Tu, Zhang, Hu, Chen and colleagues co-culture human blastoids or blastocysts with endometrial assembloids to study cellular and transcriptional adaptations of embryonic and endometrial compartments during the implantation-like process.

papers.title: Cartilage-binding coacervate with therapeutic payload delivery and biomimetic lubrication alleviates osteoarthritis by reducing joint friction and inflammation
papers.abstract: Healthy articular cartilage maintains ultralow friction through the lipid/hyaluronic acid/lubricin complex lubrication layer, in which the zwitterionic lipids mediate lubrication and the hyaluronic acid and lubricin anchor to cartilage matrix. However, in osteoarthritis this lubrication system is progressively degraded, leading to increased cartilage wear and joint dysfunction. Therefore, early and lubrication-based intervention is urgently needed. Here we present biomimetic polyzwitterionic coacervates (pZCOs) that recapitulate both the lubrication and cartilage-binding functionalities of the natural boundary lubrication layer. pZCOs exhibit strong binding affinity to fibronectin, establish a stable and ultralow-friction lubrication layer on the cartilage surface, facilitate the sustained release of anti-inflammatory drugs, and preserve the viability and anti-inflammatory paracrine secretion of encapsulated mesenchymal stem cells. In both rat and mini-pig models of osteoarthritis, intra-articular administration of drug/MSC-laden pZCOs effectively reduces cartilage degradation, suppresses inflammation and promotes cartilage integrity, outperforming clinical hyaluronic acid lubricants in lubrication performance, in vivo retention and therapeutic efficacy. These findings highlight the translational potential of engineered biomimetic coacervates as next-generation joint lubricants for integrated management of osteoarthritis. Polyzwitterionic coacervates with therapeutic payload delivery, mimicking physiological lubrication and cartilage-binding functionalities, reduce joint friction and inflammation in rat and mini-pig osteoarthritis models.

Integrative biophysical illumination of the 3D GPCRome dynamics
papers.abstract: Insights into the dynamics of G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) remain limited. Here we present an integrative strategy that bridges computational and experimental biophysical methods for probing protein dynamics. To illustrate its potential, we developed GPCRmd-NMR, a platform that synergistically combines molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with high-resolution nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy across the three-dimensional GPCRome. The resulting dataset enables structure-resolved analysis by applying the strategy across multiple GPCRs. We provide access to underexplored functional GPCR dynamics, receptor states and sites, including microswitches, hidden ligand entrance gateways and intrinsically disordered regions. Our integrated framework offers a solution to challenges faced by both experimental and computational researchers including the MD–NMR timescale gap. Medel-Lacruz et al. introduce GPCRmd-NMR, an open platform that links molecular simulations with nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy to uncover hidden conformational dynamics across G-protein-coupled receptors, improving the interpretation of experimental NMR data.

papers.title: Crystalline neutral and cationic oxoboranes
papers.abstract: The isolation of oxoboranes (RB≡O) featuring a genuine B–O triple bond has remained an outstanding challenge owing to the electron deficiency of boron and the intrinsic instability of the B≡O linkage. So far, direct evidence for such species has been largely limited to gas-phase and matrix-isolation studies and only recently inferred in solution. Here we report the isolation of a stable, free oxoborane generated via a carbon-monoxide-triggered transformation of a heterocumulene. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction establishes a terminal B≡O unit, while electronic structure analyses reveal two orthogonal π bonds consistent with a highly polarized triple bond. Mechanistic studies support a carbon monoxide coordination–insertion–isomerization pathway. The resulting oxoborane exhibits ambiphilic reactivity, enabling access to both neutral and cationic derivatives. These findings establish free oxoboranes as isolable species under condensed-phase conditions and provide a platform for exploring low-coordinate boron–oxygen multiple bonds. The isolation of oxoboranes featuring a genuine B–O triple bond is challenging owing to the instability of the B≡O linkage. Now stable crystalline oxoboranes have been prepared through a carbon-monoxide-triggered transformation, revealing a highly polarized B–O triple bond and enabling access to both neutral and cationic derivatives through ambiphilic reactivity.

papers.title: Synthesis and isolation of stable oxoboranes
papers.abstract: Oxoboranes, molecules bearing a triple bond between a dicoordinate boron atom and a monocoordinate oxygen atom, are some of the longest-sought reactive main-group species. Their syntheses have been the subject of a series of documented attempts dating back to at least the early 1960s, leading to gas-phase/matrix isolation and evidence of chemical trapping, as well as isolation of oxoborane derivatives with reduced B–O bond orders. However, their detection or isolation of base-/acid-free oxoboranes in the condensed phase remains challenging. Here we present a remarkably simple synthesis of three oxoboranes that are stable as crystalline solids at room temperature. These species feature exceptionally short (1.208(4)–1.217(4) Å) and strong B–O bonds. Their properties are elucidated by both experimental and computational methods, and an explanation for their unusual stability is provided. Oxoboranes are among the longest-sought species in main-group chemistry. Now, stable crystalline oxoboranes with exceptionally short and strong B–O bonds have been prepared through the reaction of a diboracumulene with carbonyl-bearing compounds.

Association of fetal activity patterns in utero with postnatal sleep behavior
papers.abstract: The human circadian clock, a key mechanism governing the sleep-wake cycle, starts oscillating before birth. Distinct fetal behavioral states have been described using short-duration ultrasound recordings, but the alignment of fetal activity with day and night cycles (i.e., diurnal rhythms) remains poorly understood due to the lack of long-term monitoring. This study characterizes fetal diurnal activity patterns using continuous third-trimester monitoring over at least five days across 32 mother-child pairs, yielding over 20,000 combined sensor-hours of maternal (acceleration and temperature) and fetal (acceleration) wearable data. We tracked diurnal pattern development from in utero to 6 months of age, assessing infant sleep at three postnatal time points (first weeks, 3 months, and 6 months) with sleep diaries and questionnaires. Multi-level modeling revealed early diurnal rhythms in fetuses that align with maternal activity and circadian rhythms. Random Forest analyses identified fetal day/night sleep duration ratio – a simplified proxy for fetal circadian entrainment – as the strongest predictor of postnatal infant sleep, with fetuses preferring nighttime sleep maintaining this preference postnatally. Maternal sleep regularity (i.e., consistent sleep patterns characterized by low day-to-day variability in sleep timing) during pregnancy also predicted infant sleep, being associated with a stronger preference for nighttime sleep in infants. These findings highlight the potential influence of intrauterine and maternal factors on early circadian entrainment and highlight maternal sleep as an actionable target to improve infant sleep and family well-being. A limitation of this study is the relatively small cohort size and, consequently, the findings should be interpreted with caution until they are replicated in larger, independent cohorts. Here the authors used long-term monitoring of 32 mother-child pairs to report that fetal day-night activity rhythms align with maternal circadian patterns, and that fetal sleep timing associates maternal sleep regularity and post-natal infant sleep patterns. These findings suggest that individual differences in sleep and circadian behavior may emerge before birth, although confirmation in larger cohorts is needed.

MoS2-based composites with magnetoelectric synergistic loss for enhanced microwave absorption
papers.abstract: The development of high-performance electromagnetic wave absorbing materials is crucial for addressing electromagnetic interference issues. However, a single loss mechanism often results in unsatisfactory microwave absorption performance. In this study, we report a MoS2-based composite material with a magnetoelectric synergistic effect. The hierarchical heterogeneous structure and the synergistic loss of magnetic/electric components enable excellent impedance matching and multiple energy conversions, enhancing the absorption and loss capabilities. The designed microwave absorber achieves an effective absorption bandwidth of 4.36 GHz at a thickness of 1.9 mm. The minimum reflection loss is −58.92 dB. Furthermore, the absorber exhibits a radar cross-section reduction value of up to 28.273 dB·m² in the vertical direction. Additionally, the EAB can be further broadened across the entire 2-18 GHz frequency range through the rational design of gradient metamaterials. This work provides a reference for the subsequent development and application of MoS2-based composites with high-efficiency electromagnetic wave absorption properties. This study reports a MoS2-based composite with a hierarchical heterogeneous structure, with synergistic loss of magnetic/electric components enabling impedance matching and multiple energy conversions, enhancing the absorption and loss capabilities.

papers.title: Smooth muscle DDIT4 exacerbates vascular remodeling in atherosclerosis and vascular injury by impairing PDC activity
papers.abstract: Restenosis and atherosclerosis remain therapeutic challenges. Vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic switching is a central driver. DNA damage inducible transcript 4 (DDIT4) is implicated in vascular disease, but its role in restenosis and atherosclerosis is unknown. Here we show that DDIT4 is markedly increased in PDGF-BB- or IL-1β-stimulated dedifferentiated VSMCs and reduced in differentiated VSMCs. DDIT4 is upregulated in VSMCs within neointima and atherosclerotic lesions of mice and humans, correlating with disease progression. DDIT4 overexpression promotes VSMC proliferation and phenotypic switching, whereas knockdown suppresses these effects. AAV9-mediated Ddit4 overexpression exacerbates neointimal hyperplasia in atherosclerosis and vascular injury models, while VSMC-specific Ddit4 deletion attenuates it. DDIT4 binds the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, destabilizing subunit interactions and impairing activity. Resulting acetyl-CoA decline reduces histone acetylation, especially at contractile gene promoters, diminishing H3K9/H3K27 acetylation and chromatin accessibility, thereby repressing contractile genes. Targeting DDIT4 is a promising therapeutic strategy for restenosis and atherosclerosis. Vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching drives atherosclerosis and restenosis, but key regulators remain unclear. Here, the authors show DDIT4 promotes this switch via pyruvate dehydrogenase complex inhibition, reducing acetyl-CoA and histone acetylation, repressing contractile genes.

papers.title: Building materials and emissions from rebuilding under increasing climate-driven flood hazards
papers.abstract: Floods threaten lives and infrastructure, while recovery and reconstruction require materials whose production generates greenhouse gas emissions. These material needs and emissions remain insufficiently quantified. Here we assess the impacts of riverine and coastal flooding on building materials across Europe under climate change and land subsidence. Baseline annual replacement demand is about 30 million tonnes of materials, generating about 9 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions. With flood protection maintained but not upgraded, both could increase more than tenfold by 2080 under a moderate emissions scenario, driven by coastal flooding. Impacts could be about 22% higher under a high emissions scenario. Cumulative replacement emissions over 2024–2080 under the moderate scenario could reach 4.0 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, exceeding ten times Europe’s annual building material production emissions in 2020. Increasing both mitigation and adaptation efforts is essential to reduce material losses, further emissions and human suffering. This study shows that expected annual replacement material demand and rebuilding emissions from floods across Europe could rise more than tenfold by 2080, highlighting the need for flood adaptation and climate mitigation.

papers.title: Transient efferocytosis-induced activation of IKKβ reprograms macrophages to promote tissue resolution in mice
papers.abstract: The clearance of apoptotic cells by macrophages, termed efferocytosis, activates multiple pro-resolving pathways, but whether there is a common upstream regulator remains unknown. Here, we report that in efferocytosing macrophages, MerTK activation by apoptotic cells rapidly and transiently activates an IKKβ-NFκB/-p38 pathway, which then promotes interleukin-10 (IL-10) production, continuing efferocytosis, and regulatory T cell expansion. The IKKβ and downstream resolution pathways are linked through the transcription factor Myc, the epigenetic modifier ten-eleven translocation-2 (TET2), and the immune checkpoint protein programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1). Deletion of macrophage IKKβ in male mice blocks the above resolution pathways and compromises efferocytosis-mediated tissue repair in a model of thymic injury and in atherosclerosis regression. Thus, our findings illustrate the existence of a unifying upstream signal for efferocytosis-induced resolution, which could suggest therapeutic strategies to enhance multiple tissue resolution pathways and to optimize anti-inflammatory therapies by avoiding blocking IKKβ-NFκB/p38-mediated resolution. The clearance of apoptotic cells, or efferocytosis, reprograms macrophages towards a pro-resolving phenotype to facilitate tissue repair. Here, the authors identify IKKβ as an upstream regulator of immunoregulatory and reparative processes, showing that MerTK activation by apoptotic cells transiently activates an IKKβ-dependent NFKB/p38 axis, inducing IL-10 production, Rac1-mediated continuing efferocytosis, and activation of a Myc–TET2–PD-L1 pathway that promotes regulatory T cell expansion.

papers.title: Declining spring production in the Barents Sea ice zone under climate forcing
papers.abstract: Under anthropogenic forcing, Barents Sea greening and increased annual production are well-documented, yet seasonal differences in production trends are less clear. Here, using satellite ocean color data, we report a 45% decline in spring (April-May) primary production in the nitrate-limited Barents Sea ice zone between 1998 and 2023, corresponding to a reduction of 90.43 mg C m−2 day−1 per decade (p < 0.05). This decline is driven by reduced spring nitrate availability, resulting from slower winter nitrate replenishment rates, increased upstream consumption, and net nitrate export linked to Atlantification. Moreover, a North Atlantic-Arctic atmospheric wave train and reduced freshwater input have deepened the mixed layer, lowering light availability and further limiting production. These findings indicate that continued warming will likely suppress spring production in the Barents Sea ice zone, triggering nutrient-driven cascading effects on Arctic food webs and biodiversity. Barents Sea spring primary production has markedly declined over recent decades, driven by reduced nutrient and light availability, with potential implications for the stability of Arctic food webs and biodiversity.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of end-to-end learning and foundation models for clinical-grade prostate pathology
papers.abstract: Foundation models (FMs) using self-supervised pre-training are widely advocated as a universal solution for pathology, yet their advantages over task-specific (TS) models remain unclear. Here we show, using over 100,000 prostate biopsies from 6268 patients across 15 sites, that while FMs demonstrate utility in data-scarce scenarios, their performance converges with—and is in some cases surpassed by—TS models with sufficient labeled training data. Concordance with pathologists’ grading reaches quadratic Cohen’s kappas of 0.91 (95% CI 0.90-0.92; all models) on internal and 0.87 (0.86-0.88; TS), 0.86 (0.84-0.87; UNI FM) and 0.85 (0.84-0.86; Virchow2 FM) on external cohorts at full training. Task-specific training markedly reduces misgrading, misdiagnosis of challenging morphologies, and technical variability. Notably, FMs consume up to 35 times more energy. We advocate for considering both FMs and end-to-end learning for robust, resource-efficient, and clinically applicable AI pathology. The clinical applicability and generalizability of foundation models (FM) that use self-supervised pre-training in comparison to task- specific (TS) models that utilize end-to-end learning remains to be elucidated. Here, the authors show that while FMs demonstrate better utility in data-scarce scenarios, they still require considerable task-specific training to match TS diagnostic and grading performance and consume more energy than smaller TS models.

papers.title: Overcoming circularity bias reveals a hidden linear DNA and RNA virosphere
papers.abstract: Metagenomic sequencing has transformed our view of the global viral diversity, yet a fundamental bias limits our understanding of the diversity of complete viral genomes. Current quality assessment tools rely on identifying circular contigs, systematically underestimating the completeness of linear DNA and RNA viruses, thus leaving a large fraction of the virosphere uncharacterized. Here, we overcome this bias, by leveraging within-species genomic termini conservation across diverse metagenomic datasets. Applying this approach to the metaVR database, we recover and validate 1,585 conserved, complete linear viral genomes, representing a 21-fold increase in recognized linear completeness. Our results reveal previously uncovered complete monopartite RNA genomes and individual segments of multipartite viruses across 13 classes, alongside deeply branching viral dark matter. Furthermore, we expand the known physical boundaries of linear DNA viruses, by recovering intact megaphages up to 220 kb and distinguishing true complete genomes from highly transcribed operons. Ecological profiling reveals a strong enrichment of these reassigned as complete linear viruses in specific ecosystems, highlighting their ecological relevance. By enabling systematic recovery of complete linear genomes, this framework unlocks a previously hidden fraction of the virosphere and reshapes our understanding of viral diversity and evolution. Metagenomic tools underestimate linear viral genome completeness due to circularity bias. In this study, the authors track within-species genomic termini conservation across metagenomic datasets to recover and validate 1,585 complete linear viral genomes, revealing a 21-fold expansion of hidden RNA and DNA viruses.

papers.title: Dynamically adaptive soft bioelectronics for neuro-immunomodulatory cancer therapy
papers.abstract: Many solid tumors remain refractory to immunotherapy due to profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. Although vagus nerve stimulation offers a direct neural axis to reprogram immune function, its potential in cancer immunotherapy remains unrealized due to the absence of stable, system-level neuromodulation platforms. Herein, we develop a miniature subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve stimulator (SVNS) for near-organ neuromodulation of pancreatic tumor immunity. To construct stable electrical coupling with subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve (SVN) along the esophagus, a dynamically adaptive neural interface comprising an injectable anti-fatigue adhesive conductive hydrogel and a deformable liquid metal electrode is explored. The SVNS is integrated with a battery-free lead-free wireless power module, which can be configured into a Swiss-roll architecture, enabling minimally invasive implantation. In an orthotopic mouse model of pancreatic tumor, chronic SVN stimulation using SVNS suppressed tumor growth and metastasis, reshaped tumor innervation, promoted a shift toward an M1-like TAM phenotype, enhanced cytotoxic immune cell infiltration, and further potentiated the efficacy of anti-PD-1 immunotherapy. Many solid tumors remain refractory to immunotherapy. Vagus nerve stimulation can enhance the immunotherapeutic effect: here, the authors develop a subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve stimulator for near-organ neuromodulation of pancreatic tumor immunity.

In vivo genome-editing therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Preclinical studies and first-in-human trial
papers.abstract: A single-dose AAV-CRISPR therapy restores dystrophin in humanized DMD mice and achieves durable editing with manageable safety in non-human primates. In a first-in-human DMD trial, the therapy yields molecular evidence of muscle editing but reveals a fatal dose-dependent immune complication, highlighting the urgent need to expand the safety margin of systemic AAV-CRISPR treatments.

papers.title: A microbiome-reactive TMIGD2hi Th17 subset is spatially enriched at the intestinal epithelium and expanded in inflammatory bowel disease
papers.abstract: Our understanding of how commensal-specific CD4+ T cells respond to intestinal inflammation is limited. Pedersen et al. define the phenotypic diversity of human CD4+ T cells recognizing a defined Bacteroidales epitope across disease settings. This revealed a TMIGD2hi Th17 phenotype that expands in inflamed tissue. More broadly, this work underscores the malleability of microbiota-specific T cells during inflammatory bowel disease.

papers.title: Human brain cellular xenografts in neuroimmunology and beyond
papers.abstract: Human brain cellular xenograft (HBCX) models are emerging as a system to study human brain physiology and pathology in vivo. Mancuso and colleagues discuss how HBCXs enable in vivo interrogation of human-specific brain cell biology, neuroimmunology, disease modeling, and genetic risk and their potential for functional genomics, therapeutic discovery, and preclinical assessment of cell-based therapies for central nervous system disorders.

papers.title: Finding MES: A hidden cell state in neuroblastoma
Small genomes, big lessons: What viruses teach us about structure-based riboregulation
papers.abstract: Viral RNA genomes fold into networks of compact structures, so their RNA sequences do more than carry genetic code. Hann et al. review how viral RNA structures control viral gene expression, replication, and immune evasion, revealing viruses as simple model systems for regulatory principles that also shape human gene expression.

papers.title: Amyloid-mediated RNA uptake by sperm for embryonic delivery
papers.abstract: Semen carries extracellular RNA that shapes early embryonic development, but how it reaches sperm is unclear. Mallen et al. show that amyloid fibrils in seminal fluid bind RNA, enter sperm, and deliver their cargo to the zygote at fertilization, where chaperones release it for translation.

papers.title: The 9-1-1 complex protects ssDNA gaps in BRCA2-deficient cancer
papers.abstract: Grimsley et al. demonstrate that the 9-1-1 complex safeguards BRCA2-deficient cells from lethal ssDNA gap accumulation by suppressing PRIMPOL-dependent gap formation, restraining EXO1 degradation, and promoting POLζ-mediated filling. This identifies an ATR-independent 9-1-1 role in post-replicative repair and establishes gap length as a key determinant of repair pathway choice.

papers.title: RAStoERK: A reference interaction atlas for insights into signaling and disease
papers.abstract: Vucak et al. report a high-resolution interactome map of the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK pathway in resting and active states, revealing state-, paralog-, and mutation-specific wiring and extensive crosstalk with core signaling and functional modules. The resource comprises 2,500 previously unreported interactors and will facilitate fundamental discovery and therapeutic exploration.

papers.title: Mechanisms of vesicular monoamine transporter 2 modulation by amphetamines and lobeline
papers.abstract: Wu et al. revealed how human VMAT2 recognizes amphetamine-type stimulants (ATSs) and the inhibitor lobeline through distinct binding modes. The study elucidates the structural basis of ATS-elicited monoamine redistribution and dual-site VMAT2 inhibition, expanding the comprehension of addiction pharmacology.

papers.title: Embryonic reprogramming drives anaplastic transformation in thyroid carcinoma
papers.abstract: Embryonic reprogramming drives anaplastic transformation in thyroid cancer. Using human samples and in vivo reprogrammable mouse models, Kawaura et al. show that reprogramming can induce anaplastic features in Braf-mutant thyroid epithelium without Trp53 mutation, while NKX2-1 re-expression promotes partial re-differentiation of ATC cells.

papers.title: SIR2-mediated filament assembly activates the NLR-like protein Avs5 for bacterial antiviral defense
papers.abstract: Wang et al. define a stepwise activation mechanism for the bacterial NLR-like protein Avs5. Cryo-EM structures capture monomeric, dimeric, and filamentous states, and reveal that SIR2-driven filament assembly couples NACHT remodeling and ATP hydrolysis to NAD+ hydrolysis and antiphage defense.

papers.title: Role of Leu and Val synthesis in sensing mitochondrial nutrient and energy availability
papers.abstract: Phan and colleagues found that Leu and Val synthesis links mitochondrial metabolic activity to nutrient sensing in yeast. Changes in Leu and Val regulate TORC1 and Gcn2, respectively, altering translation and transcription factor abundance. This mechanism allows mitochondrial anabolic capacity to shape cellular metabolism.

papers.title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals archetypal regulatory programs shared across T cell subsets
papers.abstract: Walker et al. integrate single-cell multi-omics with a chromatin accessibility atlas to decode the modular regulatory architecture of T cell responses to viral infection. Using archetypal analysis, they show that progenitor CD8 T cells have a composite identity, combining regulatory programs of CD8 exhaustion and CD4 follicular helper T cells.

papers.title: CCN1-mediated stress signaling underlies intrinsic cardiomyocyte dysfunction in spinal muscular atrophy
papers.abstract: Zeng et al. use patients with type 1 SMA disease-specific iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes and engineered heart tissues to uncover CCN1-associated p38/MAPK stress signaling as a contributor to SMA cardiac dysfunction. Tanshinone IIA suppresses CCN1-p38 signaling and, when combined with risdiplam, additively improves mitochondrial and contractile function.

papers.title: Early mitophagy defects and impaired mitochondrial energy metabolism drive target organ damage progression: Lessons from the Fabry heart
papers.abstract: Fabry disease has long been viewed as a lysosomal disorder. Gambardella et al. show that early mitochondrial dysfunction actively drives disease progression by disrupting mito-lysosomal homeostasis and cardiac energetics. Targeting mitochondrial dysfunction prevents cardiac manifestations, identifying mitochondrial homeostasis as a promising therapeutic strategy for Fabry disease.

papers.title: Heterogeneous contributions of APOBEC3 deaminases to substitution and indel mutagenesis in lung adenocarcinoma
papers.abstract: Striepen et al. combine CRISPR knockouts and lineage-resolved whole-genome sequencing to define heterogeneous contributions of APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B to lung adenocarcinoma mutagenesis. Common surrogate assays fail to predict these contributions, and endogenous APOBEC3A generates the indel signature InD9a.

papers.title: The compositional encoding of hand-eye coordinated movements for single neurons in the posterior parietal cortex
papers.abstract: Some brain regions are theorized to represent complex behaviors through compositions of simpler neural building blocks. Mynhier et al. provide an example, showing that hand and eye movements are compositionally encoded in human posterior parietal cortex, providing a framework for modular neural decoding.

papers.title: Mesothelin-induced lysosomal biogenesis sustains neutrophil longevity to drive brain metastasis
papers.abstract: Chen et al. show that sMSLN shed from BrM cells specifically engages neutrophil TLR4 to activate JAK2-STAT3, thereby enhancing lysosomal biogenesis and function, which curbs ROS accumulation and sustains neutrophil longevity. Blockade of MSLN reduces TAN enrichment, and concurrent TLR4 inhibition synergistically suppresses lung cancer BrM.

UBT251, a novel triple GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptor agonist, in adults with type 2 diabetes: A multicenter, randomized phase 2 trial
papers.abstract: Zhou et al. report a phase 2 trial of UBT251, a novel triple GLP-1/GIP/GCG receptor agonist, in adults with type 2 diabetes. At week 24, once-weekly UBT251 reduced HbA1c by up to 2.16% and body weight by up to 9.8% and was generally well tolerated, supporting further phase 3 evaluation.

papers.title: Shared α-helix chimeraffibodies enable linker-free bispecific protein design
papers.abstract: Bispecific proteins often rely on flexible linkers that increase conformational heterogeneity. Qiu et al. present AlphaSync, a geometry-guided framework that integrates α-helical binders through helix sharing. The resulting Chimeraffibody retains HER2-albumin co-recognition while improving pharmacokinetics, tumor localization, and predicted immunogenicity liability.

papers.title: Tumor digital twins uncover therapeutic strategies in triple-negative breast cancer
papers.abstract: Victori et al. present a mechanistic computational model of triple-negative breast cancer that integrates prior biological knowledge with patient data from the PARTNER clinical trial. These personalized tumor digital twins recapitulate treatment responses, identify mutational and transcriptomic response biomarkers, and recommend targeted therapies, highlighting their potential to support precision oncology.

papers.title: Single-cell tumour phylogenetics
papers.abstract: Single-cell genomics has entered the field of cancer research and clinical oncology, enhancing our understanding of the somatic evolution of cancer and intra-tumour genomic heterogeneity. The evolutionary history of a tumour can be represented as a phylogenetic tree, and in recent years, multiple statistical and computational methods have been proposed to reconstruct tumour phylogenies from single-cell sequencing data. The nature of tumour evolution and of single-cell sequencing, however, raises new challenges in modelling the data and the underlying evolutionary processes that are not addressed by classical phylogenetic and phylodynamic approaches. Here, we review the models and assumptions behind bespoke single-cell tumour phylogeny methods, along with recent computational and algorithmic advances in phylogenetic inference. We discuss the role these advances have in basic and clinical oncology research, and how they provide new insights into individual cancers and cohorts of patient samples. We conclude with an outlook of current challenges for single-cell phylogenetics and potential future applications. Single-cell sequencing has transformed the study of tumour evolution by enabling high-resolution reconstruction of cancer phylogenies. This Review discusses the models, assumptions and computational approaches underlying single-cell tumour phylogeny inference, and it highlights emerging applications in cancer biology, patient stratification and evolutionary forecasting.

Trace H2O2-triggered Fenton-like reaction by secondary coordination sphere in iron-based metal-organic frameworks
papers.abstract: Minimizing H2O2 consumption for efficient water decontamination is a crucial objective of Fenton-like reaction. However, the limited H2O2 activation and hydroxyl radicals (·OH) utilization efficiency are still two obstacles, mainly caused by high O-O bond energy barrier and short-lived free·OH generation. Here, we show an iron-based metal-organic frameworks with pyridine N secondary coordination sphere, i.e., N/MIL-53(Fe), whereas secondary coordination sphere has a strong interaction with the key *OH intermediates, thereby decreasing O-O homolytic cleavage barrier and promoting in-situ generation of long-lived adsorbed ·OH. Therefore, N/MIL-53(Fe) exhibits a H2O2 conversion efficiency up to about 90%, with adsorbed ·OH accounting for over 90% of the total. Meanwhile, N/MIL-53(Fe) achieves high activity for bisphenol A, tetracycline, phenol, p-chlorophenol and ciprofloxacin degradation (98% within 5 min) under trace H2O2 (0.5 mM), with H2O2 consumption equivalent to only 3% ~ 10% of reported Fenton-like catalyst. This study provides an efficient pathway for low-consumption water decontamination. Fenton-like water treatment is limited by inefficient hydrogen peroxide activation and short-lived reactive radicals. Adding nearby nitrogen sites to iron metal-organic frameworks boosts peroxide use and traps radicals, enabling rapid pollutant removal.

papers.title: Ureterovesical junction: a stem cell niche for ureteral urothelial renewal and bladder urothelial injury repair
papers.abstract: Epithelial stem cells are essential for lineage specification, tissue renewal, and regeneration. Here we show that ureterovesical junction (UVJ) of urinary tract harbors a major cluster of label-retaining urothelial cells that exhibit organoid-forming activities. During lineage-tracing, these Foxa2-expressing UVJ urothelial cells renew ureteral urothelium, but do not migrate into the bladder during homeostasis or mild bladder injury. Upon mechanical and chemical denudation of bladder urothelium, UVJ cells migrate rapidly into the bladder to replace bladder urothelium. This reepithelization also occurs during combination chemotherapies and severe bladder infection. Common to these injury repair processes is the early-phase and selective phosphorylation of TRKA and AKT which drives urothelial proliferation and differentiation. Nascent bladder urothelial cells derived from UVJ express both UVJ and bladder urothelial markers, signifying active remodeling influenced by intrinsic and extrinsic factors. Modulating the activities of UVJ cells may enhance bladder urothelial regeneration and combat challenging bladder diseases. The authors identified a major cluster of urothelial stem cells at the ureter-bladder junction. These cells efficiently formed colonies and organoids, and they renew ureteral urothelium and repair severe bladder urothelial injuries.

papers.title: Neural limits of temporal feature binding in human visual cortex
papers.abstract: Humans are able to track the change of color and orientation (CO) of an object at a stunning rate. However, spatially separating those features slows this rate by an order of magnitude – a temporal limit of feature binding that is little understood. Here, we investigate the underlying mechanisms using high-temporal resolution cortical source localization of the magnetic field response elicited by CO-pairs alternating at different frequencies in color and orientation. We show that (1) binding requires a rapid recurrent modulation (~120 ms) of activity in V1/V2, whose latency is independent of the alternation rate. (2) Performance drops to chance when the alternation rate becomes too high to accommodate the recurrent process within a single alternation. (3) CO binding itself is mediated by color-based attention, which gradually biases re-occurring CO combinations containing the attended color. These observations together demonstrate that CO-binding across space depends on rapid recurrent processing in early visual cortex, with its temporal limit being set by the time this process takes to be completed. Binding ultimately results from a slower and gradual attentional bias of the recurrent process instantiating a form of stroboscopic stationarity in the stream of alternations for unambiguous discrimination of the correct feature-combination. The speed of binding color and orientation in an alternating stream is limited by the duration of a recurrent process in visual cortex. Binding is accomplished by a gradual attentional bias of this process, causing a form of stroboscopic stationarity.

papers.title: Platelet-engineered AAV silencing of myocardial CD36 reprograms fatty acid metabolism to promote cardiac regeneration in male mice
papers.abstract: The adult heart has limited regenerative capacity after ischemic injury, and abnormal fatty acid metabolism contributes to this failure of repair. Strategies that reduce fatty acid oxidation can promote cardiomyocyte proliferation, but excessive suppression may disrupt lipid handling and worsen injury. Here we show that a platelet-engineered adeno-associated virus (AAV) delivery system enables targeted suppression of the fatty acid transporter CD36 and promotes cardiac repair after ischemia-reperfusion injury. By using platelets as injury-responsive carriers, the system preferentially accumulates in damaged myocardium, reduces neutralization by circulating antibodies, and enhances cardiac delivery of the therapeutic vector. In a male mouse model, CD36 knockdown reduces fatty acid utilization, reshapes cardiac lipid metabolism without causing overt lipid overload, increases cardiomyocyte cell-cycle activity, and improves cardiac structure and function. These findings establish a platelet-guided gene delivery strategy that links metabolic reprogramming to myocardial regeneration and suggest a promising approach for ischemic heart repair. Gene therapy for the injured heart is limited by poor targeting and neutralizing antibodies against viral vectors. Here, the authors show that platelets can ferry CD36-silencing AAV to damaged myocardium, reprogramming metabolism and restoring heart function in mice.

papers.title: Plasmonic vortex cavities toward the ultra-compact limit
papers.abstract: Compact control of optical orbital angular momentum (OAM) is central to chip-scale photonic integration. Plasmonic vortex lenses have therefore emerged as a key on-chip platform for encoding and manipulating OAM through tunable topological-charge engineering. Advancing beyond plasmonic vortex lenses, here we propose plasmonic vortex cavities as a gap-plasmon-based cavity concept for vortex confinement, in which the plasmonic vortex is supported by a metal-insulator-metal (MIM) cavity with footprints below λ/10 and annular features smaller than λ/60. A unified physical framework is established and reveals the governing physics: the strongly flattened gap-SPP dispersion controlled by the gap width compresses the SPP wavelength and shrinks the vortex size toward the ultra-compact limit set by quantum effects; meanwhile, intrinsic cavity reflection yields strong standing-wave enhancement. Full-wave simulations corroborate the framework, revealing clear and strong PV fields within deep-subwavelength footprints. The paradigm transition from lens-type to cavity-type vortices provides an ultra-compact OAM platform, advancing chip-scale integration. Optical vortices enable optical orbital angular momentum science and technology, but their spot size limits nanoscale integration and interactions with matter. This study uses a plasmonic cavity to compress their radii toward the ultra-compact limit.

papers.title: Engineered d-p orbital hybridization unlocks dilute CO2 electrolysis to byproduct-free CH4-rich syngas
papers.abstract: Electrochemical CO2 methanation from flue gas offers a promising approach for upgrading point-source emissions and synthesizing energy-dense CH4. However, it remains challenging for both the direct utilization of dilute upstream and the extra downstream separation of complex byproducts. Here, we develop a gaseous byproduct-free system with an inlet of flue gas and an outlet of CH4-rich syngas for metallurgy and energy fields, wherein rationally designed Sn-based electrocatalysts are integrated with the direct electrolysis of bicarbonate-rich capture media, facilitated by engineered electrolyte distributors within scale-up flow cells. Specifically, guided by computational screening of atomic configurations, we engineer a high-density ensemble of sub-nanoscale SnNi clusters (7~8 Å) on a Ni-N-C architecture. The atomic arrangement and local coordination are resolved via operando synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function analysis. Consequently, near-zero multi-carbon byproducts are achieved by steering enhanced d-p orbital hybridization of Ni-CHO with a partial current density of CH4 over 1000 mA/cm2. With the simulated flue gas inlet, approximately 1500 L CH4-rich syngas is collected in around five days with flow cells. Electrochemical conversion of CO2 from dilute flue gas into methane remains limited by complex byproducts. Here, the authors integrate a tin-nickel catalyst into flow cells to convert captured CO2 directly into methane-rich syngas with near-zero multicarbon byproducts.

papers.title: Emergence of chiral multi-armed spirals in an open system of migrating cells under continuous cell supply
papers.abstract: From molecular assemblies to multicellular tissues, chirality organizes living and active-matter systems into striking collective states. Across cellular collectives and active materials, weak microscopic chiral cues in motion and interaction can systematically skew how constituents coordinate, flow, and break spatial symmetries. Yet the principles that govern chiral ordering in open systems, where elements are continuously supplied and removed, remain poorly understood. Here, we show that chemotaxis-deficient Dictyostelium discoideum mutants (KI cells) form centimeter-scale, clockwise, multi-armed spirals. Each arm is a traveling band produced by short-range alignment interactions and guided by a polar-ordered rotating core that encircles the cell source. A subtle clockwise bias in single-cell migration is amplified by collective ordering into tissue-scale chirality. To uncover the minimal ingredients, we developed an open chiral Vicsek model and found that intrinsic chirality, polar alignment, and continuous cell supply are the key factors. Our study establishes a general route by which weak microscopic chirality and sustained material flux generate macroscopic chiral order, offering new insight into chiral patterning in multicellular systems. Living and active-matter systems can develop large-scale chiral patterns from weak microscopic biases, but how such chirality emerges in open, continuously supplied systems remains poorly understood. Here, the authors combine experiments in Dictyostelium discoideum with an open chiral Vicsek model to show that intrinsic cell chirality, polar alignment, and continuous cell supply are sufficient to amplify a subtle migration bias into centimeter-scale rotating spiral patterns.

papers.title: Multiproperty optimization of therapeutic antibodies through sequence editing via large language model and reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: Discovering antibodies with multiple beneficial properties is essential for therapeutic drug development, but experimentally identified antibodies require further optimization. Joint optimization remains challenging because sequence space is vast, annotations are sparse and property tradeoffs are common. Herein, we propose AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework for multiproperty antibody optimization through parallel multisite sequence editing. AbOptimizer identifies promising editing sites and edit actions, including ‘reservation’, ‘substitution’ and optional ‘insertion’ or ‘deletion’, before recommending mutations from protein language models, while surrogate evaluation and Pareto rewards shape policy training. We evaluate AbOptimizer on three therapeutic antibodies across multiproperty, data-limited and indel-inclusive optimization. In silico, AbOptimizer improves optimized properties and outperforms baseline methods. In vitro, selected variants show affinity-specificity co-optimization for emibetuzumab, improved affinity and specificity with largely maintained thermal stability for siltuximab, and indel-inclusive affinity optimization for trastuzumab. These results validate AbOptimizer as a practical framework for therapeutic antibody optimization. This study presents AbOptimizer, a computational framework that edits antibody sequences to improve multiple therapeutic properties. Tests on three antibodies show improved affinity, specificity and stability-related profiles.

papers.title: Cephalopod-inspired embodied camouflage system for simultaneous evasion of artificial and human visual perception
papers.abstract: Differences in visual perception mechanisms between biological and artificial intelligence make it difficult to design camouflage that is both visually natural and effective against modern detectors. Existing adversarial approaches often create conspicuous patterns and are typically static, limiting their use in dynamic real-world scenarios. Here we present CephCam, an embodied closed-loop camouflage system that integrates environment-aware color extraction, optimization-based texture generation that jointly balances visual naturalness and detector evasion, and angle-aware display compensation for physical deployment. This system involves an eye-brain-skin framework of sensing, computation, and display, motivated by the naturally evolved cephalopod camouflage, but implemented with specialized cameras, computing modules, and OLED screens on a model vehicle. CephCam targets simultaneous evasion of both human observers and modern object detectors across diverse digital and physical environments, significantly outperforming strong baselines targeting either alone. These findings underscore shared vulnerabilities in human and artificial visual processing systems, showcasing CephCam’s potential for robust, adaptive, and embodied camouflage applications. Authors demonstrate a cephalopod-inspired, closed-loop camouflage system that uses cameras to extract environmental colors, optimization algorithms to generate adaptive textures, and OLED screens with angle-aware compensation, that reduces detectability by both human observers and deep-learning object detectors.

papers.title: Quantitative mobile gamma-ray spectrometry through Bayesian inference
papers.abstract: Accurate quantitative mapping of gamma-ray emitters is critical for applications ranging from radiological emergency response and environmental monitoring to nuclear security and deep space exploration. Here, we show that such mapping can be achieved by combining mobile gamma-ray spectrometry with high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations and full-spectrum Bayesian inference. Using 6 s of single-pass mobile spectrometry data benchmarked against independent in-situ and laboratory assays, we demonstrate decisive source mixture identification (>5σ), meter-scale source localization, and recovery of source activities with percent-level accuracy. The developed method marks a critical advance in quantitative gamma-ray sensing, enabling improved radiological situational awareness, enhanced terrestrial geophysical and geochemical mapping, as well as more robust constraints on radionuclide abundances on extraterrestrial bodies across the Solar System. Mobile gamma-ray spectrometry (MGRS) provides the gold standard for gamma-ray source identification yet current approaches suffer inaccuracies due to scarcity of data and the inherently ill-posed inversion. Here, the authors advance full-spectrum analysis template-matching approaches in MGRS by means of a Bayesian inversion framework.

papers.title: The intermediate hippocampus integrates shock-observation and spatial information during observational fear memory in male rats
papers.abstract: Learning where danger lurks by observing others requires linking another individual’s distress to one’s own representation of space. How the hippocampus implements this mapping is unknown. We recorded Neuropixels activity across the dorsal, intermediate and ventral hippocampus of male rats during contextual fear learning by observation, subsequent rest and recall. Observers showed increased immobility in the context where they had witnessed a conspecific receive footshocks, with substantial inter-individual variability. Pyramidal neurons were recruited by shock observation, with enriched shock-excited cells in the intermediate hippocampus. In the dorsal and intermediate hippocampus, shock-observation responses scaled with baseline place-field firing, revealing a gain-like conjunctive code between observed distress and observer’s position. Following learning, shock-context spatial representations were selectively stabilized in the intermediate hippocampus, and post-learning sharp-wave ripples preferentially reactivated shock-context ensembles, especially in animals expressing contextual freezing. These findings identify candidate hippocampal mechanisms by which socially acquired threat information are mapped onto the observer’s spatial representation and consolidated into memory. The authors find that in rats, responses to witnessing others’ distress scale with hippocampal place-field firing, linking observed danger to the observer’s location. Associated spatial maps are stabilized and reactivated, particularly in the intermediate hippocampus.

papers.title: A tri-modular feline infectious peritonitis virus nanoparticle vaccine confers complete protection in female cats without detectable antibody-dependent enhancement
papers.abstract: Antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) complicates coronavirus vaccine development. Feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV) is a classic model of coronavirus vaccine-mediated ADE. Here, we develop ferritin-based FIPV nanoparticle vaccines displaying nucleocapsid (N) antigen, antigen-presenting cell (APC)-targeting ligands, and immunostimulatory factors, and evaluate their protective efficacy, serum-mediated ADE risk, and associated immune features. Compared with soluble N protein, the single-module FIPV N nanoparticle vaccine (sfNnps) enhances FIPV N-specific T-cell responses yet confers only 25.0% (2/8) protection. Dual-module vaccines incorporating either the APC-targeting ligand HCV E2 (dfN/Hnps) or the immunostimulatory factor IFNγ (dfN/Inps) further boost N-specific T-cell responses and confer 50.0% (4/8) and 62.5% (5/8) protection, respectively. The tri-modular vaccine co-displaying N, HCV E2, and IFNγ (tfN/HInps) elicits the most robust N-specific T-cell responses and affords 100% (8/8) protection in female cats, while showing no detectable serum-mediated ADE under the tested conditions and reducing peripheral-blood viral RNA levels by 73.0%. Immune profiling associates tfN/HInps with increased cDC1 representation and antigen-presentation gene expression, as well as a shift toward CD8⁺ effector-memory T cells and a FOXO1-centered program linked to transcriptional features of increased proliferation, memory formation, and cytotoxicity. Overall, this engineered FIPV nano‑display vaccine could provide a framework for cellular‑immunity‑oriented vaccine development against ADE‑prone coronaviruses. This study shows that a tri-modular ferritin nanoparticle vaccine against feline infectious peritonitis virus elicits strong cellular immunity and provides protection in female cats without detectable serum-mediated antibody-dependent enhancement.

papers.title: Organic matter composition modulates its degradation under the combined effects of iron (oxyhydr)oxides and light
papers.abstract: The extent of organic matter (OM) degradation in sunlit surface soils and shallow marine sediments is critical to global carbon and nitrogen cycling. Association with iron (oxyhydr)oxides can reduce degradation, but the role of light in iron–OM interaction is underexplored. Here we show that OM composition determines contrasting responses to iron and light. Carboxyl- and/or hydroxyl-containing OM undergoes oxidation and decarboxylation, releasing carbon dioxide, whereas protein-like carboxyl–amine OM forms cross-linked products through condensation and polymerization, with only limited degradation. Iron and light promote oxidation–decarboxylation by enhancing electron transfer and visible-light absorption, while iron promotes protein unfolding and light may provide energy for polymerization. Under high-irradiance conditions equivalent to one-month cumulative daylight exposure, a conditional assessment of representative sunlight-exposed topsoil OM indicates potential carbon losses of ~8% for carboxyl- and/or hydroxyl-type OM versus ~1% for carboxyl–amine-type OM. Photochemically promoted amide formation may limit OM degradation and carbon loss, informing carbon management and process-based carbon cycle models. This study shows that iron minerals and sunlight drive different fates for organic matter in soils and sediments depending on its chemistry: some forms are broken down and lose carbon, while others form cross-linked products that resist degradation.

An Early Jurassic soft eggshell provides insights into the evolutionary history of dinosaur eggs
papers.abstract: Early eggshell fossils offer invaluable insights into evolutionary innovations in over 300 million years of amniote egg history. However, the incompleteness of the dinosaur eggshell fossil record hinders ancestral state reconstruction and leads to uncertainty about whether the first dinosaur egg was soft-shelled, semi-rigid-shelled, or rigid-shelled. Herein, we present a fossilized soft eggshell (Mutabilisoolithus dawaensis) from an Early Jurassic basal sauropodomorph. We find that M. dawaensis has a soft, plastic-like deformation, a thick cuticle, a thin calcareous layer formed by non-interlocking shell units, and a significantly thick shell membrane. Its shell membrane is similar to that of avian eggs in structure, diameter, and arrangement of the fibers, as well as in the distinctions among outer, inner, and limiting membrane layers, but it is much thicker than that of avian eggs. In dinosaurian egg evolutionary history, M. dawaensis provides evidence of early Jurassic soft-shelled eggs, may represent the earliest stage of biomineralization, and bridges the gap between non-biomineralized membranous soft eggshells and biomineralized semi-rigid eggshells. Fossil dinosaur eggs are extremely rare, and there is uncertainty about their ancestral anatomy and evolution. A newly described Early Jurassic sauropodomorph soft-shelled egg offers valuable insights into the reproductive biology of dinosaurs.

Neoadjuvant durvalumab plus chemotherapy in resectable or borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer: the phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE trial
papers.abstract: The phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE study is investigating perioperative durvalumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy (AEGEAN regimen) in resectable and borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer and chemoradiotherapy (CRT) followed by consolidation durvalumab (PACIFIC regimen) in patients who become unresectable after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy guided by multidisciplinary team assessments during the neoadjuvant period. The primary endpoint was the overall resection rate (descriptive with no formal hypothesis testing). Secondary endpoints included event-free survival, progression-free survival, pathological complete response rate (resectable patients cohort), circulating tumor DNA clearance between baseline and presurgery/pre-CRT and safety. Overall, 142 patients received neoadjuvant treatment; 64.8% and 35.2% were deemed resectable and borderline resectable at baseline, respectively. The overall resection rate (95% confidence interval) was 74.6% (66.7‒81.6) in a population that included more than one-third of patients with borderline resectable disease. R0 resection rate was 96.2% (90.6‒99.0) in those who underwent surgery. Overall, 131 (92.3%) patients had surgery (n = 106) or CRT (n = 25) after neoadjuvant treatment, and 117 (82.4%) patients received adjuvant (n = 94) or consolidation (n = 23) durvalumab. During adjuvant or consolidation durvalumab, maximum grade 3/4 adverse events occurred in 7.4% of resected patients and 17.4% of CRT-treated patients, with 8.5% and 13.0% discontinuing treatment due to adverse events. This multidisciplinary team-guided approach was feasible and enabled delivery of curative-intent treatment (surgery or CRT), followed by durvalumab in most patients, and demonstrated encouraging preliminary efficacy with a manageable adjuvant or consolidation safety profile that was consistent with prior studies. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05925530 . As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026: In the global phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE trial, neoadjuvant durvalumab plus chemotherapy in patients with resectable and borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer, followed by multidisciplinary reassessment, enabled surgery in most patients, leading to encouraging pathological complete response rates, and no additional safety concerns were reported when patients with unresectable tumors continued with chemoradiotherapy and consolidative durvalumab.

papers.title: Continuous mass photometry by single-molecule trapping
papers.abstract: The dynamic choreography of biomolecular interactions underpins the processes of life, but its direct observation remains challenging. papers.title: The maternal–fetal interface is an early hematopoietic niche enriched in distinct erythro-myeloid progenitors
papers.abstract: Embryonic hematopoiesis is thought to occur exclusively in the extraembryonic yolk sac before hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) arise in the aorta–gonad–mesonephros region. Here we identify a previously unrecognized hematopoietic site at the maternal–fetal interface in mice, termed MIXER (Maternally Interfaced eXtraEmbRyonic) tissue, which develops contemporaneously with the yolk sac and exhibits robust hematopoietic activity. MIXER contains abundant hematopoietic precursors, including classical CSF1R+ erythro-myeloid progenitors and a unique embryonic CD4+CSF1R− Erythro-Myeloid PRogenitOR (eEMPROR) population. Lineage-tracing experiments demonstrate that eEMPROR cells contribute to select macrophage subpopulations during fetal development, primarily in the perivascular space. Notably, early human placental villi, before HSC emergence, also harbor CD4+ nucleated erythrocytes, indicating a conserved hematopoietic role for the maternal–fetal interface. These findings establish MIXER as an anatomically distinct niche for embryonic hematopoiesis and expand the developmental map of blood cell emergence in mammals. Jain et al. identify a unique extraembryonic hematopoietic niche at the maternal–fetal interface that is distinct from the yolk sac and is capable of producing CD4+CSF1R− erythro-myeloid progenitors.

papers.title: A CD4-lineage erythro–myeloid progenitor within the adult bone marrow defines an alternative pathway for macrophage generation
papers.abstract: Tissue-resident macrophages originate from distinct developmental sources, but their adult replenishment is thought to depend exclusively on circulating monocytes. Here we identify a previously unrecognized CD4-lineage erythro–myeloid progenitor (EMPROR) in the adult bone marrow that provides an alternative pathway for macrophage generation. EMPROR cells are phenotypically and transcriptionally distinct from hematopoietic stem cells, common myeloid progenitors and monocyte precursors, lacking Csf1r and Ccr2 while expressing Cd4 and Kit. Single-cell RNA sequencing, RNA velocity analysis and lineage assays reveal macrophage, neutrophil, megakaryocytic and erythroid potential. EMPROR cells generate perivascular and tumor-associated macrophages independently of CCR2-mediated monocyte recruitment and contribute to erythroid and granulocytic lineages under inflammatory and neoplastic conditions. Transcriptomic comparisons position EMPROR cells closest to embryonic erythro–myeloid progenitors, indicating the persistence of an embryonic-like program in adult bone marrow. These findings reveal an alternative pathway of adult myelopoiesis that sustains macrophage diversity beyond the classical monocyte lineage. Tissue-resident macrophages originate from distinct developmental sources, but their adult replenishment is thought to depend exclusively on circulating monocytes. Here Tikoo and colleagues identify a CD4-lineage erythro–myeloid progenitor (EMPROR) in the adult bone marrow that provides an alternative pathway for macrophage generation.

Quantification method affects replicability of eQTL analysis, colocalization and TWAS
papers.abstract: Expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) mapping, colocalization and transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) are widely used to contextualize genome-wide association study loci, yet the impact of upstream RNA-sequencing processing choices on these analyses remains critically unexplored. Two poorly characterized decisions include the transcriptomic reference annotation used for quantification of short-read RNA-sequencing samples, which defines transcript composition and structure, and the quantification method itself. Here, through a comprehensive analysis spanning 48 tissues in GTEx and 7 widely studied and diverse phenotypes, we find that these choices substantially affect eQTL detection and gene expression prediction with significant downstream impacts on colocalization and TWAS results. Concordant results across pipelines are further enriched for longer genes, genes with more isoforms, and greater expression heritability. Our findings demonstrate that seemingly minor methodological decisions substantially affect these common analyses, highlighting the need for standardized practices to ensure reproducible genetic association studies. This study finds that upstream RNA-seq processing steps, specifically transcript annotations and quantification methods, can affect eQTL mapping, TWAS and colocalization with GWAS. It serves as a cautionary message to the community to carefully report transcript annotation and quantification methods in future work.

papers.title: Enzymatic oxidative esterification with an unconventional regioselective control
papers.abstract: Esters have widespread applications in nature and industry, making the strategic installation of ester bonds critical for the synthesis of pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, polymers and other functional materials. However, achieving regioselective esterification of sterically demanding secondary alcohols in the presence of more reactive primary sites remains a formidable challenge. Here we report the engineering of aldehyde dehydrogenases into oxidative ester synthases (OxiEs) with divergent selectivities. Structure-guided protein engineering yielded two complementary catalyst classes: imidazole-dependent OxiEs1 favours primary alcohols and imidazole-independent OxiEs2 exhibits exclusive selectivity for secondary alcohols. Mechanistic studies revealed that imidazole acts as a molecular switch, allosterically tuning the active-site geometry to control regioselectivity. This system demonstrates a broad substrate scope, enabling direct, highly selective acylation of various secondary alcohols. Furthermore, we showcase its utility in controlling enantioselectivity, enabling redox-neutral synthesis and preparing valuable esters on gram-scale. This work establishes a strategy for regioselective control in esterification, transforming a classical hydride-transfer enzyme into a tunable platform for ester bond formation under mild, sustainable conditions. Regioselective esterification remains challenging, particularly when multiple alcohol groups with similar reactivity are present. Now it has been shown that aldehyde dehydrogenases can be engineered into oxidative ester synthases with programmable alcohol selectivity, enabling controlled ester bond formation through active-site remodelling.

papers.abstract: Patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain at high risk of relapse despite perioperative treatment1-3. NeoCOAST-2 (NCT05061550), a phase 2, randomised platform trial, tested novel perioperative treatments in patients with stage IIA–IIIB NSCLC. At primary analysis, combining standard chemotherapy plus durvalumab (anti-PD-L1 antibody) with oleclumab (Arm 1, n = 76), monalizumab (Arm 2, n = 72) or datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd; Arm 4, n = 54) resulted in pathological complete response (pCR) rates of 20.3%, 25.7%, and 35.2%, respectively4. Here, we present the first report of prespecified secondary endpoints of event-free survival (EFS) and circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) clearance, and exploratory analyses of associations between ctDNA dynamics and clinical outcomes. The 24-month EFS rates were 70.5%, 75.7% and 77.9% in Arms 1, 2 and 4, respectively. Using a tumour-agnostic assay, ctDNA clearance at neoadjuvant Cycle 3 Day 1 was highest in Arm 4 (50.9%, 54.5%, and 72.5% in each arm, respectively). ctDNA clearance correlated with prolonged EFS versus non-clearance (pooled hazard ratio (HR) 0.22; 95% CI = 0.11–0.45, P = 0.0000443). Patients with both ctDNA clearance and pCR had favourable EFS outcomes versus those with neither (EFS HR 0.10, 95% CI = 0.02–0.42, P = 0.002). These findings suggest combined assessment of ctDNA clearance and pCR may improve risk stratification, and that the numerically highest pCR4 and EFS rates with the Dato-DXd combination warrant further evaluation.

papers.title: Active locomotion predictively rescues head direction attractor dynamics in head-fixed mice
papers.abstract: Head direction (HD) cells in the anterodorsal thalamic nucleus form the brain’s internal compass, and are often modeled as a ring attractor maintaining azimuth coding by leveraging continuous visual and inertial sensory input. Here, we test how the common experimental preparation of head-fixed animals alters this code. Complete head-fixation that creates vestibular conflict disrupts both unit and population encoding of head direction, while selectively constraining head-on-body movements either in real or virtual reality uniquely impairs HD population activity. More specifically, attractor dynamics are altered in head-restrained male mice during periods of immobility, and a computational model recapitulates this effect by perturbing lateral connectivity among HD neurons. These dynamics recover several hundred milliseconds prior to locomotion onset, suggesting that an efference copy or prediction of a re-afferent signal is necessary to maintain HD network activity during head restraint. More generally, the results indicate that the HD network is a context- and state-dependent predictive estimator, stabilized by forthcoming self-motion signals. The classic ring-attractor models should be revised to integrate context-dependent dynamics with prospective motor signals, offering a more complete account of how the brain’s compass remains stable across both naturalistic and constrained conditions. Head direction cells in the anterodorsal thalamic nuclei provide a compass-like signal in the brain. Here, the authors investigate how head fixation and behavioural state impact head-direction attractor dynamics.

papers.title: Structural dynamics of substrate processing by the p97-Ufd1-Npl4-FAF1 machinery
papers.abstract: The AAA-ATPase VCP/p97 unfolds ubiquitylated proteins in key signaling and cellular homeostasis pathways, yet the mechanisms by which Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 adapters handle ubiquitin chains to coordinate substrate loading and processing remain unclear. Our cryo-EM study of p97-Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 engaging a substrate reveal interactions that drive substrate processing. While Npl4 is capped by distal ubiquitins, and the initiator ubiquitin can be traced from the Npl4 groove to the ATPase channel at near-atomic resolution, we find that the Npl4 tower adaptively responds to the configurational changes in the ATPase motor’s spiral staircase. A helix in FAF1 together with the Ufd1-UT3 domain engage proximal ubiquitins while providing the necessary structural plasticity to accommodate this motion and deliver ubiquitins to Npl4’s groove. Our study reveals the intricate, dynamic interplay between p97, Ufd1-Npl4, and FAF1 in efficient processing of ubiquitylated substrates. VCP/p97 uses Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 to process polyubiquitylated substrates. Here, the authors show how these adapters coordinate ubiquitin-chain engagement and delivery while adapting to conformational changes in the p97 ATPase motor during substrate processing.

papers.title: Structure and function of cyanobacterial Omp85 reveal Toc159/Toc90 as a chloroplast protein import pore
papers.abstract: Chloroplast protein-import channel Toc75 evolved from a cyanobacterial outer-membrane Omp85 protein, despite all known Omp85 proteins functioning in export. Chlamydomonas Toc75 assembles with Toc90M, the membrane-spanning domain of Toc90 (equivalent of higher-plant Toc159) into a binocular-shaped complex, but how this architecture arose and functions in import remain unknown. Here, cryo-electron microscopy and mutational analysis of a cyanobacterial Omp85 reveal a lidded 16-β-strand barrel and three POTRA-domains involved in assembling outer-membrane proteins. Structural comparisons show that the Toc75–Toc90M complex mirrors an Omp85–substrate assembly intermediate, and Toc90M can indeed serve as a bacterial Omp85 substrate. While canonical Omp85 systems release substrates after assembly, Toc75 evolved a basic patch in its barrel to anchor Toc90M as a stable lateral pore through which precursor proteins are imported. Our findings indicate that a bacterial export system was converted into a chloroplast import channel by locking a substrate in place to provide an import conduit. This requirement for a stable assembly also supports that additional parts of the ancestral complex, including Omp85 POTRA-domains and Tic236 orthologs, were recruited to facilitate chloroplast protein import. Chloroplasts evolved from a cyanobacterial ancestor. Here authors show a cyanobacterial protein export system was transformed into a chloroplast protein import channel by gaining a specific patch to lock a substrate in place to provide the import conduit.

papers.title: A multi-functionally integrated modular catalyst for efficient chemoselective hydrogenation
papers.abstract: Chemoselective hydrogenation of nitroarenes containing multiple reducible groups remains challenging due to the intrinsic activity–selectivity trade-off of conventional metal catalysts. Here we report a multi-functional Pt-based catalyst, modularly integrating molecular-sieving feedstock separation, hydrogen activation, intermediate transport and surface reaction like a nanofactory. Structurally, ~3 nm Pt nanoparticles supported on sodium titanate are encapsulated by oxygen vacancies-enriched TiOx overlayers that only permit hydrogen to adsorb on Pt particles for dissociation while preventing substrate contact. The generated active hydrogen species subsequently migrate to the catalyst surface and hydrogenate nitro groups adsorbed on surface Lewis basic oxygen vacancies, enabling an efficient condensation pathway while avoiding the use of corrosive and environmentally unfriendly alkaline solvents. The spatially decoupled yet functionally synergistic catalytic design achieves 90% 3-vinylaniline yield from 3-nitrostyrene under mild conditions with an unprecedented turnover frequency of 83,200 h−1, exceeding all previously reported metal catalysts, and exhibits broad generality toward diverse substituted nitroarenes. Collectively, these findings provide a powerful catalyst design strategy for steering complex reaction networks via spatially modular catalysis. Chemoselective hydrogenation of nitroarenes containing multiple reducible functional groups remains challenging because of the inherent activity–selectivity trade-off of conventional metal catalysts. Here, the authors report a multifunctional Pt-based catalyst that integrates molecular-sieving feedstock separation, hydrogen activation, intermediate transport, and surface reactions within a single catalytic system, enabling efficient chemoselective hydrogenation.

papers.title: Superior energy-storage performance in BaTiO3-based MLCCs via high-entropy driven multiscale optimization
papers.abstract: Multilayer ceramic capacitors are essential components in modern electronic devices. However, achieving superior performance under high-temperature and high-electric-field remains a huge challenge due to the increased leakage current and limited breakdown strength. Herein, a high-entropy driven multiscale optimization strategy is proposed for lead-free multilayer ceramic capacitors. This approach integrates multiple elements into both A- and B-sites at the atomic scale, engineers polymorphic domain coexistence at the phase scale, and introduces a uniform SiO2 coating layer on grain surfaces to form a core–shell structure while refining grain size at the grain scale. Furthermore, a SiO2 barrier layer is constructed between the electrodes and ceramics at the device scale. Remarkably, high-entropy BaTiO3-based Multilayer ceramic capacitors achieve an ultra-high energy density of 19.8 J·cm−3 and a high efficiency of 89.3% at 1421 kV·cm−1, along with an outstanding high-temperature energy storage performance. The high-entropy driven multiscale optimization strategy offers a universal approach to enhancing the overall energy storage performance of advanced dielectric capacitors. The authors propose a high-entropy driven multiscale optimization strategy to achieve recoverable energy density of 19.8 J·cm−3 and efficiency of 89.3% with excellent thermal and cycling stability in ceramic capacitors.

papers.title: Programmable roll-to-roll laser processing for high value application of low-grade carbon fiber materials
papers.abstract: Growing production of carbon fibers generates substantial short-chopped fibers that are difficult for high-value use due to their structural discontinuity. Carbon fiber felts offer potential, yet weak inter-fiber bonding and poor conductivity limit the performance. We report a roll‑to‑roll laser processing strategy that uses a liquid precursor to form laser‑induced graphene at fiber‑fiber interfaces, creating conductive pathways and mechanical interconnections. This approach increases tensile strength from 4.1 to 32.2 MPa and electrical conductivity from 1224.0 to 15151.5 S/m. The resulting films demonstrate efficient electrothermal de‑icing and, after copper deposition, lightning strike protection with a damage area of 9657 mm² and depth of 0.4 mm, comparable to aluminum mesh but with 15% lower weight. A custom‑built laser platform enables scalable production. Here, we show the conversion of low‑grade carbon fibers into lightweight, functional films for aerospace applications via scalable laser processing. This study reports a roll-to-roll strategy that converts short-chopped carbon fibers into functional films with 8-fold strength and 10-fold conductivity, with applications such as aircraft de-icing and lightning protection

papers.title: From microstructure to function: spatial visualization of magnetic permeability
papers.abstract: Understanding the physics of high-frequency magnetic response is essential for advancing electromagnetic materials. Here, a general strategy is presented for visualizing magnetic permeability as a spatially distributed, frequency-dependent field, instead of a uniform bulk parameter. Our framework reveals that high-frequency magnetic loss arises from coherent spin-wave propagation and interference, leading to spatially selective energy absorption and localized regions of negative imaginary permeability. Tailoring geometric connectivity to suppress spin-wave propagation enables the selective enhancement of localized resonances. Such resonance enables deterministic control over high-frequency response through structural design. The principle is further examined in nanoscale iron spheres. Their surface morphology plays a decisive role in reorganizing the internal resonance domains. This structural reconfiguration, in turn, reshapes the broadband magnetic permeability spectra. To navigate the high-dimensional space of surface defect configurations, machine learning models are integrated with micromagnetic simulations, allowing rapid prediction of magnetic performance across microwave bands. Computational modeling provides an ideal platform to complement experimental exploration. The physic-data framework reveals geometry-to-spectra design rules, validated on iron nanoparticles. This framework uniquely bridges the microscopic spin dynamics with electromagnetic response, enabling tunable high-frequency materials for communication and sensing. This work introduces a general framework describing permeability as a spatially varying, frequency-dependent field, showing high-frequency magnetic loss stems from spin-wave propagation and interference, establishing geometry-to-spectra design methods linking microscopic spin dynamics to tunable high-frequency electromagnetic properties.
